author: oba-one
body:
Follow-up to review on #835 and #836, targeting the top of that stack. Four small commits.

## What was wrong

Retrying a single act reported **"Some jobs failed to sync. We'll retry automatically in the background."** Both halves were wrong at that site: the person had chosen one act, and a failure that reaches this branch is one the queue gave up on rather than rescheduled.

It now has its own message, **"Couldn't send it / It's still saved on this device. You can try again."** The background flush keeps `syncError`, where a whole batch failed and the next connectivity event does retry it. A test pins the two sites apart.

## Why not jobFailed

The review suggested reusing `jobFailed(kind, detail)`. It does not fit here. `retryAndSend` is reached only from the pool tab and `FailedActAlert`, so the job is always a commitment act, while `jobFailed` takes `"work" | "approval"` and sends the reader to Your Work, where an act does not appear. Work and decisions get that accurate per-kind message already, from the `job:failed` handler in the same provider.

## Localization

The provider builds its toasts through `createQueueToasts(formatMessage)`, so every queue toast translates instead of rendering English under every locale. The provider tests move their spies behind that call and stub `useIntl` the way the other shared tests do.

That left the English-only `queueToasts` object with no caller, so this change deletes it along with its three re-exports. Source ends up 34 lines smaller than before the change (+36 / -70); tests are +40 / -8 for one new case and the mock rewiring the import change forces.

## Review follow-ups

Three more commits answer the review threads still open on #835 and on this PR. They sit here rather than in #835 because the four PRs merge together, and restacking 44 commits for a few lines is not worth the churn.

- `76d3f92b0` The provider still wrote five English sentences of its own: the three reasons an act is still queued, a "Cannot sync" toast, and a "Queue sync failed" toast. The reasons are messages in en, es and pt now; being signed out is one of them, and a retry that throws uses `retryFailed`. The provider test renders under the real `IntlProvider`, as the work provider's does, instead of mocking `react-intl`.
- `4e654e037` A declined decision is held for an explicit send, as declined work already was. Only an embedded wallet could hit this: its background flush sends every kind, so the next connectivity event would reopen the prompt the person had just declined.
- `9b43a43f4` The queue core tests restore spies in their teardown, so a test that throws cannot leave `Date.now` mocked for the rest of the file.

The duplicate-toast finding is answered in its thread without a change: the `job:failed` handler toasts only for work and decisions, and `retryAndSend` is only ever given commitment acts.

## Left for the cleanup that follows this stack

`approvalToasts.error` / `createApprovalToasts(...).error` has no callers: `useWorkApproval` reports failures through `toastService.error` directly. It was unreachable before this change, and it owns four groups of defaults, ids and locale keys, so it goes with the rest of the unused toast presets rather than being half-removed here. An earlier version of this PR corrected its wording; that edit is dropped, since nobody can see the text.

## Validation

`node scripts/dev/ci-local.js --intent push` passes all 19 selected checks on `9b43a43f4`, run by hand and again by the pre-push hook: format, lint, typechecks, the full shared, client, admin and agent suites, builds, source structure, design guardrails and ontology. `browser-proof` is not selected: no client view changes.

Rebuilt as one commit on the restacked #836 tip (`f611bedd8`). The earlier head carried the pre-restack stack, which is why GitHub showed 57 commits and a conflict.

author: reppl
body:
## What changed

`internal/hub` had two request paths answering differently about where a
response may come from: `Files` refused a cross-origin `rel="next"` page
explicitly, while `RepoInfo` followed a redirect to any host and decoded
whatever came back as fact about a model. The package now gives that answer
once.

`Client.do` is the seam. It installs `refuseOffOrigin` as `CheckRedirect` on a
shallow copy of `Client.HTTP` — same transport, so the same connection pool —
so a hop that would leave the Hub's origin is refused **before it is made**,
and then re-checks the answer that arrives as a backstop. `Search`, `RepoInfo`
and each page of `Files` go through it. `ErrCrossOrigin` is the single class
both that refusal and the pre-existing `rel="next"` refusal wrap, so a caller
asks one question of all of them.

Before the hop rather than after it, because the first pass at this got three
things wrong and the adversarial read of the diff found them:

- **The token travelled.** `net/http` strips `Authorization` only for a
  different domain — a redirect to a subdomain, or to the same host on another
  port, keeps it — so the token reached a host whose answer was then refused.
- **A detour was accepted.** `hub → other host → hub` passed a final-hop check
  while letting the host in the middle choose which Hub URL got decoded: a
  lookup of one repo answered with another repo's authentic metadata.
- **An unknown origin was allowed.** A response with no recorded final URL fell
  through to the same-origin branch. It now refuses.

`Files` keeps its own `rel="next"` check in addition rather than instead: that
URL is followed by a fresh request the token is attached to, which no redirect
policy sees.

### The one exception, stated honestly

The file-download path deliberately does **not** go through `do`: the Hub
answers a `/resolve/` GET for an LFS object with a redirect to its content CDN,
on another host by design, and refusing that would fetch nothing at all. What
anchors an LFS object is the sha256 the Hub's own API stated for it, which
`downloadFile` verifies. A file the repo stores in git rather than LFS carries
no such hash and is checked on length alone, so for those the hole is wider
than the reason it exists — that is `iss-2609190151179403`, not narrowed here,
because narrowing it rests on an unverified claim about when the real Hub
redirects and getting it wrong breaks downloads outright.
`TestDownloadFollowsTheHubsRedirectToItsContentCDN` pins the exception open
(and now redirects only the LFS object, serving the small files from the
origin, so it does not flatter it).

## Issues

- Resolves **iss-2609190023171129** (minor, security) — `impact: fix`.
- Captures, from the security review, for the maintainer:
  - **iss-2609190151179403** — the download hole is wider than its
    justification for a non-LFS file.
  - **iss-2609190200066074** — a relative `rel="next"` is refused and called
    cross-origin.
  - **iss-2609190200109978** — a download body is unbounded until after it is
    written to disk.
  - **iss-2609190200162002** — a repo id is escaped into the URL on one path
    and interpolated raw on another.

## Tests watched to fail

First commit:

```
--- FAIL: TestRepoInfoRefusesARedirectOffTheHubsOrigin
    RepoInfo read a redirected answer ({ID:org/repo ... PipelineTag:text-generation}); it must refuse
--- FAIL: TestSearchRefusesARedirectOffTheHubsOrigin
    Search read a redirected answer ([{evil/model 0 0 [mlx] ...}]); it must refuse
```

Second commit:

```
--- FAIL: TestAnAPIRedirectOffTheHubsOriginIsRefusedBeforeTheTokenTravels
    TOKEN LEAK: the bearer token was sent to the redirect target ("Bearer secret-hf-token")
--- FAIL: TestAnAPIDetourThroughAnotherHostIsRefused
    RepoInfo followed a detour through another host and answered "attacker/lookalike"
--- FAIL: TestAnAnswerWithNoRecordedOriginIsRefused
    err = <nil>, want ErrCrossOrigin
```

`TestDownloadFollowsTheHubsRedirectToItsContentCDN` was watched to fail with
the download path temporarily routed through `do` — the "simplify it into a
blanket refusal" mistake it exists to stop.

`TestRepoInfoFollowsARedirectOnTheHubsOwnOrigin` holds the other side: a
canonical-repo-id redirect on the Hub's own origin is still followed.

## Gates

`gofmt -l .` empty, `go vet ./...` clean, `go test -race ./...` green apart
from `TestExecProcessReportsAFootprintWhileAliveAndNoneAfter` in
`internal/runtime`, which fails the same way on a clean `origin/main` worktree
("a live process reports 0") and is untouched by this change.

author: davidaragundy
body:
Closes #165

Part of #161. This pull request targets the integration branch `refactor/twt-161`, not `main`.

## What changed

Two Lua scripts, in `src/features/posts/constants/`, generic over any post or
comment hash.

**`TOGGLE_REACTION_SCRIPT`** does, as one atomic step:

- flips the emoji in `reacted:{target}:{reader}`, the reader's set on that target;
- updates the target's `reactions` JSON, in the order each emoji was first added,
  dropping one that reaches zero;
- updates `reactionCount` and recomputes `rank` (score × 10¹⁰ + creation second;
  a post's score adds its comments, a comment's is its reactions);
- expires the reader's set with the target;
- refuses a target that has gone or expired (`-1`), creating nothing.

Two readers toggling at once can't lose an update, since the script runs
atomically.

**`RECORD_VIEWS_SCRIPT`** takes a whole batch (up to 50 ids from the browser's
view tracker) as **one command**. A reader is added to `viewers:{target}` once;
only a new member bumps `viewCount`; the author and expired targets are skipped;
and the set expires with its target.

**Reading.** A page's pipeline now also reads `SMEMBERS reacted:{target}:{reader}`
per item, so each reaction knows whether it's the reader's. That's two reads per
item in one request, plus the search. The optimistic client logic is unchanged:
it already appends a new emoji last, where the script puts it.

**Comments** call the same scripts with `comment:{id}` keys. They work once
comments move to Redis in #166.

## How to verify

Run against the dev server and Upstash:

1. Identity A publishes and reacts 👍. The hash holds `[{"count":1,"emoji":"👍"}]`,
   `reactionCount` 1, and `rank` equal to exactly 1 × 10¹⁰ + the creation second.
   A's set holds 👍 and expires with the post.
2. Identity B records a view on the post twice: `viewCount` becomes 1, not 2. A
   records a view on their own post: still 1.
3. A removes 👍: the chip disappears, and the server returns no reactions.
4. A and B both react 👍: the count is 2, and the rank follows score 2. B removes
   theirs: B reads 👍 1 as not theirs, and A reads it as theirs.
5. Reacting to a post that doesn't exist returns `-1` and leaves no key behind.

## Risk and rollout

Lands only on the integration branch. No schema or index change.

## Checklist

- [x] Title follows Conventional Commits and matches the work
- [x] Branch is named `type/twt-<issue-number>`
- [x] Linked issue above, so it closes on merge
- [x] Everything is in English
- [x] `pnpm lint` and `pnpm typecheck` both pass
- [x] `pnpm build` succeeds, if the change could affect the build
- [x] A schema change ships with its generated migration, and the migration only adds
- [x] Acceptance criteria on the linked issue are met

author: ollysalanson
body:
The minimal first half of the browser-load work, split out so every worker can be steered onto it now. The stepping API, the freeze helper, the input and delta-time verification, the scripted-raid CPU numbers and the fuller AGENTS.md note follow in a second PR.

## What is in it

- **`?testmode=1`** (`src/game/dev/testMode.ts`, read by `createGameConfig`): selects `Phaser.CANVAS` and `fps: { target: 10, forceSetTimeOut: true }`. Nothing else about the game changes. It is a development-build URL flag; `VITE_EPTW_TEST_MODE=1` switches it on for a build made that way. A production build ignores the URL and a plain `npm run dev` sets neither, so it cannot be on by accident - `testMode.test.ts` pins all of that.
- **Vitest capped at four workers** in `vitest.config.ts`; `VITEST_MAX_WORKERS` raises it. The suite (81 files, 1062 tests) takes 9s at four on this box, so the cap costs little.
- **One AGENTS.md note**: launch every automated check with `?testmode=1` and the browser under `nice -n 15`; verify once at real speed before reporting done.

## Measured

Real headless Chromium (Playwright build, no GPU, so WebGL is SwiftShader), 400x256 window, title screen idle for 5 seconds, whole browser process group from `/proc`:

| | renderer | fps | CPU seconds per 5s |
|---|---|---|---|
| plain | WebGL | 60 | 6.23 (125% of a core) |
| `?testmode=1` | Canvas | 10 | 0.34 (7%) |

A baseline scripted raid at real speed cost 69.8 CPU-seconds over 30.6s of wall time - 2.3 cores for one worker's browser - which is the number the second PR will set the test-mode raid against.

## One thing found, not yet fixed

Walking is not frame-rate independent: `WorldScene.advanceStep` clamps a step's progress and drops the remainder of the frame, so a tile costs about 173ms of raid clock at 60fps and will cost more at 10fps. The raid clock, dialogue and battles read delta time and are unaffected. The note in AGENTS.md says not to tune balance from a test-mode run; the second PR carries the fix and the verification that a short key press still registers at 10fps.

Lint, typecheck, the full suite and the production build pass locally.

author: marcfs31
body:
## What

Renames the published design-system package from `@marcfs31/forsight` to `@fors-corp/forsight`, atomically, so nothing at the repo root refers to a name that no longer owns this repo. This is what unblocks publishing: every Release run since the GitHub transfer has 403'd on `PUT https://npm.pkg.github.com/@marcfs31%2fforsight` because the repo's `GITHUB_TOKEN` cannot write into the `@marcfs31` namespace (last observed on run `35409111949`, after the 4.3.0 version PR #175 merged).

## Replacement rules applied

Longest-match-first, because `marcfs31/forsight` is a proper substring of the `@marcfs31/forsight`, `github.com/marcfs31/forsight`, and `marcfs31.github.io/forsight` forms above it. Running the bare `marcfs31/forsight → Fors-Corp/forsight` substitution first — before the scope and host-specific rules — silently produces `@Fors-Corp/forsight` (not a valid GitHub Packages scope; a scope must be the owner login **lowercased**) and `ghcr.io/Fors-Corp/forsight` (Docker/OCI rejects uppercase repository names). Reproduced:

```
$ printf '%s\n' 'npm install @marcfs31/forsight' 'ghcr.io/marcfs31/forsight:latest' | sed 's|marcfs31/forsight|Fors-Corp/forsight|g'
npm install @Fors-Corp/forsight
ghcr.io/Fors-Corp/forsight:latest
```

So the scope/host/tarball-prefix rules ran first, and the bare `marcfs31/forsight → Fors-Corp/forsight` (canonical casing) rule ran **last**, and only through its own anchored forms (`github.com/marcfs31/forsight`, `repos/marcfs31/forsight`) — never as a global substring sed:

- `@marcfs31/forsight` → `@fors-corp/forsight` (lowercase; covers every subpath export: `/theme`, `/chart`, `/styles.css`, `/tailwind.css`, `/fonts.css`, `/tailwind-preset`)
- `@marcfs31:registry` → `@fors-corp:registry`
- `marcfs31.github.io/forsight` → `fors-corp.github.io/forsight` (`gh api repos/Fors-Corp/forsight/pages --jq .html_url` → `https://fors-corp.github.io/forsight/`, confirmed live)
- `github.com/marcfs31/fors-design-system` → `github.com/Fors-Corp/fors-design-system` (link only — that predecessor repo really was transferred too: `gh api repos/marcfs31/fors-design-system --jq .full_name` → `Fors-Corp/fors-design-system`)
- `marcfs31-forsight-` → `fors-corp-forsight-` (the packed-tarball filename prefix `npm pack` derives from the package name)
- `github.com/marcfs31/forsight` / `repos/marcfs31/forsight` → `Fors-Corp/forsight`, anchored, last

Post-check (must return nothing, and does): `git grep -nE '@Fors-Corp|ghcr\.io/Fors-Corp|Fors-Corp\.github\.io'`

## What's excluded, deliberately

- `.github/CODEOWNERS` (`* @marcfs31`) — a **person's** GitHub login, not touched.
- `package.json`'s `author` field — a person, not touched.
- `CHANGELOG.md` and the historical package names `@marcfs31/fors-design-system` / `@marcfs31/fors-observability-design-system` — history, not touched.
- `forsight/**` in its entirety — the Go module rename is a separate PR; `forsight/web/**` and `forsight/internal/api/webdist/**` stay on the old name until a `@fors-corp/forsight` version is published and the dashboard's pin is bumped (a follow-up).
- `.github/workflows/**`, `.github/dependabot.yml`, `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/**` — reserved for the dedicated controls PR, per this repo's `CLAUDE.md`.
- `CONTRIBUTING.md`'s description of the dashboard's pin was reworded name-agnostically instead of renamed, since the dashboard keeps pinning the *old* name until the follow-up lands — renaming it here would have made the doc false.

## Why this is green without the workflow/dashboard PRs

- `ci.yml`'s `setup-node` steps declare no `registry-url`/`scope`, so the root `npm ci` never authenticates to GitHub Packages, and the lockfile's only `marcfs31` strings were its two `name` fields (now updated). The only name-coupled required check is `consumer`, via `scripts/consumer-test.mjs`'s tarball regex — renamed in this same commit.
- `forsight-ci.yml`'s `changes` job decides the `go`/`web` required checks by path regex:
  - `go`: `^(forsight/(cmd|internal|deploy|main\.go|go\.(mod|sum)|Makefile|install\.sh)|forseer/|\.github/workflows/forsight-ci\.yml)`
  - `web`: `^(forsight/web/|forsight/internal/api/webdist/|\.github/workflows/forsight-ci\.yml)`

  Every changed path in this PR is at the repo root, so both regexes evaluate false, both jobs **skip**, and a skipped job satisfies branch protection.
- `codeql.yml` has no path filter and its Go matrix leg builds `forsight/` untouched by this PR, so CodeQL's Go analysis still runs clean.

## Why publishing works after this PR alone

`publishConfig.registry` is package-level and applies to `npm publish` regardless of any npm scope→registry mapping. `release.yml`'s `setup-node` step writes a **host-keyed** auth line (`//npm.pkg.github.com/:_authToken=...`), matched by host, not scope, so the token is found for a publish of any scope on that host. The release job has `packages: write`, and GitHub Packages lets a repository publish under its **owner's** scope — Fors-Corp now — creating and linking the package on first publish (using the `repository.url` this PR also updates). `release.yml`'s `scope: "@marcfs31"` line only writes an unused scope mapping into `~/.npmrc` and is inert for the publish itself; it's cosmetic and gets fixed for hygiene in the controls PR, not to make this work.

**Residual risk to watch**: Fors-Corp currently owns zero npm packages, so this is a first publish under that scope. If the org restricts package creation, the Release run 403s again — but that fix would be an org setting (Organization → Packages) for Marc to flip, not a repo change. I'll watch the Release run that follows this merge.

## The changeset guard

New `scripts/changeset-package-name.test.ts`: one `it(...)` that reads `package.json`'s `name`, lists every `.changeset/*.md` (excluding `README.md`), parses each file's frontmatter package/bump entries, and asserts every entry names the current package — printing the offending filename and the wrong name it carries when it doesn't. This is exactly the failure mode that already killed a publish once in this repo (#156): a changeset naming a package the workspace doesn't contain silently breaks `changeset version`, and therefore every publish, while `main` stays green, because nothing in the normal gate reads changeset frontmatter. `changeset status`'s own exit code was rejected as the mechanism — not a stable gate on an unknown package name, and it doesn't name the offending file.

It runs inside `npm run test:coverage`, which the required `verify` job runs on both Node 22 and Node 24 — no workflow edit needed. `vitest.config.ts` sets no `include` (so the default `**/*.{test,spec}.?(c|m)[jt]s?(x)` glob picks up `scripts/*.test.ts`, same as the existing `scripts/forsight-treeshake-plugin.test.ts`), and its `exclude` list doesn't touch `scripts/`. Coverage's own `include` is `src/**/*.{ts,tsx}` only, so the new file adds no coverage surface. It's also added to `tsconfig.json`'s `include` array, alongside the existing `scripts/forsight-treeshake-plugin.ts`/`.test.ts` entries — without that, the new test would be invisible to `tsc --noEmit` while vitest still ran it, the one piece of new code on a required check's path that nothing would type-check.

Renamed the two pending changesets (`cardtitle-level-and-live-hint.md`, `charts-shared-reading-and-no-data-label.md`) to name `@fors-corp/forsight` instead of `@marcfs31/forsight` — this guard is exactly why they couldn't be left as-is.

## Version: why major (5.0.0)

A package rename is the most breaking change a package can make: every consumer edits `package.json`'s dependency name, the `@marcfs31:registry` line in their `.npmrc`, and every import specifier. 4.3.0 was never published (the last published version is 4.2.0), so no consumer can be on it — publishing `@fors-corp/forsight` at 4.4.0 would read as a continuation someone could `^4` into, when 4.0–4.2 only ever existed under the old name. body: ## Summary Production first-cycle FAIL log **10993** aborted the UIUC HTML crawl after XML discovery succeeded (186 subjects → 4452 course IDs). Course Explorer returned **HTTP 200 without** `h1.fw-bold` / `#schedule-course-table` chrome. Those bodies were treated as `ValueError: No course heading found …`, counted as exceptions, and tripped the unchanged **>20% Material partial failure** abort (900/4452 = 20.2%). No hard 403/429 was logged. Live probes after cool-down still see HTTP 200 + `h1.fw-bold`, so the selector is valid when unblocked. Fail-loud / no DB write is still correct. This PR does **not** raise the 20% threshold. ## Changes (`webapp/scraper/scrapers/uiuc.py` + tests only) 1. **Soft-block detection** — HTTP 200 missing `h1.fw-bold` and/or `#schedule-course-table` is a structure-miss, not a permanent parse failure. Logs status, content-type, body size, and a short title/snippet. 2. **429-style retry** — same `[2, 4, 8]` exponential backoff used for 429/5xx before counting a course failure. 3. **Consecutive abort** — after 15 structure-miss responses in a row, fail immediately with `UIUC soft-block: N consecutive structure-miss responses` instead of burning through ~900 IDs. 4. **Pacing** — `MAX_CONCURRENT_COURSES` 4 → 2; inter-batch sleep 0.2s → 1.5s ± 0.3s jitter. 5. **Ops counts** — material-failure message now includes `success=…, soft-block=…, http-error=…`. 6. **Tests** — 200-without-heading detection, retry-then-success, consecutive abort, Open/Closed HTML still parses, 20% threshold + ops counts unchanged. ## Testing `python3 -m pytest tests/test_scrapers/test_uiuc.py -v --noconftest -o addopts= -o asyncio_mode=auto` — **53 passed**. ## Out of scope NC State / other scrapers, purge scripts, prod DB / seed / activate, marketing/frontend.

author: ygallardops
body:
## Qué cambia

El paso «Auditar el lockfile completo» de `devsecops.yml` pasa de `--audit-level high` a `--audit-level low`.

## Por qué

`SECURITY-MAINTENANCE.md` declara como evidencia exigida antes de integrar:

> `pnpm audit --audit-level low` sin avisos conocidos

pero el workflow solo bloqueaba en alto o crítico. Un aviso bajo o moderado podía entrar en `main` sin que CI dijera nada, contradiciendo la evidencia publicada en el propio repositorio.

## Validación

- YAML válido; el job `quality` conserva sus 8 pasos y el último ejecuta el comando nuevo.
- `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` sobre `main` ya fusionado.
- `pnpm audit` limpio **en todos los niveles de severidad**, no solo en `low`.

El cambio no introduce deuda: fija el listón donde ya está el árbol de dependencias tras el override de `sharp` y `js-yaml` de #52.

## Consecuencia a tener en cuenta

CI se vuelve más estricto. A partir de aquí, cualquier aviso bajo o moderado en el lockfile completo rompe el build, incluidos los que no tengan parche publicado. Es justo lo que pide la documentación, pero conviene saberlo: cuando un padre fija por rango una versión vulnerable, Dependabot cierra el aviso como `security_update_not_possible` y hay que forzar la arista a mano con `overrides` en `app/pnpm-workspace.yaml`, como ya se hizo con `esbuild`, `fast-uri`, `sharp` y `js-yaml`.

Si se prefiere el punto medio, la alternativa es `--audit-level moderate`, y entonces lo que habría que ajustar es la línea de `SECURITY-MAINTENANCE.md` en lugar del workflow.

## Fuera de alcance

El job `dependency-review` sigue con `fail-on-severity: high`. La documentación solo pide «Dependency Review aprobado» sin fijar severidad, así que ahí no hay contradicción que resolver, pero los dos controles de dependencias quedan bloqueando en umbrales distintos por si se quiere igualarlos en un cambio aparte.

author: sitaramakumar
body:
## Summary
- `JwtValidator` built its HMAC signing key directly from `jwt.secret` with no length check. JJWT enforces RFC 7518 §3.2 (HMAC-SHA keys must be ≥256 bits) and throws `WeakKeyException` from a static initializer for any shorter secret, which surfaces as an opaque `ExceptionInInitializerError` on first use. Reproduced this against the real dependency classpath before fixing it: wrapped key construction so an undersized secret fails fast with a message naming the actual byte/bit length and how to fix it, and bumped the shipped dev secret to 42 bytes.
- `extractRole()` checked the `clientId` heuristic before the token's own `role` claim. A token issued with `role=ADMIN` for a clientId that doesn't contain "admin"/"write" (e.g. a service account) silently resolved to `READ` instead of the role it was actually issued with. Reordered so the explicit claim wins, falling back to the clientId heuristic only when a token carries no role claim at all.
- `UserRole.allows(null)` threw `NullPointerException` instead of denying access.
- Added a `JWT_SECRET` environment-variable override in `AppConfig` — the new weak-key error message tells callers to use it, so it needed to actually exist.
- Three source files (`JwtValidator.java`, `SharePointClient.java`, `VaultService.java`) carried a leading UTF-8 BOM, which made `mvn test` fail with `illegal character: '﻿'` before any test could even compile. Confirmed this was pre-existing on `main` (not introduced by this change) by stashing these edits and re-running the build against an unmodified checkout. Stripped the BOM from all three.
- Added `.gitignore` for `target/`, since none existed.

## Test plan
- [x] `mvn test` — 25/25 tests pass (previously: build didn't compile at all)
- [x] New `JwtValidatorTest`: round-trip generate/validate, `Bearer `-prefix stripping, missing-token rejection, cross-key signature rejection, and three `extractRole` cases (explicit claim wins, clientId fallback, default-to-READ)
- [x] New `UserRoleTest`: role×method allow/deny matrix, case-insensitivity, null-method handling, `fromClientId` heuristic
- [x] New `AppConfigTest`: properties-file fallback, default fallback, env-var-name conversion

author: stoyoda0012-cyber
body:
Adds `toyomacro.voigtfit.identifiability` (experimental): diagnostics for how well a counting spectrum determines the Gaussian and the Lorentzian width of a Voigt peak. No existing solver default and no existing public API changes; the edits to existing modules are docstrings and comments.

### What it separates

The two widths are hard to tell apart for reasons of different kinds, and the module reports them apart:

1. **A degenerate coordinate.** The profile depends on σ only through v = σ², so `I_σσ ∝ σ²`. Working in v removes this; the Fisher matrix is regular at σ = 0.
2. **Precision of a small component.** `sd(σ)/σ = ½ sd(v)/v`: a finite bound on v is still an unbounded relative error on a vanishing Gaussian component.
3. **A boundary** at v = 0 (or at a calibrated instrument variance), where the inverse Fisher matrix is not the variance of a constrained estimator.
4. **A finite window** and 5. **a background** — practical weak identification, not structural non-identifiability.

### What is in it

- `voigt_derivatives`: derivatives in (center, variance, γ), accurate down to and including v = 0. Points with |z| ≥ 7 use a 24-term large-|z| expansion, the rest the Faddeeva closed form. Worst measured error 3×10⁻¹¹ over σ/γ = 0.01…10 against an independent quadrature. The expansion is asymptotic; the limit on its term count is stated and asserted.
- `poisson_fisher`: Poisson Fisher matrix with a background that is absent, known or estimated (constant, linear, Shirley-type step of fixed shape). Width coordinates `sigma_gamma`, `var_gamma`, `fwhm_shape`, `pvoigt`, `fixed_instrument` (optionally with a calibrated instrument variance as the floor).
- `effective_information`: what is left for the widths once everything else is estimated, next to the sub-block that assumes it known.
- `assess_identifiability`: `rank_deficient` / `weakly_identified` / `identified` against stated reference scales, plus an independent `near_boundary` flag. Invariant under a change of energy unit (tested).
- `scan_identifiability`: the same over window, intensity, shape, background and peak spacing, in both coordinates.
- `examples/07_width_identifiability_map.py`, design record `docs/design/voigt-width-identifiability.md`, `docs/API.md` (Experimental tier), `CHANGELOG.md`.

These are **bounds computed from a model, not confidence intervals and not statements about a fit.** The defaults (a tenth of the FWHM; three bounds from the boundary) are conventions, and the docs say so.

### Also in this branch

- The Voigt FWHM expression `0.5346 f_L + √(0.2166 f_L² + f_G²)` was credited to Thompson et al. (1987) in six places; it is Olivero & Longbothum (1977), the simpler of their two fits. Its accuracy claim ("within 0.02 %") is replaced by the stated ~0.02 % plus the measured maximum 2.37×10⁻⁴, which Wang et al. (2022) also report.
- `tests/README.md` rows and totals for the two new test files.

### Verification

- 108 + 6 new tests, including a Monte Carlo check against exact constrained Poisson maximum likelihood (10⁴ simulated spectra; replica sd within 2 % of the bound in the interior; the distribution near the boundary is recorded, not judged). The fitter is a test helper, not shipped.
- Mutation-tested: every injected defect listed in the commit messages fails a test.
- Independent audit, two rounds (AGENTS.md roles): one Major in round 1 — an information share quoted from the raw (eV², eV) eigenvalue, which depends on the energy unit — fixed and pinned unit-free; round 2 release-ready, its four Minor findings fixed. The audit could not run Linux, so CI on this PR is the remaining check.
- Rebased onto `946d25f`; the example was renumbered 05 → 07 because main took 05 and 06 meanwhile.

Commits are kept separate on purpose (design decisions and the two audit rounds are part of the record). Please merge without squashing.

author: speedyhkjournalist
body:
## Integration status

PR #41 has now been merged into `ir` (merge commit `fa933bfbe0da4a2f4b4057315d2c7f2d047a09e7`). This PR remains targeted directly at `ir`.

The current head is mergeable against the updated `ir` branch. Relative to current `ir`, the change is limited to the fast-admission implementation, its counters/tests, the performance-smoke counters, and `docs/ir13-tuning.md`; the already-merged IR-13 acceptance work is no longer part of the effective diff.

## Diagnostic trigger

IR-core #340's same-core cold/warm smoke exposed a large synthetic hot-loop gap. The tiny `INC/JMP-back` case reached IR Tier 1/2 correctly, but IR paid roughly 799k cache admissions in the short window.

Code inspection showed that every IR cache hit performed full read-only `capture()` validation before activation and again after the architectural initial fetch. That repeatedly allocates/copies source snapshots and re-observes page tables even when the CPU-visible TLB mapping is already unchanged.

This is diagnostic input, not an application performance claim.

## Change

Add a three-state cached admission validator:

- `Match`: all saved linear->physical mappings equal current CPU-visible cached translations and physical RAM source bytes still match exactly.
- `Unavailable`: a source page is not yet cached. Pre-fetch lookup falls back to the existing read-only capture; post-fetch admission simply declines without retiring the entry.
- `Stale`: generation/mapping/source bytes differ; retire the entry.

The hot path therefore avoids snapshot allocation/page-table re-walk while still comparing authoritative physical source bytes, preserving detection of raw/unnotified SMC.

## Safety boundaries retained

- reserve/validate/finish publication still use full capture;
- link discovery still uses full capture and does not depend on cached-TLB visibility;
- architectural initial fetch/A-bit behavior remains unchanged;
- cold cross-page regions still wait for CPU-visible translations;
- dirty/reset/restore, slot ownership and active-frame reclamation are unchanged;
- execution budgets/device scheduling are unchanged.

## Evidence added

- `ir_cache_stat(8)`: cached mapping/source checks
- `ir_cache_stat(9)`: pre-fetch capture fallbacks
- cache differential requires a warmed one-page second hit to increase cached checks without increasing capture fallbacks
- IR-13 performance smoke records both counters

See `docs/ir13-tuning.md`.

This PR does not claim IR-13 completion, XP/application speedup, or readiness for IR-14.

## Validation after the IR-13 gate

The implementation head `e2b56cf2b4bad0e883ffa1f7ed451cab8ac8daaf` completed IR-core successfully, including native regressions, executable Wasm/decoder oracles, LICM/CFG/FLAGS/IR-10/forwarding/SIMD/store regressions, the complete IR-12 lifecycle matrix, the IR-13 host/browser/device acceptance smoke, and generated-source/whitespace checks. The current head only adds the resulting diagnostic numbers to documentation; its checks should be used as the final merge gate.

The green run's same-core smoke measured IR at about 454.5k instruction-counter steps/ms versus about 1.445M for the paired legacy policy, with 3,769,246 cached checks and zero full-capture fallbacks in the warmed case. This is diagnostic hosted-runner evidence, not an application speed claim.

The generic repository CI still stops on the repository-wide ESLint/rustfmt checks after debug/release/fallback and graphics-host builds pass. Those generic failures are not used here as evidence of an IR regression; IR-core is green.

IR-13 remains incomplete after this PR: XP/application acceptance, controlled workload benchmarks, remaining ISA/Tier-1 backfills and further end-to-end tuning are still required before IR-14.

author: pazdak
body:
## Description

Closes #565.

The second and last PR of the plan recorded on #565 (comment of 2026-09-19). PR #579 gave
the sweep chain names that say which half is Jamf's; PR #584 (#583) re-pointed the six
heaviest test modules at `run_enabled_collections`. This removes what the renames were
working around.

`sync_connection` was a fourteen-line forward in `backend/app/mdm/service.py` whose body was
one call, with a function-local import to defeat the `service` ↔ `collections` cycle. It is
gone, and with it the local import. The twelve remaining test modules and the manual-sync
caller in `backend/app/api/connections.py` call `run_enabled_collections` directly — the name
that owns the job. `git grep sync_connection` over the whole repo now prints nothing.

The cold trace of 2026-09-18 read five near-synonyms to learn which one opens the HTTP
client. It is now four, and `app/mdm/service.py` no longer imports `app/mdm/collections.py`
at all: the dependency runs one way, `collections` → `service`, which is the shape Addigy's
sibling (`sweep_addigy_connection`, `_stream_addigy_fleet`) will be written against.

No behaviour change.

## Scope

**Includes**

- The twelve test modules `git grep -l sync_connection -- backend/tests` still listed:
  `test_patch_matching_db`, `test_ea_census_db`, `test_device_platform_db`, `test_catalog_db`,
  `test_wire_casing`, `test_outbox_passes_db`, `test_hec_fanout_db`, `test_re_emit_db`,
  `test_device_observation_db`, `test_credential_refusal_db`, `test_collections`,
  `test_hec_fanout` — the same mechanical rewrite #583 made: the function-local
  `from app.mdm.service import sync_connection` becomes
  `from app.mdm.collections import run_enabled_collections`, and the call takes the new name.
- `run_enabled_collections` requires `trigger` where `sync_connection` defaulted it to
  `TRIGGER_SWEEP`, so the 26 calls that relied on that default now name it, and nine modules
  gain a module-level `from app.core.runs import TRIGGER_SWEEP` — the placement and the
  `# noqa: E402` on modules whose import block sits after `pytestmark` both copy PR #584.
  `test_wire_casing` and `test_credential_refusal_db` already had it in local scope and gained
  no import.
- `backend/app/api/connections.py`: `run_enabled_collections` is imported at **module level**,
  added to the existing `from app.mdm.collections import ensure_default_collections` line.
  **No cycle to keep it function-local for** — this module already imported
  `app.mdm.collections` at module level for `ensure_default_collections`, so the name comes
  from a module that was already loaded there. `sync_connection` leaves the
  `from app.mdm.service import ...` line, which still carries `set_sync_status` and
  `sync_result_kwargs`.
- `backend/app/mdm/service.py`: the function and its local import deleted; the docstring on
  `sweep_jamf_connection` that read "Like sync_connection, this reports a failure rather than
  raising" now states that contract on its own.
- `backend/app/mdm/collections.py`: the connection-level half of the deleted docstring — that
  a failure comes back as a result rather than an exception, so one expired credential cannot
  abort a sweep across several tenants — moves onto `run_enabled_collections`, which owns that
  contract now. This is the only prose added; deleting the forward would otherwise have
  dropped it.

**Deliberately leaves out**

- The three "sweep" enums (`core/runs.py:58`, `:75`, `core/scheduling.py:21`). #565 rules them
  stored and wire values that stay as they are.
- Any rename. All four landed in PR #579; nothing in the chain is renamed here.
- Any new section in `docs/troubleshooting.md`. This adds no failure path — it deletes a
  forward whose callers now call its target with the arguments it was passing. No terminal
  state, log line or error string changes, so there is nothing for an operator to step
  through that is not already written. README's ordered-paths sentence is untouched.
- `docs/` needed no edit: `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` §7 already names `sweep_jamf_connection` and
  `_stream_jamf_fleet` from PR #579, and no doc mentioned `sync_connection`.

## Validation

**Full backend suite, once, in the uv container** (no uv on the host), from the worktree root
`/…/.claude/worktrees/inspect-0565-sync-connection-goes`, against `loon-test-db` on
`loon-test-net`, database `looninspect_test_v0565`, `RUN_DB_TESTS=1`:

```
docker run --rm --user root --network loon-test-net -v "$PWD":/repo -w /repo/backend \
  -v loon-test-venv-v0565:/venv -e UV_PROJECT_ENVIRONMENT=/venv/env -e UV_CACHE_DIR=/venv/cache \
  -e RUN_DB_TESTS=1 -e DATABASE_URL=postgresql+asyncpg://…@loon-test-db:5432/looninspect_test_v0565 \
  -e ENCRYPTION_KEY="$ENC" ghcr.io/astral-sh/uv:python3.12-alpine \
  sh -c 'uv sync --frozen && uv run --frozen ruff check . && uv run --frozen ruff format --check . \
         && uv run --frozen pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider'
```

Result: **2585 passed, 68 skipped, 3 warnings in 56.44s**, exit 0. `ruff check` clean;
`ruff format --check` — 285 files already formatted. The three warnings are pre-existing
Starlette deprecations, unrelated to this diff.

An earlier `ruff check` run flagged four `I001` import-ordering errors — `app.mdm.collections`
sorts differently from `app.mdm.service` in four function-local import blocks. Fixed with
`ruff check --fix` (it also merged `test_collections.py`'s two `app.mdm.collections` local
imports into one line), then the full run above was made on the fixed tree.

Every one of the twelve modules' tests ran under `RUN_DB_TESTS=1`, including the
statement-count tests in `test_sweep_costs_db.py` that #565 names as the sharp edge — those
are in #583's half and were unchanged here, and are green.

Checks performed by hand, on the branch:

- `git grep -n sync_connection` over the whole repo — no output, exit 1. Includes `docs/`,
  `frontend/` and `README.md`; no stray mention needed fixing.
- No function-local import remains in `backend/app/mdm/service.py` (`grep -n "^\s\+\(from\|import\) "`
  matches only two docstring lines that begin with the word "from").
- `backend/app/mdm/service.py` no longer imports `app.mdm.collections` in any form; the two
  remaining occurrences of that string are prose in a docstring and a comment.
- Changed-line count, the measurement PR-01 makes:
  `git diff --numstat origin/main...HEAD -- . ':!**/uv.lock' ':!**/package-lock.json' ':!backend/migrations/versions/*'`
  → **133** (64 added, 69 deleted), limit 400.

**Not run:** the frontend lane (`npm ci`, `tsc -b --noEmit`, `eslint`, `npm test`,
`npm run build`) — no file under `frontend/` is in this diff. No Alembic migration was added,
so no `alembic heads` check. No deploy, no pod refresh, and the app was not exercised by hand:
this diff changes no runtime behaviour, and the manual-sync path it touches
(`_run_connection_sync`) is covered by the suite.

## Risk

Low, and confined to import structure.

- **Compatibility:** `sync_connection` was internal — not exported in `service.py`'s `__all__`
  (which lists only `TRIGGER_MANUAL`, `TRIGGER_SWEEP`, `TRIGGER_WEBHOOK`), not reachable from
  any route, and its only non-test caller was `_run_connection_sync` in this repo. Nothing
  outside the repo can be holding the name.
- **The one behavioural edge, and why it is closed:** the forward defaulted `trigger` to
  `TRIGGER_SWEEP`; `run_enabled_collections` requires it. A missed call site would be a
  `TypeError` at call time, not a silent wrong trigger — and a wrong `trigger` would land in
  `runs.trigger` and on the wire. Every call site was converted and the full suite exercises
  them; the one caller that already passed a trigger (`TRIGGER_MANUAL`, in
  `_run_connection_sync`) keeps it verbatim.
- **Wire vocabulary / schema:** untouched. No event shape, no key, no enum value changes;
  `docs/splunk-wire-vocabulary.md` needed no edit.
- **Data / migration:** none. No model, no Alembic revision.
- **Security:** none. No credenti

author: broccolito
body:
## The bug

`biorouter.exe` overflows its stack on **every** invocation on Windows. Not a particular subcommand — `--version` and `--help` die too:

```
thread 'main' has overflowed its stack
```

## Why the existing guard didn't cover it

`build_agent_runtime` already sizes the runtime's **worker** threads to 16 MiB, and that fixed the subagent SIGABRT it was written for. It can't help here: `block_on` drives the future on the **calling** thread, and for both `biorouter` and `biorouterd` that's the process's main thread.

> ⚠️ On Windows the main thread's stack is fixed in the executable header (`SizeOfStackReserve`, 1 MiB by default) — no runtime setting can reach it. Linux and macOS give 8 MiB, which is why this was invisible everywhere else.

And why it stayed invisible: **the test beside `build_agent_runtime` is `#[cfg(unix)]`**, so this platform had no coverage at all.

The CLI's `async_main` future is large enough on its own to blow 1 MiB the moment it's materialised — which is why even `--version` fails. The overflow happens before any argument is parsed.

## Diagnosis was measured, not inferred

The same debug binary with `editbin /STACK:16777216` applied printed its version and ran `session list` correctly. So it's purely stack **reservation**, not runaway recursion.

## The fix

`run_on_agent_stack` runs the host body on a thread carrying `worker_stack_size()` — the same 16 MiB, the same `BIOROUTER_WORKER_STACK_SIZE` escape hatch. Both binaries use it. `biorouterd` shares the shape even though its own `block_on` future is smaller, because the hazard is identical and the fix costs nothing.

A thread beats a `/STACK` linker flag: no per-target `rustflags`, identical across toolchains and cross-builds, and the size plus its override stay in one place instead of two. A panic in the body is re-raised with `resume_unwind` rather than converted to an error, so panic output and exit behaviour are unchanged.

> ⚠️ **Applied unconditionally, debug and release alike.** Whether a release build also overflowed was never determined, and deliberately so: the fix is free (reserved address space, committed lazily), and a guard that applies only to the configuration where the bug was *observed* is exactly how the unix-only test above came to miss Windows entirely.

## Verification (run on Windows)

| check | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `biorouter.exe --version` | 🔴 stack overflow | ✅ `1.90.5` |
| `biorouter.exe --help` | 🔴 stack overflow | ✅ |
| `biorouter.exe session list` | 🔴 stack overflow | ✅ lists sessions |
| `biorouterd.exe --version` | ✅ | ✅ (unchanged) |

| suite | result |
|---|---|
| `cargo test -p biorouter-cli --lib` | **478 passed, 0 failed** |
| `cargo test -p biorouter --lib -- execution::runtime` | **4 passed** |

New coverage: a Windows stack probe (`GetCurrentThreadStackLimits`) mirroring the unix one, so the assertion runs on **both** platforms — with the same negative control the existing test uses, asserting a default thread is *smaller* than the target first, or it couldn't tell a sized thread from an unsized one. Plus a value round-trip and a panic-propagation case.

body:
Three steps toward Nicholas's Blender render of the Aramon lodestone, on the engine side.

Light glances off a smooth surface along its silhouette. The PBR shader adds the Schlick fraction, faded out as roughness rises, so his glass crystal and any polished metal catch the sky at their edges while stone stays stone.

A material whose name has glow or pulse in it breathes: its emission rises and falls over about two seconds on a clock the view sets each frame. That is the living light in a lodestone, which he asked how to animate, with no animation data at all.

Blender writes an object's custom properties into its node's extras and has no way to write the root's, so tak_scale is read from a node when the root has none. He sets one property on the base object and leaves the model at its Blender size.

Cases cover the node level scale with the root winning when both say, and the glow flag on a material's name. The rest of what his render has and ours does not is on the artist's side and is written up for him: bake the procedural bricks to textures, a brighter base and an emissive gradient for the crystal.

body:
The /t/file/upload endpoint returned a 500 Internal Server Error with a
plain-text body whenever ParseMultipartForm failed — for example when an agent
POSTed with application/x-www-form-urlencoded or when a human submitted the
form without selecting a file. The error was not distinguishable from
unexpected server failures, and screen-reader users received no announcement
of the validation failure.

A new uploadError() method renders the full files list page at status 400 with
a danger alert banner (role="alert") and an aria-live region so assistive
technology announces the error. ParseMultipartForm failures are classified as
"please select a file", oversized uploads get their own message, and the
original upload form is re-rendered for immediate retry. Two tests cover wrong
Content-Type and missing-file paths.

The chat composer's s.fail() path still delivers plain-text errors when
ParseMultipartForm fails — this is consistent with the pre-change behaviour
and out of scope. The string-matching check for "multipart" in the error
message is a known fragility against future Go stdlib changes; it can be
removed once only http.ErrNotMultipart needs covering (backlog item filed).

author: streamentry
body:
## What changed?

Implements **spec 12 — workflow pack** as `lumi-packs`, the reusable-automation layer that workflow mode runs on:

- **Pack manifest (§12.2/§12.4)**: pack_id, semantic version, owner, hardening status (`EXPERIMENTAL → ALPHA → CERTIFIED → DEPRECATED` with ordering; certification demands a real compatibility matrix), runtime range, supported OS/apps, required connectors, required model capabilities, privacy classification, default budgets.
- **Schema-defined I/O (§12.5)**: required/optional typed fields; missing required fields or type mismatches **fail before any execution**.
- **Steps (§12.6)**: id, purpose, capability, operation, preferred tier + allowed fallback tiers, risk class, approval rule (Always/PerPolicy), pre/postconditions, retry+idempotency metadata, evidence requirements, resource/target templates, exception route.
- **Exception routes (§12.7)**: explicit canonical-category triggers routed to user/approver/specialist/alternate-executor/retry/stop with human guidance text.
- **Compatibility matrix (§12.8)**: concrete runtime/OS/app/connector versions — no generic "supported" claims.
- **Economics baseline (§12.9)**: manual/residual minutes, runs/month, labor cost, variable cost, implementation hours, payback hypothesis — feeding the spec 16 economics engine.
- **Isolation (§12.13)**: steps carry argument **templates** with `$input.<path>` references (type-preserving whole-leaf substitution plus inline string interpolation), resolved at run time from schema-validated inputs. Customer data structurally cannot be embedded in a pack; credentials stay SecretRefs.
- **Runner**: `prepare_run()` validates pack + inputs, then materializes one `ActionProposal` per step with workflow/step correlation and idempotency — packs execute through the **same** policy → approval → journal → verifier → audit gate as everything else (no parallel authority path).

## Evidence (spec 12.14 certification fixtures)

A realistic 3-step quote-followup pack (CRM read → draft → approved send) driven through the orchestrator covers: structural validation (duplicate ids, certified-without-matrix, consequential-step-without-postconditions all fail), missing-input rejection, template resolution incl. inline interpolation, the happy path (2 ungated steps + approval-gated send with journal-verified single send carrying pack idempotency), connector failure mapping to the step's declared Retry route, ambiguous send surfacing to the User route with an unresolved journal record (no blind re-send), and verifier failure marking the step not-verified.

33 test suites workspace-wide; clippy clean at `-D warnings`; hermetic and deterministic.

## Release impact

None: no packaging/signing/updater/permissions changes.

author: magicsih
body:
## 문제

`Podfile.lock`의 `COCOAPODS:` 줄이 **빌드하는 사람에 따라 뒤집히고** 있었습니다.

| 경로 | CocoaPods |
|---|---|
| `pod install` (brew / rbenv shim) | 1.16.2 — 저장소에 커밋된 값 |
| `bundle exec pod install` | **1.15.2** |

`Gemfile.lock`이 `xcodeproj < 1.26.0` 제약 때문에 cocoapods 1.15.2에 묶여 있고, Xcode Cloud(`ci_post_clone.sh`)는 `brew install cocoapods`로 받은 판을 씁니다.

실제로 이 차이를 모른 채 `bundle exec`로 만든 archive가 심사에 올라갔습니다. `use_frameworks! :linkage => :static`에 RNFB 계열만 static library로 강제하는 구성이라 링키지가 민감하고, 도구 버전이 환경마다 다르면 재현되지 않는 빌드 차이가 생깁니다.

## 변경 범위

`apps/mobile/Gemfile`에 주석 13줄. **코드 동작은 바뀌지 않습니다.**

설치 경로를 brew 하나로 두고, 왜 이 Gemfile로 Pods를 설치하면 안 되는지를 그 파일에 적었습니다. 함정에 다시 빠지지 않게 하는 것이 목적입니다.

## 검토한 대안

**Gemfile.lock을 올려 맞추기** — 시도했지만 해결되지 않습니다.

```
$ bundle update cocoapods
Bundler attempted to update cocoapods but its version stayed the same
```

`xcodeproj < 1.26.0`이 막고 있습니다. 그 제약을 풀면 cocoapods가 **1.17.0**으로 올라가 brew 판(1.16.2)보다 앞서서 불일치가 그대로 남습니다. 정확한 버전을 핀해도 brew가 올라가면 다시 어긋납니다.

**Xcode Cloud를 bundler로 전환** — 리뷰에서 지적된 대로 막혀 있습니다. `Gemfile.lock`의 `BUNDLED WITH`가 **4.0.6**인데 macOS 기본 Ruby는 **2.6.10 / bundler 1.17.2**입니다. Ruby까지 별도 설치해야 하고, 그 경로는 Xcode Cloud에서 검증할 수 없습니다.

두 경로를 유지하면서 버전을 맞추는 방법이 없으므로, 경로를 하나로 두는 편이 단순합니다.

## 검증 결과

`pod install`(brew 1.16.2) 실행 후 `Podfile.lock`이 그대로 유지되고 작업 트리가 깨끗한 것을 확인했습니다.

```
$ pod install
Pod installation complete! There are 84 dependencies from the Podfile and 101 total pods installed.
$ tail -2 Podfile.lock
COCOAPODS: 1.16.2
$ git status --porcelain
(비어 있음)
```

즉 저장소는 원래 일관돼 있었고, `bundle exec`를 쓴 것이 원인이었습니다.

## 후속

`xcodeproj < 1.26.0` 제약은 초기 커밋(1e60095)부터 있었고 이유가 기록돼 있지 않습니다. CocoaPods 업그레이드가 필요해지면 그 근거부터 확인해야 합니다. 이 PR에서는 다루지 않습니다.

author: docalencar
body:
## Purpose

Governed Review promotion tooling for **exactly one migration**: `0133`. This PR
publishes the tooling only — Review is not contacted, no credential is read, and
0133 is **not applied anywhere**. Promotion itself is a separate, later gate.

The governance rule this follows: mutation-capable Review tooling is versioned,
reviewed and merged to canonical main *before* it is ever handed a credential.
The runner enforces that on itself — it refuses to run unless its own three files
hash-match `origin/main`, and that check happens before it reads the Keychain.

## Target

| | |
|---|---|
| Migration | `supabase/migrations/0133_create_development_plan_origin_read_boundary.sql` |
| Migration SHA256 | `2791febff1b790712ffe60f13cf9e8227427c498b8310fcaf2f91977899509eb` |
| Source commit | `ef36ac130c8b655e0635102a9a6d89c45e483b4b` |
| Review ref | `rwfvxvbzaosgcyfxdjpt` |

The mutation identity is the **pair** (source commit, migration SHA256). A
filename is not an identity, so the hash is recomputed before the push and again
at TOCTOU; either half changing means this is a different operation needing
re-governance.

## Files

- `promote-d-r2-development-origin.sh` — single-attempt promotion runner
- `verify-d-r2-development-origin-pre.sh` — read-only PRE inventory
- `verify-d-r2-development-origin-post.sh` — read-only POST verifier
- `run-d-r2-local-db-gate.sh` — local real-PostgreSQL tooling gate
- `promotion-tooling-guards-d-r2.test.mjs` — structural guards (19 tests)

## Safety

**PRE** proves the target is canonical Review (not loopback, migration ledger
present, four Supabase roles), that history through 0132 matches the repository
exactly, that 0133 is absent — by **name count**, not one signature lookup, so an
unexpected overload cannot make the ledger misleading — that no partial artifact
exists, that D-DB1 is in place, and that retention is healthy.

**TOCTOU** re-takes the entire PRE snapshot and compares it byte for byte, then
re-checks the migration hash and that HEAD still equals `origin/main`. A dry run
must show exactly `0133` pending and nothing else.

**One mutation.** Exactly one invocation site, two transports, both
non-interactive. A nonzero exit is `UNKNOWN_REMOTE_OUTCOME`, never `FAILED`: the
statement may have reached the server before the transport died. The runner stops
with exit 2 and directs the operator to the **read-only** POST verifier. It never
retries, never falls back, and never executes SQL of its own to finish the job.
If POST then shows part of the target state, that is `PARTIAL_REMOTE_APPLICATION`
and needs its own adjudicated plan.

**POST** reads properties from the catalog rather than matching text: exactly one
function of that name, the canonical signature, `SECURITY DEFINER`, `stable`,
`search_path=public, pg_temp`, expected owner, EXECUTE to `authenticated` only
with zero grants to PUBLIC/anon/service_role, the exact five-column return shape,
zero template-table dependency, and an overload probe that excludes the signature
it approves. Two behavioral probes confirm anon is refused at the privilege
boundary and an identityless authenticated call is refused by the boundary's own
`AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED` rather than leaking rows.

## Local real-PostgreSQL tooling gate — PASS

Structural guards pattern-match; they cannot find a planner error. This repository
has paid for that twice — a `"char"` concatenation of `provolatile` in the 0127
verifier and a FILTER on a non-aggregate in the 0128 runner — and both times the
first real reader of the SQL was canonical Review.

`run-d-r2-local-db-gate.sh` closes that gap. Because `supabase db reset` applies
every migration including 0133, a reset database is never the pre-migration state,
so the gate **constructs** it: reset, remove 0133's own artifacts, run the real PRE
snapshot against a real server, apply the canonical migration file verbatim, then
run the real POST verifier with the PRE fingerprints handed over exactly as the
promotion runner hands them over. It is loopback-only and asserts so.

Authoritative run:

```
D_R2_LOCAL_GATE=PASS
DB_RESET=PASS
PRE_SNAPSHOT=PASS
PRE_CONTRACT=PASS
READ_ONLY_PROOF=PASS
MIGRATION_APPLIES=PASS
POST_SNAPSHOT=PASS
D_R2_POST=PASS
MIGRATION_0133_SHA256=2791febff1b790712ffe60f13cf9e8227427c498b8310fcaf2f91977899509eb
REVIEW_ACCESSED=NO
REVIEW_DB_0133=NOT_APPLIED
```

`READ_ONLY_PROOF=PASS` means `transaction_read_only=on` measured in the verifier's
own context and a mutation refused there with **SQLSTATE 25006**. The real POST
verifier returned the canonical shape:

```
ORIGIN_RESULT=TABLE(plan_id uuid, template_id uuid, template_version_id uuid, template_name text, template_version_number integer)
ORIGIN_ARGUMENTS=p_company_id uuid, p_plan_id uuid DEFAULT NULL::uuid
ANON_ORIGIN_RPC=DENIED
AUTHENTICATED_ORIGIN_RPC=AUTHENTICATION_REQUIRED
```

## Harness defect history — kept, not tidied away

The **first** Mac run failed one property: `read-only transaction accepted a write`.
Investigation proved two independent defects, both in the local probe:

1. it opened a **new psql connection**, so it was not measuring the PRE verifier's
   session at all;
2. it used `psql -c "set default_transaction_read_only = on; create table ..."`,
   which psql sends as one simple query in one implicit transaction. That GUC sets
   the default for transactions started *afterwards*; the in-flight transaction's
   read-only flag was already fixed at start, from `off`. The write was always
   accepted, so the probe could never have passed on any database.

The PRE verifier never had that problem — it feeds psql from **stdin**, where each
statement gets its own transaction and inherits the read-only default.

Classified **HARNESS_DEFECT**. Not a migration, security-contract, D-DB2 or Review
defect. Migration 0133 was not touched, and the three production scripts
(`promote`, `pre`, `post`) are byte-identical across the two commits. The fix is a
separate commit (`33b2d3f`) and the second Mac run is the authoritative PASS.

## Privacy finding — unchanged, follow-up still required

The pre-existing tenant-wide visibility of the application ledger to authenticated
members remains **OPEN**. D-R2 does not touch lineage or snapshot grants, RLS,
policies or retention. PRE fingerprints all of them and POST fails if any moved —
widening *or* hardening. Repair belongs to its own adjudicated slice, not to a
promotion runner.

## Environments

Review not accessed · 0133 **not applied** to Review · Production not accessed ·
Legacy not accessed · no hosted run.

## Summary
Two A/C-class product bugs found by the 2026-09-19 overnight QA campaign (real learner-style journeys on Production dogfood + local repro), fixed locally, then challenge-reviewed and closed by a V2 release-closure pass. Full campaign ledger in the worktree PROGRESS.md; durable evidence in TEST_REPORT.md (2026-09-19 section).

## Bugs fixed
1. **Player kept playing the sample video** when a new video was loaded during YT-iframe-API init (`YouTubeEmbed.tsx`) — the pending switch was dropped forever, so every seek/replay/active-line sync silently ran against the wrong video. Fix: `status` joins the switch-effect deps. Reproduced in Production dogfood and deterministically; 4-test regression suite incl. no-cue-loop / startSeconds / benign initial re-cue invariants.
2. **Unverified account could never sign out** (`AuthContext.tsx`) — the sync-before-logout guard is unsatisfiable for unverified accounts, deadlocking behind "Reconnect and try again.". Fix: guard gated on `emailVerified`; the account-boundary data wipe is unconditional again. The intermediate keep-data variant was **falsified as a cross-account leak** by test A2 (the next verified login's auto-sync would merge the previous account's items into its cloud).

## Bounded UX/a11y
i18n for sentence-jump/bookmark labels (hardcoded English in the Chinese UI), mobile bookmark accessible name, transient-Analyze fallback copy now suggests retry.

- vitest 659/659 (64 files; +11 tests), tsc clean, eslint 0 errors, build OK

- Zero intentional paid calls (Supadata/Groq/ASR: 0 in this branch's validation)

PROGRESS snapshot (2026-09-19), TEST_REPORT dated section, DECISIONS entries — including the corrected Supadata cost claim (2 proven credits; the earlier "every load re-burns" hypothesis withdrawn) and the hardcoded-provider-badge fact.

author: zbennett10
body:
The unit's script keeps piece state by the shipped model's node order, and an artist's model has its own pieces and its own count, so it drew at rest. The store now maps each artist node to the shipped node of the same name once, when the model is built, and the draw takes each piece's state through the map. A node named like a shipped piece turns, moves, hides and shows as that piece does; one with a name of its own stands still.

This is how the original animates everything, and it is the right seam for custom models: the lodestone's light is aralode and aralode_off shown in turn, so a model with objects of those names blinks as the original does, and a Veruna ship with Oar1 to Oar6 rows to the same nine keyframes the script has always played. No animation data in the file, nothing to sync to the simulation.

Cases: the pure name map on hand meshes, and against the real lodestone through the store, where an artist's model whose one piece is named ARALODE_OFF takes that shipped piece's slot and one named spire takes none.

docs/CUSTOM_MODELS.md replaces "what is not there yet" with how to name and pivot pieces so they follow.

author: effortlesssteven
body:
## Post-merge disposition

> [!CAUTION]
> **Merged at `89d1376390726a34ae8b2cac14f69af7e684153d`, but not accepted as completed remotely durable checkpointing.**
>
> The merged head `3d9a0cd80c6cd576b9ffb14c5b038c21f199cdb3` is retained on `main` as a useful synthetic contract and journal-gate hardening slice. Its terminal CI demonstrates the current in-memory/synthetic denominator only. It does not satisfy the provider-backed acceptance criteria in #3922, and #3922 has been reopened.

```text
original base:       4d1b0fe10e82f506424f9dc7b7ff3bf81403191b
merged head:         3d9a0cd80c6cd576b9ffb14c5b038c21f199cdb3
merge commit:        89d1376390726a34ae8b2cac14f69af7e684153d
blocking exact-head review retained: 5254260221
ordinary synthetic CI: 35417218077 — success
UB Review wrapper:     35417218068 — success
owner issue:           #3922 — reopened / P0 / release blocker
```

## What the merge validly contributes

- canonical immutable `Missing`/no-readback checkpoint bytes;
- opaque runtime readback witnesses for progress gates;
- exact canonical payload-byte comparison in the synthetic model;
- verified journal chain/header/row/event/state gates;
- stable checkpoint-link digests;
- duplicate-selection rejection;
- replay-consumption rules;
- monotonic incident and first-irreversible-row posture;
- source-controlled schemas, documentation, tests, policy and evidence records;
- zero real provider, registry, credential, tag, package, release or live-setting mutation.

These are useful foundations. They do not establish a wireable GitHub Actions Artifact protocol.

## Remaining P0 provider contract

1. **Verified predecessor authority.** Sequence extension still accepts a public/deserializable predecessor whose fields say `readback = Complete`; it does not consume the opaque exact-byte witness. A self-edited serialized predecessor can therefore manufacture later checkpoint authority.
2. **Payload / provider receipt / readback split.** The bytes that must exist before upload cannot already contain the provider-assigned numeric artifact ID, provider archive digest/size, or observed provider timestamps.
3. **Separate identities.** Retain distinct canonical payload digest/size and provider artifact/archive digest/size. Verify a bounded archive containing exactly the expected payload path, then compare extracted payload bytes exactly.
4. **Observed retention.** Requested `created + retention_days` arithmetic is intent, not provider evidence. Authority must use observed provider `created_at` and `expires_at` and prove the actual lifetime covers the release/recovery window.
5. **Fresh-runner bootstrap.** Recovery must begin from surviving canonical operation/head plus exact workflow run/attempt identity, list only that run's provider objects, reject zero/multiple matches, and then bind the returned numeric ID.
6. **Canonical parent composition.** The checkpoint must consume the #3940 operation identity digest and exact operation head instead of reconstructing journal-local operation meaning.
7. **Readback ordering.** Equal-time replacement is permitted only for an exactly idempotent observation over the same receipt and bytes; a different outcome must require a strictly later observation.

## Required target architecture

```text
PublicationCheckpointPayloadV1
  immutable operation/head/row/checkpoint-chain payload

PublicationCheckpointProviderReceiptV1
  provider-assigned ID/name/archive digest/size
  exact workflow/ref/run/attempt/head identity
  observed created_at/expires_at

PublicationCheckpointReadbackObservationV1
  provider listing/download result
  bounded archive verification and exact extracted payload bytes
  observation time and trust result

VerifiedPublicationCheckpointV1
  opaque authority binding payload + receipt + readback
```

Sequence extension, upload permission and dependant permission must consume `VerifiedPublicationCheckpointV1` or an equivalent opaque proof.

## Correct implementation order

```text
accept #3940 PR A (#4303) on its current main pair
→ #3940 PR B: migrate journal/checkpoint/lease/tag/release children
  and complete the reopened #3922 provider adapter
→ #3940 PR C: workflow/head/evidence cutover, owner inventory,
  anti-duplication guard, zero-mutation rehearsal
→ #3924 deterministic unknown-upload recovery
```

## Claim boundary

The merged code characterizes and tests a synthetic checkpoint contract. It does **not** yet prove that a remotely durable GitHub Artifact checkpoint can be produced, discovered after total runner loss, verified against actual provider/archive metadata, retained for the required window, or composed with the canonical release-operation authority. No release execution is authorized by this merge.

author: sritampatnaik
body: ## Problem Sritam’s production create-account flow returned: ```json { "error": "This endpoint requires a valid Bearer token" } ``` `GET /api/auth` was `configured: true` (Vercel had `SUPABASE_URL` + `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`). Local signup worked because `.env.local` only had the public anon/publishable key. ## Cause `signUpStudent` called `auth.admin.createUser` whenever `getSupabaseAdmin()` was non-null, and that helper treated **any** non-empty `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY` as a privileged Auth Admin client. New Dashboard keys (`sb_publishable_…`, `sb_secret_…`) are **not JWTs**. GoTrue Auth Admin requires `Authorization: Bearer `, so that path 401s with the message above. Public `POST /auth/v1/signup` with the publishable key succeeds, and the existing `on_auth_user_created_confirm` trigger confirms the email. ## Fix - Classify keys by **value** (JWT `role`, `sb_publishable_`, `sb_secret_`), including a publishable key pasted into `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`. - Student signup/login always uses a public anon/publishable client (`signUp` / `signInWithPassword`). Auth Admin is no longer on the create-account path. - Strip opaque `Bearer sb_*` headers that `@supabase/supabase-js` still copies onto Auth requests. - `/api/auth` reports `configured` only when a public Auth key is present. ## Env (no secrets committed) Added **new** Vercel production+preview vars `SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY` and `SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` (public keys). Did **not** change `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`. After this lands, create-account needs a publishable or anon key on the server. A privileged key is optional (evals / RLS bypass). ## Verification - Unit tests for key classification, including publishable pasted into `SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`. - Direct Auth Admin vs public signup against this Supabase project: admin + publishable Bearer → exact 401; public `signUp` → 200 and auto-confirmed. - `tsx` client with only `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY=sb_publishable_…` created a confirmed user (no Auth Admin). - `POST /api/auth` signup on local Next returned `configured: true`, a user, and a conversation id. - Browser create-account on http://localhost:3000: form → desk, no Bearer error, **Signed in** with the new email. [Create account form](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-b08e2bcc-7261-57cb-9a11-3a97bc3b995d/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fsignup_form.webp) [Signed-in desk after signup](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-b08e2bcc-7261-57cb-9a11-3a97bc3b995d/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fsigned_in_desk.webp) [create_account_signup_desk.mp4](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-b08e2bcc-7261-57cb-9a11-3a97bc3b995d/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fcreate_account_signup_desk.mp4) To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

author: starhearthunt
body:
## 动机

`src/mw.d.ts` 里 `window.Sentry`（由 `src/entries/sentry.ts` 挂上去）的类型是手抄的，和 SDK 已经漂移：

- `captureException` 写成 `(error: unknown) => string`，吞掉了第二个 `hint` 参数
- `showReportDialog` 退化成 `(...args: any[]) => void`，等于没类型
- `showFeedback` 的 `tags` 是 `Record<string, boolean | number | string>`，比 SDK 的 `Primitive` 窄（少了 `bigint | symbol | null | undefined`）

## 改动

三个签名都改成从 `@sentry/browser` 的类型里取：

```ts
type SentryBrowser = typeof import("@sentry/browser");
type SentryFeedback = ReturnType<SentryBrowser["feedbackIntegration"]>;
type SentryFeedbackTags = NonNullable<Parameters<SentryFeedback["createForm"]>[0]>["tags"];
```

几点说明：

- `showFeedback` 是本仓库自己包的（`createForm` + `appendToDom` + `open`），SDK 没有对应 API，所以保留手写签名，只有 `tags` 从 `createForm` 的参数推导。
- 绕 `feedbackIntegration` 这条链，是因为 `@sentry/feedback` 只是间接依赖，pnpm 严格布局下不能直接 `import("@sentry/feedback")`，而 `OverrideFeedbackConfiguration` 也没从 `@sentry/browser` 入口 re-export。
- 文件顺带从「全局脚本」改成「模块 + `declare global`」（末尾 `export {}`），让新增的几个类型别名留在文件作用域内，不污染全局类型名。`Window` 的增强照常生效。

代价：这个 d.ts 是全项目 ambient 的，现在每次类型检查都会把 `@sentry/browser` 的类型图拉进来。

## 验证

- `vue-tsc -b --force` 通过
- `eslint src/mw.d.ts src/entries/sentry.ts` 通过
- 临时探针文件确认类型确实收紧了（验证后已删除）：
  - `showFeedback({ bad: { nested: 1 } })` → `Type '{ nested: number; }' is not assignable to type 'Primitive'`
  - `captureException(err, { mechanism: { type: "generic" } })` → 通过编译（旧签名下会报参数过多）

body:
### 问题

Windows（尤其 Windows 11 深色任务栏）下，桌面快捷方式与任务栏按钮的应用图标带**白色底板**。

### 修复

统一改用**透明底**素材重新生成应用图标资产，并同步相关生成脚本：

- 重新生成 `icon.ico`、`icon-windows.png`、`Square*.png`、`StoreLogo.png`（透明底 + 圆角）；
- `icon.ico` 覆盖 **16 / 24 / 32 / 48 / 64 / 128 / 256** 多尺寸，适配 100% / 150% / 200% DPI；其中 16–128px 使用 32bpp DIB + AND 掩码，256px 使用 PNG 条目；
- 生成脚本 `scripts/gen-windows-rounded-icon.py` 默认源改为 **`public/icon-transparent.png`**（透明底），并新增 `--src` 可指定其他源图；
- 在 `build.rs` 中声明 `icons/` 下图标文件为构建输入，确保图标资源变更能被正确打包。

### 影响面

- 涉及应用图标素材、图标生成脚本与 `build.rs`；
- 无接口 / 数据结构变更，无新增运行时依赖；
- macOS / Linux 的应用图标（`icon.png` / `icon.icns` / `32x32.png` / `128x128*.png`）不受影响。

### 验证

- [x] `cargo check` 通过；托盘相关单测 15/15 通过
- [x] 各图标尺寸均含透明像素，且无不透明纯黑像素
- [x] 重建后 `icon.ico` 的 256px 条目字节存在于生成的可执行文件中
- [x] Windows 11：桌面图标、任务栏按钮、Alt-Tab 均无白色底板
- [ ] macOS：应用图标与托盘图标无变化

### 变更文件清单

```
src-tauri/build.rs                    声明 icons/ 为构建输入
scripts/gen-windows-rounded-icon.py   默认源改为透明底 + 新增 --src + ICO 打包按尺寸区分条目类型
scripts/gen-tray-icon.py              默认输出尺寸 64 → 32
src-tauri/icons/icon.ico              重新生成（透明底，16–256 多尺寸）
src-tauri/icons/icon-windows.png      重新生成（透明底 + 圆角）
src-tauri/icons/Square*.png           重新生成（透明底 + 圆角）
src-tauri/icons/StoreLogo.png         重新生成（透明底 + 圆角）
```

### 附：重新生成方式

```bash
python scripts/gen-windows-rounded-icon.py                          # 默认使用 public/icon-transparent.png
python scripts/gen-windows-rounded-icon.py --src public/icon.png    # 需要不透明底时显式指定
```

> `gen-windows-rounded-icon.py` 依赖 Pillow。

author: austinkelsay
body:
Brain and Sites layouts from #930 and #931 are already on main through #945, but ordinary dashboard users still see disabled tabs. This follow-up enables both pages with truthful unavailable states while their real data integrations remain pending.

| Before | After |
| --- | --- |
| Brain and Sites navigation and direct routes require design preview mode. | Both links work for authorized selected agents, using the existing account/agent access checks and canonical redirects. |
| Brain can only display its synthetic overview. | The ordinary page says “Brain overview isn’t available yet” and offers an editable chat draft to discover or create brains. The existing empty-state chat action is shared with the preview. |
| Sites has only a generic fetch-error state for missing listing data and displays empty column headers. | The ordinary page says “Site listings aren’t available yet,” explains that users can still work in chat, and hides irrelevant headers. Create a site retains its existing editable draft. |
| Sample data is broadly enabled by development preview configuration. | Both pages require development mode, the preview flag, local account auth, and the exact fixture agent for samples. Visible labels identify synthetic records. Production cannot enable samples even with both flags set. |
| Brain's prototype overrides the shared page layout and crowds the mobile navigation button. | Brain uses the normal dashboard spacing; browser coverage checks the heading clears mobile navigation. |
| Navigation coverage only inspects source text. | Environment-matrix and browser tests cover sample isolation, direct links, unavailable Chat, mobile layout, and draft-only actions. The local fixture can disable previews with `FC_WEB_DESIGN_PREVIEWS=0`. |

The chat path is unchanged: the selected-agent UI dispatches `StartTopicChatIntent` through the Dashboard action route, which checks the existing Agent binding and asks the Hosted Web Device to select a new chat. The existing chat composer reads the URL prompt as an editable draft. No message is sent automatically. This adds no storage writer or protocol variant; the browser checks exercise the existing local services and the existing chat regression covers retained history, reconnects, and older-service snapshots. No production rollout or infrastructure changes are included.

Validation in the pinned Nix development environment:

- Dashboard unit tests: 314 passed, including production/development preview-boundary combinations.
- Dashboard typecheck and lint: passed; the existing unused-variable warning in `core-client.ts` remains.
- Production build: passed, with workspace file-tracing warnings from the existing auth/workspace path imports.
- Brain/Sites browser checks: passed for ordinary pages, mobile screenshots, preview isolation to the fixture agent, keyboard folder expansion, unauthorized-agent deep links, unavailable Chat, and editable prompts without message sends.
- Existing chat browser regression: passed for tab-scoped history, reconnects, send feedback, and older-service snapshots.
- Desktop and 390px mobile screenshots inspected; `git diff --check` passed.

Real Brain membership reads (FIN-89) and Sites listing/access metadata (FIN-69) remain unconnected. These checks prove the dashboard UI and existing chat entry path against local fixtures; they do not claim live Brain/Sites integration or production deployment proof.

Handles stay available while the Text tool is active, resize live in XY, preserve text/CNC depth, and keep the opposite corner anchored while dragging. Resize uses the existing transform/history pipeline, invalidates stale CAM as a Text size change, updates Inspector Size controls, and records Undo as resize text. Includes regression tests for anchored scaling, depth preservation, Text-tool interaction, CAM invalidation, and undo labeling.
