author: rds-renan
body:
Telas 3a e 3b da E3, com a regra corrigida na E4: a refeição **permanece fiel ao cardápio previsto** mesmo quando houve troca — é isso que dá sentido à justificativa —, e a alteração guarda à parte os gêneros e quantidades que entraram no lugar, mais o motivo em texto livre.

## Critérios de aceite

- [x] Uma alteração por refeição, com justificativa obrigatória em texto livre e sugestões de motivos frequentes.
- [x] Quantidades em inteiros, com a unidade padrão do item e teclado numérico (US003).
- [x] Escolher gênero não tira a merendeira da tela de registro.
- [x] Gênero novo criado no fluxo entra no catálogo com sua unidade.
- [x] A alteração aparece resumida no cartão da refeição (decisão 8 da E3).

## O que entrou

**Duas listas de gênero por refeição**, com a mesma peça e o mesmo stepper de inteiros — são duas porque alimentam colunas diferentes do documento oficial ([decisão 7 da E4](docs/04-banco-de-dados/decisoes-de-modelagem.md)). A chave da lista é o **nome normalizado**, e não o identificador, porque é assim que o servidor decide se dois gêneros são o mesmo: repetir um item não duplica nem devolve a quantidade para 1. O "−" de quem está em 1 tira o gênero, já que quantidade zero não existe no banco.

**A folha "Escolher gênero"** sobe sobre o registro ([decisão 7 da E3](docs/03-ux/decisoes-de-design.md)), com busca que ignora acento e cadastro de gênero novo ali mesmo. O gênero cadastrado nasce no envio — `save_meal_map` cria no catálogo o que ainda não existir —, então funciona sem rede e sem catálogo carregado.

**A alteração** tem os gêneros da troca e o motivo com sugestões, aparece resumida dentro do cartão da refeição e é uma só por refeição (RN#2 da US002).

**`canBeSent` ganhou a segunda dobra**: alteração sem motivo ou sem gênero fica guardada no aparelho em vez de ir para uma recusa certa, como já acontecia com o dia não letivo. A tela diz o que falta sem chamar de erro o meio do caminho.

## Duas decisões que valem o olhar

**O rótulo da refeição virou "Cardápio previsto".** "Realizado" é o nome da coluna do formulário oficial, mas na tela ele pedia à merendeira exatamente o que a 3a lhe diz para não fazer. O nome da coluna continua onde importa, na geração do documento. Canvas republicado e PNGs reexportados junto.

**"Confirmar" não é salvar.** Cada tecla da 3a já vai para o aparelho — não existe botão de salvar (decisão 3 da E3) —, e os dois botões do rodapé decidem se a alteração *fica*: confirmar fecha e limpa a alteração vazia, cancelar devolve o retrato de quando a tela abriu. Entrou também um "Remover a alteração", que não está no desenho da E3: sem ele, desfazer uma troca registrada por engano seria tirar os gêneros um a um e apagar o motivo.

**As duas telas sobrepostas ficam dentro do container central de 390 px** ([decisão 1 da E3](docs/03-ux/decisoes-de-design.md)). Presas à janela, esticavam de ponta a ponta do monitor sobre uma coluna estreita. O `left`/`right` do menu fica de fora de propósito: o mesmo lado serve à barra lateral da direção, que é tela de desktop de verdade.

## Verificação

`npm test` (149 casos, 13 arquivos), lint, tipos, build e `npm run check:size` (193,4 kB de 205 kB). Os novos cenários estão em `register.test.ts` (as regras) e `menu-change.test.tsx` (as telas, critério por critério), e a tabela deles está no [registro do dia](docs/05-web/registro-do-dia.md). As três telas foram conferidas renderizadas no Chrome, em largura de celular e de desktop.

Vai junto uma correção que não é desta issue: a primeira rodada da CI reprovou num teste antigo da visão do mês, que conferia a faixa do dia bloqueado sem esperar. O título do dia sai do endereço e aparece antes da resposta do servidor; o bloqueio só o servidor conhece. Reproduzi aqui com execuções simultâneas disputando a CPU, e a asserção passou a esperar.

body:
<!-- Title: feat(orchestration): cap review WIP and act on the review order (MARXY-81) -->

## Summary

The review queue now has a hard cap of four, so implementors stop when review is the constraint instead of lengthening a queue that cannot drain. Each cycle refreshes only the next behind pull request in the computed order, a conflicted branch goes back to its implementor without spending an attempt, and an approval cannot be signed until that pull request is first, current and clean. That makes the signed-approval livelock structurally impossible rather than a thing the loop warns about.

## Changes

- `reviewLanes` is 4 in `models.json`; `lanes` stays null; `ready.mjs` prints `blockedByReviewWip` and dispatches nothing while In Review is full
- `cycle.mjs` calls `gh pr update-branch` on at most one BEHIND pull request per cycle and returns a DIRTY one to In Progress with attempts unchanged
- `approve.mjs` refuses to sign when the pull request is BEHIND, DIRTY, or not first in the order, with no new environment-variable escape hatch
- `review.mjs` names the four boundary checks that cannot run when `state.json` has no branch
- Hold-reason strings from before this change are kept as a fixture and remain a subset of what the cycle can print

## Verification

```
✓ check:story
✓ check:one-parse

✓ pnpm test
```

A reviewer can run `node --test orchestration/test/review-wip.test.mjs` and `node orchestration/approve.mjs --selftest`.

## For the reviewer

This implements ADR-0025 against the order `review-order.mjs` already computes (MARXY-80). `cycle.mjs` and `approve.mjs` are CODEOWNERS — please do not `--admin` merge. The live cycle body is now behind `isMain` so tests can import `processReviewQueue` and inject `updateBranch`; every hold-reason fragment from before this PR is in `orchestration/test/hold-reasons-before.json` and still appears in the source. A returned DIRTY story is written through `saveState` (In Progress, attempts untouched) because `state.mjs` is outside this story's paths and its `return` command goes to todo. author: alkmimm
body:
## Why

Yesterday's preflight refused a redeploy while the Windows host had **102 GB free**: it judged the VM by the guest's own numbers (`MemTotal−MemFree` = 66 GB, page cache 55 GB) after a `make validate`, and the guest cannot see that the host had already reclaimed that cache. This morning it flagged **8.8 GB of swap** as "already under pressure" — with PSI `full avg60` at 0.06 %; `autoMemoryReclaim=gradual` swaps idle anon pages out on purpose.

Both scripts exist so this stack never takes the host down again (2026-09-16). A guard that cries wolf gets bypassed, which is worse than no guard.

## What

- **`scripts/wsl-memory-lib.sh`** (new) — shared probes: Windows free memory, **the vmmemWSL working set** (what the host is actually charged for the VM — measured ≈ guest footprint + 3–7 GB), guest footprint/cache/swap, PSI. Every probe returns `""` when it cannot measure; `""` is unknown, never zero.
- **`host-memory-preflight.sh`** — checks host free ≥ 24 GB, **host charge for the VM ≤ 60 GB**, **PSI full avg60 ≤ 10 %**. Guest footprint + cache caps only apply when the host cannot be asked (then the guest cannot tell reclaimed cache from pinned cache). Swap in use is printed, never fails. `PREFLIGHT_SOFT=1` downgrades every refusal (build residue is something only the operator can recognise).
- **`wsl-memory-guard.sh`** — trips on the same charge figure (guest footprint without a host view) or host free < 16 GB, 2 consecutive polls.
- **`scripts/ci/wsl-memory-guards-selftest.sh`** (new) — 20 hermetic cases (no host, no docker) through the lib's `WSL_MEMORY_PROBES_OVERRIDE` seam and the guard's `GUARD_STOP_CMD` seam; asserts the case count so a deleted case cannot silently un-gate a behaviour. **Wired into the `static-checks` stage**, which every image build reaches.
- Runbook §7b + Makefile help: new semantics; `.wslconfig memory=96GB` **stays** (the other workloads in this VM need it) — the durable fixes are #397 (daemon stops re-reading the corpus on restart) and these guards.

## Verified

- Self-test natively in WSL: `20 cases, 0 failed`.
- Real run on this host: `host charge 23.9 GB (guest 17.3 used / 11.1 cache)`, PSI 0 %, swap 8.0 GB → safe; tight thresholds → hard refuse / soft continue; fake `powershell.exe` returning 0 → host unmeasurable → exit 2 and guest caps applied; dry guard with `VM_GUARD_STOP_GB=1` → `breach 1/2`, `breach 2/2`, `TRIP`, exit 3.
- Static gate: see the build log in the merge comment.

author: limineol
body:
The upstream extractors miss current Codex response items and archived sessions, OpenCode2 databases, and several installed harnesses. This adds private raw and normalized backups with per-store integrity manifests and explicit coverage.

One monthly job on Nexus runs local extraction and triggers workers on Vector and Forge over SSH, then collects completed archives with SCP. Nexus verifies transferred SHA-256 hashes and sizes before marking the aggregate backup set complete. Local immutable archives use hard links when available. Failed hosts do not prevent collecting others. There are no remote schedules or cloud uploads.

Cleanup is report-only pending approval of retention/protection rules. Antigravity is explicitly binary-only; empty histories are not treated as live verification. Raw database exports preserve orphaned conversation rows while flagging incomplete normalization. Failed outputs retain an `.incomplete` suffix. Active JSONL snapshots, mixed Codex event ordering, Cursor protobuf traversal and repeated branch messages are covered.

Validation: 54 tests covering extraction contracts, transfer integrity, SSH fleet failure isolation, scheduler locking/status and cleanup reporting. CI covers Linux, macOS, Windows and Python 3.9. Live history extraction verified on Nexus, Vector and Forge, including Forge’s OpenCode2 schema. Independent read-only Claude review findings evaluated and actionable defects fixed; the fleet coordinator received a focused follow-up review. Initial Nexus/Vector/Forge archive collection completed with transferred checksums verified.

author: ashrahossain
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #14 (project 16, production agent).

- **Tools can read your support API.** With `SUPPORT_API_URL` set, live mode's `lookup_order`, `track_shipment` and `refund_policy` send `GET` requests to `/orders/{id}`, `/shipments/{id}` and `/refund-policies/{category}` on that service instead of the sample data. The contract is in the README. `--questions FILE` supplies real customer questions, because the built-in ones name sample orders that a real API won't have.
- **Alert dashboard and Slack notifier now work.** A commit pushed after #14 merged added these, and both were broken. The poster crashed on every line (it parsed epoch timestamps as ISO strings), and the dashboard was never committed because it sat in gitignored `outputs/`. This PR replaces both with tested versions.
- **The project README is rewritten** to cover connecting an API, the alert tooling, the five alert rules and the known limitations.

## Related issue(s)

Follow-up to #14.

## Type of change

- [ ] Bug fix (non-breaking change that fixes an issue)
- [x] New feature (non-breaking change that adds functionality)
- [ ] Breaking change (fix or feature that would change existing behavior)
- [x] Documentation update
- [ ] Tooling / CI / scripts

## How has this been tested?

- `uv run pytest` in `projects/16-production-agent`: 132 passed, 1 skipped (the live-API test). That's 20 more than before:
  - 13 for the HTTP backend, run against `httpx2.MockTransport`. They cover the contract fields and nothing else reaching the model, 404, retry then success, a service that stays down, 401 with no retry, off-contract bodies, and path encoding. I checked that the encoding test fails when the encoding is removed.
  - 3 for the CLI: questions-file errors, and live mode asking your questions against your API.
  - 4 for the Slack notifier, using lines in the sink's real format.
- Both dry runs finish exactly as before. `bad-canary` aborts on `loop_detected` and `late-regression` rolls back on `tool_error_rate`.
- Root suite: 888 passed, 91.44% coverage.
- The dashboard was loaded in a browser against a real `alerts.jsonl` with a resolved alert and a malformed `<script>` line appended. It showed correct UTC dates, only the unresolved alert as still firing, and the malformed line counted as unreadable, not run. No console errors.
- black, ruff, and CI's detect-secrets scan: clean for every changed file.

- [x] `uv run pytest --cov` passes locally
- [x] Added/updated tests covering the change
- [x] Manually verified on: macOS

## Checklist

- [x] My code follows the style guidelines of this project (`black`, `ruff`)

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code

- [x] My changes generate no new warnings from `ruff` / `mypy` / `bandit`
- [x] I have not committed any API keys, secrets, or `.env` files

## Additional notes

**Worth a reviewer's eye**

- **The backend is chosen only in `main.py`.** `tools.py` never reads the environment. That's why dry runs stay on the sample data, with pinned timelines, even when `SUPPORT_API_URL` is set.
- **The support API is treated as untrusted.** Only contract fields reach the model, so an extra `customer_email` is dropped. Values must be strings or null. Error logs record the field names received, never the values.
- **Retries** cover timeouts, connection errors, 429 and 5xx: 3 attempts, 0.25s then 0.5s backoff, 5s timeout. Any other 4xx fails at once, since that's a configuration problem. Every failure becomes a `ToolError` the model can explain to the customer.
- **Known limitation, documented rather than fixed.** `tool_error_rate` can't tell a tool the model misused from a support API that was down. An outage during a rollout can abort or roll back a healthy canary. Separating them needs a second error kind and its own alert rule. Tell me if you want that next.
- **`httpx2` is now a declared dependency.** It was already imported (by `fake_model.py`) and installed through `anthropic`.
- **This branch includes the original dashboard/Slack commit (`d42a14b`),** and the next commit rewrites it. I kept it so the history shows what was broken.

author: ffmathy
body:
## What was failing

The `deploy` job of releases **2.2.0** ([run 35352478688](https://github.com/ffMathy/hey-jarvis/actions/runs/35352478688)) and **2.2.1** ([run 35415175876](https://github.com/ffMathy/hey-jarvis/actions/runs/35415175876)) both died about two minutes in, and not on anything they deploy. Turbo reaches the apps' `initialize` on the way to `turbo deploy`, and one of them failed:

```
watch:initialize: $ cd .. && bash watch/.scripts/initialize.sh
-- Skia iOS package: .../react-native-skia-apple-ios
-- Skia macOS package: .../react-native-skia-apple-macos
Error: ENOENT: no such file or directory, chmod
'.../@shopify/react-native-skia/libs/ios/libskia.xcframework/ios-arm64_arm64e/libskia.a'
```

## Why

`install-skia` writes into the **installed package's own** `libs/`, and it clears each directory before copying into it:

```js
fs.rmSync(path.join(libsDir, "ios"), { recursive: true, force: true });
fs.mkdirSync(path.join(libsDir, "ios"), { recursive: true });
copySync(iosPackage + "/libs/*.xcframework", path.join(libsDir, "ios"), ...);
```

Three things then line up:

- Both apps ran it as their own `initialize`.
- Nothing ordered the two — `turbo deploy --dry` shows `mobile#initialize` and `watch#initialize` with `dependsOn: []`, and both are `cache: false`, so both run every time.
- Both resolve the **same physical copy** of `@shopify/react-native-skia`. Verified: `readlink -f mobile/node_modules/@shopify/react-native-skia` and the watch's equal `node_modules/.bun/@shopify+react-native-skia@2.6.2+70118785601b4f19/...`.

So Turbo ran them in parallel against one directory: one process deleted `libs/ios` while the other was still copying into it, and the loser died on the file it had just written. A coin flip decided which — 2.2.0 lost as `mobile`, 2.2.1 as `watch` — and both logs show the two inside the Apple copy at the same moment.

The watch's notes claimed the opposite, that *"this app and the phone app resolve different copies of Skia"*, which is why running it twice looked safe. That is what made this hard to see.

## The fix

The step becomes one root task, `//#install-skia`, that both apps depend on. Turbo runs a root task once, which is the whole mutex.

It fixes every entry point at once — `turbo build`, `turbo deploy`, `build:aab` and `build:apk` all reach `initialize` the same way and were all equally exposed, so CI was flaky here too, not just the release.

- `watch` is left with no `initialize` of its own, since that step was all it had.
- `mobile` keeps `setup-skia-web`, which copies into its own `public/` and races nothing.
- The script still walks the apps rather than assuming a single copy: if their closures ever diverge Bun gives them a copy each, and each needs its own libraries. Identical closures collapse to one directory — the case today — and that copy is done once.

Also fixes: `mobile`'s `android` and `eas-build-post-install` skip Turbo, so they would have silently lost the native libraries and failed in CMake. They now name both halves of the setup themselves.

## Verification

| Check | Result |
| --- | --- |
| `turbo deploy --dry` | one `//#install-skia`; both app initializes depend on it |
| `turbo build --dry` (the CI entry point) | same |
| `turbo build:apk --filter=watch --dry` | `['//#install-skia', 'watch#build:apk', 'watch#initialize']` |
| `turbo build:aab --filter=mobile --filter=watch --dry` | one `//#install-skia` for both |
| `turbo initialize --filter=mobile --filter=watch` | installs once, logs `watch: shares its Skia copy with an app already done`; `libs/` restored after being deleted |
| `turbo build --filter=mobile` | passes end to end through the new chain |
| `turbo lint` | pass — 12 tasks, no errors |
| `turbo test` | pass — 999 tests, 0 failed, 0 skipped |

`turbo deploy` itself needs 1Password credentials, so it is CI that will confirm the deploy job; everything upstream of it is exercised above.

Adds an Agent-3-owned fail-closed admission layer for the correction machinery. author: toastygm
body:
A body image whose pathname names a package no Foundry install carries reached a
journal as the authored pathname and nothing said so: the shared renderer
swallowed the refusal, `lint` reported nothing and `package compile` exited 0.
The compiled document carried a `src` that resolved against nothing, which looks
exactly like an address that worked.

## What it does now

`engine/pathnames.mjs` gains `foundryAddressProblem(raw, config)` — the sentence
for "this pathname resolves on every surface but the Foundry one" — beside the
`pathnameProblem` it already states, and `servesFoundry(config)` for the one
package kind that has no Foundry surface to be dead on.

- **The compile refuses, located.** `convertNoteWikilinks` scans the body after
  embeds are rewritten and fails the note with its file, line and column.
- **The address passes report it.** `content-build lint` holds an authored
  `![alt](…)` to the rule, and `content-build links` holds the pathname an
  `![[…]]` embed resolved to, reported against the embed the note wrote.
- **`resolveImg` states its refusal through the same function**, so an art field
  and a body image tell an author the same thing in the same words.
- **`packagebuild` gets its own sentence.** package-build is an npm dependency
  rather than a package Foundry installs, so "declare it under `relationships`"
  is advice that cannot be followed — the message says where those files do
  reach instead.

Swept in with it: a Foundry-spelled `systems/…` / `modules/…` body image also
fails the compile now. It is the same line of code and the same rule — every
surface refuses such a value rather than deriving an address from it — and it
removes the case where `package compile` emits a body `lint` refuses.

## What still passes through

An absolute URL, a protocol-relative `//host/…`, a `data:` URI and a `/`-rooted
path name no package at all and reach a journal untouched. A blank pathname
stays a deliberate blank. A `documentation` package installs nothing in Foundry,
so its notes are not asked the question.

## Verification

`npm run lint`, `npm test` (169 files, 3975 tests), `npm run format:check` and
`npm run build:types` all pass. Twelve of the sixteen new cases fail against
`main`.

Both consumers were compiled against this branch, in worktrees cut from their
own `origin/main` with their own `npm ci`:

- **`sohl-thalorna`** — `content-index`, `lint`, `links`, `package compile` and
  `content-build site` all clean, with the same advisory warnings `main` shows.
  Injecting the defect into one being note produced the located error from
  `lint` and from `package compile` for `![alt](…)`, and from `links` and
  `package compile` for `![[…]]`, with one message and one position for both.
- **`Song-of-Heroic-Lands-FoundryVTT`** — `lint` and `links` clean;
  `npm run build:db` fails identically with and without this branch, on the
  three map notes whose `bgImage` addresses resolve to nothing (filed already).

Closes #518

author: roysalisbury
body:
## Issue

Closes #259

Target: `development/v1`

## Outcome

A container profile revision can be built into an image on one approved execution host and contract-verified there; only a verified digest becomes provisionable on that host. Nothing here approves a hire or creates an employee.

## Scope And Exclusions

- `ProfileBuildContext`: deterministic build context (one generated `Dockerfile` in a fixed-metadata tar; SHA-256 = context hash). Pinned base tag, owner fragment, features as fixed apt recipes, `containerEnv` as `ENV`, lifecycle as labels, fixed worker-contract trailer.
- `RemoteWorkerOperations`: `ImageTag`, `ImageBuild` (stdin tar, `--pull=false --no-cache`, no args/secrets/cache/context), `ImageInspect` on tags, `ImageVerify` (fixed base64-carried Python program run with no network/caps), `ImageRemove`; `ImageBuildTimeoutSeconds` (900). Container-create now accepts the host's approved set (base + verified builds); bootstrap is base-only.
- `ProfileBuildCoordinator` + `ImageContractVerifier`: intent-first per-host build state machine; inspect + in-image verification; transport loss → `uncertain` → reconcile by tag.
- Schema **v9**: `profile_builds` (additive; identity immutable, never deleted/replaced, one live + one verified per revision/host). Revision-level `build_status`/digest/verified are a fold of per-host rows.
- API `GET/POST /api/profiles/{id}/revisions/{revisionId}/builds`; `POST /api/workers/enroll/plan` takes optional `imageDigest` from the host's set. `/profiles/{id}` gains per-host builds + build action.
- Review-process trim (agreed on #265): parent review is index-only; correction parent template added.

Out of scope: hire approval/provisioning (#260), rebuild/cleanup (#261), execution-host UI.

**Live evidence** (on #259): `generic-employee` built and verified on `home-dev-02` through the real API in 77 s (`pbld-70a44cbd7c4ff102`), independently inspected on the host, cleaned up; schema v7→v8→v9 deployed to `home-docker` (image `deploy-4b2edfe`, quiesced snapshot `agentcontrol-v2-backup-pre-4b2edfe` 3830/3830 verified, both create-once schema backups hash-verified, all endpoints healthy, session preserved). `home-docker` host enrollment was **held by the owner** (no SSH identity created). The deployed image predates the review corrections and will be redeployed from the merged head.

## Changed Behavior

- Per-host approved digests replace the single global digest for long-lived containers.
- `docker build` over the pinned SSH path exists, but only from controller-rendered context.

## Local Validation (head `7222f03`)

```text
dotnet build --warnaserror: succeeded, 0 warnings
dotnet format --verify-no-changes: clean
dotnet test (hermetic selection): 1286/1286 (ProfileBuildTests 20, provisioning-from-profile e2e, schema v8→v9 migration 2)
```

body:
## Ticket

Ticket: #86 · F2-03 · VectorWidget y FreeBodyWidget · desarrollador

## Qué se hizo

- `packages/widgets/src/VectorWidget/` — `compute.ts`, `compute.test.ts`, `VectorWidget.tsx`, `VectorWidget.test.tsx`, `VectorWidget.stories.tsx`, `index.ts`
- `packages/widgets/src/FreeBodyWidget/` — `compute.ts`, `compute.test.ts`, `FreeBodyWidget.tsx`, `FreeBodyWidget.test.tsx`, `FreeBodyWidget.stories.tsx`, `index.ts`
- `packages/widgets/src/shared/SceneOverlay.tsx` (+ test), `ReadoutPanel.tsx`, `useSceneTransformValue.ts` — capa de interacción sobre el lienzo y panel de valores de `DESIGN.md` §5
- `packages/widgets/src/Scene2D/context.ts` y `Scene2D.tsx` — la transformación vigente, que la escena ya guardaba en una `ref`, se expone por el contexto (decisión 3). El pintado no cambia y ninguna captura existente se movió.
- `packages/widgets/src/index.ts`, `src/dev/StoryGallery.tsx` y su test — registro de las tres stories
- `packages/i18n/locales/es/widgets.json` — claves `widgets.VectorWidget.*` y `widgets.FreeBodyWidget.*`
- `apps/web/e2e/visual/widgets.spec.ts`, `VectorWidget.png`, `FreeBodyWidget.png`

## Cómo probarlo

```
pnpm --filter @trayectoria/widgets test
pnpm --filter @trayectoria/widgets exec vitest run --coverage
pnpm --filter @trayectoria/web exec playwright test e2e/visual
pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm test && pnpm build
```

## Evidencia por criterio de aceptación

| Criterio | Evidencia |
| -------- | --------- |
| Archivos completos; stories en `/dev/widgets` | `StoryGallery.test.tsx` fija el orden `VectorWidget/Curriculum`, `FreeBodyWidget/Plane`, `FreeBodyWidget/Ramp15`; las tres se ven en `/dev/widgets` |
| Valores dorados de T-0.2 exactos | `VectorWidget/compute.test.ts`: `(0.5, 30°) → (0.433, 0.25)`; `(0.3, 0.4) → 0.5, 53.13°` (±0.01°); `(1.2, 0.5)+(−0.4, 0.8) → 1.526`; ángulo entre `(0.3, 0.4)` y `(0.5, 0)` = 53.13° |
| Valores dorados de T-2.1 exactos | `FreeBodyWidget/compute.test.ts`: `F = 0.72 N`; `N = 8.829 N`; rampa 15° → `2.285 N` y `8.528 N`; `a = 1.222 m/s²` |
| Arrastrar una punta con teclado actualiza magnitud y ángulo | `VectorWidget.test.tsx`: una flecha mueve 0.1 y el panel pasa de `0.500 m / 53.13°` a `0.566 m / 45.00°`; Shift+flecha mueve 1.0 |
| Capturas de ambos widgets | `VectorWidget.png` (Curriculum) y `FreeBodyWidget.png` (Ramp15); `playwright test e2e/visual` pasa 10/10 sin `--update-snapshots` |
| Solo tokens; sin literales de UI; `aria-live` | Colores por nombre de token (`tokenColor`), textos por `t()`, `LiveStatus` con `role="status"`/`aria-live="polite"` refrescado como mucho cada 2 s |
| `pnpm lint && typecheck && test && build` | Los cuatro en verde; 204 tests; cobertura por archivo ≥ 90 % (global 99.8 % líneas) |

## Riesgos y decisiones dentro del alcance

- `Scene2D` no interactúa, así que la punta arrastrable es un `button` transparente colocado sobre el lienzo (decisión 3). La escena mantiene la transformación en una `ref` y no re-renderiza a sus hijos al redimensionar: la capa observa el mismo elemento con un `ResizeObserver` y vuelve a leer la `ref`. No se añadió ningún re-render por frame.
- Las fuerzas se resuelven en el marco de la superficie (x paralelo a la pendiente); en plano coincide con el marco del mundo, como pide la decisión 5. El peso y la normal se derivan siempre de `mass_kg` y `slope_rad` bajo las claves reservadas `weight` y `normal`.
- T-2.1 escribe el ángulo de la fricción como `3.1416`, no como π: con tracción y fricción iguales la resultante queda en ~3 µN en vez de cero exacto. El test lo comprueba como «menor que 1e-4» y el widget no redondea ningún número por su cuenta.
- La escala N → m del dibujo (`M_PER_N`) es solo de presentación; ningún número del panel pasa por ella.

## Qué NO se hizo (obligatorio)

- Vectores 3D, más de dos vectores y animación: fuera de alcance explícito del ticket.
- Ejercicios de T-0.2 y T-2.1: son de F2-10.
- No se tocó `docs/` (ni la entrada de `WIDGETS.md`, que ya describe ambos widgets y coincide con las props implementadas), `.github/`, `package.json` raíz ni otros paquetes.
- Sin dependencias nuevas; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` sin cambios.
- No se añadió `mu` al `FreeBodyWidget`: `WIDGETS.md` no lo declara en sus props y la fricción llega como una fuerza más de la lista, como en el «Explora» de T-2.1.

## Spec gaps abiertos

ninguno

- [x] Solo archivos de los entregables
- [x] CI en verde

- [x] Tests con valores dorados
- [x] (widget) entrada en WIDGETS.md, stories, captura, a11y, i18n
- [ ] (content) no aplica

~150 k tokens · ~35 min

author: alexander-turner
body:
With AI review off, which is the shipped default, a tool call left no record on the host's audit log: the guest dispatcher returned before posting, and the host answered 503 to any `/check`. The dispatcher now posts each call once and the host records that the request arrived, judging nothing. Every record also carries its own provenance. This is increments 1 and 3 of #6782, and its first acceptance criterion.

This moves a supervision boundary: the guest gains a new admission path onto the host's audit log in a session nothing judges. The diff also carries two obvious bugs in their own commits, a file-size paydown, and a fix for a delegate setup-phase test that red this PR's cross-platform shard. Nothing `MonitorPipeline.tla`, `MonitorGate.tla` or `AuditChain.tla` asserts moves: the first names the guest dispatcher as outside its arms, the second tracks a verdict and its source where this posture renders neither, and the third models a record's chain links rather than its fields. The acceptance criterion is NOT graded here — the `sbx-live` shard ran and declined, because this branch changes a guest-image input and no image is published for its revision, so the first round after merge is what grades it.

```
POST /check, judging leg off, tool_use_id tu-1
  before -> 503, nothing on the log
  after  -> 200 {"attempt":true,"ok":true}, one claimed audit-only record naming tu-1
```

- **Provenance.** `monitorlib/provenance.py` owns five writer-owned fields every record now carries inside its hashed core, and the walk refuses a claimed record asserting a host-only scope.
- **The attempt record.** `sandbox-policy/monitor-server.py` replaces the judge-off 503 with one claimed `audit-only` record drawn on the result budget, and a reply carrying no `hookSpecificOutput`.
- **Session start.** Each host writer opens the log with a record saying what the launch captures, so a reader can tell a session that recorded nothing from one that did nothing.
- **One log, two writers.** `services.bash` spawns the sink and the monitor against one `audit.jsonl`. Each write now seeds its seq, prev and epoch from that file under a cross-process lock, and both state the launcher's review posture.
- **The guest dispatcher.** `monitor-dispatch.mjs` posts once under a 1500 ms bound in the `off` posture and writes nothing to stdout. `poll` stays silent: a session reaches it only after the host endpoint or its port grant already failed.
- **Consumers.** `chain.is_verdict_record` is the one definition of which records are verdicts, so attempt records stop counting as calls. Two readers run where `monitorlib` does not import — a jq filter on the launch path, and the archive lister — so `scripts/gen_audit_verdict_selector.py` writes that predicate into both from the enums, and a pre-commit hook keeps them fresh.
- **Live grading.** `supervision-gap-control.bash` gains a third phase that boots the shipped posture and reads the attempt record back out of the host's own log.
- **Two obvious bugs.** The custom-leg audit call crashed at runtime, and `bin/subcommands/audit` counted claimed records as calls.
- **A raced test verdict.** The delegate setup-phase driver spawned the delivery as a two-second timer, so a slow shard landed its marker before the pass returned. The driver now holds that child until it has read the verdict.

## Decisions made

- Attempt and session-start records reuse `audit-only`, with `evidence_scope` telling them apart. A new decision value would be a second non-verdict vocabulary beside the one both guest daemons already write.
- Attempts draw on the result-record budget. The gate bucket writes a witnessed `DENY` on its first refusal, which is a verdict-shaped record in a session nothing judged.
- The two outside readers get a generated region rather than a shared JSON file. Deriving the enums from JSON would drop their static typing, and jq must still run with no Python at all.

## Review focus

Read `write_audit` in `glovebox-monitor/src/monitorlib/audit_sink.py` first: two host processes append to one log, so the seq it assigns is correct only under the sidecar lock, and one screen cannot show that second writer. The part I am least sure of is the dispatcher's 1500 ms attempt bound, which is chosen against a dead host rather than measured.

## Lessons Learned

- The provenance fields were added at the writer and every direct call site, but `custom_legs.py` passed the writer as an untyped callback, so the missed site failed at runtime instead of at type-check. A `Protocol` on that parameter is what makes the next such call site fail early.
- Narrowing the history census to "a verdict or a claimed kind" also dropped a record whose decision is absent or corrupt, which are calls that happened. `evidence_scope` already names the set the drop was for, so the scope check alone is the whole rule.

author: wrenchtokeys
body:
Closes **C3 · Findability** (`docs/strategy/IMPROVEMENT_SESSIONS.md`), the marketing-site scope C1 explicitly deferred and the last piece of step 6 in `PRODUCT_DIRECTION.md`. The 2026-09-17/18 readiness audit found five gaps; all five are closed here.

Two decisions were Drake's and are recorded in the session doc: **Plausible Cloud behind a first-party proxy** for analytics, and **five guides published** (sales tax, progressive pricing, multi-break, getting paid on time, warranty).

## Analytics that does not move the CSP

`common/analytics.py` serves Plausible's tracker at `/js/p.js` and forwards the beacon at `/pa/event`, both on our own origin. The allowlist stays `'self'` plus Turnstile — adding `plausible.io` to `script-src` and `connect-src` would have re-opened the S1/S17 argument on an app that takes card payments. Self-hosting was the alternative and was rejected on ops: ClickHouse plus Postgres plus upgrades is a second system to keep alive, and the thing being measured is five marketing URLs.

The proxy adds the two headers Plausible cannot otherwise see, because from its side the client is our server. It takes the **right-most** `X-Forwarded-For` hop, not the left-most: the EB load balancer appends the peer address, so everything to its left is whatever the client typed, and reading `[0]` would have let any visitor choose the country their pageview was counted in.

Both failure paths are quiet on purpose — an upstream outage serves an empty script with `Cache-Control: no-store`, a failed forward returns 202 — so a Plausible incident can never put an error in a prospect's console.

The tag renders for a **signed-out reader only**. "Public shell" looked like the rule and is not one: `/onboarding/` and a signed-in owner reading a guide both wear it.

Off entirely unless `PLAUSIBLE_DOMAIN` is set — no tag, and both routes 404.

## Five help guides published

`'public': True` in `HELP_TOPICS` is the only switch, and `public_topics()` is read by the view, `sitemap.xml` and `robots.txt`, so a guide cannot be published in one place and gated in another. The thirteen written for an account holder still redirect to `/login/` with `?next=` intact, and the hub stays signed-in only.

**Publishing a page is not the same as publishing a URL, and that was the actual work.** Every guide extended `base_app.html` — a shop's own branded navbar with a user menu — and each of the five carried a deep link into Settings, the guide hub, or (in "Get paid on time") a gated guide. Served as-is, a visitor arriving from Google would have been shown a shop's app chrome and four links that bounce them to a sign-in page. That is the exact defect C1's switching section shipped with for four months. The view now picks the shell, the deep links and the thumbs widget are authenticated-only, and the signed-out footer is the other four published guides plus one CTA. A test asserts no published guide renders an href a visitor cannot follow.

## Everything else

- `{% page_meta %}` (`core/templatetags/seo.py`) emits description, canonical, Open Graph and the Twitter card from one call. `/pricing/`, `/terms/`, `/privacy/`, `/sms/` and `/contact/` had a `<title>` and nothing else; each now carries its own sentence.
- `summary` → `summary_large_image`, with a 1200×630 crop of the real dashboard capture (`scripts/og_card.py`). Never a hand-authored mock — UI_MAGIC S14's rule applies to the most-seen image the product has.
- `robots.txt` and `sitemap.xml` are generated from the URL conf plus the published-guide list. robots now keeps crawlers out of `/quote/`, `/invoice/`, `/pay/`, `/app/` and `/tech/` — a token route is a customer's own document — and no longer names `/portal/`, `/customer/` or `/setup-database/`, none of which the app serves. URLs come from `SITE_URL`, so staging cannot advertise production's.
- A guard on the landing page's JSON-LD price range, which C1 flagged as a rich-snippet liability and C2 showed drifts.

## Verification

- `tests/test_findability.py` — 30 tests, green.
- Guard set + `test_support_contact`: 364 tests, OK.
- Full suite: 5,002 tests. Every difference from the committed baseline was checked against a full run of `main` itself; see the comment below.
- `collectstatic` passes under `ForgivingManifestStaticFilesStorage`.
- Verified against the real service: the proxied script is the genuine 2,841-byte tracker, it honours `data-api`, and a POST through `/pa/event` returns Plausible's own `202 ok`. The one link that cannot be verified locally is the browser firing the beacon — the tracker refuses to send from `localhost` **and** when `navigator.webdriver` is true, which is its own bot filtering working. Confirm once on prod: load rssystems.io in a normal browser and watch for `POST /pa/event → 202`.

## Before this measures anything

No migration. Two `eb setenv` calls are Drake's:

1. Create the Plausible site for `rssystems.io`, then `eb setenv PLAUSIBLE_DOMAIN=rssystems.io`.
2. Verify Search Console by DNS TXT — or `eb setenv GOOGLE_SITE_VERIFICATION=<token>` and use the meta tag, which now renders on every public page. Then submit `https://rssystems.io/sitemap.xml`.

Worth doing the day this is read: query data accrues from the moment the property exists.

## One finding recorded, not fixed

`LoginAttempt.get_client_ip` has the same left-most-`X-Forwarded-For` bug. It feeds `SecurityAuditLog`, not the rate limiter (`django_ratelimit` keys on `REMOTE_ADDR`), so it is a data-accuracy problem rather than a throttle bypass — but every IP in that audit log is client-controllable. Out of scope here; flagged for its own change.

body: The live homepage “Start your case review” funnel showed a broken Step 1 on mobile: a blank white input above the step label, literal **1234** between that input and the label, and a delivery-date control that didn’t match First name / Email / Year / Make. **Cause** - The Formspree `_gotcha` honeypot was the first control in the form. `.hero-form input` (and the case-review page’s matching rules) restyled it as a normal field, and `.hero-form .intake-hp { width: auto }` overrode the hide width. - Progress markers were literal `1` `2` `3` `4` text nodes. When those circles collapsed, they read as **1234**. **Fix** - Delivery date is now the first Step 1 field: label above a `type="date"` input, same layout as the fields below. - “Step 1 of 4 — Delivery date” sits cleanly above the fields. - Honeypot moved off the visible step, wrapped with `aria-hidden`, `tabindex="-1"`, `autocomplete="off"`, and clip/clip-path `!important` hide CSS that beats hero-form input styles. No value (no 1234 leak). - Progress numbers come from CSS `::before`, so they cannot render as “1234” if styles fail. Homepage and case-review assets are cache-busted (`?v=intake-step1`) so GitHub Pages/Netlify pick up the CSS/JS. **Verified on mobile-width Chrome:** no stray input, no 1234, labeled date field first. [Fixed Step 1 intake on mobile](https://cursor.com/agents/bc-37bf7590-fd59-54bb-9002-09cff9406206/artifacts?path=%2Fopt%2Fcursor%2Fartifacts%2Fscreenshots%2Fintake-step1-mobile.png) To show artifacts inline, enable in settings.

author: rileyr
body:
Card 11 of the GH #646 recursive-workflow plan, stacked on #702 (card 10, accepted). Merge order: #696 → #700 → #701 → #702 → this. The substrate fix the card 10 review asked for is merged (#704, `aa66bf15`).

## What it does

`TaskRun` in `dna/core/workflow_runtime.hl` is the resident of one admitted Task, root or child: it holds the bound recipe, decoded into its own catalog at birth, and from it the leaves and children of every step, and births the one `WorkflowRun` that runs them. `Executions` is the Task owner the contract names, one per scope: it accepts every `TaskRun`, never releases one, and births one per Task id — a root asked of it (`ExecutionAsked`, its admission already in the record as card 07 leaves it) or a child asked by its parent Task. One engine runs every level; there is no separate child path and no hardcoded one-step child.

**A child member.** A step that dispatches one asks its own Task (`ChildRequested`, keyed by the parent task), which holds the recipe the child is bound in. The Task cuts the subtree the recipe bound under that child, exactly, and asks the owner (`ChildAdmitRequested`, keyed by scope); a request naming a child the recipe does not bind under that step and key is ignored. The child proposes its own `workflow.admitted` — parent, spawning step, member key, the subtree — which the card 06 projection accepts only for what the parent bound, from a step that is registered, active and unsettled; it runs only once that landed. Refused by the record, it holds and re-proposes on `RecordResumed` or when its spawning step is fenced; refused by the state, it retires under the settled or fenced spawning step, exactly as a never-admitted leaf does.

**Parent completion.** A child that settled tells the step that spawned it once (`ChildSettled`, keyed by that step) after its row landed. The step counts the exact child bound under the key — a settlement for another Task under the key, for a key that is no child of the step, for the wrong step, or delivered again changes nothing — and a failed child fails the step at once, as a failed leaf does. No barrier counts settlements: the projection's join is by identity and kind (card 06), the step's by the bound child id.

**Cancellation reaches down.** A step fenced by its Task's cancellation cancels a running child through the child's own `workflow.settled cancelled` proposal, so the fence reaches every level below and each drains and reclaims from the leaves upward.

## The oracle (`dna/tests/workflow_children_test.hl`, native)

The contract's canonical three-level example (`close-month` → `collect-receipts` → `chase-supplier`):

- **A delayed grandchild prevents root D from starting**: A, the child's B1 and the grandchild's C1 are requested, in that order, and nothing more; the root's second step is not registered; D is not requested until C1 answers, then the settlement climbs (grandchild → child's step 1 → child → root's step 0 → D) and the root settles done.
- **A failed grandchild blocks the ancestors' later steps**: C1 tried twice (its allowance), then its step, the grandchild, the child's step 1, the child, the root's step 0 and the root fail in turn; D's step is never born.
- **Wrong-step / duplicate child settlement does nothing**: a leaf's key, another root's child under the key, the grandchild's settlement delivered to the root's step, the same settlement delivered to the child's other step, and the real settlement delivered again after completion.
- **Two concurrent roots, two uses of one definition, never one id**: t1 and t3 run at once with distinct child and grandchild ids (six admissions), and t3's grandchild answering first advances only t3.
- **A child admission the record refuses once**: nothing of the child runs (no step registered, no workflow born) until `RecordResumed` lands it once; a child request naming the wrong step and the real one asked again birth nothing.
- **The root cancelled while the grandchild's leaf is out**: child and grandchild settle cancelled, the leaf settles under the fence, D is never born, the tree reclaims, and the leaf's late reply is recorded.
- **Cleanup from the leaves upward**: the reclamation order in the observed lives is C1's Work → the grandchild's step → its workflow → its Task → the child's step that invoked it → the child's Task → the root's step → … → the root's Task.

## Mutation evidence

| mutation of `workflow_runtime.hl` | result |
|---|---|
| child settlement matched by key only | fails: the root's step does not complete on the real child |
| a failed child does not fail the step | fails: the child's step 1 does not fail |
| the fence does not reach a running child | fails: child and grandchild never settle cancelled |
| child runs before its admission landed | fails: a workflow of the refused child is born |
| child request answered from the wrong recipe node | fails: the forged request reaches the owner |
| executions owner births a Task twice | fails: repeated requests birth executions |
| held child admission not re-proposed on resume | fails: the admission never lands |
| child settlement not deduplicated at the step | survives: equivalent by set semantics (a repeated done adds nothing, a repeated failed keeps the first failed member) |
| child settlement told to the step twice | survives: equivalent for the same reason |

## Docs

`spec/dna.md` (new section "Workflow execution: child workflows"), `dna/WORKFLOW-CONTRACT.md` (§5 item 5 fence-reaches-down proof, §9 resident-type note, §11 row), `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/src/dna/reference.md`.

Stop line respected: no recursive engine fork; no parent barrier based on a settlement count.

body:
<!-- ccr-slack-attribution -->
> Opened from Slack by Mike Brown via Claude. Session: https://claude.ai/code/session_01Rz1rFsyfzUP6wJWt9wntv2

## What this fixes

When a request drops mid-flight (`fetch()` rejects with `TypeError: Failed to fetch`) or the platform answers with an HTML error page instead of JSON (`res.json()` rejects with `SyntaxError: Unexpected token '<'`), these public and staff surfaces rendered the browser's internal error text verbatim. They now show the plain translated `common.connectionError` sentence from #2352 (`lib/http/requestFailureCopy.ts`), keep the raw error in the console under a per-surface label, and still pass through any message the server sent on purpose. Existing English fallbacks are unchanged. No new message keys and no duplicate helper: every mount point sits under a provider whose slice includes `common` (root chrome, portal, or admin slice).

### Public
- `app/q/[token]/PublicEligibilityForm.tsx` (no-account eligibility form)
- `app/invite/page.tsx` (login-code lookup and invitation accept)
- `app/org/[slug]/outcomes/OrgOutcomesClient.tsx` (partner outcomes loader)

### Staff
- Counselor: `CounselorProfileForm`, `CounselorNotesPanel`, `AdvisorSessionNotesPanel`, `counselor/placements/page.tsx` (record placement), `AtRiskDashboard` (loader, status update, bulk acknowledge), `AtRiskDetailModal` (add note), `LabReviewQueue`, `LabEvidenceReview` (load and save), `TriageNudgePanel`, `StaffMemberResumePanel`
- Admin / leader: `admin/chapters/page.tsx` (loader), `leader/dashboard/page.tsx` (loader)
- Partner: `PartnerInviteMemberButton`
- Employer: `EmployerLoiForm`, `EmployerOutcomesDashboard` (loader is now a `useCallback` so the hooks rule is satisfied)
- Billing: `BillingPacketList` (send packet)

### Member loaders (cheap, same pattern)
- `ReadinessMemberClient`, `RefreshCourseraProgressButton`, `MobileProfileSkillsResume` (resume preview), `InterestProfilerClient` (questions, score, PDF export), `CareerCounselor` (session start; the transcript-save failure keeps its existing "start a new session" warning for connection failures too, since "try again" would be wrong there), `MemberLabWorkspace` (reload saved draft; the save path already special-cased `TypeError` with a more specific message and is left alone)

### Skipped and why
- `app/careers/CareersInterestForm.tsx`, `components/public/PublicInterestProfilerClient.tsx`, `components/forms/ParentalConsentForm.tsx`: no importer on master (no `app/careers/page.tsx`; the profiler and consent form are unmounted), so nothing reaches a user.
- `components/portal/tools/ElevatorPitchClient.tsx`: its fetch catch is already bare; the remaining `err.message` is the camera/microphone permission error, not a request.
- `components/portal/OtherProgramsList.tsx`, `kit/**`, the auth forms (#2353) and everything #2352 already covered.

## Before / after

Dev server on :3160, `/en/invite` login-code form, request to `/api/invite/validate` blocked (Playwright `route.abort('failed')`, which is exactly what a dropped connection produces):

- before: form alert reads `Failed to fetch`
- after: form alert reads `We couldn't connect right now. Check your internet connection and try again.`

Screenshots are in the session scratchpad (`forms2/shots/before-invite-code.png`, `after-invite-code.png`).

## Tests

- New `tests/components/public-staff-form-connection-failure.spec.tsx`: renders the real invite login-code form (public), `CounselorProfileForm` (counselor), `EmployerLoiForm` (employer, HTML 500 and dropped connection) and `BillingPacketList` (billing) against a fetch that rejects with `TypeError` or resolves with an HTML 500 body; asserts the translated copy, never the browser text, plus server-message pass-through. 5 of 7 cases failed before this change and all 7 pass after. Collected by the existing `tests/**/*.spec.tsx` include.
- `tests/components/lab-evidence-review.test.tsx`, `counselor-note-saves.spec.tsx`, `member-lab-workspace.test.tsx` and `components/portal/tools/CareerCounselor.test.tsx` now mount the message catalog (same approach as #2352 for the skill-mission test); their assertions are unchanged.
- `lib/http/requestFailureCopy.test.ts` (from #2352) is a `node:test` file: it is owned by `npm run test:unit` (`scripts/test-unit.mjs` globs `lib/**/*.test.ts`), which `ci-gate.yml` runs, and it executes and passes there (`ok 931`/`ok 932` in the TAP output). Vitest reporting "No test files found" for it is expected for a node-owned suite, so it is deliberately not added to `VITEST_LIBRARY_SPECS` (that manifest is for suites that import `vitest`).
- `tsc --noEmit` clean; eslint clean on changed files apart from the pre-existing `jsx-a11y/label-has-associated-control` warning in `EmployerLoiForm.tsx` (present on master); `npm run test:unit` 1757 pass / 0 fail; full `vitest run` green.

Stakes touched: none (`.github/workflows/locked-product-stakes.yml` list checked; no locked file changed).

Note on history: the second commit is the merge of `origin/master` (#2353). It conflicted only in generated `docs/knowledge-base/generated/*` files and was mistakenly recorded under a `chore(kb)` message with the conflict markers still in those generated files; the following commit regenerates the index on the merged tree (`node scripts/knowledge-index.mjs --check` reports `changedOutputs: []`). Source files were never in conflict (tsc, eslint and the suites were re-run on the merged tree). Not amended, since that would need a force-push.

body:
## What was wrong

A number written as an argument to a model head took the width the rule that reached the head runs in, and it should take the width the head's body uses that parameter at. Every rule in the tree stays at one width from top to bottom, so the two are the same number everywhere today, and they come apart the moment an addressing mode is reached through from a rule of another width.

The rule from the issue:

```
(rule (lower (load.i32 (add.i64 (value.i64 a) (mul.i64 (value.i64 i) (iconst.i64 4)))))
      (x64.mov_rm_32 (amode_base_index_scale a i 4))
      ...)
```

`amode_base_index_scale` has no width in its name, so it took the rule's width, which is 32 because the rule loads an `i32`. The four went into the parameter map as a 32 bit literal and the mismatch came out inside `(bvmul index scale)`, where `index` is a 64 bit address register, as `bvmul is given something 64 bits wide and something 32 bits wide`.

## Why this does not do what the issue says to do

The issue asks for each parameter's width to be worked out once per head by reading the body. That means a second walk with its own context propagation over CONVERSION, MEMORY, CONCAT, the solver builtins, `float_op`, `float_test`, REINTERPRET, CROSSING and head expansion, which is the whole of what `write_at` already does. Two copies of that rule, kept in step by hand, is a worse thing to own than the bug is.

So the number is carried into the body instead. A literal argument is not written where the application sits, it becomes a `Bound::Number` in the parameter map, and it is written out at the point the body names it, at whatever width the body is being read at there. That is the one interpreter answering the question, in the place it already knows the answer.

The check the issue asks for is still there. A `Cell<Option<u32>>` beside the number records the width it was first written at, and a body that goes on to use the same parameter at a different width is refused and says which two widths. Anything other than a number already got that for free, since two different sorts flowing out of one binding would have been caught downstream, and this holds a model entry to the same standard for the one kind of argument with no width of its own.

One thing the deferral needs that is easy to miss. `beside`, `combine` and `reach` all ask whether an argument is a number, and inside a body a carried number is a `Var`, not an `Int`. Without teaching them to ask the bindings as well, `beside` would have short circuited at `(bvmul index scale)` and handed back the rule's width again, and nothing would have changed. That is what `numberish` is for.

## The smaller half

`fail(path, term, said)` was given the rule file's path and a term whose line and column are in the model file, so every error raised from inside a `semantics` body pointed at the wrong file. The issue's example reports `x86-64.rules:319:66`, and line 319 of the rule file is not that entry. `Meaning` now carries the path its body was read from and the body is written out under that path.

## Evidence

`build-tools/rucc-verify/tests/widths.rs` is five tests: the scale from the issue comes out `(_ bv4 64)` and not `(_ bv4 32)`; the rule's width is not what a number in a head takes; `(x64.bit_of_8 x 1)` still gives the one a single bit, which is the case the issue says the obvious fix would break; a body using one number at two widths is refused and names both; and a complaint about a body reports the model file.

On server3, at 5d4ef86e:

- `cargo fmt --all --check` clean.
- `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` clean.
- `RUCC_REQUIRE_SOLVER=1 cargo test -p rucc-verify`: 76 tests, all ok.
- `cargo xtask ci`: every check passed.
- The shipped rule set discharges unchanged. `x86-64.rules` 294 rules with the one bounded proof `docs/UNVERIFIED.md` already lists, then `canonical` 20, `compare` 72, `safety` 7, `simplify` 181, `strength` 40 and `width` 66, all at full width, none bounded, none refused. The `safety` file was timed on server2 rather than server3, because server3 was carrying another session's gate at a load average of 27 on 8 cores and z3 gave up on one 64 bit symbolic rule inside its 300 second budget there; on an idle machine all 7 discharge in 114 seconds.

Closes #915.

author: hanaroline
body:
제안서 산출물을 **화면(proposal.html) · 엑셀** 두 벌로 줄입니다.

PPT 에서는 자산배분 작업을 할 수 없습니다 — 화면이나 엑셀에서 다 고친 뒤 결과만 옮기는 자리였습니다. 그 한 벌을 위해 렌더러(pptxgenjs)와 조정안 JSON 내보내기를 유지할 값이 없어 접습니다.

## 빼기 전에 무엇이 딸려 있는지 봤습니다

| | |
|---|---|
| 워크플로 | 제안서 PPT 를 만드는 워크플로 **없음** |
| CI (`pr-check.yml`) | 제안서 스크립트를 건드리지 **않음** |
| 문서 | PPT 를 가리키는 문서 **없음** |
| `scripts/make_deck.mjs` · `verify_deck_claims.py` | **다른 덱** — 손대지 않았습니다 |
| `package.json` 의 `pptxgenjs` | `make_deck.mjs` 가 아직 씁니다 — **남겼습니다** |

지운 것은 `scripts/build_proposal_pptx.py`, `scripts/proposal_deck.mjs`, `고객제안서_자산배분.pptx`, 그리고 화면의 「조정안 (PPT용)」 단추와 그 내보내기입니다(그 JSON 을 받는 쪽이 없어졌습니다).

## 그런데 CSV 가 화면에서 고친 것을 안 싣고 있었습니다

제안값(`plan.w`)과 처음 고른 상품(`D.products`)을 그대로 적고 있어서, **비중을 고치고 상품을 빼도 CSV 에는 고치기 전 것이 나갔습니다.**

지금까지 드러나지 않은 까닭이 있습니다 — 조정안 JSON 이 조정 결과를 제대로 들고 있어서 그쪽으로 가려져 있었습니다. **그 JSON 을 없애면 CSV 가 유일한 자료 내보내기가 되므로**, PPT 를 빼기 전에 CSV 부터 고쳤습니다.

- 비중·상품을 `effAll()` / `S.sel` 에서 읽습니다
- 상품별 **배분액** 열을 더했습니다
- 머리에 「화면에서 조정함 / 성향 기준 제안값」을 적습니다

## 고치면서 한 번 넘어졌습니다

파이썬 `portfolio()` 는 한글 키(`과거1년실적`)를, 화면 `metrics()` 는 영문 키(`ret`)를 냅니다. 한글 키를 옮겨 적었더니 **CSV 단추가 통째로 죽었습니다** — 눌러도 아무 일도 일어나지 않습니다. 빌드에 넣어 둔 「화면 띄우기 검사」와 실제 클릭 테스트로 잡았습니다. `node --check` 는 이런 것을 못 잡습니다.

## 확인

| | 결과 |
|---|---|
| CSV 조정 반영 | 브라우저에서 국내주식 5.0% → **12.0%** 로 고치고 국내ETF 1 종을 뺀 뒤, CSV 가 `12.0%` · `1,200만원` 과 남은 **4 종**을 싣는 것을 확인 |
| 화면 | 띄우기 검사 통과 — 도넛·범례·묶음·표·상품 모두 채워짐, 콘솔 오류 0 |
| 인쇄 | A4 **3 쪽** 그대로 |
| 엑셀 | 재생성 — 시트·수식 변화 없음 |
| PPT 자취 | 저장소 전체 검색해 남은 참조 **0** |

body:
Moves the `lithos-llm` pin from `55add45` to `43a42ac28e9d9bcf40a91abc02be4f12ca274ebb` (18 commits: the Vercel and TypeSafe providers, `Client::evaluate`, and the adapter/codec schema split from lithoscomputer/lithos-llm#12 and #13) and the two Pebble pins from `a39f43e` to `67c9f486dd28f15c04e8d590a91e6f5563f7605d`, Pebble's `main`, which pins the same lithos-llm revision so the graph holds one lithos-llm crate. The twins pins stay at `ca45f0e5`: `cargo tree -i twin-core` shows one source, and Pebble's twin dependency never enters this graph. The pinned-revisions table in `crates/fabro/acceptance/CONTRACT.md` and the README citation move with the manifests; `mise run check:pins` reports "pins agree".

## The breaks

- **Removed Cargo features.** `openai`, `anthropic`, `gemini`, and `openai-compatible` each meant `runtime` and are gone. Three manifests drop them: `fabro/frontend`, `attractor/steps`, and `petri/lib`. `runtime` is present wherever the client is needed.
- **Catalog schema.** `adapter` now defaults to `http`, `codecs = [...]` replaces `codec`, and the loader rejects the old `codec` key and the four protocol-named adapter ids. Six sites migrated: the three `fallback.rs` providers become `codecs = ["openai-responses"]`, and three test catalogs keep their custom `test-adapter` id with `codecs = ["test-codec"]`.

No code change was needed: Petri names none of the removed lithos-llm items, and the Pebble API delta is crate-private to Pebble.

## Verification

`mise run check` passed end to end on the committed tree: fmt, clippy, actions audit, bundles, pins, whitespace, remote tests, 1563 tests, doctests, release build. `GIT_SSH_COMMAND=false cargo fetch --locked` passed. Three timing-sensitive tests flaked under a machine load average of 50 to 70 during earlier runs; each reproduced on unchanged `origin/main` at the same rate and passed in isolation on both trees, so no test was changed.

**Not run:** `mise run test:fabro:differential` and `check:fabro:readiness`, which the acceptance contract names as the gate after a pin move. `crates/fabro/HANDOFF.md` lines 41-42 still cite the old shas; they describe what Fabro `main` holds rather than Petri's pins, so they were left.

author: cwhorton
body:
## What Changed

Three call sites built an identical AJAX person-search TomSelect against
`GET /api/persons/search/{query}` by hand. The `valueField`/`labelField`/`searchField` triple and
the `load` callback — the 2-character guard, the `fetch`, the `.catch(() => callback())` — were
byte-for-byte the same in all three; everything around them had drifted (two CSS class
conventions, two of three setting `dropdownParent: "body"`, one setting a placeholder, one
setting `render`, none setting `maxOptions`).

This adds `webpack/common/person-select.ts` — a non-entry shared module in the style of
`webpack/common/fc-locale.js` — and moves **all three** copies onto it:

| Site | Now |
|---|---|
| `webpack/event-checkin.js` walk-in `.person-search` pair (`#child` / `#adult`) | `initAllPersonSelects()` |
| `webpack/event-checkin.js` check-out supervisor modal (`#checkoutBySelect`) | `attachToModal()` |
| `src/skin/js/GroupView.js` `.personSearch` "Add Member" | `window.CRM.initPersonSelect()` |

No `new TomSelect` remains in `webpack/event-checkin.js`, and no hand-written
`/api/persons/search/` fetch remains outside the module.

The module exports:

- `initPersonSelect(el, opts)` — the shared settings plus optional `endpoint`, `mapResult`,
  `placeholder`, `render` and `onChange`. `window.CRM.root` is read lazily inside `load()`, not
  captured at module scope, because `window.CRM` is populated by inline PHP script that runs
  after the bundles execute.
- `initAllPersonSelects(opts, root)` — scans **both** `.personSearch` and `.person-search`, so no
  `.php` template changes were needed.
- `attachToModal(modalEl, selector, opts)` — registers the `shown.bs.modal` → init /
  `hidden.bs.modal` → `destroy()` pair once, with an `onInit` hook for post-init setup.

Volunteer Management v2 (#9701) needs this picker on five screens (#9707, #9709, #9711, #9712)
against a different endpoint; without this it would have added a fourth, fifth and sixth copy.

### Two deliberate behaviour changes

Both are at the **walk-in check-in selects** (`#child` / `#adult` in
`src/event/views/checkin.php`), and both come from the shared defaults:

1. **They gain `dropdownParent: "body"`.** This is #9488's fix, which landed on the other two
   sites but not on these — even though they sit inside a `.card > .card-body`, exactly the
   container that clips the dropdown. This is the bug the new Cypress spec pins.
2. **They gain `maxOptions: null`.** Every site previously inherited TomSelect's silent default
   of 50 (#9677). Harmless today only because the endpoint hardcodes `limit(15)`
   (`src/api/routes/people/people-persons.php`) — the cap was invisible, not absent.
   Note this trades against the guidance in `frontend-development.md` that type-to-search pickers
   *want* a cap; the issue asked for `maxOptions: null`, so that is what landed. Easy to flip to a
   default of `50` in `person-select.ts` if you would rather keep the cap for search pickers.

Nothing else changed behaviour. The group "Add Member" flow, the check-in `tomselect:change`
wiring, the "Assign to me" buttons, the check-out pre-population and the clear/reset handlers all
behave as before.

### Decision taken in this PR — maintainer's to overturn

The issue left `src/skin/js/GroupView.js` open: it is loaded as a plain `<script src>` from
`src/groups/views/group-view.php` and is not part of any bundle, so it can only consume the
helper through a `window.CRM.*` export.

**This PR migrates it**, exposing `window.CRM.initPersonSelect` / `window.CRM.initAllPersonSelects`
from `webpack/skin-core.js` — the same pattern `webpack/common/email-composer.ts` already uses for
`window.CRM.emailComposer`. The alternative (leave GroupView.js for a follow-up) would have left
one of the three copies standing and the `window.CRM` surface undecided. Say the word and that
commit comes out.

Two smaller calls worth flagging:

- The module takes the TomSelect constructor from `window.TomSelect` (set by `skin-core.js`)
  rather than `import TomSelect from "tom-select"`. There is no `splitChunks` config, so importing
  it would have embedded a second copy of the library in the `event-checkin` bundle and given that
  page two distinct TomSelect classes.
- `tom-select` ships no type declarations, so the instance members this codebase uses are
  declared in `webpack/types/window.d.ts` alongside the new option interfaces, following the
  existing `CRMEmailComposerOptions` pattern.

No `webpack.config.js` change was needed — the module is imported, not an entry, exactly like
`webpack/common/fc-locale.js`.

Two agent-skill files are updated: `frontend-development.md` points future work at the shared
module (and reconciles its `maxOptions` guidance with the change above), and `cypress-testing.md`
records how to target one body-mounted TomSelect dropdown.

The branch is merged up to current `master` (the merge was clean; only the two skill files
overlapped with master's changes).

### Files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `webpack/common/person-select.ts` | new shared module (+162) |
| `webpack/event-checkin.js` | both pickers onto the module (-80 net) |
| `webpack/skin-core.js` | `window.CRM.initPersonSelect` / `initAllPersonSelects` exports |
| `webpack/types/window.d.ts` | TomSelect instance + option interfaces |
| `src/skin/js/GroupView.js` | Add Member picker onto `window.CRM.initPersonSelect` |
| `cypress/e2e/ui/events/standard.event-checkin-person-select.spec.js` | new, 4 tests |
| `cypress/e2e/ui/groups/standard.tomselect-dropdownparent.spec.js` | two assertions narrowed (see below) |
| `.agents/skills/churchcrm/frontend-development.md`, `cypress-testing.md` | guidance |

Fixes #9819

## Type

- [ ] ✨ Feature
- [ ] 🐛 Bug fix
- [x] ♻️ Refactor
- [ ] 🏗️ Build/Infrastructure
- [ ] 🔒 Security

## Testing

New spec: `cypress/e2e/ui/events/standard.event-checkin-person-select.spec.js` (4 tests) — there
was no UI spec for `/event/checkin/{id}` at all. It creates an event via the API in `before`,
checks person 1 in, and covers:

- `#child` searches, renders its dropdown as a direct child of `<body>`, and selects a person
- `#adult` does the same
- both keep their `data-placeholder`
- the check-out modal's picker initialises on `shown.bs.modal` and leaves no orphaned dropdown
  after close

Assertions are scoped to `body > .ts-dropdown > #<select id>-ts-dropdown` rather than a bare
`body > .ts-dropdown`: TomSelect appends the dropdown at construction time and ids its
`.ts-dropdown-content` after the select, and this page now has several body-mounted dropdowns at
once.

Against **unmodified master** the two body-mount assertions fail — that is the missing #9488 fix:

```
4 tests, 2 passing, 2 failing
AssertionError: Expected to find element: `body > .ts-dropdown > #child-ts-dropdown`, but never found it.
AssertionError: Expected to find element: `body > .ts-dropdown > #adult-ts-dropdown`, but never found it.
```

After the change: **4 / 4 passing**.

### `standard.tomselect-dropdownparent.spec.js` needed a two-line narrowing

Its check-out test asserted that **no** `body > .ts-dropdown` survives the modal close. That held
only while the walk-in pickers on the same page were *not* body-mounted; now that they are, their
dropdowns legitimately persist and the assertion failed. Both of its assertions are now scoped to
`#checkoutBySelect-ts-dropdown`, which restores the original intent — and makes the "exists" half
meaningful again, since a bare `body > .ts-dropdown` would now be satisfied by a neighbouring
picker's dropdown even if the modal's were broken. No test was removed or weakened. 3 / 3 passing.

### Regression runs on the merged branch (Docker test stack, seeded)

| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| `cypress/e2e/ui/groups/` (8 specs, incl. the Add Member picker in `standard.tomselect-dropdownparent.spec.js`) | 61 / 64 — the 3 failures are the "Remove an assigned property" block of `standard.group.properties.spec.js`, whose own `beforeEach` logs `No gro

author: morehao
body:
## Why

`backend/pkg/middleware` is a middleware package, but a large part of its exported surface was not middleware: identity context keys and readers, the OIDC key-source assembly (config → dependency object), request-header parsers, and transition aliases. That mixed placement had two concrete costs:

1. **The read side of identity was trapped in the auth middleware.** `svcauth` (a business service) and `rpapi/internal/middleware/directory.go` (a policy middleware) each imported `pkg/middleware` only to read the caller identity. The direction is wrong: authentication belongs to the middleware, while "which identity is this and is it allowed to do this" belongs to whoever enforces policy — and that code should not depend on the authentication package.
2. **The middleware package owned startup wiring and the cross-app assembly contract.** `auth` → `gateway` → the other apps injected `pkg/middleware.KeySource`, so every app's `Init` signature named the middleware package; and two structurally identical interfaces (`middleware.KeySource` = `rp.KeySource`, `pkg/goidc.KeySource` = `logout.JWKS`) described the same capability, so access-token verification and back-channel logout could not share one source.

This PR moves each responsibility to the package that owns it. It is a pure restructuring: no route, response envelope, schema, or `sdk/` change, and the identity context keys keep byte-identical string values.

## What changed

### New `pkg/identity` — the request identity contract

`SetClientID` / `SetOIDCIdentity` (write side, called by the auth middleware) and `ClientIDFromContext` / `OIDCIdentityFromContext` (read side, used by services and policy). Context key literals are unchanged, so `client_id` and the full `rp.Identity` are still where they were; only the owner of the API moved. Nil-ctx and wrong-type reads return nil.

### `pkg/goidc` → `pkg/oidckit` — one rp-side OIDC capability package

- `keys.go` takes over the config → `KeySource` assembly (`NewKeySourceFromConfig` / `ResolveKeySource`) that used to live in `pkg/middleware`. Priority is explicit JWKS URL → issuer → local signing-key snapshot; a configured-but-unreachable JWKS endpoint is an **error**, never a silent fallback to the local snapshot, because silent degradation turns "key rotated, so every token 401s" into "starts up fine".
- `KeySource` is now a single alias of `sdk/rp.KeySource`, so the verifier, the middleware option, and the back-channel logout receiver share one type. `TestKeySourceIsSDKAlias` hands it to `rp.NewVerifier` and `ParseLogoutToken` without a conversion, so the alias cannot quietly degrade into two look-alike interfaces.
- `kid` derivation stays duplicated on the OP side (`svcoidc`) because `pkg` cannot import `apps`; both sides now assert the same golden `kid` literal instead.

### Deprecated transition APIs deleted

Confirmed zero in-tree callers, so they are gone rather than kept as shims: `middleware.OIDCCompatibleAuth`, `middleware.LoadSigningPublicKey`, `middleware.staticKeySource`, `middleware.KeySource`, `middleware.TokenClaims`, `middleware.ContextKeyClientID` / `ContextKeyOIDCIdentity`, and the middleware-side identity readers.

### `pkg/middleware` is middleware again

Exported surface goes from 26 funcs/types + 3 constants to 17: four `gin.HandlerFunc` producers (`OIDCAuth`, `ApiKeyAuth`, `NewApiKeyAuthMiddleware`, `SilentSSORequired`), their option builders, and the small callback types. `authHeaderKey` / `authBearer`, `extractApiKey`, `authenticateApiKey` are package-private, and the silent-SSO options use the named `SilentSSOOption` instead of raw func types. The write-only `apikey.ContextKeyUserType` is gone too.

## Compatibility

- No route, response envelope, DB schema, or frontend change; `sdk/` untouched (whitelist `stdlib + jwt/v5` still enforced by `make sdk-check-deps`).
- Identity context key strings are unchanged, so the built-in apps behave identically.
- Breaking only for out-of-tree importers of the removed deprecated symbols above; in-tree consumers now use `oidckit.NewKeySourceFromConfig` / `middleware.WithOIDCKeySource` and `pkg/identity`.

## Verification

- 7 modules build; `go vet ./...` clean; full test suite green, including a run under deliberate CPU load; `go test -race` on `pkg/identity`, `pkg/middleware`, `pkg/oidckit`.
- `make sdk-check-deps` and `make test-sdk` green.
- Each of the four commits builds independently in a `git worktree`, so the history is bisectable; the `goidc` → `oidckit` rename is its own commit and `git revert` restores it.
- Real gateway run: with no token, `/v1/rp/directory/members`, `/v1/platform/tenants`, `/v1/tenant/users` all return 401; `POST /oidc/bc-logout/{platform,tenant}` is routed (400, not 404); `/oidc/keys` returns 200; the startup window has zero JWKS-prefetch errors and zero panics.
- All four apps start standalone; with `auth` down, `rpapi` / `platformadmin` / `tenantadmin` log `key source unavailable`, still mount their routes and answer 401 (fail-closed) without panicking; once `auth` is up the warning disappears (JWKS fetch succeeds).

## Reviewer notes

- The work was planned as four commits; the rename and the key-source move are merged into one, because both edit the same regions of `oidc_auth.go` (the alias block and the assembly functions) and splitting them would have meant hand-building an intermediate state of a single file. Every commit in between was still verified to build.
- Not run: `make lint` — `golangci-lint` is not installed in this environment; `go vet` plus `gofmt -l` were used instead.
- Per-AC evidence lives in `.dsh/docs/plans/2026-09-19-pkg-oidc-boundary-plan.md` §10, which is git-ignored and therefore not part of this diff.

## Summary

Restore the `deploy` job in `🐳 Docker CI/CD` that POSTs the Dokploy deploy webhook once after `build` succeeds on `main`. This reverts the direction taken in #632.

## Why

Since #632, Dokploy has been redeploying through the Docker Hub repository webhook. That webhook fires once per pushed tag and manifest — the semver tags plus `canary`, and for each of those the amd64/arm64 images and their SBOM/provenance attestations — so a single workflow run redeployed Dokploy several times.

Calling the webhook from the workflow gives exactly one deploy per successful build. Unlike the #631 version, the job no longer skips silently when `DOKPLOY_WEBHOOK_URL` is unset: a missing secret fails the job instead of quietly never deploying.

## Follow-up (manual, before merging)

- [ ] Add the `DOKPLOY_WEBHOOK_URL` repository secret (Dokploy → application → Deployments → Webhook URL)
- [ ] Delete the Dokploy webhook on Docker Hub (`marukome0743/robopo` → Webhooks) so deploys are not triggered twice

## Test plan

- [ ] `🐳 Docker CI/CD` builds the `pr-N` image on this PR and the `deploy` job is skipped
- [ ] After merge, the `canary` push runs `deploy` once and Dokploy redeploys exactly once

成功したメインブランチのビルドごとに、Dockerワークフローから直接Dokployのデプロイを一度だけトリガーします。

author: atomchild411
body:
`IdleParkState::park` sleeps in 1 ms slices and re-reads `hot.interrupts` only
at the top of each one. An interrupt raised on another thread therefore waits
out the rest of the current slice before the CPU notices it — IOC device
lines, the compare timer's IP7, `set_interrupt`, and `Signal::Interrupt` from
the bus all pay it, and it is every interrupt that ends an idle stretch, which
is the common case for a sleeping guest process.

Measured from `fetch_or` on the raising thread to `park` returning on the CPU
thread, otherwise idle:

    sleep slices          649 us - 1.26 ms, spread across the slice
    park_timeout + unpark 6.2 - 6.8 us at every phase

The spread is the tell: the latency is not a fixed cost, it is wherever in the
slice the interrupt happened to land.

The parked thread registers itself and sleeps with `park_timeout`; the writers
unpark it after setting their bit. The slice stays as an upper bound — nothing
signals `running` or the `ci_clock` cycles threshold, so those are still
polled.

The ordering is the only subtle part, and it is a Dekker pattern: the parker
stores `PARKED = true` **before** its last look at the pending word, and each
writer sets its bit **before** reading `PARKED`, both `SeqCst`. Either the
parker sees the bit or the writer sees the flag; a wakeup cannot be lost. A
spurious unpark — the writer reads the flag just before the parker clears it —
leaves a token that ends the next `park_timeout` early, the loop re-checks and
parks again.

Every exit from the loop clears `PARKED`. The `ci_clock` exit is easy to miss
behind its feature gate, and a stale `true` would put every interrupt writer on
the mutex while the CPU is running, which is the cost the flag exists to avoid.

`an_interrupt_ends_the_park_without_waiting_out_the_slice` sweeps the interrupt
across the slice in 200 us steps and asserts the worst phase, so it cannot pass
on an interrupt that happened to land just before a boundary. It retries the
sweep up to three times, which cannot rescue a broken build — every sweep
contains a slow phase without the fix — but keeps a scheduling stall on a busy
machine from failing it. With the slices restored:

    worst-phase latency [1.254875ms, 1.256584ms, 950.542us] over 3 sweeps

`idle_park` is gated on the feature in `lib.rs` and `default` does not include
it, so none of this compiles into a default build or CI run.

    cargo test --release --features idle-pause --lib -- wake_tests

Note: `rules/perf/idle-pause-wake-the-parked-cpu.md`.

Two things worth stating plainly. `PARKER`/`PARKED` are module statics, which
assumes the one CPU thread this emulator has; a second would need them moved
into the core. And `unpark` on a thread that has already exited is a no-op, so
the handle left behind when a machine stops is harmless rather than something
the stop path has to clear — that is relied on, not overlooked.

Independent of #115, which is also in `idle_park.rs`: that one is about whether
to park at all (`update`), this one about how long to stay parked (`park`).
They merge cleanly. #115 is worth taking first — until it lands, a guest that
parks with every interrupt masked still hangs, and this change makes that hang
marginally busier, since each interrupt now unparks the thread to re-check a
condition that is still unsatisfiable. About a hundred extra wakeups a second
against the thousand the timeout already does, so it costs nothing measurable,
but the ordering is the sensible one.
