author: santoshkumarradha
body:
## What was wrong

A second hand-off in one conversation renames the first run's store to `plandb.db.1` and seeds a fresh one. Every read opened only the live store. The first run's row stayed on the rail, but its page, its parts and its notes could no longer be opened, and the `tasks` tool could no longer answer for it.

## What changed

- Reads take every ended store oldest first, then the live one. The listing carries each run's rows, and a task of any run opens by the id the rail shows. A root's id is the rail's number and is never reused; a part's id is random.
- Only the live run takes the six steering verbs. A task of an ended run answers `that task's run has ended`, and a test asserts the ended store's bytes are unchanged after every verb.
- An ended store never changes, so it is opened once and kept for the life of the conversation. The handles are given back when the conversation closes. The live store is still opened per read so another process's writes are seen.
- One function names the archives for the door that makes them and the reads that find them.
- With no archive the listing is byte for byte what it was, pinned by a test.

## Hosted drive on the real binary, 2026-09-19

Built from this branch merged with #1231 and #1232, because a rail row is not a door without #1231. `codeaf chat` with no flags, belt on. Two hand-offs, the second typed after the first had ended.

1. The session folder held `plandb.db` and `plandb.db.1`. The rail drew `#1` and `#2`.
2. A click on `#1` opened the first run's page: brief, folder, its three notes, its steps.
3. A note typed on that page was answered `that task's run has ended` on the page's own line, with the words left in the box.

## A defect this PR had, and how it was found

An earlier head of this PR froze a conversation's engine for good. It passed the cell's checker and the whole `internal/session` suite, and was found only by a real-binary drive in hosted mode.

- **What happened.** The reader that opens every run's store takes the plan's lock and returns a closer that releases it. With a plan armed and no store to open yet, it returned no stores, and all three callers returned on that before the line that deferred the closer. Nothing released the lock.
- **What a person would have seen.** A run whose rows stop moving, a third hand-off that never ends, and an engine that does not leave when the terminal is closed. It is a race on the first hand-off, so one drive in six hit it.
- **How it was found.** The engine from a failed drive was still alive an hour later and ignored a terminate signal. A goroutine dump showed `Agent.Close`, the plan listing over the wire, the run's driver and the turn loop all waiting on the same mutex.
- **The fix.** The helper unlocks before it answers that there is nothing to read, as the shipped single-store opener does, and each caller defers the closer on the line after the call. The failing test came first.
- **The law.** `internal/guard/lockcloser_test.go` covers every lock handed out through a returned closer, in two halves. The helper never answers nil while locked. Its caller writes no return before the closer is deferred or called, except on the first result being nil. Pointed at the leaking head it names the three exact lines. Two older helpers of this shape are on trunk and neither is exposed.

This is the argument for #1241, which puts that drive in the repo.

## Proof

- Whole `internal/session` on Spark under the box lock at 87dac1550: `ok github.com/Agent-Field/codeaf/internal/session 238.001s`, exit 0, 2026-09-19T04:04:37Z.
- Hosted, real binary, this head: `scripts/hosted-drive.sh` three times in a row, 15 of 15 each time.
- Laptop: build, vet, gofmt clean; the focused session set with the road ratchet, Schema, Prefix, Landing and Stand tests; `make test-laws` including the new law; manual and name gates; change entries. No prompt, schema or tool description changes.

## Order

Head 87dac1550 sits on santos/dev 1cbcb4b7d, which carries #1231, #1232 and #1240.

author: laird
body:
## Defect

`translate_messages` in `src/providers/anthropic.rs` — shared by the direct Anthropic adapter and the Vertex Claude translator (`src/providers/vertex/claude.rs`) — passes user content arrays through verbatim (`translated.push(m.clone())`; documented "MVP scope: string-only message content"). OpenAI-format `image_url` content parts therefore reach Anthropic-family backends untranslated.

## Symptom

Every image-bearing chat request routed to Claude-on-Vertex fails with:

```
400: Input tag 'image_url' found using 'type' does not match any of the expected tags: 'text', 'image', 'tool_use', 'tool_result', ...
```

Observed at volume (284+ occurrences in one day) from a downstream consumer's diagram-classification path.

## Fix

New `translate_content_block(s)` helpers in `anthropic.rs`, applied at every point `translate_messages` handles a content array (user turns, assistant array content, `tool_result` content). Both adapters get the fix for free since they share the function.

- `data:<media_type>;base64,<data>` → `{"type":"image","source":{"type":"base64","media_type":...,"data":...}}`
- any other URL → `{"type":"image","source":{"type":"url","url":...}}`
- legacy flat string form (`"image_url": "https://..."`) accepted alongside the nested `{url}` object
- text parts, string-only content, and already-native `image` blocks pass through **byte-identical**
- a malformed data URL (no comma, non-base64 encoding) or a url-less `image_url` part passes through verbatim without panicking, so the provider's own error names the real problem

## Testing

- TDD: the 5 new translation assertions failed on the unmodified tree, green after the fix; the pass-through/byte-identity tests were green before and after (proving no behavior change for existing traffic).
- New `image_content_tests` module in `anthropic.rs` (10 tests): string content byte-identical, text-only arrays byte-identical, data-URL → base64 block, https → url source, legacy flat string, mixed text+image ordering, malformed data URLs, url-less part, native image block pass-through, tool_result array translation.
- New Vertex-path test in `vertex/claude.rs`: `translate_request` body carries native `image` blocks for both data-URL and https parts.
- `cargo test --lib`: **419 passed, 0 failed** (default features, vertex included).
- `cargo test --test test_vertex --test test_messages --test test_anthropic_cache`: **97 passed, 0 failed**.
- Full integration-suite run (all ~60 test binaries) could not complete on my host — linking ~60 × ~470 MB debug test binaries exhausts its disk (same host-capacity limit noted on #65's PR). The suites covering the changed code are the three above, all green.
- `rustfmt --check` on both touched files: the only diffs are the 7 pre-existing hunks already present on `main` (verified against a pristine checkout); zero new. `cargo clippy --lib`: zero findings in either touched file.

## Reference

author: sfmskywalker
body:
Review follow-up to #1850, which **merged while the review round was still in progress** — so these two fixes did not make it in. Nothing here changes behavior of the Elsa 3 move itself; both changes are to architecture-test infrastructure.

## 1. `Path.Join`, not a guarded `Path.Combine`

The bot flagged `Path.Combine(repoRoot, root)` in `ModuleRoots`. My first fix guarded it with an `IsPathRooted` ternary — which the analyzer could not see through, and on reflection a human reader would not either.

`Path.Join` is the better answer: it does not discard earlier segments when a later one is rooted, so **the hazard is removed rather than guarded**. The explicit rejection stays, moved into a statement-bodied helper, because an absolute module root is a programming error worth failing on loudly. `Path.Join` is already the prevailing idiom in this test project.

Why this mattered enough to fix rather than wave off: `Combine` silently discarding everything before an absolute segment would redirect a guard's sweep *outside the repository*, and the guard would keep reporting green about whatever it found there. That is the same failure mode #1850 exists to fix.

## 2. A guard against the enumeration going vacuous — which was itself vacuous first

#1850 established that `ProjectFiles()` feeds fifteen guards, and that moving a module out of a root it was pinned to made all fifteen silently stop seeing that module while the suite stayed green. This adds `Project_enumeration_covers_every_module_root` so that cannot recur unnoticed.

**The first version of that guard was circular and worthless.** It iterated `ModuleRoots.All` — the same list the enumeration is built from — so removing a root from that list also removed it from the check, and the guard passed. I only caught it because I bite-proofed it and watched it *not* fail.

It now discovers roots from the working tree: any top-level directory holding a `.csproj` must contribute projects. `samples/`, `tools/` and `docs/` are excluded with reasons — `docs/reports/repros/` carries standalone reproduction projects attached to written reports.

## Evidence

| Direction | Result |
|---|---|
| Tree as it stands | guard **passes** |
| `extensions` removed from `ModuleRoots.All` | guard **fails**, naming exactly `extensions` |
| Same revert against the *first, circular* version | **passed** — the flaw |
| Full architecture suite on current `main` | **240/240** |

body:
## Summary
- Campaign `million-entity-render`, slice D0.2 (`fleet:wip` until the campaign checkpoint), stacked on the D0.1 PR: measure the lit response on the revoxelized staircase and decide whether it is the light on real steps or a defect.
- `scripts/render-revox-face-metric.py --shadow-overlay` reads a `--debug-overlay shadow` capture and compares every sun-facing interior pixel with the resampled lattice's own sun visibility (a 3D DDA from each face centre toward the demo's sun through the destination cells; sun-averted faces are excluded, since they get no direct light whatever the map says). Reports false shadow (expected lit) and missed shadow (expected occluded).
- Finding, cyan cube at zoom 8, five yaws, AO off: the demo's default authored-cell casting (`--source-face-shadows`) marks 75k–147k false self-shadow pixels at every yaw, whole half-faces across the cube; resampled-cell casting (`--voxel-face-shadows`) marks 0–9k. Only the caster geometry differs between the runs, so the tooth pattern in the lit captures is the authored caster cutting through the resampled receiver, not the staircase. What resampled casting still misses is the tread band behind each riser (all 24,696 expected occluded pixels at yaw 0) plus a few tread tips at 45°. AO darkens 6.9% of the cube by at most 5.9% (`render-ao-staircase-metric.py`), so it is not the source of the look.
- Decision (campaign ledger, `revoxelized-display-fidelity.md` § Direct sun): a revoxelized canvas casts from its resampled cells, the geometry its receiver reads and its display shows; the authored-cell caster is retired for that path in D0.3, which also traces the near-riser band through the surface receiver and re-blesses the canvas_stress floor-shadow references. No engine code changes in this slice.

## Test plan
- [x] `python3 scripts/tests/test_render_revox_face_metric.py` — `Ran 12 tests … OK` (sun classes, occlusion found on the rotated cube, false and missed detection, blank overlay); source-face and mixed-canvas suites `OK`; `ruff check scripts/` — `All checks passed!`; `scripts/lint_comment_refs.py` — none above budget.
- [x] Sun oracle on the ten shadow captures (five yaws × two caster modes), table in the design doc; every `fleet-run IRCanvasStress …` capture `ir-run: RESULT=CLEAN`.
- [x] `render-ao-staircase-metric.py` on the yaw-45 AO overlay against the D0.0 lit capture: `occluded_frac 0.0689`, `max_darkening 0.0588`.

## Decisions taken
- Revoxelized casters must be the resampled cells. Rejected: keeping authored casters for a smoother floor shadow (the object on screen is the staircase, and the campaign spirit puts receiver, caster and visible face on one geometry), and any receiver bias that hides the mismatch.

## Evidence
Retained under `docs/pr-screenshots/claude/million-entity-render-lit-staircase/` (shadow overlay, zoom 8, 2560x1440, AO off). Docs and Python only; no visual change to any demo.

| Authored casters, yaw 45 (magenta = shadowed) | Resampled casters, yaw 45 | Oracle errors on the authored capture (red = false shadow) |

| ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jakildev/IrredenEngine/380a6174f8de9d1c6b135e19e0e0fac2c6ca9874/docs/pr-screenshots/claude/million-entity-render-lit-staircase/revox1_shadow_source_yaw45.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jakildev/IrredenEngine/380a6174f8de9d1c6b135e19e0e0fac2c6ca9874/docs/pr-screenshots/claude/million-entity-render-lit-staircase/revox1_shadow_voxelface_yaw45.png) | ![](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jakildev/IrredenEngine/380a6174f8de9d1c6b135e19e0e0fac2c6ca9874/docs/pr-screenshots/claude/million-entity-render-lit-staircase/revox1_sun_errors_source_yaw45.png) |

Checkpoint 1 (2026-09-19). Fresh-context reviewer (Opus class): approve, nits only; all ten evidence rows and the AO numbers reproduced, the sun frame and the DDA verified against the demo's `kSunDirection` and a brute-force ray march (0 disagreements at that sun; 55 corner-graze ties at an off-axis sun, all DDA-conservative). author: monglong0214
body:
No-Issue: the runnable halves of #1036 and #1037. Neither closes here — both need a measured run, which needs a pilot and a budget.

**The study runs now.**

```
run.ts --cases X --seed S                     # plans; writes nothing
run.ts --cases X --execute --run-dir NEW \
       --actor node --actor-arg actor.cjs     # runs; writes evidence
report.ts over that directory                 # reads it back
```

### The actor is a command, not a model

That is the whole reason the loop could be verified **before a token was spent**: a node script that edits files and commits exercises the same code path a host CLI will. A real host invocation carries flags and a fake actor is a script the node binary runs, so one shape covers both — the zero-cost proof sits on the measured path rather than beside it. #1035 asks for exactly this separation.

The loop makes no decision of its own. The plan and reservation, phase order, invocation, snapshot, envelope, verdict and repair each come from their own module; what is here is wiring, and the wiring is the part that had no test until this existed.

- **A run directory is new, always** — two protocol revisions, case sets or budgets sharing a file is a file whose reader cannot tell them apart.
- **A pair the budget cannot fund whole stops the run** and records the refusal, because a run that quietly skipped would produce gaps that look like ordinary failures.
- **The report imports `node:fs` and the shared arithmetic and nothing that can spawn**, so #1037's "zero model/checker calls" is enforced by what is reachable rather than promised. It starts from the plan, keeps a planned pair whose episode never landed, and reports a feedback pass with an audit failure and no repair as a **detector miss** rather than folding the two verdicts together.

### Running it found two defects the unit tests could not

**`readManifest` discarded everything but the three fields a plan needs** — the discussion, staged files, checker and described checks were dropped, so a valid runnable manifest was refused with *"has no discussion"*. The plan path never reads those fields, so nothing had exercised the loss.

**My own report fixture wrote `over.score ?? true`**, which turns an explicit `null` into `true`: an unresolved row silently read as a pass. That is the `value || 0` mistake the accounting module forbids, in a test helper rather than in the code under test.

### Verification

Ten report cases and six execution cases against real git repositories and real child processes, then the whole thing driven through the CLI — a plan, an execute that wrote evidence, and a report read back from that evidence:

```
H1 — first workflow pass, three-level mean:
  OFF    0.0%    (1/1 rows observed, 0 unresolved, 1 source group(s))
  NATIVE 100.0%  (1/1 rows observed, 0 unresolved, 1 source group(s))
  difference +100.0 points
  relative reduction withheld — needs both means and a positive control
```

The relative reduction was withheld because the control mean was zero: the rule firing on real data rather than on a fixture.

Full suite 4750 passed, 4 skipped across 226 files, exit 0.

### Limits

**No model was called, and nothing here says anything about CommitLore's effect.** The actors are scripted — the `+100 points` above is what the script wrote, not what the product did. No real host has been exercised and no pilot has measured a per-episode cost.

This Pull Request introduces the **Advanced Llama Settings** configuration hub and custom UI components to manage fine-grained inference, routing, sampling, context, LoRA, embeddings, and diagnostics for Llama models:

   - Enabled `viewBinding = true` alongside Jetpack Compose to support generated view bindings for XML-based layouts and RecyclerView adapters.

2. **AdvancedSettings Model (`AdvancedSettings.kt`)**:

     - Connection parameters (Base URL, API key, timeouts, keep-alive, headers).
     - Router Mode configurations (fallback routing, load balancing, health checks).
     - Model selection (default, fallback, and routing list).
     - Inference & Compute (GPU layers, thread counts, batch sizes, CPU thread pinning, Flash Attention, mlock/mmap).
     - Generation parameters (max tokens, temperature, top_p, top_k, min_p, repetition penalty, frequency/presence penalties, stop tokens).
     - Sampling techniques (Mirostat mode, Mirostat tau/eta, dry run, TFS, typical p).
     - Context & Memory (context size, prompt cache, KV cache quant, slide window).

     - Embedding Settings (batch size, normalization).
     - Performance & Diagnostics (verbose logging, logprobs, latency metrics, debug mode).

3. **AdvancedSettingsViewModel (`AdvancedSettingsViewModel.kt`)**:
   - Reactive LiveData state (`settings`, `models`, `loading`, `error`, `saved`).
   - Persistent storage backed by `SharedPreferences`.
   - Input validation routines for network addresses, token limits, and numeric ranges.

4. **UI Layouts & Components (`fragment_advanced_llama_settings.xml`, `item_router_model.xml`, `RouterModeAdapter.kt`)**:
   - Nested scrollable Material Design 3 layout organized into distinct cards for each configuration domain.

5. **Fragment Implementation (`AdvancedSettingsFragment.kt`)**:
   - Bi-directional UI bindings, lifecycle observation, and safe input parsing.

body:
When visitors open the showcase app (such as on GitHub Pages), the application previously defaulted to an already-authenticated session because MSW initialized `currentUser` with Ada Lovelace's credentials.

This change switches the default auth state in mock handlers to unauthenticated (`null`). When visitors land on protected routes without an active session, they are redirected to `/login`, where they can explore the sign-in form or use the "Quick Demo Sign In" button to log in.

### Initial Auth Flow

#### Before
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Visitor opens showcase"] --> B["MSW initializes currentUser = Ada"]
    B --> C["GET /api/me returns 200"]
    C --> D["AuthContext sets user"]
    D --> E["ProtectedRoute renders Home"]
```

#### After
```mermaid
flowchart LR
    A["Visitor opens showcase"] --> B["MSW initializes currentUser = null"]
    B --> C["GET /api/me returns 401"]
    C --> D["AuthContext sets user = undefined"]
    D --> E["ProtectedRoute redirects to /login"]
    E --> F["Visitor signs in via Quick Demo"]
```

<details>
<summary>Technical details</summary>

### Implementation notes
- `src/mocks/handlers.ts`: Set initial `currentUser` to `null`, update `resetAuth()` to reset to `null`, and export `setAuth(user = defaultUser)` to seed authenticated user in targeted test suites.
- `src/App.test.tsx`: Use `setAuth()` for testing the sign-out and sign-in cycle; verify route protection under the new default unauthenticated state without manual server overrides.
- `src/components/NavMenu.test.tsx`: Added `authenticated` parameter to `setup()` defaulting to `true` (calling `setAuth()`), allowing tests to exercise both authenticated and unauthenticated navigation states cleanly.
- `src/components/Settings.test.tsx`: Added `beforeEach` to call `setAuth()` ensuring protected settings component tests run with a valid user session.

author: mrityunjaybhardwaj
body:
## What was wrong

When a song changes the reverb's shape from note to note (`.size("<1 4>")`, `.roomlp(…)`, `.size(perlin…)`), a bounce didn't follow. Every note in a four-second stretch played in the **last** room asked for in that stretch.

Each orbit has **one** reverb, and superdough rebuilds it whenever a note asks for a different shape (`superdoughoutput.mjs:69-92`). Live, a note reaches superdough just before it sounds, so each note gets its own room. A bounce hands a whole window of notes to superdough at one pause, so every rebuild landed at that pause and only the last one survived.

## The fix

The render also pauses just before each note that would rebuild its orbit's room, and hands that note (and the ones after it) over there. That's how live playback does it, since a single reverb per orbit gets swapped just ahead of each note. The alternative in the issue, one reverb per shape, would give each shape its own tail, which live doesn't do.

`roomChangeTimes` replays superdough's `getReverb` rule over the notes:
- an undefined value keeps the room (`hasChanged`, `:14`);
- a rebuild takes **every** value from its note, with `generate`'s defaults for what it leaves out (`reverb.mjs:41`), so asking for the old value again is a change;
- a different impulse sample is a change;
- orbits are independent, and a note with no room touches nothing.

When unsure it predicts a change, which costs at most one spare pause. Pauses closer than two render blocks are merged. A song that never reshapes a room pauses exactly as before.

## Observed (Chromium)

The clock at each impulse-response hand-over, offline render against live playback:

| song | offline, before | offline, after | live |
|---|---|---|---|
| `size("<1 4>")`, a note every 2 s | 0, 0, 3.95, 3.95 | 0, 1.95, 3.95, 5.95 | 0, 1.93, 3.91, 5.93 |
| `c3*4` + `size("1 4")` | four at 0, four at 3.95 | 0, 0.95, 1.95, 2.95, … | 0, 0.93, 1.91, 2.93, … |

In a real bounce (new arm in `bounce-stems.spec.ts`), with a half-second room then a four-second room:

| | gap after the small-room note | gap after the large-room note |
|---|---|---|
| `main` | 0.00088 | 0.00089 (both in the large room) |
| this PR | **0.00000** | 0.00088 |

## Cost (measured)

60 s song, 240 notes, `.size(perlin.range(1,4))` so the room changes on every note: `main` 2.1 s, this PR 3.4 s, about 5 ms per extra pause. The same song with a constant room is ~1 s on both.

Closes #1676

## Test plan

- [x] unit: the replay rule (7 arms, including rebuild-resets-defaults, orbits, impulse sample, tempo) and where the render pauses and hands notes over (5 arms). Against `main`'s render 7 go red, while the "nothing changes" guards stay green by design. A break making a rebuild keep old values turns exactly its arm red.
- [x] browser: new `bounce-stems` arm, green here and red against `main`'s build; all 6 bounce spec files 63/63
- [x] editor full suite: 288 files / 4658 tests
- [x] app full suite: 138 files / 1815 tests (20 untracked probes moved aside, all restored)

author: kevinschaper
body:
Adds `kb/disorders/Usmani-Riazuddin_Syndrome.yaml` — the neurodevelopmental disorder caused by variants in *AP1G1*, which encodes the gamma-1 adaptin subunit of the AP-1 clathrin adaptor complex.

**The decision this PR had to make first:** *AP1G1* causes both a dominant and a recessive disorder, and MONDO and OMIM give each its own identifier. I curated them as **one entry with two `has_subtypes` rows**, not as two sibling files. **Only the dominant form is actually curated** — the recessive row carries its identifiers and says "NOT CURATED" in as many words.

Closes #12177

## Why one entry rather than two

Design decisions section 3 says a separate file needs a distinct MONDO identity **and** a substantially independent mechanism. Here the first is satisfied and the second is not.

- MONDO:0859174 (dominant, OMIM 619467) and MONDO:0859196 (recessive, OMIM 619548) both assert `RO:0004003` to `hgnc:555` AP1G1 and both sit directly under MONDO:0003847. There is no umbrella term over them.
- Both forms were delineated in the *same* cohort, in one paper, whose title calls them one disorder: "De novo and bi-allelic variants in AP1G1 cause neurodevelopmental disorder..." (PMID:34102099).
- The follow-up literature states the overlap explicitly: "Its dominant and recessive forms have been reported in a cohort of patients showing overlapping clinical features" (PMID:41226632). A separate 2024 report writes both MIM numbers under one syndrome name.
- Both act through the same complex on the same pathway.

KB precedent for this shape: `Thomsen_and_Becker_disease` (CLCN1), `COL11A2_Hearing_Loss` (DFNA13/DFNB53), `Alport_Syndrome`. I considered and rejected the two-file precedents (`POLG` PEOA1/PEOB1, the `UNC13A` pair, `LBR`); those split because the two modes engage genuinely different protein functions, which is not the case here.

**What this means for the recessive form.** It is not curated. It has no phenotypes, pathophysiology, prevalence or treatments of its own in this PR, and the subtype row and `notes` both say so. There was no stub for it on `main`, so binding MONDO:0859196 on the subtype row does not retire anything from the curation queue. A curator taking it should populate subtype-scoped content on that row, or argue the two apart into sibling entries — the reasoning is recorded in an `OPEN_QUESTION` discussion in the file so the argument does not have to be reconstructed.

## Mechanism

The dominant allele classes are **not one lesion**, so the pathograph splits them:

```
AP1G1 Haploinsufficiency ─┐
(truncating, splice,      │
 whole-gene deletion)     ├─► AP-1 Adaptor Complex ─┬─► TGN Cargo Sorting Failure ─┬─► Somatodendritic Sorting
                          │       Dysfunction       │                              │      Failure in Neurons ─┐
Dominant-Negative ────────┘                         └─► Endosomal Recycling ───────┘                          ├─► Perturbed
Gamma-1 Adaptin Missense                                   Impairment                                         │   Neurodevelopment
Protein                                             └─► Cadherin Mis-sorting / AJ Instability ────────────────┘   & Reduced Brain
                                                                                                                  Growth
```

- **Haploinsufficiency** is evidenced by a de novo 16q22.2 whole-gene deletion (PMID:38840441). A whole-gene deletion makes no mutant protein, so it can only act by halving dosage. The zebrafish heterozygote independently shows that one allele is not enough (PMID:37108275).
- **Dominant-negative** is evidenced by the zebrafish co-injection result: wild-type human *AP1G1* mRNA rescues the null, mutant mRNA does not, and co-injecting both still does not rescue (PMID:41226632). The node is marked `mechanism_confidence: PROVISIONAL` because both groups say in print that they have not separated dominant-negative from toxic gain-of-function. That is recorded as a `KNOWLEDGE_GAP` discussion rather than resolved by me.

## What I deliberately did not do

- **No `conforms_to`.** `just list-modules` and a grep of `kb/modules/` for clathrin, adaptinopathy, AP-1 complex and trans-Golgi return only `synaptic_vesicle_cycle` (presynaptic AP-2-mediated endocytosis) and `apical_neuroependyma_integrity_failure`. Neither covers AP-1 cargo selection at the trans-Golgi network. An AP-1/adaptinopathy module would be a reasonable follow-up once a second adaptinopathy is curated.
- **Two phenotypes left unconnected in the pathograph.** Abnormal facial shape and Abnormality of limbs are real reported features, but nothing links *AP1G1* to craniofacial or limb patterning, so there is no honest edge to draw. Each carries a description saying why. 8 of 10 phenotypes are connected.
- **No frequency band on epilepsy, hypotonia, spasticity or autism.** The source says those were "variably expressed"; only intellectual disability, speech delay and aggressive behavior are reported in 100% of the founding cohort, and only those three carry a band.
- **Dropped PMID:41420732.** It reports an *AP1G1* variant of uncertain significance at 3% in a small autism cohort. A VUS frequency is not disease evidence, so the fetched cache file was discarded rather than committed.
- **No gnomAD constraint claim.** I did not consult gnomAD, and the `genetic:` notes say so rather than implying a pLI I did not look up.

## GeneReviews baseline

No GeneReviews chapter exists for this disorder. Verified offline with `just check-genereviews` against the committed Bookshelf index snapshot of 2026-09-10 (958 chapters indexed): `NO_CHAPTER` for both GeneReviews and StatPearls. The phenotype baseline is therefore the primary literature, and that is recorded in the entry's `notes`.

## Validation

All green:

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `just validate` | No issues |
| `just validate-terms` | passed |
| `just count-verified-snippets` | **76/76 verified** |
| `just validate-disorders` (authoritative) | passed, 76/76 |
| `just list-gene-term-mismatches` | 8/8 gene bindings name AP1G1, 0 mismatches |
| `just check-causal-targets` | no new broken targets |
| `just check-entity-refs` | resolve |
| `just check-snippet-grading` | no new divergences |
| `just check-title-snippets`, `check-snippet-length`, `check-folded-hyphens` | no new findings |
| `just check-duplicate-keys`, `check-enum-values`, `check-qualifier-terms` | OK |
| `just check-case-collisions`, `check-stubs`, `check-environmental-evidence` | OK |
| `just check-reference-titles` | no new mismatches |
| `just prose-figure-audit` | no unattributed figures |
| `just validate-history-all` | No issues (10,853 records) |
| `just list-disconnected-phenotypes` | 8/10 connected, both gaps intentional |

Five references cited, all cached and committed: PMID:34102099, PMID:41226632, PMID:37108275, PMID:38665048, PMID:38840441. Cache CSV changes are 13 added rows, all introduced by this entry. Stub `stubs/Usmani-Riazuddin_Syndrome_Autosomal_Dominant.yaml` deleted.

author: dkmobilewash
body:
Diego saw a phone save take several seconds to appear in the list, although the server already had it.

## Measured (production, 2026-09-18)
Each phone API call took **0.5–1s**, and the first after a pause took 2.6s. After a save, the Time screen made eight calls: a parallel batch of five, then the ratio, then sign-offs, then reports and delays, in sequence. So the list waited about 4–5s.

## Fixes
1. **`requireApiContext`** called `clerkClient().users.getUser()` on every request before touching the database. That's a network round trip to Clerk that's only needed to *adopt* a new Clerk id, by reading the verified email that links it to an existing row. A known `clerkId` is now answered from the database alone, and `recordLastSeen` still runs. It returns the same row `adoptCompanyContext`'s own first step would.
   - New test in `lib/auth.test.ts`: a second request for a known user makes **zero** Clerk lookups.
   - Checked by reverting the fast path: the test fails.
2. **Time screen `load`** runs every call in parallel (`Promise.allSettled`), and each part renders as it arrives.
3. **Just-saved rows show immediately**, as "Syncing…", for time entries (Log time and clock-out) and delays.
   - They're kept while their `clientOperationId` is still queued (the new `queuedOperationIds()`).
   - They're dropped once it's sent (the server's row replaces them) or set aside as refused (the refused banner explains).
   - Offline, the row stays visible instead of vanishing on reload.

No schema change, no migration. Web: 294 unit test files pass, tsc and eslint are clean. Mobile: tsc and eslint are clean.

After merge I'll re-time the API calls on production and save an entry from the phone to confirm it appears at once.

author: famouslytrill-boop
body:
## Purpose

Turns the platform limitations identified in the September 18 product review into a machine-readable engineering and business expansion program.

## What this adds

- 15 governed capability-expansion tracks in the existing infrastructure source of truth
- Android native client path (Capacitor primary, Trusted Web Activity fallback)
- passkeys/device-security path without a biometric database
- provider-neutral integration gateway path
- gated durable-event consumer activation path
- agent authority and approval continuity
- exact-head release proof as a permanent capability gate
- provider resilience/circuit-breaker path
- specialist software adapter strategy instead of false replacement claims
- opt-in ActivityPub federation boundary
- dedicated WebRTC/SFU media-plane path
- offline/local-first mutation and resumable-upload path
- governed repository activation
- OpenTelemetry + k6 + read-replica/DR evidence path
- AI decision assurance
- market/ecosystem scale evidence before competitive scale claims

## Product integration

The existing infrastructure manifest/readiness endpoints and public/admin infrastructure pages now expose the expansion control plane. No new untracked route surface is added.

## Truth boundary

A research source, roadmap target, or external provider catalog is not relabeled as a shipped SONARA capability. Each track carries:
- maturity status
- phase
- customer value
- business value
- target architecture
- technologies
- proof gates
- claim boundary
- production-enabled state

## Engineering sequencing

This PR is intentionally separate from the currently red Google/canonical-billing release branch. Do not merge it as a way to bypass those release failures.

## Research basis

Primary documentation used includes Capacitor, Android Trusted Web Activities, Google passkeys/FIDO, Nango integration infrastructure, W3C ActivityPub, LiveKit, OpenTelemetry, Grafana k6, and Supabase read replicas.

## Gate

Keep draft until the normal SONARA matrix proves the new manifest/routes/tests do not weaken release, security, tenant, documentation, or route-surface invariants.

author: nbaliyan260
body:
**Description of your changes:**

`SubprocessRunner` substitutes the local Python executable into generated bootstrap commands. The substitution currently continues past the component source into executor arguments, so input values such as `python3.11`, output paths containing `python3`, and function names such as `python3_identity` are rewritten. This can silently corrupt input data or prevent a component from running.

Stop substitution at the existing component-source boundary, preserving both the source and all following executor arguments. Interpreter substitution remains active in the installation and execution bootstrap commands.

Add regression coverage using generated lightweight-component commands with and without the package-install wrapper. The tests cover input JSON, output paths, component source, function names, and bootstrap interpreter replacement.

**Validation:**

- Python 3.12: 127 focused tests passed across subprocess interpreter replacement, subprocess execution, executor input/output conversion, placeholder resolution, and component command generation.
- Both new regression cases fail against the original replacement function with corrupted executor input, then pass with this fix.
- Public-API smoke test: a `python3_identity` component received `python3.11`, preserved a `python3` source literal, and wrote output under a directory containing `python3`.
- isort 5.10.1 and 9.0.1, YAPF 0.43.0, docformatter 1.7.7, Python 3.9 syntax parsing, and `git diff --check` passed.

The remaining applicable pre-commit hooks (whitespace, conflict/debug checks, flake8, and pycln) passed. The pinned formatter checks above were run separately to avoid source-build setup; Go and workflow hooks were excluded for this Python-only change.

**Checklist:**

- [x] The PR title follows the repository convention.

author: mbeacom
body:
## What this does

Three separable changes, each in its own commit.

### 1. `fix(telemetry)` — capability route redaction registry

`PUBLIC_CAPABILITY_ROUTE_PREFIXES` in `lib/telemetry/capability-privacy.ts` enumerates the routes whose path segment is the credential. The list had fallen behind the application as capability routes were added feature by feature. This brings it back in line, so the existing scrubbers cover all of them.

Both regex families derive from the array, so each entry gains raw and percent-encoded redaction with no further wiring.

One route carries its credential as a query value rather than a path segment, which the prefix patterns structurally cannot express. A parallel `PUBLIC_CAPABILITY_QUERY_PARAMS` registry handles that form, with its own raw and percent-encoded patterns and the same placeholder guard, so redaction stays idempotent.

The same registry gates `AnalyticsProvider`, so pathnames on these routes no longer reach Umami or GA either. **This is a behavioural change**: page-view and web-vitals collection stops on the affected routes. That is intended — those pathnames are credentials — but it is worth knowing before merge.

`publicWishlistRoute` is renamed to `publicCapabilityRoute` there; the registry stopped being wishlist-specific some time ago.

The identifier-addressed public routes are deliberately excluded, and the module now documents why: `/associations/<slug>`, `/rinks/<slug>` and `/signups/<eventId>` address public records by identifier, and `/venue-relationships/<relationshipId>` is authorized server-side by `requireTargetAuthority`.

Tests assert the registry's exact contents, so a capability route added without registering it fails a test rather than shipping unredacted.

### 2. `docs(ci)` — release workflow description

`AUTOMATION.md` documented a release flow that no longer exists: steps 5 and 6 claimed the job updates `package.json` and commits the version change with `[skip ci]`. `release.yml` has neither step. The description now matches the workflow, and carries the rationale the file was missing — tags are the source of truth, and `package.json`'s version trails them by design.

### 3. `docs(adr)` — nine backfilled decision records

An audit of specs, workflows, schema and history found nine durable choices that were never recorded. ADR-0011 through ADR-0019, each with the alternatives actually rejected and the evidence gaps left open.

| ID | Decision |
|----|----------|
| 0011 | Public capability links are bearer credentials, redacted from telemetry |
| 0012 | Segment conflict is declared; drawn geometry only proposes |
| 0013 | CI never pushes to `main`; versions from tags, reports from an orphan branch |
| 0014 | Public reads go through explicit column whitelist modules |
| 0015 | In-memory rate limiting is advisory, not a security control |
| 0016 | The sport capability catalog stays in code, not the database |
| 0017 | Sentry is DSN-optional and degrades to a no-op |
| 0018 | Game proposals are append-only entry rows |
| 0019 | Every PR is gated on type-check, lint and the full suite |

**All nine are `proposed` and govern nothing until ratified.** Ratifying is a status flip to `accepted` plus `provenance.ratifiedBy` per record; 0001–0009 show the shape.

## Three records that need a decision, not just a review

- **0015** may document an oversight rather than a decision. The limiter's own comment calls it a development tool while `proxy.ts` runs it in production. If that was never intended, reject the record and replace the limiter.
- **0017** has no recorded rationale anywhere for choosing Sentry over any alternative. The options listed are a reconstruction, not a comparison that happened, and the record says so rather than inventing history.
- **0019** documents CI policy rather than an architectural constraint, and may belong folded into ADR-0005.

## Verification

- `bun run type-check` — clean
- `bun run lint` — clean
- `bun run adr:lint` — 19 records, 0 errors, 0 warnings
- `bun run adr:check-integrity` — OK
- `bun run test` — 2,888 passing, 0 failures

### Correction on the six failing tests

An earlier revision of this description said 6 tests failed in `game-proposals` (5) and `gear-context` (1), called them pre-existing, and guessed they were "genuine logic failures rather than fixture rot". The first part was right and the diagnosis was wrong, so the fourth commit fixes them.

They were **date-fixture rot**. Both files encode windows authored as "near future" that have since aged into the past: `gear-context` asserts a future-reallocation warning for 2026-09-10..12, which `lib/actions/gear-context.ts:437` only issues when `requestedStartDate > today`; `game-proposals` builds a proposal whose terms start 2026-09-05T22:00, which `isTermsExpired` now rejects. Quality Gates last passed on `main` at 9e1d0be on 2026-09-05 — the same date those fixtures encode. Same code, same tests, different day.

Fixed by pinning both files to 2026-09-01 with `vi.useFakeTimers({ toFake: ["Date"] })`, so only `Date` is faked and timer/promise scheduling is untouched. Verified non-vacuous: moving the pin past the fixture window reproduces the original failure exactly, and restoring it passes.

## Notes for review

Reconciliation was re-run live against the corpus immediately before each ADR write rather than from the audit's frozen snapshot, since every write moves the corpus fingerprint. No `rejected`, `superseded` or `deprecated` record exists in the corpus, so none of these re-proposes an abandoned decision.

The ADR CI comment on this PR will flag 0011 and 0013 as active proposals touching the change set — that is the new `affects` matchers binding correctly, not a conflict.

author: remyluslosius
body:
## OW-047: the signing-key export gate stops before the upload

From the founder's rc.3 documentation review. The runbook's export block checked for a stubbed master with `... | grep -q gnu-dummy && echo OK || echo ABORT`, then ran `gh secret set`. `echo` succeeds, so a pasted block printed ABORT and uploaded anyway. Same control-flow class as the pre-OW-037 Stage 2 block. The exported material has never been shown to contain the master.

### Change

- `docs/runbooks/RELEASING.md`: the block is a subshell with `set -euo pipefail`; export to a `mktemp` path; a trap shreds it on every exit; the gate is an `if` that exits 1 with ABORT on stderr before any upload; the subkey fingerprint is captured, not pasted.
- `release-ci-gates` 1.18.0: C-15 and AC-24.
- `packaging/tests`: AC-24 extracts the block and runs it with `bash -c`, `gpg` stubbed to report a stubbed or a real master, `gh` stubbed to record calls. Stubbed master: exit 0, exactly `GPG_PRIVATE_KEY` then `GPG_PASSPHRASE` uploaded. Real master: non-zero exit, ABORT, zero `gh` calls. No export left on disk in either case.

No production behavior changes; `release.yml` is untouched. Not docs-only because of the test.

### Evidence

- Real `gpg`, throwaway key: a subkey-only export carries a `gnu-dummy` packet (1) and a full secret export does not (0). The tracked block run against each: OK / exit 0, and ABORT / exit 1 with nothing uploaded and the export shredded.
- Mutations gone red: the original `echo` gate (real master: exit 0 and both secrets uploaded, the exact defect); the gate's exit neutralized; the trap removed (export left on disk in both runs).
- `make spec-check` 100%; `go test ./packaging/tests/` ok; gofmt/goimports clean.

Not to be merged without authorization; OW-047 closes after merge and verification on `main`.

author: rumi-ali
body:
## Read this part first

The 404 in the reported screenshot **is not produced by this repo**, and this PR cannot fix it.

`https://www.rumi.build/book` embeds a Cal.com calendar pointed at **`rumi-app/30-min-meeting`** — both halves renamed away on 2026-08-05 (`rumi-app` → `rumi-ai`, `30-min-meeting` → `call-30min`). Cal.com issues no redirect, so it renders `Error Code: 404. Cal Link seems to be wrong.` That page also **takes no payment at all**: it is a bare "Book a 30-minute call" page with no Stripe.

That deployment is not built from this checkout. Its nav reads "Request a demo", a string that has never appeared anywhere in this repo's git history (`git log --all -S`), its nav is navy (this repo has shipped a white nav since v1.2.0.0), and its `/book` has no checkout.

Verified against the Vercel API today:

| Host | Vercel project | This repo? |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `rumi.build`, `www.rumi.build` | `rumi-build` | no |
| `rumiai.ai`, `www.rumiai.ai` | `rumi-ai-website` | no |
| — | `rumi-ai` (what this checkout was linked to) | **zero domains attached** |

So this repo currently serves no domain, and CLAUDE.md's "one deployment, four hosts, one canonical" section was false. Corrected here.

## What this PR does change

The defect that is real in this repo and correct regardless of which slug is right: a dead Cal.com link stranded a customer who had already paid.

`CalEmbed` revealed its full-height box on **script** load, which says nothing about whether the event type resolved — so Cal.com painted its raw 404 into a white card with no link and no address, on `/book/success`, after the card was charged. It now reads Cal.com's own runtime signals:

- `linkReady` reveals the embed; `linkFailed` replaces it with a recovery block carrying the direct calendar link and `support@rumi.build`.
- A timeout covers the case that emits no event at all (blocked script, dead network, Cal.com outage), which previously sat on "Loading calendar…" forever with no way out.
- Email is always offered, because when the **event type** is what broke, the direct link is equally dead.

`calUrlFor()` in `src/lib/data.ts` now backs both the exported URLs and the embed's recovery link, so the calendar and the escape hatch beside it cannot name different calendars. A stale escape hatch is read only once the embed has already failed.

`tests/unit/cal-link.test.ts` is right that no offline test can *detect* a rename. Detection and handling are different problems, and the handling was missing.

## Also corrected

- **CLAUDE.md** — domain section rewritten against the live Vercel records, with a note that `get_project`'s `domains` array is a stale cache and `list_project_domains` is authoritative. The two disagree right now, which is how this stayed invisible.
- **package.json** said `1.2.2.0` while `VERSION` and `CHANGELOG.md` said `1.2.3.0`.
- **TODOS.md** — two P0s recorded, below.

## Open P0s this turned up (not fixed here)

1. **The live funnel is down and takes no money.** `www.rumi.build/book` 404s and has no Stripe. Fixing it means working in `rumi-inc/Frontend_Rumi_AIEmployees` → Vercel project `rumi-build`.

author: nickpismenkov
body:
`cycle` was the last algorithm the corpus reaches that the SmartArt
layout subset did not model, so the decks built on it painted nothing.

Children are spaced around the ellipse inscribed in the node, from
`stAng` across `spanAng`, in degrees clockwise from twelve o'clock; a
negative span runs the other way and a partial arc reaches its far end
instead of closing. `ctrShpMap="fNode"` takes the first child off the
ring and hubs it at the centre. `rotPath="alongPath"` turns each shape to
face along the path, which is the rotation `a:xfrm@rot` already carries.

The cycle layouts give every shape the whole diagram extent and leave the
ring to the algorithm, exactly as the linear ones do, so the same
shrink-to-fit applies: two shapes one step apart on a ring of radius r
are `2 r sin(step/2)` apart, and the ring plus one shape has to fit the
node, which bounds the factor. Without it all sixteen shapes of
`smartart-autoTxRot.pptx` landed on the same point at the full frame
size.

`pyra` is now the only named algorithm still refusing.

## Measured

Local fidelity corpus (hard-v2), ink percentage of the scored slide,
LibreOffice as reference:

| file | ink before | ink after | reference |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| smartart-autoTxRot.pptx | 0.00 | **4.48** | 13.75 |

The render is the deck's sixteen-arrow ring, each arrow turned to face
along the path and lettered a–p, which is what the reference draws. Ours
sizes each arrow so its box clears its neighbours on the ring;
LibreOffice overlaps the boxes and so paints more ink from the same
arrangement.

No other file moved: smartart-autofit-sync 48.73, smartart-background
37.22, smartart-bullet-list 35.14, smartart-children 32.29, table-list
38.07, fill-color-list 22.10, smartart-org-chart 16.92,
smartart-org-chart2 18.87, smartart-chevron 6.91,
smartart-background-drawingml-fallback 31.74, smartart-picture-strip
0.72 — all unchanged.

`smartart-center-cycle.pptx` still refuses: its `radial` node reads its
own `w` before anything defines it, because this evaluator resolves every
constraint before laying out and so never sees the extent a node
inherits from its parent. That is an evaluation-order change, not a
cycle gap.

author: wayne19870129
body:
## Summary

The resource allocation was inverted, and that is the real finding here — not the cost saving.

| 执行者 | 模型 | 额度 | 在做什么 |
|---|---|---|---|
| ChatGPT 网页版 | 5.6 Soar，**高推理** | 近乎无限 | 只审查 |
| Codex Cloud | 5.6 Luna，**轻推理** | 紧张（实测周额度剩 **12%**，剩余额度 **0**） | **在做判断** |

**The scarcest, weakest resource was carrying the judgement.** ADR-031 moves all judgement to ChatGPT and leaves Codex purely executing.

### What a review comment now has to contain

One comment, **two different consumers**:

| 消费者 | 读什么 | 缺了会怎样 |
|---|---|---|
| `scripts/automerge_gate.py` | `Verdict:` 行 + 完整 40 位 head SHA + 作者写权限 | 闸门停在 `WAIT`，**不报错** — 看起来像卡住 |
| Codex | 指令卡 | 它不知道改什么，或者自己猜 |

Missing either stalls the pipeline **silently rather than loudly**, which is exactly why both are now specified rather than left to habit. Template in `docs/85` §3.1.

### How granular the instruction card must be

"Write an instruction card" on its own doesn't achieve the goal — a vague card just *moves* the thinking instead of removing it. `docs/85` §3.1b now makes it concrete:

| ❌ 让它思考 | ✅ 让它执行 |
|---|---|
| "补一下续费的测试覆盖" | "在 `backend/tests/unit/test_billing.py` 新增 `test_renewal_order_can_be_confirmed`：构造 `OrderType.RENEWAL` 订单，调用 `admin_confirm_payment`，断言不抛 `ValueError` 且状态变成 `PAID`" |
| "这里的错误处理有问题" | "`services.py` 第 210 行附近，`except Exception` 改成捕获后返回 `PENDING_MANUAL`，理由：ADR-026 要求补偿失败不得降级成 `FAILED`" |

Plus five rules: exact paths and function names; test names and assertions spelled out; name the file to imitate rather than letting it search; one reason per item pointing at the TASK or ADR; an explicit not-doing list.

The resource argument is the justification: **审查侧多写三行，执行侧少烧一半。**

## Three things recorded because they are easy to get wrong later

**1. Light reasoning on the executor is a constraint, not a preference.** Executing a real task — read the repo, edit files, run tests, push — consumes quota by itself, so under a tight cap only the light tier finishes a whole task. So the architecture must assume a weak executor **permanently**, not treat it as a temporary state to be upgraded away.

**2. The cost is stated, not glossed.**

> **指令卡越具体，Codex 越像一只手 —— 如果指令本身是错的，它不会拦住。**

A high-reasoning executor might say "this contradicts the TASK". One told to follow a list will not. **The pipeline loses a layer of redundant checking at the execution end.** The conclusion is not to abandon the split — it is that ADR-030's periodic supervision becomes **more** load-bearing under this ADR, not less. Any proposal to weaken supervision now has to revisit ADR-031 first.

**3. The instruction card may not widen the TASK's allowed-file list.** If a fix needs a path outside it, ChatGPT **stops** and Claude amends the TASK.

Otherwise the strongest scope guardrail in this repo drifts out of the TASK file and into PR comments — the same failure ADR-029 §7 and ADR-030 §2 were both written to prevent: **whoever issues the instructions must not also define the constraints on them.** §3.1b restates the matching boundary: the detail belongs to *how*, never to *what*.

## Why 5 → 3, and why not back

The clock is the lesser reason (ChatGPT polls hourly, so five rounds is five hours). The real one:

> **三轮不收敛，通常说明 TASK 写错了，不是 Codex 不会改。**

Continuing to iterate uses execution-side rework to mask a specification-side defect. Re-specifying and re-dispatching is cheaper than grinding rounds four and five against a wrong spec.

That is why ADR-031 §8's re-evaluation condition says repeatedly hitting the cap should trigger a review of **the TASK template**, never a return to 5 — and `docs/85` §6's breaker table now says the same thing in the place someone would actually go to change the number.

## Verification

- [x] Tests and lint pass.
- [x] No real credential, `.env`, or target-host `*.conf` file is included.
- [x] External-system claims are classified in the facts ledger. *(n/a — nothing external is contacted. The quota figures are from the account's own analytics page, dated in the ADR.)*

```
$ python -m ruff check backend ops infrastructure scripts
All checks passed!

$ python -m pytest backend/tests/unit backend/tests/guards -q
663 passed, 2 warnings in 4.14s

$ git diff --check
# clean
```

Documentation only — no code, no workflow, no business logic. No new tests, because nothing executable changed here.

**Coordination with [PR #140](https://github.com/wayne19870129/lingsway-platform/pull/140):** `scripts/pipeline_health.py` carries `REVIEW_ROUND_CAP`, and that file exists only on the S10 branch. The constant is updated **there** (now `3`, citing ADR-031 §6) rather than here, to avoid a conflict. I also wrote and then removed a guard test asserting the constant matches CLAUDE.md's wording — it would have red-CI'd #140 until this PR merged, and coupling two open PRs' CI is worse than the drift it guards against. **Merge order doesn't matter; both are self-consistent.**

## Existing-customer impact

- [x] 是否影响存量客户连接 — **No.** Documentation only.
- [x] 是否触发 Xray 或 Mihomo 重载 — **No.**

## Rollback plan

- [x] 回滚方案

`git revert` this merge commit. Restores the 5-round cap and removes §3.1/§3.1b/§3.2. *Verify:* `CLAUDE.md` reads "at 5 rounds per PR" and `docs/85` §6's table says 5.

Worth knowing before choosing that: reverting also removes the **written requirement that review comments carry a machine-readable `Verdict:` line**. Without it, ChatGPT can write a perfectly good review that the merge gate silently ignores, and the PR sits at `WAIT` with nothing indicating why. If the goal is only to undo the cap change, revert the `CLAUDE.md` / ADR-030 / §6 hunks and keep §3.1–3.2.

## Risk classification

- [x] 风险等级 low / medium / migration / high

**Expected label: `risk:low`** — everything here is under `docs/**` except `CLAUDE.md`, which is at the repo root with no classifier rule and falls through to `high`. So it may well come out `risk:high` for the same reason as #136/#137/#140. `TASK-S11` (queued in `docs/85` §5.3) is meant to fix that path table.

Per `CLAUDE.md`'s governance rule: **this PR changes who is allowed to decide what gets changed**, and tightens a behavioural safety limit. Read it as governance-level regardless of the label. No auth, payment or secret-handling code is touched. `AGENTS.md` is **not** modified by this PR.

**`CLAUDE.md` itself is modified**, and its own closing section asks that changes to it be shown as a diff and not committed until you confirm. This PR is that diff — please confirm the cap change specifically rather than as part of the whole thing.

## Changed files

| File | Change |
|---|---|
| `docs/80-decisions/ADR-031-thinking-execution-split.md` | **new** — the split, the stated cost, the scope boundary, the cap |
| `CLAUDE.md` | cap 5→3 in all three places (**needs your confirmation**) |
| `docs/85-agent-operating-model.md` | §3 cap; **new §3.1** comment format; **new §3.1b** granularity; **new §3.2** scope boundary; §6 breaker table; §5.8 numbering; header date |
| `docs/86-codex-operating-instructions.md` | **new §5.1** executor-side rules; header now describes Codex **Cloud** rather than desktop, and names the model split |
| `docs/80-decisions/ADR-030-*.md` | §5 halt table cap 5→3 |

## Known unresolved / deliberately out of scope

1. **Nothing enforces the comment format mechanically.** If ChatGPT omits the `Verdict:` line or the full SHA, the gate waits silently. `pipeline_health.py`'s `PR_STUCK_OVER_12H` alert catches it eventually — after 12 hours. A faster "PR is green and reviewed but the verdict is unparseable" alert would be a real improvement; not in this PR.
2. **`SAME_FINDING_FAILED_TWICE` still isn't mechanically detectable** and stays in `judgement_only_signals`.
3. **Codex dispatch still needs you.** `@codex` in Issue #138 got no response in over an hour; the confirmed entry point is the Codex web task box, which I cannot operate.
4. **PR #132 (backup/restore) remains the only unreviewed merged code on `main`.**

body:
## What this does

This builds the Stripe payments pilot, following `projects/stripe/architecture.md` v1.3, `design.md` v1.3 and PRD v1.11. It targets the pilot branch `payments-stripe-preview`, not `dev` [owner, 72].

- **S1:** a pay block on dates with a price (button, no-refunds notice, policy link). Tapping it opens Stripe Checkout (Server Action). After payment, a screen shows the one-time QR code, with Save, plus Share where the browser supports it. Also a placeholder policy page and EN/RU strings.
- **S2:** a signed webhook at `/api/stripe/webhook/`, a `Reservations` tab in the existing spreadsheet, Telegram messages, and an alert when saving a row fails. When Stripe redelivers, the missing row is restored without duplicates.
- **S3:** a status page at `/[locale]/bookingstatus/[id]/` with three states: valid, not valid, not found. If the booking can't be read, it returns a 500 error page. Before showing "not found", it asks Stripe.
- **S4:** a chargeback marks the booking "not valid" and sends a Telegram message.
- Dates with a price of 0 or none show no price and no button.
- The Checkout session expires after 31 minutes, above Stripe's 30-minute minimum.

## Checks

- `npm run lint`: 0 errors.
- `npm test`: 94/94 passed, with Stripe, Sheets and Telegram mocked.
- `npm run build`: passes.
- Existing pages keep identical canonical, hreflang and robots output. The new pages are noindex.
- The code reads `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `PILOT_SHARE_URL` from the environment. No values are committed. Without them, payment fails closed.

## Not yet verified

The Stripe and Vercel facts in architecture.md V1–V17 have only been checked against mocks. They need the S0 setup and a live test payment. The riskiest are V2 (Stripe accepting the notice text on its page) and V10 (the share token still working after later pushes).

## Preview

Preview for this branch: https://austin-city-tours-git-feat-stripe-pilot-build-tatiana-orlovas-projects.vercel.app. It needs a Vercel login, and Vercel may have shortened the name.

**Phone check: needed.** This changes the date card and date page, and adds three new pages. The Stripe keys are scoped to `payments-stripe-preview` only, so the full payment flow can only be tested after merging. This branch's preview shows the pay block, but tapping it fails safely.

author: iamenahs
body:
Phase 2, part A, of the Agents and Goals roadmap (`docs/superpowers/plans/2026-09-17-agents-and-goals-roadmap.md`). Phase 1 landed in #770. This part is the host, the files and the shipped content, with no new screen; part B, the screens, follows as its own pull request stacked on this one.

## What it adds

- **A seating that says why.** Every candidate a seating passes over carries a structured reason and the fix that removes it (install, sign in, usage, the runtime, or this machine's seats), and a refusal lists every candidate rather than the first. A runtime that never answers is passed over within a deadline instead of being waited on.
- **`agent/seat/dry`** answers what a seating would do without opening anything.
- **A passed-over seat leaves nothing behind**: a conversation a seating opened and could not use is removed only if nobody touched it, and a person's own handle is never closed.
- **`~/.harnessdesk/seating.json`** holds this machine's seats per Agent, replacing an Agent's `prefer` on this machine; one read, written aside and renamed, `__proto__` refused.
- **Nine Agents ship with the app** (reviewers, a judge, an implementer, a researcher and others), written as ordinary `AGENT.md` files.
- **The roster watches its folders** and pushes `agent/changed`, following the roster's own rule for links and never watching outside a project.
- **An Agent's folder can be saved, copied, removed and revealed** (`agent/create`, `agent/copy`, `agent/remove`, `agent/reveal`), and the editor may open an Agent's own files.
- **A backup carries this machine's Agents and seats**, and a restore adds them without overwriting anything.
- **Per-model spent windows** (#769) become a structured reason, `spentModel`, worded as main words it.

## What a cloned repository cannot do

A repository controls `.harnessdesk/agents`. It cannot make a file verb act on a path the roster did not list, write outside a project, overwrite an existing Agent, delete or trash a folder this code did not make, or turn the roster watch into a watch on the whole checkout (a committed link to the project's root is walked past, not watched). A backup is treated as data from anyone: a restore makes only folders under an id the roster lists, only files whose every segment stays inside, never carries `.git` in any case spelling, and one bad folder, file or seat never stops the rest.

## How it was checked

Every task was reviewed independently, the reviewer re-running each red-first proof itself rather than trusting the report; several needed two to four rounds. A final whole-branch review then looked across tasks and found three cross-task defects, each confirmed by running it and fixed in the last commit. `pnpm verify` passes in full.

## Verified in the app

No screen changes in this part: its renderer edits are store and transport state, and its desktop edits ship the nine Agents in the package. Nothing to photograph. Checked in the real app, on staged homes with fake runtimes and the fake `codex` first on `PATH`:

- **Seating.** An Agent whose first seat's runtime cannot start (not installed) and whose second can: the second is seated, the first is passed over with its reason and fix (`notInstalled`, fixed by installing), and exactly one conversation appears in the sidebar. The path where a candidate is opened and then passed over is covered by the host tests, not exercised here.
- **Backup.** With an Agent folder and a `seating.json` entry staged, Settings › Backup exported both; restoring the file into a second fresh home brought the Agent (listed and parsing) and its seat back, and restoring it again changed nothing (file times unchanged).
- **Package.** The packaged app's smoke run: `ok — the 9 shipped Agents are on disk and parse`.

The Backup sentences still count runtimes as "agents" and do not count Agents or seats; that wording belongs to part B's rename of Settings › Agents to Runtimes, and is fixed there.

## Left for later, deliberately

- A brief hand-over failure on an in-use candidate can still bring back an older stall; nothing is lost and reopening recovers it. Fixing it changes the sentence part B's start dialog words.
- A request made inside `createSession`, before the seat is recorded, is not marked as a use; the worst case deletes an empty conversation a window merely opened.
- A runtime reusing a conversation id can briefly rename it in memory before the refusal.
- A name that appears a few milliseconds after the roster watch attaches can be missed; the desk's own writes always announce themselves.
- Pre-checking effort against a runtime's catalogue waits on a product decision.

  `0x422489ba6bddd5954c379c41b6c97ab0e4494f90` live in `wildcat-finance/collateral-contract`
  branch `multi-exchange` at `46dba596fa111f868200358f551796e8f73b5fd7`, built
  under the repository's own `ir` profile with solc 0.8.28. The factory and lens
  reproduce modulo 4 and 1 immutable slots; the stored init code's keccak256
  equals `collateralInitCodeHash()`.
- The open-access role provider `0x5620553d8881335f74ad19259daacd1d9b373101` lives
  in `wildcat-finance/chainalysis-ofac-role-provider` at
  `5d7f8c889a8d29935838a3906172feb8d9861807`, Sourcify full match, reproducing
  modulo the two oracle immutable slots.

The collateral sources were committed on 2025-11-24, three months after the
2025-08-18 deployment, so the deployer built from a tree committed later. The
`audit_2026_feb` and `kethic/underflow-fix` branches share the factory and lens
blobs but carry a child whose creation code does not hash to the stored init
code; the default branch carries none of the three. That is recorded rather
than resolved: an exact deployer checkout is not established.

## The three items the issue named

**Third FixedTermHooks template** `0x731c775385d0efb2cac61074ba2d885d343a09cd`:
created at block 22081282 by the operations account and registered at block
22094295 through the arch controller owner Safe, transaction
`0x1d9aee83f68194a287314d553f72f96e742a6b917a30ae1799199504117d7175`, with the
fee recipient at 500 bips. It is enabled, carries 11 instances and 16 markets,
and its source stays `5838b2f3` on the plasma line.

**Both MarketLens deployments**, by epoch and consumer.
`0xc672760757da93b5f3275dc97203d145806dae33` is the core-set lens, block
21788205, source tag v2.0.0, named only by `v2-protocol`
`deployments/mainnet/deployments.json` and, as a stale in-repo book, by
`project-aleph`. `0xfda5c5b96bb198d2fca1a01d759620b64ae5afe7` is the lens every
application-facing consumer reads: `wildcat.ts` as `MarketLensV2`, the
`wildcat-app-v2` lender and borrower hooks, the docs deployment page,
`wildcat-juris` and `project-aleph`. Both stay in the row because both are
deployed, source-matched code. The SDK's `MarketLens` key is the deprecated V1
lens `0xf1d516954f96c1363f8b0ae48d79c8dde6237847`, outside this row.

**Emitter pin binding.** Every emitter, interface and hooks-base path is
blob-identical at the PR #1460 pin `f5a26146`, at v2.0.0, at the deploy-era
commit `8dc8e449`, at v2.1.0 and at both plasma-line commits `5838b2f3` and
`e1f77540`. Only `src/access/FixedTermHooks.sol` differs, by the 730-day
constant. The pin therefore binds to every deployed epoch of this estate.

## Exclusions

Four scope exclusions and eight protected-set exclusions, each with its owner
and reason, are recorded in `targets.json`: the 31 borrower push providers, the
arch controller owner Safe, the Chainalysis `SanctionsList`, the SphereX
engine, the Bebop settlement address, the `protocol-ownership` delegator, the
V1 lens, and the collateral instances the factory deployed. Sepolia, Etherscan
and the V1 contracts on the shared arch controller stay out.

## Reproduction

```bash
python3 scripts/kickoff_targets.py check
python3 scripts/kickoff_targets.py specimen --specimen docs/kickoff/1359/specimens/accepted-v2-hooks-instance.json
python3 scripts/kickoff_targets.py specimen --specimen docs/kickoff/1359/specimens/wrong-instance-template-hash.json
python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -p test_kickoff_targets.py
```

`check` is clean: 58 consumers, 17 targets, 1 resolved. The suite is 47 tests,
8 of them new: a resolved row may not keep a blocker, a resolved contract needs
a source commit, and the estate map must stay complete, reproduce modulo
immutables, agree with the factory events, and keep its role providers either
the borrower or the matched shared provider. The two new specimens accept a
recorded hooks instance and reject the same instance carrying its template's
hash.

## One dated line elsewhere

`docs/kickoff/1374/capture.json`, merged the same day under #1490, records
this row's `registry_status` as `blocked` and quotes its blocker text. Those
are dated observations in another record, so this pull request leaves them
as written. The capture that record requires is unaffected: it needs chain
event data for the estate, which completing the source map does not supply.
Whoever next regenerates that record picks up the new status.

## What this does not establish

The coverage claim is about block 26006289; contracts deployed later are not in
it. Nothing here establishes contract safety, current chain state, an exact
deployer checkout among equivalent trees, or completion of a consumer's own
capture, corpus, audit or campaign. The two private repositories were read
through the GitHub API; their blob identifiers and digests are recorded so a
copy can be checked without access.

author: ploteddie-bit
body:
## Problème

La page publique **https://cborweb.com/metrics/** affichait encore le score du **10/09/2026 (337/1000)**, alors que le calcul du 19/09 donne **469/1000**. Elle n'avait jamais bougé depuis sa création.

Deux causes cumulées :

1. **Le cron était cassé** — `indice-quotidien` a échoué 8 fois du 11 au 18/09 (chemin `scripts/` doublé dans `jobs.json`, et lien symbolique que Hermes refuse). Réparé le 18/09 : `hermes cron doctor` ne remonte plus d'anomalie et un run forcé a réussi.
2. **Le script ne peut pas publier** — `indice-iic.py` écrit la page dans `serveur-dev:/home/webmaster/repo/docs/site/metrics/index.html`, un fichier **non suivi par git** dans le clone présent sur le serveur. Rien ne le transmet à Cloudflare Pages.

Autrement dit, même avec un cron qui tourne tous les jours, la page publique ne se met jamais à jour.

## Cette PR

Elle publie la page telle que le cron vient de la générer :

- **score 469/1000**, delta +15, 3 jours d'historique (10/09 : 337 · 18/09 : 454 · 19/09 : 469)
- composantes du jour : social 100 (142 mentions brutes) · adoption 5 · IETF 100 (78 brutes) · web 2 · presse 0
- fichier repris **bit à bit** depuis le serveur — `md5 32ee3c5e11433ed412d99d7b2d674b45`, 14 037 octets, 209 lignes

## Ce que cette PR ne fait pas

**La publication reste manuelle.** Tant que le canal de publication n'existe pas, la page redeviendra fausse dès le prochain jour. L'automatisation est un chantier séparé, tracé dans le cockpit du projet ; les options identifiées sont : jeton dédié au dépôt côté serveur-dev, génération déplacée sur le poste, ou table intermédiaire lue par un job de publication.

À noter dans les données : les composantes *adoption* (5) et *web* (2) proviennent en partie des événements de test de la vérification de télémétrie. Elles se normaliseront avec le trafic réel.

## Vérification après merge

```bash
curl -s https://cborweb.com/metrics/ | grep -o "Dernière mise à jour : [0-9-]*"
# attendu : Dernière mise à jour : 2026-09-19
```
