author: ptr727
body:
Promotes one change: the reader for Copilot's second review-body format.

## What lands

`scripts/pr_review.py` now reads the `<!-- ccr-overview-v2 -->` format. Before this, its three unvetted markers exited 43 on every Copilot-reviewed pull request, so no review loop could close on the digest.

- The three blocked markers are vetted, plus `Resolved since last review (N)`, which a later round introduced. Emphasis tags around a marker are dropped before comparison rather than vetted with it.
- `effort=` reads both spellings. Reading only the first format's bullet printed `effort=unknown` over a body stating the level outright.
- `overview=T/M` is new. `T` is the finding total the round states in its overview preamble, `?` where none is found, and `None` reads as zero since a round raising nothing states it in words. `M` is the number of review threads that round opened, read from the API. A total larger than the thread count prints a `FINDINGS WITH NO THREAD` block. No exit code rides on it.

## Why `M` comes from the API rather than the review body

Six readings took it from the body's own enumeration and four shipped a false green: a shortfall of zero over a body that withheld findings, because something that was not an enumeration entry got counted. A prose back-reference, a change-summary link, a nested sub-bullet, a back-reference on the entry line, a list inside an entry's collapsed detail. Telling those apart needs each list marker's own content column and each HTML block's own extent, which is a Markdown parser rather than a line scan.

The count was never in the prose. Each entry's anchor is the database id of that thread's own comment, so the threads the round opened are the same set the enumeration names, already structured. `Q_FULL` gained a review id and each thread's opening review to link them. That round deleted more than it added.

## What is recorded as unmeasured

The equivalence above holds while a round's enumeration lists what that round raised. A round on the feature pull request carried a `Resolved since last review (N)` section, so the format tracks a finding's state across rounds rather than describing one round, and an `Open (N)` carrying what an earlier round left open would state a total whose threads belong to that round. No round read here has shown it. Until one does, a shortfall and a `?` both send the reader to the review body rather than standing in for it, which the digest and every reader-facing surface say.

Whether a stated total includes a suppressed section's findings is unmeasured the same way, so `suppressed=2` beside a shortfall of 2 is either two findings or four.

## Coverage, and why this merged without it

Four rounds in this format have been read across two pull requests, and only the first stated its file coverage. The three on the feature pull request carried neither the `fleet-review` marker the carried `code-review` instructions ask for nor a `Files reviewed` line, on a head carrying those instructions, so two re-requests did not clear it. `status` exits 45, `COVERAGE_IS_UNSTATED`, on each. The maintainer took that decision explicitly with every other Merge Gate item satisfied: one finding found, fixed and resolved, two later rounds raising nothing, and checks green.

That inconsistency is recorded in the module docstring rather than left as a surprise, and it is worth its own issue against the instructions or the reader.

## Verification

Against the live round that raised the original issue, `status` moves from `shapes=UNRECOGNIZED` with three listed markers and `effort=unknown` to `shapes=ok`, `effort=lite effort_source=explicit`, `overview=2/2`. Five first-format pull requests read identically before and after, carrying no `overview=` field. The reader then read three live rounds of its own pull request, one of which raised exit 43 on a shape it did not know, which is the contract working on the change that adds it.

Mutations across every guard on this change, each killed by the case whose name claims it. Ten adversarial local review passes and three hosted rounds, and every commit after the first two answers one of them.

Closes #1688

author: jss367
body:
## The problem

Merging two keywords refused outright whenever a merged-away row had children:

> A keyword being merged has child keywords. Select individual leaf keywords instead.

And the retained row's identity won every field — its name, parent path, type, Google place link and species link. Coordinates were the only value that could come from another selected row.

Together those made the common geocoding mess unfixable in the UI. Geocoding can leave a second copy of a whole place chain hanging off a bare ZIP code:

```
92004 > United States > California > San Diego County > Borrego Springs > Unnamed Road > Borrego Palm Canyon Trailhead  (3 photos)
United States > California > San Diego County > Borrego Springs > {Nature Trail, Visitor Center}
```

Merging the two `Borrego Springs` rows was blocked by the child guard. The suggested workaround did not exist either: the only tagged leaf in the stray branch has no counterpart under the good one to merge into, and there is no reparent operation, so the subtree could not be moved by hand.

## What changed

**The dialog composes the survivor.** Name, parent path, type, linked place, species link and coordinates are each pickable from any selected row, and the name and coordinates are free-text on top of that. Keeping one row's spelling alongside another row's Google place is now the ordinary case rather than something the guards actively prevented.

**Different links become a question, not a refusal.** Two rows carrying different Google places or different taxa no longer fail the merge. The preview names the field, withholds its token so the button stays disabled, and asks which one is right — a question only the user can answer, since the code cannot tell "same place imported twice" from "two genuinely different places".

**Merging a row with children reparents the subtree.** `_merge_keyword_into` already did this correctly, including the recursive collapse of colliding siblings and the place-id disambiguation that keeps two distinct Google places under one name; only the explicit merge path declined to use it. Merging the two roots of a duplicated chain now collapses the whole thing in one pass instead of requiring a merge per level.

The one arrangement still refused is a selection whose rows nest inside each other — that would write the survivor as its own parent.

**A map.** The dialog plots every selected keyword that has a point plus the point the combined keyword will keep, on OpenStreetMap tiles via the same lazy Leaflet loader `location_review.html` uses. Every coordinate pair in the dialog is also an OSM link, routed through `openExternalLink` so it works in the desktop webview.

## Keeping the preview honest

Per `CORE_PHILOSOPHY.md`, the preview has to state what the merge will actually do, so it replays `_merge_keyword_into`'s own collision rules in memory rather than describing an idealized version. That replay is not only for display — `merge_keywords` uses the predicted paths to queue the sidecar rewrites, and a test asserts the predicted paths equal the paths the write path produces.

That matters because a reparented descendant keeps its flat `dc:subject` word but its `lr:hierarchicalSubject` path and `vireo:locationKeywords` marker name ancestors it no longer has. Each moved row gets a `keyword_merge` change carrying old path → new path, plus a `location` resync for location rows.

`_rename_keyword_dependents` is split out of `_normalize_keyword_row_name` so a chooser rename carries pending sidecar edits and species curation rows with it, the way a plain rename already did.

## Tests

- `vireo/tests/test_keyword_identity.py`: **85 passed** (9 new tests — subtree reparenting, collision fidelity against the write path, root-chain collapse, the place and species questions, cross-row attribute mixing, rename dependents, override validation, token coverage)
- Affected suites (`test_db`, `test_app`, `test_places`, `test_duplicates`, `test_keyword_migration`, `test_keyword_provenance_contract`, `test_workspaces`): **1924 passed, 1 skipped**
- Full unit suite: **8765 passed, 86 skipped, 1 failed** — `test_browse_lightbox_arrows_regression`, which fails identically on `origin/main` (HTTP 500 on `/photos/<id>/full?prefetch=1`), unrelated to this change
- `ruff check vireo/`: clean

Driven in a real browser (Playwright) against a seeded copy of the reported tree: the reported merge now succeeds, the subtree lands where the preview said it would, the two-different-places case asks before merging, and the OSM map renders both candidate points plus the kept one.

## Noted, not fixed

The existing "View place" link in the location-review section (`keywords.html`) is a plain `target="_blank"` anchor, which silently no-ops in the desktop webview. Pre-existing and outside this change.

  * Rebuilt keyword merge dialog lets you compose the resulting record by selecting its name, type, parent, linked place, species, and coordinates.

* **Bug Fixes**

author: jnnngs
body:
## Summary

Fixes the Playwright CI stage failure reported at [run 35424804864, job 105850858030](https://github.com/eyupio/zoomies/actions/runs/35424804864/job/105850858030#step:9:1), where all 551 Playwright tests failed identically at browser launch with:

```
chrome-headless-shell: error while loading shared libraries: libnspr4.so: cannot open shared object file: No such file or directory
```

- The "Install Playwright Chromium" step gated `--with-deps` on `sudo -n true`. On a Zoomies pool running the process backend, the agent's systemd unit sets `NoNewPrivileges=yes`, which makes `sudo` refuse to escalate no matter what the sudoers file says (this is the exact mechanism already diagnosed and fixed for the `installer` job's dash/shellcheck step in a sibling PR). The step silently fell into the plain `npx playwright install chromium` branch, downloading the browser binary with none of its runtime shared libraries — a failure that only surfaced 15 minutes later as a wall of identical test failures.
- Unlike dash/shellcheck, Chromium's runtime libraries genuinely need installing and can't be swapped for a standalone static binary. Where sudo is unavailable, the fix downloads the needed `.deb`s with apt's cache and state redirected into a writable prefix (`Dir::State::Lists` / `Dir::Cache`) and unpacks them with `dpkg -x` — both root-free — then points the browser at the unpacked libraries with `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`.
- The package list is exactly what `playwright install-deps --dry-run chromium` reports on the runner image's own Ubuntu 24.04, minus `xvfb` and the font packages (which only matter for a display `chrome-headless-shell` never opens and aren't exercised by any snapshot test in this repo).

## Verification

Since I don't have access to a process-backend Zoomies runner to reproduce directly, I validated the mechanism on a matching Ubuntu 24.04 x86_64 host:
- Confirmed `playwright install-deps --dry-run chromium`'s exact package list.
- Ran the new root-free branch verbatim as a non-privileged user: `apt-get update`/`download` with redirected state/cache succeeds (exit 0), `dpkg -x` unpacks cleanly.
- Compared every `NEEDED` entry from `objdump -p` on a `chrome-headless-shell`/`headless_shell` binary (including `libnspr4.so`, the library named in the failure) against the unpacked prefix: everything Playwright's own installer would add is present; the only libraries not unpacked by this step are glibc/base-system libraries (`libc.so.6`, `libpthread.so.0`, `libdl.so.2`, `libm.so.6`, `libgcc_s.so.1`, `ld-linux-x86-64.so.2`, `libudev.so.1`, `libexpat.so.1`) that any stock Ubuntu 24.04 install already carries, and that Playwright's own dependency list doesn't include either.
- `go test ./internal/docs/...` passes, including the workflow-shape tests (`TestEveryActionIsPinnedToACommitWithItsVersion`, `TestNoMultiJobWorkflowGrantsWriteToEveryJob`, `TestCIDogfoodsZoomiesWithRecoveryForEveryJob`).

I could not run the actual `Playwright` CI job end-to-end (it requires a live Zoomies process-backend runner), so I'm asking CI to confirm on this PR.

## Test plan

- [x] `go test ./internal/docs/...`
- [x] YAML parses (`python3 -c "import yaml; yaml.safe_load(...)"`)
- [x] Root-free download/unpack mechanism validated against the exact library list `chrome-headless-shell` needs
- [ ] CI's own `Playwright` job goes green on this PR

- External editing now requests a session-level handoff instead of launching a terminal process inside a Terminal.Gui event callback.
- Unwind the UI, save the pane snapshot, and call Program.ShutdownUi before the editor can start. A runner guard rejects calls while a driver is still active.
- Inherit stdin/stdout/stderr without invoking a shell; snapshot arguments and append the draft path as one argument.
- Retain the same draft, filesystem connections and transfer queue across editing and re-editing. Recreate the UI and offer Save, Save as, Re-edit, Keep or Discard after the child exits.
- Queue SSH authentication until the editor releases the terminal. Launch failures and nonzero exits retain edited data.

## Validation
Added Issue17Tests for handoff-only event handling, refusal to launch with an active TUI, inherited stream configuration, spaces/Unicode arguments, draft retention after launch/exit failures and pane restoration. CI will run Windows/Ubuntu regressions, Ubuntu loopback SSH/SFTP integration and all publishing targets before merge.

A physical terminal session with the user's configured editor is not claimed by these fake-driver tests.

author: xizhibei
body:
Upgrading the CLI while an older background runtime is still running can leave lifecycle records without process identity. On Linux, explicit `serve --stop` and `serve --restart` now recover a positively verified supervisor/worker pair using procfs evidence. macOS and Windows preserve those records and provide actionable one-time migration guidance through operator verification and the original CLI or service manager.

Linux recovery verifies exact arguments, claim, parent, user, namespaces and scope files; it rechecks ownership before signals and cleanup and aborts on ambiguous or replacement evidence. Modern persisted-identity restart behavior remains unchanged. Status and client attachment do not initiate recovery.

The implementation adds no native helper or runtime dependency. Build, standalone-binary and release scripts remain unchanged from the base branch. Project control-flow rules favor guard clauses and named decisions over tangled conditional expressions.

Validation:
- Lint, typecheck, standard build, documentation build and actionlint passed.
- 5,532 unit tests passed locally; three platform-specific skips on macOS.
- The installed npm artifact contains no native process helper.
- Real published 0.38.0 Linux stop/restart passed in an isolated container, including copied-scope refusal and subsequent normal restart.
- Real macOS legacy stop/restart refused with guidance, preserved metadata and kept the old runtime ready; normal restart passed after fixture-owned migration.
- Independent safety/scope review completed; CI covers Linux automatic recovery and macOS guided migration, including installed npm entrypoints.

The separate hostname-drift defect is outside this change. All GitHub Actions and CodeQL checks passed at bd745413, including Linux automatic recovery and macOS guided-migration package tests. The latest CodeRabbit review is pending. No merge or release is requested.

author: richpjames
body:
## What

SoundCloud joins Bandcamp, YouTube and Apple Music as a source the release page can play inline: a release with a SoundCloud link gets a listen word in the listen row, and clicking it loads SoundCloud's compact widget into the draggable player window.

## Why the urn dance

SoundCloud's widget refuses permalinks (`soundcloud.com/artist/track`) in any encoding — verified against the live widget — it only plays `api.soundcloud.com/tracks/<id>` resources. That id exists only in the hydra-state JSON in the page body, so the arrangement mirrors Bandcamp's `album_id`:

- `server/soundcloud.ts` (new): `extractSoundcloudUrn` lifts the page's own resource urn (`soundcloud:tracks:123` / `soundcloud:playlists:456`, preferring the playlist on set pages, which also embed their tracks' urns); `soundcloudWidgetSrc` builds the widget URL using SoundCloud's own encoding (colon escaped, slashes literal) and the classic compact player with artwork hidden — the page already shows the cover.
- `server/scraper.ts`: the SoundCloud scrape reads the page body (like Bandcamp) and stores `{soundcloud_urn}` as the link's embed metadata; `server/added-link-scrape.ts` does the same for hand-added links.
- Release page (`+page.server.ts` / `ReleasePage.svelte`): builds the listen word from the stored urn — primary link first, then the first SoundCloud secondary link (Apple Music's hunt order). To support secondary links, `MusicItemLink` now carries its scraped `metadata` (selected in `fetchFullItem`, returned by the add-link endpoint). A link with no stored urn keeps behaving as a plain link out.

## Backfill

SoundCloud links saved before this change have no stored urn, so they stay plain links until rescraped. `scripts/backfill-soundcloud-urns.ts` walks them once (mirroring `backfill-secondary-links.ts`: `--dry-run` / `--limit` / `--delay`; idempotent; merges into existing metadata keys rather than overwriting). Verified end to end against a copy of the dev DB: stored the real urn for a real track, preserved an existing `mixcloud_url` key, and the re-run found nothing left to do.

## Notes

- The player window's audio iframe title changed from "Bandcamp player" to "Audio player" — four services share that iframe now.
- On touch devices the listen word hands off to the SoundCloud site, the same as the other listen words.
- e2e (`playwright/soundcloud-link.spec.ts`) runs the full flow against a real track (live scrape, like the Bandcamp specs), asserting the stored urn, the widget URL on the button, and the player window loading it.

## Verification

- `bun test tests/unit` — 1031 pass (incl. 6 new for the extractor/widget builder)
- `bun run test:e2e` — 61 pass (incl. 1 new)
- `bun run typecheck`, `bun run lint`, `oxfmt --check` — clean

author: teknium1
body:
An inline image of a format the Responses backends do not accept (an SVG source from an old `vision_analyze` result, a BMP/TIFF pasted into a turn) no longer makes the Codex backend reject the whole request — and every later turn — with 400 `The image data you provided does not represent a valid image`.

- `agent/codex_responses_adapter.py::_input_image_part` downgrades a `data:image/<subtype>` part whose subtype is outside jpeg/png/gif/webp to an `input_text` placeholder (`[image omitted: image/svg+xml is not a supported image format]`). It is the single seam behind user/tool message content, `function_call_output.output` (the persisted `vision_analyze` tool-result carrier) and the preflight validator, so all three carriers are covered in one place. Remote `http(s)` image URLs pass through untouched; valid images in the same message still go as `input_image`.
- The recovery half — the loop recognising Codex's "does not represent a valid image" wording as an image rejection and retrying text-only — is already on main (`0241619068`); this PR closes the send-side gap so a poisoned part never reaches the wire in the first place.
- Docs (`website/docs/user-guide/features/vision.md`): `agent.image_input_mode` (`auto` | `native` | `text`) and the explicit `auxiliary.vision` override are now documented — the supported way to keep an `openai-codex` main model while routing image analysis to another vision provider when that backend answers image requests with `server_error` (#82250 asks exactly this).

Root cause: the Responses converter forwarded every `data:image/*` URL as `input_image` regardless of subtype; the input-side guards (`image_routing` skips SVG, `vision_analyze` rasterizes it) do not cover images already baked into history.

**Live repro** (fake Responses API on localhost replaying the exact 400 body from #29711, request built through the real converter + preflight and sent with the real SDK client; `/tmp/batch-openai/lanes/vision-image-openai/probe_codexsvg.py`):

| | wire `input_image` headers | result |
|---|---|---|
| before (`afaa53e5fe8`) | `png`, `svg+xml` (user turn), `svg+xml` (function_call_output) | HTTP 400 "does not represent a valid image" |
| after (this PR) | `png` only; two `[image omitted: image/svg+xml …]` text parts | HTTP 200 |

Tests: `tests/agent/test_codex_responses_adapter.py` — two invariants (history conversion + preflight), red on base (2 failed), green after; `tests/agent/test_codex_responses_adapter.py tests/agent/test_run_agent_multimodal_prologue.py` → 41 passed; `tests/agent/test_provider_parity.py tests/agent/transports/test_codex*.py` → 293 passed.

Fixes #29711
Salvages #47299 (@hanzckernel) — same fix direction, redone against the current converter (superseded).

## Dropped hunks
- #47299's `conversation_loop` phrase addition: already on main as `agent/message_sanitization.py::_IMAGE_REJECTION_PHRASES` (`0241619068`).
- #47299's three separate `_codex_image_or_placeholder_parts` call sites: collapsed into the one `_input_image_part` seam that now exists.

## Follow-up (df4b748926e6188dc790a8529185ef162e15a037)

Rasterize instead of drop, as the #29711 thread asked: an inline `data:image/svg+xml` part is now converted to a PNG `input_image` at the same send-layer seam when a rasterizer is installed (`cairosvg`, `svglib`+`reportlab`, `rsvg-convert` or `inkscape` — the soft dependencies `vision_analyze` already uses, reached through a new `tools/vision_tools_image_prep.rasterize_svg_data_url`, lazily imported), so the model still sees the drawing. Without a rasterizer the text placeholder from the first commit still applies, so SVG source never reaches the wire. ~30 LOC; vision.md documents both outcomes; 1 new invariant test (rasterizer present → PNG `input_image`), the two placeholder tests now pin the no-rasterizer case explicitly.

Live (real converter, temp `HERMES_HOME`, throwaway venv with cairosvg): base + cairosvg → `input_text` placeholder; fixed + cairosvg → `input_image` `data:image/png;base64,…` (PNG magic `89 50 4E 47` verified); fixed without any rasterizer → placeholder.

## Infographic
![SVG image no longer breaks the whole request](https://v3b.fal.media/files/b/0aab0521/Jv-JYXuHoJZzN6Wuci3ka_DlYi6zgK.png)



## Follow-up (a580d1991b1a98c9fd9b8fe3d5aad96b27a98d4a)

- `image/jpg` alias (`agent/codex_responses_adapter.py`) — **fixed**: the guard treated `data:image/jpg;base64` as unsupported and downgraded a valid JPEG to a text placeholder; it now counts as JPEG like every other image site in the tree. Assertion added to the existing placeholder test (red before, green after).
- Anthropic sibling (`agent/anthropic_message_convert.py::_image_source_from_openai_url`) — **fixed**: inline `svg+xml` / `bmp` / `tiff` were forwarded verbatim as `media_type` (400 on every turn once in history). The converter now applies the same rule as the Responses path — SVG rasterized to PNG when a rasterizer exists, any other unsupported inline subtype → text placeholder, `image/jpg` normalized to `image/jpeg`. Both paths share one helper (`tools/vision_tools_image_prep.unsupported_inline_image_media_type`) next to the existing supported-set constant. 1 new test through `convert_messages_to_anthropic` (red before, green after).
- Attribution — **independent redo**: compared `gh pr diff 47299` with this PR's diff — no code or tests were reused (different helper names, placeholder text, seam and test files), so no `Co-authored-by` trailer is warranted; "Salvages #47299" above means same fix direction only, redone from scratch.

Tests: `tests/agent/test_codex_responses_adapter.py tests/agent/test_anthropic_adapter.py tests/tools/test_vision_tools.py` → 173 passed.

author: roed-math
body:
Adds a second machine header to `STATUS.md`, `tauceti-coverage:v1`: the report's verdict on each layer of the roadmap (done / partial / untouched / unassessed, with one line on what remains), in a form a script can read. The prose already says these things; the header exists so forty roadmaps' worth of them can be put on one page without a person re-reading every report. The consumer is the Progress page proposed for the TauCeti site in TauCetiProject/TauCeti#7502, which today reads the same verdicts from a hand-transcribed file and would read them from this header instead.

## What changes

Following the repository's design rule, the model still only writes prose, and every decision is made by tested code:

- **`plan`** records the roadmap's layers in the plan: the README's `Layer` / `Lane` / `Part` / `Stage` headings (or `L0A`-style labels), each with its id, title and line, plus `readme_sha`, a SHA-256 of the README's text. A README with no such headings gives no layers and no header. The extraction rule is the same one the consumer uses, and the cross-check below confirms the two agree on every current roadmap.
- **The writing prompt** asks the model to end the status prose with a fenced ```` ```coverage ```` block, one line per listed id in the plan's order: `Layer 0: partial — what remains`. The state is one of four words; the note is optional, one line, at most 200 characters.
- **`apply`** removes the block from the prose, checks that it names every listed layer exactly once and nothing else with a legal state, and writes the header. A block that does not fit is refused on the worker, so a half-right assessment never reaches a pull request. A body with no block gives a report with no header, exactly as every report was before this change.
- **The format and the gate** (`files.py`) treat the header as part of the canonical prefix: it must sit on the line after the status header and nowhere else, name the same roadmap and commit, and pass a closed schema (bounded layer count, restricted ids, notes without angle brackets so nothing can close the HTML comment). The reserved-marker scan strips it along with the status header before scanning the prose. A status file without the header is unchanged and still passes.

What the gate proves about the header is its shape, never its truth, as for the prose. It cannot check `readme_sha` (it never checks out the roadmap repository); the consumer does, and refuses a header whose hash does not match the README it read the layers from, showing those layers as unassessed rather than applying an old verdict to new requirements. That binding is why layer ids alone are not enough: a layer's requirements can change under an unchanged heading.

## Scope of this first version

`plan` reads the selected labelled area's own README and nothing below it. An umbrella area whose README is an index of sub-roadmaps with READMEs of their own (RepresentationTheory) has no layer headings itself, so its reports carry no header, and the sub-roadmaps' layers are not assessed by this pipeline at all: on the Progress page they stay on hand transcriptions. A sub-roadmap assessment needs a carrier of its own (its own roadmap identity, README hash and layer-id namespace) agreed with the gate and the consumer together; it is not done here, and a planner test records the limitation.

The standalone `prompt status` template is a second interface. It is handed no layer list, so it stays prose-only and now says so: a report written from it carries no coverage header. The worker's `prompt progress` is the one that asks for the block.

## Files

- `progress/layers.py` (new): heading extraction, the block parser, and the assembly of a validated payload.
- `progress/files.py`: the marker, its schema and validators, the prefix, parsing and the reserved-marker scan.
- `progress/plan.py`, `progress/apply.py`: carrying the layers, and turning the block into the header.
- `progress/prompts/progress.md`: the block instructions.
- `README.md`: a section on the header.
- Tests: `tests/test_layers.py` (new), and additions to `test_files.py`, `test_apply_announce.py`, `test_window.py` (the plan's exact inventory and hash; the umbrella case) and `test_prompts.py` (the prompt's states and bound are checked against the validator's constants, by interface). `./tests/run` passes in full.
- `tests/test_contract.py` with `tests/fixtures/coverage-contract/` (new): an offline producer/consumer fixture. A README, the model's body with its block, and `expected.json` recording what `plan` and `apply` emit and what the consumer at TauCeti `9477d5c` made of it: layer ids and lines, states, notes, and its refusals against an edited README body, an edited title with stable ids, and another library commit. The test proves the producer still emits that header byte for byte and that the gate accepts the pair. Nothing is fetched in CI.

## Cross-check with the consumer

Run locally against a current TauCetiRoadmap checkout: the producer and the consumer extract identical layer ids for all 49 roadmaps and 12 sub-roadmaps; a status rendered from EllipticCurves' real README with a synthetic block is accepted by the consumer's validator with the intended states and notes, and refused by it against an edited README.

## After merging

- TauCetiRoadmap's `progress-merge.yml` pins this repository by SHA in two places; that pin needs a bump for the gate to accept the new prefix (until then a report carrying the header would be refused by the old gate, and one without it is accepted by both).
- The worker's `PROGRESS_REF` moves the same way.
- No report changes until the pin moves; a report without the block is still a valid report afterwards.

author: hedalu244
body:
## 目的

段 1〜5 で書いた規則(`DEVELOP/ARCHITECTURE.md`)の言い直しと、未達の是正の段(臨時の段 5.5)。**新しい規則は書いていない。**

段 5 までは、判定の無い規則を「許可リストが空だから満たした」と扱っていた。この段では、判定できる規則を形で判定し直し、判定の無い規則を洗い出して、見つけた違反をこの段の中で直した。直さずに残すものは、規則の文面を暫定で狭めるか、例外として理由を書いた。

## 変更

### 書き直した規則
- **ARCHITECTURE R3**: 所有者は状態を宣言したクラス。モデル層の面は命令・読み取り面・出来事だけで、可変な public 欄と `set` アクセサを持たない(export する型も可変な欄を持たない)。整合性は所有者が保つ。
- **ARCHITECTURE の層の中身(`physics/`)**: 定数・純関数・結果を変えないメモ化キャッシュ(R1)・意味を持たない容器だけ。
- **CODING-RULE 1.11**: モデル層の可変な public 欄を禁じる文を足した。

### 検査(`tools/check-boundaries.mjs`)
- 構文木で判定する2つを足した: 「モデル層の可変な公開欄の禁止」(R3)と「直列化された形をコンストラクタで受ける禁止」(R12。名前の正規表現の行と置き換えた)。
- 名前の列で装置の命令を拾っていた「命令 API の禁止」の行は外した(名前で形を代用していたため)。
- **許可リスト(`tools/boundary-allowlist.json`)は空になった。**

### 洗い出しの結果
段 5 までの規則を規則ごとに洗い(R1・R3・R5・R7・R8・R11/R12・R13)、振り分けの表に行を足した。この段で直したもの:
- **R3**: 運動の値は運動だけが書き、外からは命令(推力・トルク・生死・状態の差し替え・質量)で変える。武装・部品・スコア・高度警報ほかのモデル層の欄も、宣言したクラスだけが書く。スコアの集計器・給弾ベルトの配列・出来事の列を可変のまま外へ渡さない。即時実行の計画の消化は自機の命令にした。
- **R7**: 音の装置(効果音・UI 音・BGM)は宣言だけを受ける。単発音は出来事の通し番号で二度鳴らさない。BGM は音量・ランの進行・試聴中の曲を毎フレームの宣言で受ける。閃光の装置は見え方(色・大きさ・明るさ)だけを受け、どの出来事がどう光るか・照準ズームで減光するかは表示の導出が決める。カメラのフレームからビューを外した。
- **R8**: 時間加速の段の上下を領域の命令にし、キーの解釈を入力の表へ移した。ステージの決着は出来事として記録し、launcher がフレームの後に読む。
- **R11/R12**: 実体の採番は `create`・`deserialize` が行い、コンストラクタは採番済みの id を受ける。顔ぶれは記録の列を構築の引数で受ける。生死を実体の共通の記録に持たせた。子の記録は持ち主が直列化・復元する。保存の版の刻印をモデル層から launcher の記録本体へ移した(形式は同じ)。
- **R13**: マーカー群は受けた側が装置から作り、計画折れ線とビューは作った根が畳む。同じ協力者を二経路で受けない。
- **CODING-RULE 1.11・1.6**: 状態を進めて副産物を返す関数(ブースターの燃焼と点火、燃料、射撃、スロットルの推力とトルク、接触代理の置き直し、タンパク質の撃つ部位と被弾、計画のノード追加ほか)を命令と問い合わせに分けた。閉包の注入をやめた。不在を `null` で表した。
- 表示の不具合: マーカーの `cls` の貼り直し、窓の行の見出しの差分、天体ラベルの古い状態、戦闘ビューに残る相対交点。
- 定数の手写し: 既定部品の性能を自機の側から渡し、基地のトルク・軌道ガイドの系の一覧を所有者から引く。

段の終わりにもう一度、5.5-3 の後に変わったファイルを規則ごとに洗い、見つけた違反をこの段で直した。後の段が対象ごと作り直す行は、その段(6・7・8)の手順へ回した(`dynamic-motion.ts`・`plan-editor.ts` の長さを含む)。

### 規約点検(`/refactor`・`/comment-cleanup`)
- lint の自動修正(型だけの import)を当て、要らなくなった suppressions を消した。
- コメントを点検した: 禁止に当たる説明を削り、実装と食い違っていたコメントを直し、足りない呼出規約と文脈を足した。コードは変えていない。

### 次の段まで有効な暫定(10)
- `hud/` は表示の導出として扱い、モデル層とアプリ寿命の正本への import だけを禁じる(段 8)
- `game/` はモデル層と表示の導出の同居として扱う(段 6)/表示の導出の置き場は当面 `src/game/` の中(段 8)
- **軌跡**: `dynamic-trajectory.ts` と `ApsisTrack` は可変な記録を持ったまま `physics/` にある(段 6)— 行き先が実体・運動・軌跡の設計で変わりうるので、段 6 の着手前に決める
- R3: 表示の導出はモデル層の根と所有者を具象のまま受けてよい(段 8)
- R5: 被選択物の2フレームの猶予を通した解決から、視点への命令を作ってよい(段 8)
- R7: カメラの投影は `render/` が確定させ、表示の導出が読んでよい(段 8)
- R8: 入力の解釈は押し続ける入力を実時間 `dt` で積んでよい(段 8)
- モデル層が装置を import しない規則は `src/game/` の中のパスで当てる(段 6 で層の規則へ置き換える)
- R13: 実体と運動・反応は、同じ協力者を構築時に受けながら呼ぶたびにも受けてよい(段 6)

洗い出しで足した5つ(R3・R5・R7・R8・R13)は、直すと後の段がすぐ作り直すものか、直し方に設計の判断が残るもの。

### 例外(`例外(ARCHITECTURE Rn):` のコメント)
- **R12 — 保存の形式が2つの持ち主の値を1つの記録に混ぜている(4か所)**: 実体の記録に運動の値(状態・姿勢・熱・生死。自機では運動の部品の記録も)、顔ぶれの記録に `Simulator` の `simTime`、カメラの記録の `offset`・`up`・`rotatingWith`(向きと注視距離の合成)、記録本体の最上位に launcher の形式の版。持ち主ごとに分けると保存の形式が変わり、段 5 の版(4)の記録が読めなくなる。
- **R12 — `DynamicSystem` が個体の記録を構築の引数で受けて復元する**: 個体の復元は顔ぶれそのもの(採番器・出来事の記録)を要るので、組む前には復元できない。
- **R11 — `RunEventLog` を直列化しない**: 出来事は進行の位相の先頭で空にする1フレームの通り道で、読み手もランと一緒に作り直す。保存すると、読み込んだフレームに前のランの音と通知が出る。
- **再設計の提案**: R12 に形式の混在の例外が重なった。規則のほうではなく形式が誤っているので、**版を上げて形式を持ち主ごとに直す**ことを提案する。上げると段 5 の記録が読めなくなるので、段 6 以降の検証の基準(段 5 のセーブが読める)と一緒に判断が要る。

### 変えた挙動
- **タンパク質の銃口と被弾部位を、表示中の揺らぎではなく静止構造から決める**(K10-11)。ズーム・時刻スライダー・揺らぎの表示設定で変わらなくなった。部位マーカーと結合線は、これまでどおり表示中の揺らぎに追従する。PR #82 の意図(見た目と判定・発射の一致)をここで戻す。見た目との一致は、判定形状の近似か揺らぎか潜在バグかが未評価なので、`fix_protain_combat.md` で別に調べる。SPEC は先に `docs(spec):` の単独 commit で削った(PROTEIN.md・RENDERING.md。挙動を固定していた文・実装の近似・INVARIANTS §3 の言い直し)。
- 一時停止中に消した補給物・失った自艦・壊れた基地が、セーブを読み込んでも生き返らない。
- セーブデータ画面は、形式の版が合わない手動セーブを読み込めるものとして並べず、開こうとしたら理由を出す(黙って新しいランを始めていた)。
- BGM の消音を音量と別の設定に持つ。消音前の音量が再読み込みを跨いで残る。手で 0 にした音量から消音ボタンで戻すと、既定の音量 1 になる。
- 相対昇交点・降交点・再接近点は、マップビューでだけ出す(戦闘ビューでは前のマップのフレームの位置が残っていた)。
- 決着から結果画面・BGM の切り替えまでが最大1フレーム遅れる(決着を出来事として読むため)。

### この段で書いていないこと
実体と運動の境界(K10-6)、軌跡の置き場(K10-7)、実体の形状の正本(K11)は段 6 で扱う。

## 注意
- **セーブの形式の版は変えていない(4)。** 実体の記録に省略可能な `alive` を足した。無い記録は生存として読む。
- 設定の鍵 `tepui.settings.bgm_muted` を足した。

## 検証
CI(`.github/workflows/build.yml`)の順で、手元(Windows)で回した。
- `npm ci`: 通過
- `npm run verify:ui-style`: 通過(129 ファイル)
- `npm run lint`: error 0
- `npm run check:boundaries`: 通過。許可リストは空
- `npm run typecheck`: 通過
- `npm run test`: 1003/1003
- `npm run build`(CI の既定の環境変数): 通過。webpack の容量の警告 2 件
- `npm run earth-surface:pages-stage`: 通過
- `npm run earth-surface:pages-check`: **手元で落ちる**(`Pages receipt does not match bundle`)。検査ツールと入力(ツールが組む fixture)はこのブランチで触っていないので、手元の環境に依る失敗と見ている。CI で確かめる
- `npm run smoke:browser`: 通過(`?stage=00`)。通過の後の一時ディレクトリの削除が Windows の EPERM で落ちる

**回していないもの(目視)**: `npm run dev` での確認 — 射撃・装填・被弾・空撃ちの音と、一時停止中・決着後に効果音が鳴り続けないこと、設定画面の BGM の音量変更・消音・試聴、決着から結果画面、時間加速の上げ下げ、マップの右クリックとプロパティ窓の時刻表示、ブースターの燃焼と分離、敵の射撃と敵の一覧、版の違う記録を置いたセーブデータ画面、タンパク質陣形(5i4r)が撃ち撃たれて部位が壊れること(揺らぎを切っても部位 HP の減り方が変わらない)、段 5 で書き出したセーブの読み込み。

author: danielmake
body:
## Summary

Follow-up to #21. Adds tests for the untested pure logic and the registry, and fixes two bugs those tests exposed.

**Bugs fixed**
- `nodevin view` always showed 0 days of uptime. `extractUptime` parsed Docker's `"Up 3 days"` with `Sscanf("%d days")`, which cannot match the leading `Up`, so the uptime-based health tiers never triggered. It also ignored `Up 2 weeks`, `Up 3 months`, `Up 2 years` and `Up About an hour`. Hours still count as 1, as before.
- `--cpu-limit`, `--mem-limit`, `--cpu-reservation` and `--mem-reservation` were merged in `CreateComposeFile` but never applied to the main service. They only worked for companion services (`ord`, `ipfs-cluster`). The main service now gets `Deploy` the same way companions do.

**Tests added** (`utils` 25% to 90%, `compose` 71% to 79%, `nodes` 9% to 18%)
- Registry: structural invariants (unique container names, `<mainnet>-testnet` naming that `delete`/`stop` rely on, testnet networks not command-supported), every accessor, sorted lists, `GetSizeDescription`, the testnet flag logic
- `createExtraServices`: init container and dependency wiring, `Environment` carried through, user volumes and existing data (>= 1 GB, using a sparse file) skipping the init container, and the full `CreateComposeFile` composition with a companion plus watchtower
- User-flag overrides for image, version, restart, ports, container name and resource limits
- `nodes` helpers: `formatPorts`, `extractUptime`, endpoint helpers, `getDirectorySize`, name switches, extra `parseRPCCount` edge cases, and `makeRequest`'s `jsonrpc` 1.0/2.0 behavior from #19
- Cross-checks that tie the hand-maintained endpoint chain, `view.go` name switches and `isEthereumStyleRPC` to `networkInfoMap`, so adding a chain to one place and not the others fails a test

## Reviewer notes

- Production changes are limited to `view.go` (`extractUptime`) and `compose.go` (one `if isDeploySet` block).
- The suite passes with `-race` and `-shuffle=on -count=3`; the tests share global `viper` state, and a per-test unique service name is used where `viper.Set` can't be undone.
- Two things I noticed but did not change: `ord`, `ord-testnet`, `ord-litecoin` and `ord-litecoin-testnet` all bind host port 80, so `ord` and `ord-litecoin` can't run together; and the watchtower command's container order comes from map iteration, so it varies between runs.

## Test plan
- [x] `go build ./... && go vet ./... && go test ./... -count=1` pass locally
- [x] `go test ./... -race` and `-shuffle=on -count=3` pass locally
- [x] CI workflow from #21 runs green on this PR

author: obvious-autobuild[bot]
body:
## Why

IdeaForge's Wave-1 spec is a set of honesty promises, and the UI was quietly breaking them in seven places: preferences you saved in Settings were ignored on the Dashboard, the Trend Radar spoke generically instead of naming your niche, the save toast confirmed a save without ever showing where the idea went, reminders could only be snoozed for one fixed duration, a wrongly logged analytics number could never be corrected, and the Dashboard copy path skipped the LinkedIn quality lint that runs everywhere else. Each fix here restores a promise the product explicitly makes.

## What

Seven focused fixes, each commit mapping 1:1 to a fix in the spec (art_YGBAEBjk, §Honesty bundle):

| # | Fix | Commit |
|---|-----|--------|
| 1 | Dashboard opens on the saved niche and tone from preferences | `7dd7ef8` |
| 2 | Trend Radar heading tracks the selected niche | `1ef982e` |
| 3 | Craft-pack pricing comparison, BYOK spelling, move copy (landing/board) | `ea6fb60` |
| 4 | Save toast links to the Board | `d7e134f` |
| 5 | Snooze offers 1h, 4h, and 24h options | `ead71ff` |
| 6 | Logged analytics metrics are viewable and correctable | `f923dab` |
| 7 | Dashboard copy path runs the LinkedIn lint | `4a58b9e` |

**Salvage provenance:** this work was authored by a prior worker thread that pushed the branch and died before opening a PR. It was verified commit-by-commit against the spec (no implementation gaps found, nothing rewritten), validated from zero, dogfooded against the release base, and shipped here unchanged apart from this PR itself.

Coverage added by the bundle: 9 new unit test files (~920 lines) plus E2E journey `j12-dashboard-copy-lint.spec.js`.

## How to Review

- Fix 1 is the restore rule only: `resolveSavedDefaults` in `Dashboard.js` is pure (testable without the page), and a stored value the selectors can't render is ignored rather than guessed at. Tones match case-insensitively because the backend stores them lowercase while the UI list is display-cased.

author: willywang8216
body:
## Problem

Every X publish was failing with:

- `Page.goto: Timeout 30000ms exceeded`
- `TargetClosedError` mid-typing
- `RuntimeError: Twitter publish button did not become ready in time`

The composer is not the problem: x.com serves the **home timeline next to the compose page**, and that timeline autoplays multi-megabyte 4K clips from `video.twimg.com`. Those downloads saturate the browserless session (bandwidth + decoder), so the composer never becomes interactive inside the timeout budget.

## Fix

Route the publish session and abort bulky responses:

- resource types `media` and `font`
- URLs containing `video.twimg.com` and `pbs.twimg.com/amplify_video_thumb`

Page markup, GraphQL and `CreateTweet` calls are untouched — only the heavy media pressure is removed.

Best-effort by design: if routing cannot be installed the failure is logged and the unmodified context is used, so this can never make a publish fail on its own.

## Tests

`tests/test_twitter_block_heavy_media.py` — 7 tests: aborts video-host media, aborts the amplify thumbnail, aborts fonts, passes documents/GraphQL/scripts through, swallows a routing failure, and asserts the blocklist covers `video.twimg.com`.

body:
## 問題

https://harukaho-cell.github.io/my-first-repo/ を開くと、床屋ぐっさんのページではなく README が表示されていました。

## 原因

このリポジトリの GitHub Pages は **2026年5月28日から「Deploy from a branch」方式で有効**になっていました（`main` の直下を公開する設定）。

`index.html` を `public/` へ移動したことで直下からHTMLが消え、Jekyll が `README.md` をトップページとして変換・表示していました。

追加した Actions ワークフローによる公開は成功していましたが、その32秒後に旧方式のビルドが走って上書きされていました（実行記録で確認）。

| 時刻 | 実行 | 結果 |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 06:50:37 | Deploy to GitHub Pages（追加したワークフロー） | 成功 |
| 06:51:09 | pages build and deployment（旧方式） | 成功 → **こちらが最終的に反映** |

## 修正内容

Pages の設定変更を必要としない方法として、旧方式に合わせて構成を戻します。

- `public/index.html` → `index.html`（直下）
- `public/sakura-seikotsuin.html` → `sakura-seikotsuin.html`（直下）
- `.nojekyll` を追加し、HTMLを加工せずそのまま配信
- 上書きされて機能しない `.github/workflows/deploy-pages.yml` を削除
- `README.md` / `DEPLOY.md` を実際の公開方式に合わせて修正

マージ後、旧方式のビルドが自動で走り、トップページが床屋ぐっさんのページになります。

## 補足

`hello.py` などの練習用ファイルも公開URL配下に置かれる形になります。分離したい場合は Settings → Pages → Source を `GitHub Actions` に切り替える必要があり、その手順は `DEPLOY.md` に記載しています。

author: agenta-asaf
body:
Implements Phase 2 of `docs/specs/SPEC_AGENT_PANE_CLOSE_GRACEFUL_SHUTDOWN_2026_09_18.md` (§9, spec merged in #3405). Follow-up to #3402.

## What changes

Closing a pane, a pane tab, a window tab or a window now stops each agent gracefully instead of hard-killing it.

- **New `Controller::shutdown(deadline) -> StopOutcome`.** The default is today's immediate stop. The persistent (Claude stream-json) controller:
  - interrupts an active turn with the control-protocol interrupt and waits for its result;
  - then sends EOF;
  - force-kills only at the deadline.
  
  This follows the Phase 0 measurement (spec §5.1): EOF alone lets a running turn finish first (22.8s), while the interrupt ends it in about 2s.
- **A requested stop is not a failure.** The interrupted turn's `is_error` / `error_during_execution` result no longer raises a failure banner or triggers a stale-resume retry (`shutdown_generation`).
- **`shutdown_agents()`** is used by `delete_block`, `close_pane`, `delete_tab` and `delete_workspace`.
  - Agents stop concurrently under one deadline, so ten agents take about 5s, not 50s.
  - The process tracker is dropped only after the process has exited.
  - One `agent_shutdown` log line per agent records the outcome and elapsed time.
- **`delete_tab`** checks the last-tab guard under a per-workspace lock *before* stopping anything. A refused close can't leave a tab of stopped agents.
- **`agent.open`** waits for this agent's closing blocks before its live-elsewhere check. A reopen during the grace window can't start a second `--resume` on the same session.
- `stop(true, …)` stays immediate. The watchdog, controller replacement and `delete_controller` all rely on that (spec §9.3).

## Not in this PR

- **ACP and app-server controllers keep the immediate stop.** Spec §9.3 requires measuring each provider's exit behavior first.
- **Picker reattach wait:** that is Phase 3.

## Tests

- `persistent::shutdown_tests` runs a real node stub that behaves as measured:
  - mid-turn → interrupted, `Exited`, no `EVENT_AGENT_FAILURE`;
  - idle → exits on EOF;
  - ignores both → `Killed` at the deadline;
  - never spawned → `NotRunning`.
  
  These tests skip if `node` isn't on PATH. The check uses a PATH lookup, not a spawn, so it doesn't trip the I7 spawn-site inventory.
- `close_pane::tests` covers:
  - three agents that take 1s each finish in about 1s;
  - last-tab refusal stops nothing;
  - a window-tab close stops its agents;
  - the closing-wait signal.
- Full `agentmux-srv` suite run locally with `--test-threads=1`: all passed after the spawn-inventory fix.

author: nadaverell
body:
## Summary

Fix container-specific log findings appearing under “Notes without a card” even when Radar captured the relevant logs. When an agent omitted `container` from `get_pod_logs`, the response did not name the selected container, and Findings substituted the literal identity `default container`. A claim naming the real container therefore could not match its log card.

## What changed

- `get_pod_logs` returns the container it explicitly requested. If the argument is omitted, Radar reads the Pod with the caller-scoped client and explicitly selects its sole application container. Explicit requests, including init/ephemeral containers, need no extra metadata read.
- A denied or failed Pod metadata read does not prevent a permitted log read. Ambiguous multi-container Pods keep the existing Kubernetes selection/error behavior; Radar does not choose the first container or invent an identity.
- Findings prefers the response identity. Saved runs without that field can use an explicitly recorded container argument. Otherwise the stream is labeled “container unknown”; separate unknown reads are not merged as if they were the same stream.
- Container-specific claim matching remains strict: a claim about `app` can attach to the `app` stream, not `proxy` or an unknown stream. Current and previous instances remain distinct.

## Testing

- `make tsc`
- `make test`
- `make build`
- `npx vitest run src/components/diagnose` — 632 tests passed
- Focused Go regression tests cover explicit/resolved identity, logs-only permissions, ambiguous streams, API failures, filtering, previous-instance reads, and capped/uncapped responses.
- Projection and rendering tests cover saved results, producer identity precedence, unknown streams, and named-container claim placement.
- Live GCP nonproduction: a crash-looping Pod's current and previous log reads omitted `container` and returned the correct container identity.
- Live AWS nonproduction: an existing multi-container Pod retained Kubernetes' selection error when `container` was omitted; explicit reads returned the correct identity for each of its two application containers.
- End-to-end safeguarded investigation: the agent independently called `get_pod_logs` without `container`, received the resolved identity, and cited that exact result with a named-container cause claim. The completed Findings UI attached the claim to the matching log card and included it in the analysis, rather than leaving it as a source-only note.
- Visual-test: inspected the expanded live log card and its attached cause claim. No cluster mutations or remediation; temporary local test servers stopped afterward.

## Tradeoff

Requests omitting `container` add one best-effort Pod GET. When metadata cannot establish the identity, the captured logs remain available but cannot support a container-specific card placement. This deliberately preserves uncertainty rather than guessing.

<!-- CURSOR_SUMMARY -->
---

> [!NOTE]
> **Low Risk**
> Changes log-fetch metadata and evidence projection UX; no auth or cluster mutation paths, with conservative behavior when container identity cannot be resolved.
> 
> **Overview**
> **`get_pod_logs`** now names the log stream in every response via a **`container`** field, and the MCP docs describe **`previous`** / **`since`** plus when callers must pass **`container`** for multi-container pods.
> 
> When **`container`** is omitted, the handler best-effort **GETs the Pod** and pins the sole application container on the log request; explicit container names skip that read. If Pod metadata is forbidden or the pod is ambiguous, logs still fetch but **`container`** may be empty rather than guessing. Responses are always the structured wrapper (logs + optional **`container`**, **`narrowHint`**, **`warnings`**) instead of returning bare filtered logs when there are no hints.
> 
> **Findings / investigation UI** stops treating missing container as **`default container`**: it prefers the tool result’s **`container`**, falls back to saved args, otherwise labels **container unknown** and gives each unknown read a distinct stream identity so container-specific cause claims attach only to matching log cards (current vs previous unchanged).
>

author: furgalep
body:
## Summary

- report the installed summarizer's real policy, token budget, configured percentage, and pending/ready state
- start automatic compaction earlier, at 75% of the usable input window by default
- make the percentage user-configurable with `threshold_fraction`
- keep compaction fully asynchronous: model generation never waits for an in-flight summary
- retain `max_tokens` as an explicit absolute-threshold override

## Root cause

`get_summarization_status()` read attributes that do not exist on `TokenBudgetSummarizer`; the values live under `summarizer.config`. It therefore reported `policy=none` and zero limits despite an installed summarizer.

Separately, automatic compaction started at 80% of usable input. On a large session, the background summary could still be running while the active prompt consumed the remaining headroom, allowing the TUI to report context above 100% of the usable window.

## Behavior

When `max_tokens` is unset, the trigger is:

```text
(model context window - reply-token reserve) * threshold_fraction
```

`threshold_fraction` defaults to `0.75`, must be strictly between `0` and `1`, and is recalculated when the model, reasoning level, or reply-token limit changes. Setting `max_tokens` pins an absolute threshold instead.

Compaction remains non-blocking. A pending summary is applied at the normal turn boundary once it is ready.

## Verification

- regression tests were observed failing before the production changes
- 100 affected summarization/runtime/coding-agent tests pass
- full nooa-cli suite: 289 passed, 2 skipped
- Ruff and `git diff --check` pass
- live GLM 5.3 E2E deliberately blocked the summary request and proved the parent returned `READY` without waiting; after release, the summary applied, input dropped from 6,663 to 2,155 tokens, and all exact facts survived the continuation

author: jaro-c
body:
## Summary

- `Email/get` returned header values exactly as they sit in the message, so a subject `=?UTF-8?B?wqFIb2xhIQ==?=` reached a JMAP client as that literal string instead of `¡Hola!`. RFC 8621 defines `subject` as `header:Subject:asText` and the address properties as `asAddresses`, and both forms decode RFC 2047 encoded-words. Every subject with an accent was affected.
- `Email/set` create wrote a non-ASCII subject as a raw 8-bit header. It now writes UTF-8 `B` encoded-words.
- IMAP `SEARCH SUBJECT` / `FROM` / `TO` / `CC` / `BCC` and `SORT (SUBJECT)` compare against the decoded text. `ENVELOPE` stays raw, because clients decode it.

## Changes

- `src/util/encoded_word.rs` gains `encode`: printable ASCII is returned unchanged; anything else becomes `=?UTF-8?B?...?=` words of at most 75 characters, never splitting a UTF-8 character across two words, folded with `CRLF SP`.
- `src/api/jmap/objects.rs` (helpers in `objects_headers.rs`): the address list is parsed FIRST and the display name decoded AFTER, so an encoded-word that decodes to `a>, <evil@example.net` stays data inside `name` and cannot become a second address.
- That parser fixes a defect that was already there: `from[0].email` used to carry the whole header value (`Alice <a@example.org>`), and the test asserted it. It is now `{ name: "Alice", email: "a@example.org" }`.
- `sanitize_header_value` still runs before `encode`, so CR and LF in user input never reach a header; the header-injection test is extended to a non-ASCII subject.
- Two leftovers in `src/cli/`: the `reports` arm printed `error:` by hand instead of through `style`, and a doc comment said "DMRC".

## Test plan

- [x] `cargo fmt --all --check` is clean
- [x] `cargo clippy --locked --all-targets --all-features -- -D warnings` is clean
- [x] `cargo test --locked --all-features --workspace` passes locally
- [x] `RUSTDOCFLAGS="-D warnings" cargo doc --locked --no-deps --all-features` is clean
- [ ] interop and e2e: left to CI (this touches `src/imap/**`)

- [x] New or changed checks were verified by deleting the control and watching them fail. On the final tree: leaving display names undecoded, writing the subject without `encode`, and searching the raw header each turn their own test red. Decoding the header before parsing the address list turns the injection test red (two addresses instead of one). Splitting encoded-words on bytes instead of characters turns the round-trip test red.

- [x] Targets `develop`

- [x] Conventional Commit title on the pull request

author: marutama
body:
## Summary

Second installment of the post-Stage-L inventory, **stacked on #469**. Five more `unsafe fn` go, but the point is the duplication underneath them: four call sites reached for `libc::strtol` on a raw `*const c_char` although every one already held the bytes in something Rust owned.

- **`support/strtol.rs` (new)** — one `strtol(&[u8], base) -> i32` reproducing exactly the part of C's `strtol` this crate uses. It replaces `table/cmap.rs`'s `atoi` **and** `parse_hex`, two hand-rolled copies from Stage E differing only in the digit predicate.
  `support/ttinstr.rs` deliberately keeps its own `strtol_base0`/`strtol_base2`: those return how many bytes they consumed (their caller is a lexer that must advance past the number) and base 0 sniffs `0x`/`0` prefixes. Folding them in would hand every other caller an end position it does not want — noted as follow-up, not forced.
- **A latent panic fixed on the way** — the predecessors accumulated into an `i64` and cast, so a long enough digit run overflowed: silently wrapping in release, but *panicking* under `debug_assertions`, which is Miri and `cargo fuzz`'s default profile. The object keys reaching `parse_unicode` come straight from fuzzed JSON, so this was reachable. Explicit `wrapping_*` keeps release behavior and makes debug agree with it.
- **`json_reader.rs`'s `place_order_entries_from_cmap`** inlined the `U+XXXX`-or-decimal parse byte for byte (`strlen`, `strtol`, `.offset()` over the key's raw storage) — and its own comment said it was the same as `cmap::parse_unicode`. It now calls that. The file's private `atoi` copy had no other caller.
- **`logger.rs`'s `logger_indent`** was a `*const c_char` shim over `logger_indent_sds`; all three callers passed a `b"otfccdump\0"`-style literal. Deleted — they call `logger_indent_sds` directly, which is already how the crate's ~30 `logger_start_sds` sites work.
- **Both `bin/` `atoi` copies** go, and with them the `CString::new(..).expect("must not contain a NUL byte")` dance that existed only to produce a pointer. `--glyph-name-prefix` lost the same round trip.

`main_0` still cannot lose its marker, now for exactly two named reasons: `fprintf`/`stderr` for usage and CLI-error output, and `stopwatch.rs`'s `time_now`/`push_stopwatch` (the `%g` work the user has deferred). Converting those `fprintf`s to `eprint!` is the obvious next step and is deliberately not here.

## Test effectiveness

Checked rather than assumed, both ways. A temporary counter showed `place_order_entries_from_cmap` runs **24,167 times in `golden.rs` alone** (all decimal keys) and `parse_unicode`'s hex branch **4,712 times** across the integration suite (via `cycles.rs`'s dump→build round trips, where the dump writes `U+XXXX` and the build reads it back) — so both branches sit under byte-exact coverage. Then a deliberate one-digit bug in `strtol`: the two new unit tests fail, and so do `golden.rs` (3 of 4 payload tests) and `cycles.rs`.

## Verification

- `cargo build --release --locked`, `clippy --release --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`: clean
- `cargo test -- --test-threads=1`: 412 passed (incl. the two new `strtol` tests)
- Miri: 376 passed, 36 ignored, 0 UB
- fuzz `otf_parse` / `otf_dump` / `json_build` 90s each clean; every `tests/fuzz-corpus/known-issues/*.bin` re-run against each target, no failures
- `survey-unsafe.sh` (vs. #469): `unsafe fn` 49 → 44, `unsafe blocks` 162 → 160, raw pointer types 678 → 658, `.offset(` 24 → 22

body:
## Summary

Raises the workspace MSRV from 1.95 to 1.97. The development toolchain pinned in
`pixi.toml` (Rust 1.98) is unchanged — the floor stays deliberately below it,
because the PyPI *sdist* compiles this workspace on the user's own rustc and we
publish wheels for Linux and Windows only.

The dependency tree was already pressed flat against 1.95: the egui 0.36 stack
declares exactly 1.95, and `libsqlite3-sys` 0.38.1 (via `rusqlite` 0.40) needed
1.95 for the `cfg_select!` in its build script while declaring no `rust-version`
at all. `openjd-expr` 0.9.0 declares 1.96, so the next routine dependency upgrade
would have forced a bump anyway. Setting the floor at 1.97 — one release behind
the dev toolchain — buys headroom, so the next GUI-stack minor does not
immediately force a second bump.

## Changes

- `Cargo.toml` — `rust-version = "1.97"` in `[workspace.package]`, inherited by
  all ten crates (none overrides it). The comment above it is rewritten to record
  why the floor sits one release behind the dev toolchain rather than at whatever
  the dependency tree happens to require today. It also corrects a stale line that
  said `pixi.toml` pins 1.97; it pins 1.98.
- `AGENTS.md` — the "Python 3.14 and Rust 1.98 are pinned…" bullet now reads
  1.97, and states the one-release-behind policy. The explanation of why MSRV is
  not the dev toolchain is kept, as is the `libsqlite3-sys` anecdote, which is a
  historical statement about 1.95 and stays accurate as written.
- `specs/gui/action-log.md` — the `jiff` rationale cites the workspace MSRV; 1.95
  → 1.97 (`jiff` needs 1.70, so the conclusion is unaffected).

Nothing else in the repo states the floor. In particular `.github/workflows/ci.yml`
needed no edit: the `msrv` job `sed`s the version out of `Cargo.toml` and passes
it to `pixi exec`, and no literal 1.95 appears in a job name, cache key or matrix
— the only occurrence there is inside the `libsqlite3-sys` anecdote in a comment.
`Cargo.lock` is untouched. Dated snapshots under `reports/` are left alone; the
one MSRV-adjacent finding there is already marked done.

## Testing

- `pixi run cargo fmt` — clean, no reformatting.
- `pixi run cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings` — clean. No new
  MSRV-aware lints fire at the higher floor.
- `pixi run doc` — clean (rustdoc warnings are errors).
- `pixi run cargo check --workspace` — clean.
- `pixi run cargo test -p sfmtool-core --test license_headers` — passes.
- **MSRV verified against a real 1.97 toolchain**, using the exact command the CI
  `msrv` job runs (no 1.97 rustup toolchain was installed locally, so this went
  through `pixi exec` as CI does):

  — finished successfully, and `--locked` confirms `Cargo.lock` needs no change.

Full test suites were not run: this is a metadata and documentation change with no

While auditing for ≤1.96 compatibility shims, the only candidate found is

`crates/sfm-explorer/src/layout.rs:731` and `crates/sfm-explorer/tests/ui_basic.rs:638`,
whose own comments say the function was un-deprecated in 1.85 — already dead under
the old 1.95 floor, so it is not this PR's to remove. There is no `clippy.toml`
and no `#[allow(clippy::incompatible_msrv)]` anywhere in the workspace.

body:
## What

A new, isolated lab — `backend/app/labs/momentum/`, its own `mom_*` tables (migration `0099_momentum_lab`, new tables only), behind `LAB_MOMENTUM_ENABLED` (default **off**, added to the compose anchor). Page at `/momentum-candles` ("Momentum Lab" in the nav). **Paper only** — nothing in the package reaches a key, a signer or a chain.

- **Universe:** Jupiter's top-traded / trending / organic lists (12 keyless calls every 30 min). Admitted only if the token's **first pool is older than 7 days**, it has $50k+ liquidity, and it isn't a stable, LST, wrapped major or tokenised stock. One DexScreener pool per token, pinned by address. Live check 2026-09-19: 358 listed → 142 eligible → 132 admitted.
- **Candles:** every pool sampled every 30s (≤15 DexScreener calls/tick, ~2.5s), folded into 5m candles; 15m/1h aggregated in SQL. A bar is judged once, after it closes, only against earlier bars.
- **The momentum candle (base):** green, +2%, 3× the token's usual body, 3× normal volume, closing in the top 40% of its range, more buys than sells. Fires on ~1% of 5m bars (rate-calibrated on 4,020 real candles; not tuned on returns).
- **50 strategies**, one factor changed at a time: 16 entry variants, 6 universe slices (pool size, token age), 13 exits (holds, stop at candle low/mid + 1R/2R/3R, trails, take-profits, first red candle, **split exit** half at +1R), 15m and 1h families, a mid-candle "catch", the opposite dip bet, and **5 random controls** (random time at the base's measured rate, same moments with random tokens, random green candle, 15m and 1h).
- **Fills:** a buy decided on one tick fills on the **next** tick's price (never the price it decided on); stops sell on the next price; fee + constant-product impact + network fee on both legs; >3% impact is refused.
- **Board:** each trade measured at $100 and re-walked through a **$1,000 wallet at 1/2/5/10/20 splits**; each strategy judged against its yardstick at z ≥ 3, error measured between hours.

## Touches outside the lab (additive only)
`api/v1/router.py` (+include), `models/__init__.py` (+import), `workers/celery_app.py` (+include, +3 beat entries: tick every 30s, universe :07/:37, prune :17), `docker-compose.yml` (+`LAB_MOMENTUM_ENABLED` in the anchor), `frontend/src/lib/design/nav.ts` (+1 item). Nothing existing changes behaviour; with the flag off every task returns before opening a session.

## Verified
- 22 lab tests (21 pure + 1 Postgres tick cycle: judged once → filled on the next price → midpoint stop sold on the next price → pullback filled at the dip → time exit → wallet), `ruff` clean.
- `alembic upgrade head` on a fresh DB; `alembic check` mentions `mom_` zero times.
- Beat entries resolve to registered tasks; compose/beat contract tests pass (102).
- `tsc` clean for new code (the 9 pre-existing test-file errors are main's baseline); `next build` passes; nav guard test (96) passes.
- Live dry run on a scratch DB against the real feeds: 132 pools, 5 calls, ~2.3s a tick, 0 failures; page rendered locally at desktop and phone widths.

## Load on prod
+1 Celery task every 30s (~3s), ~10–15 DexScreener calls/min, 12 Jupiter calls per 30 min. Storage: 5m candles kept 3 days (~100–150k rows/day), positions kept.

body:
The previous fix correctly checked the analyzed 'content' variable instead of item.content alone, but still used an arbitrary 150-character cutoff to decide isHeadlineOnly. Oba pliki treściowe na stałe nazwy, z nagłówkami wersji (`07.13 · 2026-09-09` dla CV, `08.07 · 2026-09-07` dla Seventeen). Z tytułu Seventeen usunięty doklejony numer wersji.

**CV 07.12** — poprzednia wersja przeniesiona do `osierocone-html/cv/` jako migawka archiwalna, z wersją odnotowaną w nagłówku. Pod jej starym publicznym adresem stoi przekierowanie **na aktualne CV**, nie na migawkę: rozesłany kiedyś link powinien pokazywać wersję bieżącą, a nie nieaktualną.

## 3. Anchory przy stabilnych adresach

Audyt wszystkich stubów w repo. Trzy gubiły `#anchor`, bo były czystym `meta refresh` bez JavaScriptu:

- `osierocone-html/audhd/opis-po-ludzku-20-prac-naukowych.html`
- `piosenki/SOL-audyt-danych-2026-09-07.html`
- `piosenki/sol-o-co-kaman-HTML-v01-00.html`

Wszystkie przepisane na wzorzec `location.replace(cel + location.hash)`, z `canonical` i `noindex`. Sam `meta refresh` gubi fragment adresu i zostaje wyłącznie jako zapas dla wyłączonego JS.

**Wynik: 62 stuby, 62 zachowują anchor.**

## 4. Archiwum i sieroty

`dokumentacja-archiwalna/piosenki/` — trzy pliki na stałe nazwy, wersje do nagłówków jako archiwalne, stuby pod starymi adresami. Dwa wskaźniki z `piosenki/` przepięte i przepisane tak, by też przekazywały anchor.

## 5. Dokumentacja

`SOL_DOKUMENTACJA-KATALOGI-AKTUALNA.md` dostaje **sekcję 0.1** z normatywnym opisem konwencji: stałe nazwy plików, wersja `XX.YY` i data w nagłówku dokumentu, stabilne wejścia katalogowe, stuby archiwalne i wymóg przekazywania anchora przez każde przekierowanie, wraz z powodem, dla którego sam `meta refresh` nie wystarcza.

Sekcje o CV i Seventeen zaktualizowane, z odnotowaniem, że stabilny adres Seventeen był do teraz kopią treści. Przepięte nieaktualne odwołania w `SOL_DOKUMENTACJA-SLOWA-LYRICS-TAGI-AKTUALNA.md` i w podsumowaniu audio. `osierocone-html/README.md` przepisany: zasada zostawiania przekierowania, spis zawartości z nowym `cv/`, notatka o duplikatach do rozstrzygnięcia.

## Weryfikacja

- 169 HTML-i w repo
- **0 martwych linków** (`href`, `meta refresh`, `location.replace`, ze ścieżkami względnymi)
- **0 błędów parsowania**
- **0 martwych linków w dokumentacji** `.md`
- **0 odwołań do nieistniejących plików** w dokumentacji
- **62/62 stuby zachowują anchor**

## Czego świadomie nie ruszałem

**`rosja/` — 11 plików `X.html` obok `X-anchory.html`.** Wyglądają na sieroty, ale ich własny audyt klasyfikuje je jako *świadomie zachowane zamrożone oryginały*. Zostają.

**`audhd/` i `rosja/` — 46 plików treściowych** nadal ma wersje w nazwach, ale każdy ma działający stabilny adres przez stub-katalog i każdy z tych stubów zachowuje anchor. Nic nie jest zepsute; ujednolicenie nazw to osobna operacja.

author: newisdartagnan
body:
C'était la dernière grande rubrique des canevas que l'application ne savait pas remplir : l'UNTA du centre de santé, l'UNTI de l'hôpital et l'unité de supplémentation. Elle tenait sur des fiches cartonnées dans une boîte et se recomptait à la main le 30 du mois — alors qu'un enfant admis pour malnutrition sévère revient ici chaque semaine pendant deux mois.

## La mesure

Poids, taille (couché ou debout — deux centimètres déplacent un score), **périmètre brachial en millimètres** comme sur le ruban, **œdèmes bilatéraux** cotés de + à +++.

L'application classe : sévère sous 115 mm, modéré sous 125, et **les œdèmes priment sur la balance** — un enfant œdémateux est sévèrement malnutri même si le poids dit le contraire, parce que l'eau pèse. Le plus grave des trois critères l'emporte.

## Sur le score poids/taille, l'application ne calcule rien

C'est la décision la plus importante de cette modification, alors je la pose franchement.

Les tables de référence de l'OMS ne sont pas dans le dépôt. Les reconstituer de mémoire pour t'épargner une saisie enverrait un jour un enfant dans la mauvaise unité. **Le soignant lit son z-score sur l'abaque et le saisit** ; l'application n'en tire que la classification, exactement comme elle le fait du bras et des œdèmes, qui eux se lisent directement. L'écran dit d'où vient le chiffre, pour que personne ne croie qu'il est calculé.

Conséquence assumée : une mesure sans périmètre brachial ni score reste **« non évaluable »**. Elle ne déclare pas l'enfant bien portant faute de savoir.

## Le suivi

Une admission, un motif, une issue — l'épisode dure des semaines et survit aux visites. Ce n'est donc ni une visite ni une consultation.

- **L'UNTI ne prend que le compliqué** : c'est ce qui la distingue de l'ambulatoire, et le canevas ne lui connaît aucune ligne sans complication. L'admission la pose d'office.
- **Les motifs ne circulent pas d'une unité à l'autre** : « MAM dépistée » n'est pas une entrée thérapeutique, « œdèmes » n'est pas une entrée en supplémentation.
- **Les issues non plus** : l'UNTA réfère vers le haut, l'UNTI contre-réfère vers le bas. Les confondre ferait un rapport faux dans les deux sens.
- **Un patient n'est pas suivi deux fois à la fois** : sinon le rapport compterait deux entrées et deux issues pour un enfant.

## La décision reste au soignant

L'application propose l'unité que la mesure appelle. La **complication médicale** ne se lit sur aucun ruban et ne peut venir que de l'examen — l'écran le dit en toutes lettres : *« Sans complication, c'est l'UNTA ; avec une complication médicale, c'est l'UNTI — cela, seul l'examen le dit. »*

## Le rapport

La rubrique suit l'échelon : le **CS** remonte l'UNTA et l'UNS, l'**HGR/HST** l'UNTI. Entrées par motif et issues par catégorie, ventilées par sexe et par les trois tranches du canevas nutritionnel — **6-23 mois, 24-59 mois, 5 ans et plus**, qui ne sont pas celles du reste du rapport. Plus le **report du mois précédent**, que le canevas demande en tête de tableau et qui ne se retrouve nulle part ailleurs, et le **taux de guérison**.

Un nourrisson de moins de six mois est compté à part plutôt que rangé de force dans une case : le canevas nutritionnel commence à six mois.

La ligne « prise en charge de la malnutrition » quitte donc les rubriques déclarées non suivies, où elle figurait à juste titre jusqu'ici. Le rapport HGR passe de 8 à 9 sections, le CS de 6 à 7 — les tests de numérotation sont mis à jour en conséquence.

## Fichiers

| | |
|---|---|
| `MesureAnthropometrique` | la mesure d'un jour et sa classification (nouveau) |
| `PriseEnChargeNutritionnelle` | l'épisode : unité, motif, issue, tranches (nouveau) |
| `NutritionService` | mesurer, orienter, admettre, décharger, agréger (nouveau) |
| `NutritionController` + 5 routes + 2 écrans | le registre et le dossier du patient (nouveau) |
| `SystemeSanteService` | rubrique `nutrition` + unités par échelon |
| `RapportSnisService` | la section, l'écran, l'impression et le tableur |

## Vérification

- **713 tests / 2917 assertions** au vert (42 nouveaux)
- **34 vérifications au navigateur** : parcours complet d'un enfant de 18 mois — mesure à 108 mm classée sévère, admission à l'UNTI, refus d'un motif de supplémentation, décharge en contre-référence — et **la ligne du canevas vérifiée case par case**, en contrôlant que le total égale la somme de ses six cases et que l'enfant ne tombe dans aucune autre tranche
- `pint --dirty` au vert, `npm run build` à jour, aucun débordement à 390 px

## Ce qui reste hors de portée

L'UNS n'est offerte qu'au centre de santé, donc ses groupes spécifiques (femmes enceintes et allaitantes au PB < 230 mm, PVVIH et tuberculeux à l'IMC < 18,5) ne se remplissent que si tu bascules le canevas sur CS. C'est le formulaire qui le veut ainsi.

## Summary

## What changed

The Helm board's converse-sittings rows now say what they are about.

**Before:** the SUBJECT column showed only the bare subject-bead id, and a
sitting with no attributed `gc.takeaway` fell the HEADLINE through to the visit
bead's own title — which on an old-path first reaction is the generic "first
reaction ready: accept or redirect" and says nothing.

**Now:**
- The gather keeps each sitting's SUBJECT-bead **title** as the new
  `board.Sitting.SubjectTitle`, read in the same batch that already fetches the
  takeaway. Unlike the takeaway it carries no span test, so it rides every row.
- Two model helpers hold the fallback once, so the CLI (`helm-svc board`) and
  the web dashboard share one derivation: `Sitting.Topic()` (the subject title,
  else its id) and `Sitting.Headline()` (the takeaway, else the topic, else the
  visit title as a last resort).
- Both renderers show the topic in the subject cell — the web keeps the id as
  the drill target and hover title — and fall the headline back to the topic. A
  row with no takeaway therefore shows its topic in both the subject cell and
  the headline: intended, and strictly more than the prior bare id + generic
  title.

The wire contract gains `subject_title` (additive): `contract.ts`, the parity
fixture, and the embedded `web/dist` bundle are regenerated to match.

Renderer-only; capture is unchanged. Backfilling old takeaway-less gascity rows
is a deferred follow-up (the old rows age out). Operator intake: tk-dqk1w0.

<details>
<summary>Dispatch — what this work was asked to do</summary>

## Problem

The helm board renders rows with no reliable indication of their topic. Two
gaps, both from tk-dqk1w0 (operator intake + root-cause analysis):

- The "subject" column shows only the bare bead id, never the subject bead's
  title, so a row can carry no sign of what it is about.
- The "headline" column is the subject's attributed gc.takeaway; when a row has
  no attributed takeaway it falls through to the visit bead's generic title
  ("first reaction ready: accept or redirect"), which says nothing.

Takeaway-folding already works for current reactions (operator confirmed
tk-3f6vi2's PR#778 row reads well on the live board), so this is a renderer
fix, not a capture change.

## Change

In the helm board renderer and model (services/helm/internal — the board
source is source/facts.go attributeTakeaways and internal/board; see tk-dqk1w0
notes for the exact call sites):

- Show the subject bead's title as the row's topic, so a bare id is never the
  only context on a row.
- When a row has no attributed takeaway, fall back to the subject bead's title
  for the headline instead of the generic visit title.

## Acceptance

- Every board row surfaces the subject's topic (its title), not just the id.
- A row with no attributed takeaway shows the subject's title as the headline,
  never "first reaction ready: accept or redirect".
- A row WITH an attributed takeaway still shows the takeaway headline — no
  regression against the current good rows.
- Board-model tests cover the no-takeaway fallback (internal/board derive_test
  and internal/source facts tests).
- One PR.

## Out of scope

- Backfilling old takeaway-less gascity rows (optional cleanup via gc-helm
  react) and confirming gascity runs the takeaway-folding pack — a separate,
  lower-value follow-up, not this PR.
- The takeaway-folding workflow itself, which already works for current
  reactions.

Root cause / operator intake: tk-dqk1w0.

</details>

author: nckrtl
body:
## Why

`orbit top` showed `CPU/MEM` for Docker Processes and nothing for systemd ones. The two usage queries matched cAdvisor's `name` label, which only containers have.

Measured on the live fleet:

| shape | labels cAdvisor sets |
| --- | --- |
| container | `name=orbit-process-67-executor`, `id=/system.slice/docker-{sha}.scope` |
| systemd unit | *no `name`*, `id=/system.slice/orbit-process-69-agentation.service` |

A systemd unit is a raw cgroup, so it is identified only by its `id` path. Matching `name` alone found 4 series where 18 exist.

## What changed

- Each query asks for both cgroup shapes via an `or` arm.
- The lookup reads a series' key from `name` when present, else the last segment of `id`, and skips a cgroup that is neither — an unrelated series can never be read as some Process's usage.
- The unit selector writes its literal dot `\\.`. A PromQL string is Go-quoted before it compiles as a regex, so a lone `\.` is rejected outright with `unknown escape sequence`. This bit the first attempt, so a test asserts no lone backslash survives — the query text still looks correct when one does.

## Verification

Against the live fleet's Grafana datasource proxy, both queries return **18 series** (was 4), covering containers and units alike:

```
orbit-process-67-executor             199737344
orbit-process-62-valkey                 6017024
orbit-process-68-proxycli.service      67375104
```

The reworked fixture builds series with the label shapes cAdvisor actually emits; reverting only the two source files fails 2 of the 5 tests on exactly the systemd path. Pint and PHPStan pass. The 9 other failures in these suites are the known macOS ones (exit 64/127, missing `systemctl`/`caddy`).

## What
Pure refactor: break the over-250-line modules into single-purpose files. **No logic, prompt, or contract change** — every moved function is byte-identical to develop (verified by diff), all three suites pass, and a real sandbox run confirms the behavior is unchanged (verified outcome, clean run.log with no internals, teardown proof confirmed).

## The splits
| Before | After |
|---|---|
| `agent_runner.py` 389 | `agent_runner.py` 42 (command_for) + `agent_script.py` 351 (the raw in-container SCRIPT string) |
| `agent.py` 335 | `agent.py` 123 (run_agent) + `agent_context.py` 218 (context helpers, toolbelt, system prompt) |
| `executor.py` 316 | `executor.py` 89 (AzureExecutor wrapper) + `runloop.py` 254 (the provision→launch→stream→teardown body) |
| `runner.py` 369 | `runner.py` 254 (state machine) + `_settle.py` 131 (settle/abort/finish) |

## Notes for review
- **Import-path compatibility preserved**: tests touch `agent._clip/_prune_tools/_est_tokens/_compact/_KEEP_RECENT_TOOLS`, `agent_runner.command_for`, `runner._run_real/_TICK_SECONDS`, `runner._finish_run` — all still resolve (re-exports kept).
- **One design choice to sanity-check**: `_say` moved into `_settle.py` (and `runner` imports it back) to break what would otherwise be a circular import between `runner` and `_settle`. Net effect is the same names, same behavior.
- **The GeneratorExit-safe teardown in `run()` moved verbatim** — I did not touch that logic; it's the riskiest part and it's byte-identical.
- `agent_script.py` (351) is a single raw string and `runloop.py`/`runner.py` (~254) are single-purpose; they sit at/just over 250 and can't shrink further without editing working agent code, which this refactor deliberately avoids.
- AGENTS.md dir map + the `agent_runner.SCRIPT` reference updated to the new layout.

## Why now
Clears the rule-1 debt before the files grow further, and makes the TODO #19 harness decision (adopt LangGraph when a task breaks our loop) far easier to act on — we'd swap one module instead of untangling a 389-line file.

author: anttiluode
body:
The Windows/Python 3.13 CUDA run reached the masked decoder and failed with:

`RuntimeError: Input type (struct c10::Half) and bias type (float) should be the same`

Cause: the vendored masked SDXL community pipeline upcasts the VAE to float32 for decode but leaves denoising latents in float16. The standard Diffusers path handles this dtype transition; our vendored helper did not.

Fix: cast latents to the actual `post_quant_conv` parameter dtype immediately before VAE denormalization/decode.

This is a runtime compatibility fix only; P2's scientific gate and masks are unchanged.
