body:
## 背景

上游 [blader/humanizer](https://github.com/blader/humanizer) 于 2026-09-06 发布了 **v3.0.0**，本仓库（最后更新 2026-01-19）仍基于 v2.x 的 24 模式结构。#34 同步的是 v2.9.1，而 v3.0.0 是一次结构性重构，本 PR 直接对齐到 v3.0.0（内容上可视为 #34 的超集替代，若维护者愿意也可以只取本 PR）。

## 主要变更

### SKILL.md

1. **对齐 v3.0.0 结构**：24 模式重排为 A–E 五组 25 条，补入 v3.0 新增的谚语式深沉、起跑式铺垫（拆分）、与假想敌辩论、句式开头复读、模糊关联、首句复读标题、谈论上一稿等条目。原有中文示例（加泰罗尼亚统计局、索马里菜肴、Gallery 825、浩来河、寺庙三色等）尽可能保留，新增条目配了同风格的中文示例
2. **新增强度分级**（v3.0 核心机制）：A 组"单发即改"；B 组等标注"聚堆才改"——单独出现时人也可能刻意为之，需与其他痕迹佐证才处理，避免机械全文替换
3. **新增 file-mode 保护协议**：处理文件时只改散文，代码块、行内代码、链接目标、front matter、路径、标题层级绝对不动
4. **新增"为什么 AI 文本读起来是一个味"**：v3.0 的根因模型（统计默认选择）与两条总则；原"核心规则速查"的内容并入其中
5. **新增"声音校准"与"何时不动"**：写作样本优先于规则；引文/专名/2022-11-30 之前的文本等边界保护
6. **新增 F 组中文专属规则（§26–§31，本 PR 的核心增量）**：
   - 的的不休（"的"连用 ≥3 个）
   - "进行 + 动词"名词化（进行测试 → 测试了）
   - 被字句堆叠（翻译腔）
   - 四字词排比（"稳定可靠、快速响应、易于维护"）
   - "随着……的发展"式开头
   - 套话收尾（总而言之 / 综上所述 / 拭目以待）
   另新增**反向过度修正判据**（一票否决项）：删套话 ≠ 删光连接词——"后来、于是、不过"这类承载真实逻辑的连接词必须保留，否则产出电报体。这是在实际批量改写十几篇中文技术文章中沉淀的教训
7. **中文语境适配更新**：标题大写模式并入"装饰性标题"（英文大小写在中文不适用）；弯引号模式本地化为"引号体系混乱"；AI 高频词表补充"赋能 / 抓手 / 闭环 / 一站式 / 无缝"

### README.md

- 模式列表更新为六组 31 种，标注各强度档位
- 新增"版本同步记录"小节与 v3.0.0 机制说明
- 词汇警示列表同步扩充

## 编号说明

本 PR 基于当前 main（24 模式）编号顺延，F 组为 26–31。若 #28（新增 25–27 号模式）先行合并会产生编号冲突，届时 F 组顺延改号即可，不影响内容结构。

## 兼容性

- front matter 字段（name / description / allowed-tools / metadata）结构不变，仅更新内容，Claude Code skill 加载不受影响
- 全文中文，沿用"改写前 / 改写后"示例体例
- MIT 许可不变，署名与来源在文末"参考"一节完整保留

author: remigit55
body:
## Le défaut, mesuré sur le paquet PUBLIÉ

`@blueprint-modular/core@0.3.14` ne contient les déclarations que d'**UN** répertoire de composant : `Button`. Les 188 composants vivent à la **racine du dépôt** (`components/bpm/`), hors du `include: ["src"]` du tsconfig — vite-plugin-dts n'émet donc aucune de leurs déclarations, et `bpm.d.ts` référence leurs types par des chemins qui **sortent du paquet** :

```
dist/packages/core/src/bpm.d.ts → ../../../../../../components/bpm/LiveGauge
                                   └─ six niveaux = node_modules/components/bpm/ — hors paquet
```

Chez le consommateur, `skipLibCheck: true` avale les `TS2307` correspondants. **Les props valent `any` en silence.** C'est ce qui explique très exactement les cinq composants couverts — `button` plus les quatre locaux.

## Ce que le correctif change

| | avant | après |
|---|---|---|
| `.d.ts` émis | 76 | **254** |
| déclarations de `components/bpm/` | **0** | **178** |
| références de type sortant du paquet | **324** | **0** |
| entrée `package.json#types` | `dist/packages/core/src/index.d.ts` | **inchangée** |

Deux causes, deux correctifs :

1. **`include` couvre `../../components/bpm/**/*`.** `entryRoot` est laissé au plugin : le poser explicitement **double** le préfixe de sortie (`dist/packages/core/src/packages/core/src/…`) et fait disparaître l'entrée `types` — mesuré, et c'est la garde ci-dessous qui l'a attrapé.
2. **`beforeWriteFile` ramène dans `dist/` les `import("…")` EN LIGNE.** Le plugin réécrit les spécificateurs d'*instruction* mais pas ceux des positions de *type* — **162** d'entre eux pointaient six niveaux au-dessus du paquet, et ce sont précisément eux qui portent les props. La réécriture est structurelle et ne suppose l'existence de rien : c'est la garde qui vérifie.

## La garde — c'est la pièce qui compte

`assert-types-self-contained` : aucune déclaration de `dist/` ne peut référencer un type absent du paquet, et l'entrée `types` doit exister. La règle est **dérivée du défaut**, pas proxifiée par un compte de fichiers.

Sans elle, l'émission dépendrait d'une condition **tacite** — un `node_modules` à la racine du dépôt, d'où TS résout `react` pour `components/bpm/*.tsx`. Condition remplie sur bpm-prod (`publish-core.yml` publie depuis `~/blueprint-modular`, une app Next installée), et **invisible si elle cessait de l'être** : le build resterait vert en publiant un paquet aveugle. On refuse de publier plutôt que de se taire.

## Preuve — dist RÉEL posé dans blueprint-maker

Sonde `bpm-props-visibility`, **sentinelles vertes dans les deux régimes** (une faute franche hors `bpm.*` qui doit lever, un appel connu-bon qui ne doit pas) :

```
avant : 172 sondés · 5 couverts · 167 aveugles
après : 172 sondés · 172 couverts · 0 aveugle
```

## Ce que la publication fera aux gates — mesuré, pas plaidé

Sur le gate de compilation des six artefacts d'étape du Maker, le dist candidat fait apparaître **exactement 3 diagnostics**, tous réels, tous dans du code de **vue libre écrit par le modèle** (`velo-mesure`) :

```
app/_page-content.tsx:1536 — TS2322 — Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'LiveGaugeSize'
app/_page-content.tsx:2243 — TS2322 — Type 'number' is not assignable to type 'LiveGaugeSize'
app/_page-content.tsx:1221 — TS2322 — Property 'status' is missing … StatusTrackerStage
```

**Le premier EST la panne `microbrasserie` du 30/08** : `bpm.liveGauge({ size: 180 })` compile aujourd'hui, est retenue en `full`, passe K-15, et lève `TypeError: Cannot destructure property 'w'` **au rendu** — la table de tailles du core n'a que `sm|md|lg`. Publier les types la fait attraper **au gate** ce que K-15 ne voit qu'à l'affichage.

**Témoin** : avec le dist d'origine, le même gate passe **6/6** et `LiveGaugeSize` n'apparaît pas une seule fois. L'avant/après est donc porté par ce changement et par rien d'autre.

## ⚠️ Conséquence à assumer avant de publier

Les trois diagnostics sont dans du code LLM. Une fois les types publiés **et** le Maker dépinglé, le gate assemblé **rejettera** ces vues libres au lieu de les expédier — c'est le comportement voulu (on attrape au lieu de planter), mais c'est un durcissement réel du canal des vues libres, pas un correctif neutre.

**Cette PR ne publie rien.** Elle rend le paquet correct ; la publication (`Publish core to npm`) et le dépinglage côté Maker restent deux décisions séparées.

## Gates

| | |
|---|---|
| `npm run gate` (CI) | **VERT** |
| `packages/core` → `gate:types` | **VERT** |
| build du core | **VERT**, garde silencieuse |

author: malkreide
body:
## Was ändert sich

Dieser Commit war für #57 gedacht und hat den Merge um Sekunden verpasst. #57 wurde um 07:00:50 mit einem Commit gemergt; der zweite kam um ~07:01:55 und landete auf einem Branch, den der Merge gerade gelöscht hatte — der Push legte ihn neu an. `main` trägt deshalb bis jetzt die ungenauere Fassung.

Kein Code, keine Tests, keine Workflows. Ein Commit, zwei Korrekturen an `CLAUDE.md` Teil 2:

### 1. «Rund drei Minuten» stand auf einer einzigen Beobachtung

Inzwischen sind es zwei, und sie liegen weit auseinander:

| PR | Codex startet | «Completed» | Dauer |
|---|---|---|---|
| #55 | 06:35:42 | 06:38:29 | **167 s** |
| #56 | 06:56:47 | 06:57:48 | **61 s** |

Jetzt als Spanne ausgewiesen statt als Erwartungswert. Wer aus zwei Messungen «etwa eine Minute» macht, mergt beim nächsten Mal zu früh — und das ist genau der Fehler, den der Abschnitt verhindern soll.

### 2. Der Connector meldet Befundlosigkeit anders, als Teil 1 es beschreibt

Teil 1 sagt, ein Lauf ohne Befund komme als Issue-Kommentar («Codex Review: Didn't find any major issues»). Auf #56 kam der nicht. Gemessen:

```
Summary-Kommentar 5740067789: «✅ Completed», 06:57:48
get_reviews         -> []          (kein Review-Objekt)
get_review_comments -> 0 Threads
get_comments        -> nur der Summary-Kommentar
reactions           -> 0           (kein 👍, kein 👀)
```

Einziges Signal ist die Statustabelle im **fortgeschriebenen** Summary-Kommentar: «🔄 Running since …» wird zu «✅ Completed …», gleiche ID. Wer auf den Prosatext wartet, hält einen sauberen Lauf für einen ausgebliebenen — derselbe Fehlalarm wie in Teil 1 beschrieben, nur in die andere Richtung.

Das Fortschreiben ist ein **Edit** und löst kein `issue_comment`-Ereignis aus. Auf #55 wanderte `updated_at` von 06:35:44 auf 06:38:29, ohne Webhook; der P2-Befund dort wurde nur gefunden, weil gepollt statt gewartet wurde.

**Teil 1 bleibt unberührt** — die Beobachtung hängt an der Connector-Konfiguration dieses Repos und gehört deshalb in Teil 2.

### Nebenbei

Beim Schreiben waren weiche Trennzeichen (`U+00AD`) in den Text geraten: unsichtbar im Editor, kaputt bei jeder Suche. Entfernt, und das Änderungsskript prüft jetzt, dass keines übrig bleibt.

---

Merget sauber auf `main` (`b52f760`), gegengeprüft mit `git merge-tree`: null Konfliktmarker. Alle fünf Gates lokal grün mit dem gepinnten `ruff 0.16.5`: 170 Tests, `check_ruff_pin.py`, `ruff check`, `ruff format --check`, `check_version_sync.py`.

author: profhepta
body:
## Scope

Converge the cognitive knowledge-graph path on one deterministic semantic owner instead of maintaining parallel graph rules.

Target chain:

`durable cognitive facts -> canonical adapter -> hepta-kg V2 generation/publication -> same SQLite transaction -> persisted generation digest -> product query consumer`

## Implemented

- `hepta-memory` now depends on and invokes the canonical `hepta-kg` V2 kernel.
- The cognitive adapter maps physical SQLite occurrences to canonical V2 node/edge identities, explicit support lineage and validity windows.
- Custom relation identities are lossless; the adapter no longer collapses product relation strings into a closed enum.
- `refresh_scope_projection_tx` builds the complete V2 candidate, reconstructs its predecessor and validates `publish_generation` before publication.
- Physical projection rows, immutable V2 semantic receipts and the current-generation CAS are committed in the same SQLite transaction.
- Migration `0011_kg_generation_semantics.sql` persists source snapshot, generation vector, graph profile, generation and predecessor-bound publication digests.
- Reopen recomputes physical input/output truth, canonical V2 generation truth and predecessor-bound publication truth; generation/publication tamper fails closed.
- Product GraphOneHop no longer owns graph selection policy in SQL. It reconstructs the persisted V2 generation, fences it by `generation_sha256`, calls `hepta_kg::query_relations` for relation/temporal/bound semantics, then uses SQL only to resolve selected support identities to physical memory occurrences.
- Legacy pre-0011 projections can remain historical/lexical data but cannot drive digest-bound GraphOneHop expansion.
- The oracle covers one source lineage through full rebuild, incremental rebuild, SQLite materialization, reopen, product query, correction and tombstone. It explicitly compares physical `output_sha256`, V2 `generation_sha256`, predecessor-bound `publication_sha256`, canonical identities/support lineage and visible query behavior.
- Agentd product E2E carries the same persisted KG receipts through remember, restart/recall, correction and forget under the explicit `qualification-cognitive-write` profile.
- Module TECHNICAL, implementation dossier, implementation map and Lane-C SQLite owner documentation are aligned with the implementation.

## Claim boundary

- Cognitive graph **read** product caller: composed.
- Cognitive SQLite write integration: composed and exercised only by the explicit `qualification-cognitive-write` profile.
- Default production writer: **not established**; default Agentd binaries keep that feature disabled.
- `apply_incremental_delta`: oracle/reference equivalence path, not the selected durable runtime writer.
- Prompt-factor graph projection: still uncomposed.
- Module-wide `productionImplementation`: remains **false**.
- Independent acceptance / activation / release: unchanged and false.

## Qualification note

The repository's current `main` already fails the global consolidated-source formatting gate in unrelated owners (for example `hepta-codex-adapter` / `hepta-context-compiler`). This branch does not modify those files. KG-specific formatting/compile/product failures discovered on this candidate will be fixed here; the pre-existing main formatting failure is tracked as a baseline external gate rather than being hidden by unrelated cross-owner edits.

No second fact store or alternate graph execution spine is introduced.

author: raufimusaddiq
body:
## What

Post-merge hygiene from the Hermes review on #11, both items it flagged.

## Boundary manifest

`docs/literouter-baseline/phase-minimal-boundary.md` still listed `basic-chat`, `cli-tools`, `mitm` and `media-providers` as *hidden* prefixes, but #10–#12 deleted them. A reader following that doc would look for a guard that no longer exists.

The doc now separates **deleted** from **hidden** and records which PR deleted each surface, so the manifest matches the build:

| Deleted | PR |
| --- | --- |
| `basic-chat` | #10 |
| `media-providers`, `/v1/audio/*`, TTS voice routes | #11 |
| `cli-tools` (19 API routes), `mitm` page, `mitmAlias` cache | #12 |

Also corrected: the `console-log` note claimed it was hidden. It was briefly hidden, then **retained** with its API moved off the hidden `/api/translator` prefix. The doc now says so and lists it under retained.

## Dead skills

`SKILLS` carried `9router-tts` and `9router-stt` entries advertising `/v1/audio/speech` and `/v1/audio/transcriptions`. #11 deleted both endpoints, so the `/dashboard/skills` page was promising capabilities the gateway cannot serve.

Removed the two entries, their `skills/9router-tts` and `skills/9router-stt` markdown, and the two index rows linking to them.

## Out of scope, deliberately

- **README rewrite**: still advertises self-hosted TTS/STT via `/v1/audio/*`. That is a user-facing claim needing a product decision (rewrite to provider passthrough vs delete), so it wants its own PR rather than being folded into a hygiene pass.
- **`docs/ARCHITECTURE.md`**: still describes `db.json` persistence and the translator playground surface. Broader docs pass.
- **`open-sse` TTS/STT engine**: removal is a dependency audit of its own.

## Verification

Docs and one constant only — no code path changed. `SKILLS` is read solely by the gated `/dashboard/skills` page. No test references the removed skill ids outside the new boundary assertions.

body: ## Summary Independent architecture/safety review and integration of: 1. **PR 94** — canonical Candidate PostgreSQL persistence (`4fd8c1a90b27`) 2. **PR 93** — canonical TradePlan application layer + durable DB binding 3. **PR 95** — learning attribution over the journal lifecycle **Verdict: READY FOR FINAL PHASE 7 REVIEW** **Do not merge to main.** ## Integration order 1. Review PR 94 independently. 2. Integrate PR 94 first (owns Alembic `4fd8c1a90b27`) — `c50cedf`. 3. Review PR 93 against integrated Candidate persistence. 4. Close the durable canonical TradePlan / ActionEligibility gap with the next migration after that head. 5. Integrate PR 93 — `8cfb97f` + binding `54ddc76`. 6. Review and integrate PR 95 — `bbc2dd7`. 7. Resolve governance ID collisions. 8. Run the complete validation matrix; ruff/mypy follow-up `55dea92`. ## Findings ### PR 94 (Candidate PostgreSQL) Safe adapter. `CandidateLifecycleService` remains the only Candidate authority. Watcher persist uses `SELECT FOR UPDATE` lease fencing in the same transaction. Not wired into FastAPI/workers. Paper-only flags unchanged. ### PR 93 (canonical TradePlan application layer) `CanonicalTradePlanService` is the only first-slice plan authority. Semantic content stays `CanonicalTradePlanContentV1` (hash-stable). PVC cannot mint canonical plans. Approval binds revision id + content hash only. Source PR left persistence unbound because `trade_plan_revisions.candidate_id` still FK'd `paper_validation_candidates`. ### Persistence binding (this wave) Alembic **`c9e2b4a1d078`** after `4fd8c1a90b27`. Durable ActionEligibility with deterministic identity and append-safe history. `plan_authority` discriminator: legacy PVC rows stay `paper_validation` / `canonical_candidate_id` NULL and are **never** reinterpreted as canonical Candidate ids. Canonical rows FK `canonical_candidates` and tenant-owned `compiled_setup_definitions`. Lineage is a side table beside unchanged semantic payload. Organization-scoped uniqueness and idempotency. Canonical plan root remains UUID5(org, user, account, candidate) via compatibility `TradeProposal.plan_root_kind=canonical_plan_root`. `PLAN_CREATED` runs in the same transaction via `on_inserted`. Execution remains outside this wave. ### PR 95 (learning attribution) Record-only. `JournalLifecycleProjector` remains the only `JournalTrade` writer. Sticky `payload.lineage`. REJECT/SKIP never create executed outcomes. Narrative/LLM output is excluded from `facts_hash` and cannot override deterministic facts. No Alembic in this slice. ## Conflicts and resolutions All three source PRs claimed `AT-051` / `AT-ADR-031`. | ID | Owner | |---|---| | AT-051 / AT-ADR-031 | PR 94 Candidate PostgreSQL | | AT-052 / AT-ADR-032 | PR 93 TradePlan application layer | | AT-053 / AT-ADR-033 | PR 95 learning attribution | | AT-054 / AT-ADR-034 | TradePlan / eligibility PostgreSQL binding | Ruff I001 on `models.py` TradePlan side-effect imports and mypy `on_inserted: Callable[[], Candidate]` vs `Callable[[], None]` were fixed in `55dea92`. ## New migration `c9e2b4a1d078` → down_revision `4fd8c1a90b27`. Single Alembic head verified. Upgrade / downgrade to `4fd8c1a90b27` / reupgrade passed. Downgrade fails closed if canonical plan rows exist. ## Final database authority model - **Candidate:** `CandidateLifecycleService` + `PostgresCandidateRepository` / `canonical_candidates` (+ creation keys, transitions, transition keys). - **ActionEligibility:** `PostgresActionEligibilityStore` / `action_eligibility_evaluations` + `action_eligibility_identity_bindings`. Identity bindings fail closed. Candidate row locked for append-safe history. - **TradePlanRevision:** discriminator `plan_authority`. Legacy PVC ids unconstrained UUID, not canonical FKs. Canonical `canonical_candidate_id` FK `canonical_candidates`. Setup bind: `compiled_setup_definition_id` → tenant `compiled_setup_definitions`. Lineage: `canonical_trade_plan_lineage`. Roots: `canonical_trade_plan_roots`. Idempotency: org-scoped `canonical_trade_plan_idempotency_keys`. - **JournalTrade:** `JournalLifecycleProjector` only. Learning copies lineage from events; it does not write trades. - **Not in this wave:** execution dispatch, FastAPI/worker wiring, attribution PostgreSQL. ## Final branch / HEAD - Branch: `cursor/phase7_integration` - HEAD: `55dea92843eaf12ddfa871e976b842661eec5bab` - Base: `main@e308fa19331daa824c9f9a8cb6c3e101baabb5b7` ## Tests | Check | Result | |---|---| | Focused learning + journal lifecycle | 69 passed | | Full backend pytest | **2199 passed** (local EXIT 0; GitHub 2199 passed, 235 warnings, 1225s) | | Ruff check / format | pass | | Strict mypy (30 affected modules) | pass | | Alembic heads | one head `c9e2b4a1d078` | | Alembic upgrade / downgrade / reupgrade | pass | | Frontend lint / typecheck | pass | | Frontend unit tests | 184 files / **1137 passed** | | Frontend build | pass | | Deployment safety pytest | 49 passed + scripts executable + `--self-check` | | Evaluation | agent 16/16, RAG 5/5, guardrails 7/7 | | E2E smoke | **20 passed**, 13 skipped (local); GitHub e2e-smoke pass | | Docker build | GitHub pass (38s). Local Docker daemon unavailable. | ## CI GitHub Actions run [35429714538](https://github.com/Fejjii/AlphaTrade-AI/actions/runs/35429714538): **success** backend, frontend, deployment-safety, evaluation, e2e-smoke, docker-build all green. ## Remaining risks - Persistence adapters are not imported by FastAPI, workers, or feature flags. - Learning attribution store is in-memory; later PostgreSQL is out of this wave. - Alembic downgrade of `c9e2b4a1d078` fails closed if canonical plan rows exist (intentional). - Compatibility `TradeProposal` dual-parent exists only to satisfy the existing plan-root FK. - Execution, Watcher, Telegram, and live trading remain disabled. ## Safety Paper only. `ENABLE_REAL_TRADING` remains false. Watcher remains disabled. Telegram remains disabled. No exchange mutation. No deployment. ## Verdict **READY FOR FINAL PHASE 7 REVIEW** Do not merge to main.

author: belfordzjeeves
body:
## Summary

Closes the gap carved out of #46: `SafeExpressionEvaluator.evaluate()` checked the expression timeout once *before* tokenization, but `tokenize()` itself had no timeout enforcement, so a pathological tokenization pass could run unbounded past the deadline.

## Changes

- **`src/expression-evaluator/tokenizer.ts`**
  - New exported `TokenizeOptions` (`startTime`/`timeoutMs` plus optional step context), threaded through `tokenize()` → `tokenizeExpression()` → `TokenizerState`, including the recursive template-literal call.
  - New `checkTokenizeTimeout()` helper called from every character-advancing loop (main loop, references, string/template/object/array literals, numbers, and the object-literal lookahead scans). The check fires every 1024 characters — coarse on purpose, per the issue's acceptance criteria, so normal expressions see no measurable slowdown.
  - On deadline expiry it throws `TimeoutError.forExpression()` with the step/stepType context, matching the evaluation phase.
- **`src/expression-evaluator/safe-evaluator.ts`**
  - `evaluate()` now builds the timeout options up front and passes them to both `tokenize()` call sites (the dangerous-identifier pre-pass in `validateExpression()` and the main pass).
  - `validateExpression()`'s catch deliberately does **not** swallow `TimeoutError` (only `TokenizerError`), so an over-deadline tokenization aborts instead of being deferred.
- **Tests**: new `src/__tests__/expression-evaluator/tokenizer-timeout.test.ts` (10 tests) covering: immediate-deadline abort, mid-stream abort in the main loop and inside nested reference scanning (via mocked `Date.now`), error contents (timeout value, `isExpressionTimeout`, step context), the no-timeout path, partial config, and `evaluate()`-level propagation.
- `jest.config.js` thresholds bumped by `jest-it-up` (all new code at 100% coverage).

## Test results

- Full suite: **67 suites, 1012 passed, 5 skipped** — green, coverage thresholds met.
- `npm run build` clean, ESLint 0 errors, Prettier clean.

Fixes #163

body:
## Summary

**This PR is a delivery vehicle, not a merge candidate. Do not merge it into `main`.**

The owner asked for a new repository containing a setup for running a powerful uncensored
local model on their personal workstation (i7-8700 / 32 GB / GTX 1060 6 GB / Windows 11 /
Ollama). Creating a new GitHub repository was rejected — this session's GitHub token is
scoped to this repository only (`403 Resource not accessible by integration` on
`POST /user/repos`). The kit is therefore staged here on the designated branch so it is
not lost, with `local-llm-rig/scripts/bootstrap-new-repo.ps1` to split it into its own
standalone repo in one command.

It shares no code, config, dependency, or import with the Rico application, touches no
Rico file, and has nothing to do with Rico's AI provider routing.

## Scope

One objective: deliver the local-LLM rig kit as extractable content. No Rico code is
changed.

## AI Workspace

- Related task in `AI_WORKSPACE/TASKS.md`: none — this is outside the Rico product roadmap.
- Decision entry in `AI_WORKSPACE/DECISIONS.md`: n/a
- Handoff note in `AI_WORKSPACE/HANDOFFS/`: n/a
- Evaluation note in `AI_WORKSPACE/EVALS/`: n/a

## Changed files

All additions, all confined to a new top-level `local-llm-rig/` directory:

- `local-llm-rig/README.md`, `README.ar.md` — bilingual setup guide, tiered recommendations
- `local-llm-rig/docs/MODEL_SELECTION.md` — the VRAM arithmetic, the picks, and each rejected alternative with the reason
- `local-llm-rig/docs/HARDWARE_NOTES.md` — Pascal-specific tuning
- `local-llm-rig/docs/TROUBLESHOOTING.md` — failure modes and fixes
- `local-llm-rig/modelfiles/hunter-{fast,smart,dolphin,max}.Modelfile` — context windows capped to keep each tier GPU-resident
- `local-llm-rig/scripts/bench.py` — stdlib-only throughput + GPU/CPU-placement harness
- `local-llm-rig/scripts/doctor.ps1` — health check that exits non-zero if Ollama silently stops using the GPU
- `local-llm-rig/scripts/setup.ps1` — pulls bases, sets `OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0`, builds the tuned models
- `local-llm-rig/scripts/bootstrap-new-repo.ps1` — extracts this directory into its own git repo
- `local-llm-rig/LICENSE`, `.gitignore`

The two substantive engineering calls behind the content: CUDA 13.0 dropped compute
capability 6.1, so this card is on the CUDA 12.x line and an Ollama upgrade can silently
disable the GPU — hence `doctor.ps1`. And i-quants run *slower* than the larger `Q4_K_M`
on Pascal, which inverts the usual "smaller quant is better on a small card" advice.

## Verification

- [x] Unit tests: n/a for Rico. `bench.py` was exercised end-to-end against a mock Ollama
      server (`/api/version`, `/api/tags`, `/api/ps`, `/api/generate`) — table rendering,
      tok/s math, JSON output, and the CPU-spill warning all confirmed. `py_compile` clean.
- [x] Frontend build: not run — no frontend file is touched by this diff.
- [ ] Local smoke script: n/a
- [ ] Manual smoke test: the PowerShell scripts are **unverified**. No Windows host, no
      NVIDIA GPU, and no PowerShell interpreter in this environment. They are written
      defensively but have not been executed anywhere.
- [ ] Expected deploy commit: none — this must not deploy.

Model tags and file sizes were compiled in September 2026 from the Ollama registry.
Registry tags get re-pointed, so the docs direct the reader to `ollama show` / `ollama list`
as the authority over any figure in the table.

## Safety

- [x] No secrets changed
- [x] No unrelated files changed — every file is new and under `local-llm-rig/`
- [x] No `dashboard.html` changes
- [x] No async DB rewrite
- [x] **No Redis/vector/local LLM in Rico.** Worth stating explicitly given the subject:
      this adds nothing to Rico's provider chain and does not introduce a local LLM
      dependency to the product. It is documentation and tooling for a personal
      workstation, isolated in its own directory.

Note on the content itself: abliterated models have had refusal behaviour removed and
have no safety layer. The READMEs say so plainly and scope the models to local use only.

## Rollback plan

`git branch -D claude/ollama-powerful-model-bre7zo` and close this PR. Nothing has merged,
nothing deploys, and no Rico file is modified, so there is nothing to revert on `main`.

The intended end state is that this branch is **closed unmerged** once the owner has run
`bootstrap-new-repo.ps1` and pushed the kit to its own repository.

author: t-webb1
body:
Three products carry a near-identical composition layer above `webbpulse.http.create_app`: a frozen `Domain` dataclass, `build_domain_app`, `configure_logging`/`configure_tracing` with the `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT` gate, `check_signing_key`, `add_local_authorizer`, a `RepositoryScope`/`scope_for` helper, and 19 per-domain `entrypoint.py` files of 41 to 51 lines that all do the same four calls. Plus a subprocess "each entrypoint imports only its own domain" test that exists in two of them.

This adds `webbpulse.composition` as that layer, designed so all three can adopt it with no behaviour change, and leaves the genuinely product-specific parts as seams.

## Public API

**`webbpulse.composition`**

- `Domain` — frozen descriptor: `name`, `title`, `load_routers`, `load_unprefixed_routers`, `router_prefix`, `router_tags`, `service_name_template`, `requires_secrets`, `repositories`, `read_repositories`, `extra`; properties `service_name`, `app_title`, `all_repositories`. Everything but `name` defaults. A loader returns a bare `APIRouter` or a `(router, prefix, tags)` triple, which is the union of the two shapes the products use.
- `DomainRegistry` — ordered immutable `Mapping`; `names`, `entrypoint_module`, `entrypoint_modules`. Refuses duplicate names, accepts a plain dict.
- `build_domain_app(domains, *, registry, settings, title, service_name, configure, after_routers, instrument, **create_app_kwargs)` — the one builder both roots go through. `configure` runs before the routers so a product's middleware sits inside the CORS and request id middleware; `after_routers` runs once the route table is complete. Sets `app.state.repository_scope`.
- `domain_entrypoint(domain, *, registry, build, settings, check, serve) -> (build_app, main)`.
- `configure_logging(settings, *, service)`, `configure_tracing(domain, settings, *, registry)`, `check_secrets(domains, settings, *, require, strict, warn_on)`, `local_authorizer(app, settings, *, build_identity_settings, issuer_attribute)`, `resolve_domains`, `scope_for`, `RepositoryScope`, `OTLP_ENDPOINT_ENV`, and the `SettingsLike`/`SecretsChecker`/`AppConfigurer`/`RouterSpec` types.

**`webbpulse.testing`**

- `assert_entrypoint_isolation(registry, *, entrypoint_module, package_root, module_template, cwd, env, domains)` — builds each domain's entrypoint in a fresh interpreter with a stripped environment and asserts it imported only its own domain package.
- `entrypoint_imports(...)` and `EntrypointImports` for the single-domain form.

## Shape decisions

**The Dockerfile CMD stays unchanged.** `domain_entrypoint` returning the `(build_app, main)` pair is the shape chosen over a `python -m webbpulse.composition.entrypoint` runner. Both products' `CMD` is `python -m app.domains.${DOMAIN}.entrypoint` (Standupless via `/etc/standupless-entrypoint`), and a per-domain module is also what makes `build_app` importable by name for the route-cut and isolation tests. A generic runner would need a registry import path in the environment and would give every domain the same module name, so the isolation probe would lose the thing it asserts on.

**`RepositoryScope`/`scope_for` is folded in** — the question "which repositories may this application reach, and which only for reading" is generic wherever a function's IAM grant is narrower than the codebase. **Not folded in:** `Domain.tables`/`read_tables`, which resolve names through a product's own `tables_for`, and `bundle_for`, which builds a product's own bundle type. Both stay in the product and read `scope_for` for the names.

**`build_identity_settings` is a callable**, not an import, so this module never reaches a product's identity glue — importing it here would put that glue into every other domain's image and break exactly the isolation the split exists for.

**`instrument` defaults to `False`**, because `configure_tracing` runs in `main` before the app is built and all three products call `instrument_fastapi` last, after their own middleware rather than underneath it.

## Per-product migration

| | Adopts | Keeps locally |
| --- | --- | --- |
| CarModPicker | `Domain` (+`service_name_template`), registry, builder, `check_secrets`, `configure_tracing`, `local_authorizer`, 9 entrypoints → 3 lines each, isolation test → 1 call | `startup_tasks` seam via its own `lifespan`; the 5 root routes and sitemap handlers as an `after_routers` hook; `bundle_for`/`tables` |
| Standupless | the same, 8 entrypoints, plus `read_repositories` and `scope_for` | root routes hook; `bundle_for` with `read_only`; `tables`/`read_tables` |
| WebbPulse-Terraform | `Domain`, registry, builder, `domain_entrypoint`, 2 entrypoints | `TrailingSlashMiddleware` and `DomainHeaderMiddleware` as `configure` hooks, the latter closing over the resolved domains for its per-domain header |

No product repo is modified by this PR. Registry contents (`domains.py`) stay in each product.

## Checks

`uv sync`, `uv run ruff check src tests`, `uv run ruff format --check src tests`, `uv run mypy src tests` and `uv run pytest -q` are all green. 49 new cases in `tests/test_composition.py`, including a generated two-domain product on disk that exercises the three-line entrypoint and both the passing and the leaking isolation check.

Docs: new `docs/composition.md`, linked from the README module map, with a pointer from `docs/http.md` where `create_app` is documented. `CHANGELOG.md` gains an `## Unreleased` heading with a "Migration for adopters" subsection carrying before/after for an `entrypoint.py` and a `wiring.py`. No version bump, no tag.

author: hsinatfootprintai
body:
## Summary

Third and last slice of #1922 step 6, stacked on the `tracker_conn` minting PR (#1944). Closes the loop opened by the previous two PRs (claim propagation in #1943, minting at `RunAgentSkill` in #1944): the six tracker verb RPCs now actually check the claim. This completes step 6 of the design note's build order.

## What's here

- `internal/server/tracker_server.go`: `enforceConnectionBinding` — a run token carrying a `tracker_conn` claim may only use the tracker verbs against the ONE connection it's bound to; naming a different one is `PermissionDenied`, rejected before the store is even consulted (so it can't distinguish "wrong connection" from "no such connection" for one it's not bound to). An operator/human token (no claim) may name any connection in its own tenant, per the design note's D3 decision.
- `internal/server/tracker_issues_server.go`, `tracker_write_server.go`: wired into `resolveReaderConn` and `resolveWriterConn` — the single choke point all six verbs (`GetTrackerIssue`, `ListTrackerIssues`, `GetTrackerChange`, `CommentOnTrackerIssue`, `ClaimTrackerIssue`, `SetTrackerIssueLabels`) already funnel through, so this is a two-function change rather than six separate ones.

## Test evidence

`internal/server/tracker_conn_binding_test.go`:
- `TestEnforceConnectionBinding_NoClaim_AllowsAnyConnection` / `_MatchingClaim_Allows` / `_MismatchedClaim_Rejects` — pure unit coverage of the helper, no store needed (runs in the default test lane).
  - Verified `_MismatchedClaim_Rejects` is load-bearing: temporarily short-circuited the mismatch check to always allow, confirmed the test fails, then restored the fix and confirmed it passes.
- `TestResolveConnection_RunTokenUsesClaim_RejectsMismatch` / `_OperatorTokenMayName` — the design note's own named tests for this step, exercised end to end through `GetTrackerIssue` (not just the helper in isolation): a run bound to `"default"` naming a second, real `"other"` connection is rejected; the same token naming `"default"` still works; and an operator token can name `"default"` directly.

Full-repo sweep run locally before pushing:
- `go build ./...`, `go vet ./...` — clean
- `golangci-lint run ./...` — 0 issues
- `gofmt -l internal/` — clean
- `TestEveryRPCHasAuthGuard` — 191 RPCs (unchanged — no new RPC)
- `TestRegisteredServicesMatchesDualServer` — clean
- `go clean -testcache && go test -race -count=1 ./internal/...` — all pass (the two DB-gated `TestResolveConnection_*` tests skip locally, no Postgres in this sandbox; added to `store-integration.yml`'s name-list, will confirm via the CI run link here)

## What a reviewer should look at first

- `enforceConnectionBinding`'s placement inside `resolveReaderConn`/`resolveWriterConn` rather than at the top of each of the six RPC handlers — confirm there's no code path that reaches an adapter call without going through one of these two functions (there shouldn't be; both are the sole connection-resolution path for their respective verb groups).

## Not in scope here

This completes #1922 step 6. Remaining for #1922 per the build order: step 7 (platform MCP `tracker_*` tools, `CONTAINARIUM_MCP_TOOLS` allow-list, in-box mount, recipe binary shipping) — depends on this step and the write-verb RPCs (#1940-#1942), both now done. Also still open: the label allow-list acceptance criterion (needs a new field on `TrackerConnection`, not started).

Per #1920's gate: this PR should not be merged until the human D1 custody decision is made.

body:
Adds the missing half of the test suite: something that runs it.

Three checks on every PR and every push to main:

| step | what it catches |
|---|---|
| `node --test` | the 35 behavioural tests |
| `bash -n bin/*` | shell syntax errors before they reach a user's shell |
| executable bit on `bin/*` | the plugin invokes these by path; a lost bit fails at runtime, where it is much harder to diagnose |

`permissions: contents: read`. It never writes to the repository or touches the marketplace listing.

Note for whoever reads this later: the unit test step must be bare `node --test`, not `node --test test/`. Node resolves a directory argument as a module and fails with `MODULE_NOT_FOUND`.

This PR is also the proof the workflow works, since opening it runs it.

Une fois les courses faites, la liste de courses continue de servir toute la semaine : on retire les articles pris, on en rajoute à la volée. Les recettes sélectionnées, elles, doivent rester cochées — c'est ce qu'on regarde pour cuisiner.

## Le problème

`refreshRecipesInList()` décochait automatiquement une recette dès que sa dernière ligne quittait la liste de courses. « Retirer les *n* cochés » après les courses, ou la suppression d'une ligne à la main, faisaient donc disparaître toute la semaine du carnet de recettes.

## Le changement

- `refreshRecipesInList()` est supprimée, avec ses deux appels (`remove-item`, `clear-done`).
- Une recette ne se décoche plus que sur un geste explicite : le bouton « dans la liste » de sa tuile, « Tout décocher », ou la suppression de la recette.
- Le commentaire qui justifiait l'ancien comportement est remplacé par celui du nouveau.
- `CACHE` passe à `panier-v13` dans `sw.js`, pour que les téléphones déjà installés récupèrent la page.

La liste de courses et le carnet de recettes sont désormais indépendants.

## Vérification

Syntaxe du script d'`index.html` contrôlée avec `node --check` (le dépôt n'a ni test ni build).

body:
## Details

Any CrewAI tool that accepts `version` as a keyword argument (or any other name that happens to match a named parameter in `process_crewai_response`) silently fails at runtime:

```
TypeError: process_crewai_response() got multiple values for argument 'version'
```

The tool body executes successfully, but the telemetry recording wrapper calls `process_crewai_response` with both a positional `version` (the openlit/app version string) **and** the tool's original `**kwargs` forwarded. When a tool kwarg is named `version` (e.g. the Azure DevOps MCP `repo_file(version="refs/heads/main")`), Python sees the parameter bound twice and raises `TypeError`. CrewAI catches the re-raised error and reports it to the LLM as a tool failure, discarding the real result.

**Root cause:** `crewai.py` and `async_crewai.py` call `process_crewai_response(..., version, ..., **kwargs)` where `**kwargs` is the tool's original keyword arguments. Any key in that dict that matches a named parameter in `process_crewai_response`'s signature triggers the conflict.

## Fix

Replace the `**kwargs` expansion with a dedicated `tool_kwargs=None` parameter in `process_crewai_response`'s signature. Callers pass `tool_kwargs=kwargs` as a named keyword argument instead of expanding the dict directly. Inside the function, `_set_tool_attributes` receives `tool_kwargs or {}` instead of `kwargs`.

This eliminates the conflict for **all** possible clashing kwarg names, not just `version`, while preserving all tool call arguments for span attribute recording.

## Files changed

- `sdk/python/src/openlit/instrumentation/crewai/utils.py` — `process_crewai_response` signature: `**kwargs` → `tool_kwargs=None`; `_set_tool_attributes` call: `kwargs` → `tool_kwargs or {}`
- `sdk/python/src/openlit/instrumentation/crewai/crewai.py` — call site: `**kwargs` → `tool_kwargs=kwargs`
- `sdk/python/src/openlit/instrumentation/crewai/async_crewai.py` — call site: `**kwargs` → `tool_kwargs=kwargs`

## Reproduce / verify

```python
import openlit
from crewai.tools import BaseTool

openlit.init()

class RepoFileTool(BaseTool):
    name: str = "repo_file"
    description: str = "Reads a file from a repository."

    def _run(self, path: str, version: str = "main") -> str:
        return f"content of {path} at {version}"

tool = RepoFileTool()
# Before: raises TypeError (telemetry crashes, result discarded)
# After:  returns "content of README.md at refs/heads/main"
result = tool.run({"path": "README.md", "version": "refs/heads/main"})
print(result)
```

Fixes #1568

## AI-WATERMARK

AI-WATERMARK: yes

- Tools: Claude Code
- Model(s): Claude Sonnet 4.6
- Scope: CrewAI instrumentation — process_crewai_response signature + two call sites

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

## Summary by Sourcery

Fix CrewAI instrumentation so tool arguments with reserved or colliding names no longer cause tool executions to be reported as failures.

Bug Fixes:
- Prevent CrewAI telemetry wrappers from raising argument conflicts when tool keyword arguments match parameters used by response processing.
- Preserve tool keyword arguments for telemetry attribute recording while allowing synchronous and asynchronous tool calls to return their actual results.

author: athrvk
body:
**Was stacked on #1698** (`claude/happy-ride-ysw1fi-rename`), which has merged; GitHub retargeted this PR to `master` and the branch has merged `master` back in so the test matrix runs on the current head.

## Description

Three feedback gaps from the #1683 audit, in three commits.

**A disabled control now says why.** The obvious fix does not work, which is why none of the 163 gates had an explanation: `Button`'s baseline is `disabled:pointer-events-none`, so a `Tooltip` wrapped around a disabled button never gets the events its trigger listens for, and a disabled button is not focusable either - both paths close at the moment there is something to explain. `DisabledHint` is a wrapper *around* the control instead, with its own pointer events and its own tab stop. `reason` doubles as the switch so a caller passes one expression rather than keeping an enabled and a disabled copy of the same button, which is how a hover class or an `aria-label` ends up on one of them and not the other.

Two consequences worth knowing before reading the diff:

- **Crossing the gate replaces the child's DOM node**, since the wrapper is present on one side of it and not the other. Nothing user-visible depends on it (a disabled control has no focus to lose), but a test holding a reference across the flip has to re-query - one did.
- **An adopting surface now needs a `TooltipProvider` above it.** The app has one at its root, so this is a test-harness fact, not a runtime one - see the fourth commit.

**A disabled menu item is deliberately not wrapped.** `DisabledHint` works by taking a tab stop, and inside a menu that competes with Radix's own focus management, which skips a disabled item on purpose. So `RowAction` gains `disabledReason`, drawn on the item by `RowActionBody` for the `⋯` dropdown and the right-click menu at once, and `hint` for the same column carrying a value rather than a reason. The element list's Move up / Move down now read "Already first" / "Already last".

**Services rows: parity, not an exemption.** They were the last rows in the app painting their actions as always-visible icon buttons - two or three on a 32px row whose own payload is a URL, so the URL truncated to make room for controls the user had not come for. All three groups draw one hover-revealed `RowActionsMenu` now. The values the old tooltips carried (the inbox URL, "stopped, not listening" on a stopped one, the mock's base URL) ride the items' `hint`, which reads without hovering and reaches a screen reader in the item's own name - the tooltip was a strictly weaker place for them. Stopping an issuer or a mock is marked destructive because the record goes with the listener; stopping an inbox is not, because it does not.

**Move up / Move down in the tree's row menu.** The tree reordered by drag and by Alt+Arrow only: a drag needs a pointer, a chord has to be known before it can be used. The entries call the same `moveByKeyboard` the chords do, so one move still goes through one `applyPlacement`. `blockPosition` is factored out and shared with the gating, so a disabled Move up and an "already first" announcement cannot disagree about which row is first. They land above the row's destructive tail, since the separator `rowActionRows` draws there belongs to Delete.

### Safe to skim

- The fourth commit is mechanical and test-only: fourteen files rendered their panel with no `TooltipProvider`, a state the app is never in, and it only went unnoticed because nothing inside them had a tooltip. Each now wraps its renders rather than weakening an assertion to suit the harness.
- Doc edits in `docs/design-system.md` and `docs/app/COMPONENTS.md` are this repo's same-commit rule, and `design-system-doc.test.ts` / `a11y-suppressions.test.ts` check them.
- The merge commit from `master` after #1698 landed.

### Worth scrutiny

- The one new `jsx-a11y` suppression (`no-noninteractive-tabindex` on `DisabledHint`'s wrapper span), the a11y ceiling raised 20 → 21, and its entry in the Accessibility section. The argument is the one `Dock.tsx`'s three error tooltips already carry: the child is disabled, so the wrapper's tab stop is the only keyboard path to the text.
- The Services test rewrites. The assertions moved from clicking a visible button to opening the menu, which is a genuine change in what is being claimed about the surface, not a selector tidy-up.

## Deviation from the issue

#1690's first acceptance criterion asks for `<DisabledHint` in at least six files **including** `components/shared/ElementList/index.tsx`. It lists six, and `ElementList` is not one of them: its only gated controls are the two Move menu items, and a tooltip on those is the case argued against above. The reason strings that criterion was after ("Already first" / "Already last") are in that file, as `disabledReason` - rendered through the shared `RowActionBody`, so both menus get them, which the per-file JSX would not have achieved.

`CollectionTree.move.test.tsx` carries a small fixture of its own rather than sharing `CollectionTree.dnd.test.tsx`'s - the tree tests have no shared harness today, and these cases need no layout or hit-test stubs, since a menu click is not a pointer gesture.

## Acceptance criteria

```
$ rg '<DisabledHint' app/src --glob '!*.test.*' -l
app/src/modules/collections/CollectionDetail/ElementsTab.tsx
app/src/modules/inbox/index.tsx
app/src/modules/settings/main/panels/NotificationsPanel.tsx
app/src/modules/settings/main/panels/GeneralPanel.tsx
app/src/modules/history/main/SaveRunToRequestDialog.tsx
app/src/modules/request-builder/components/LoadTestConfigDialog/index.tsx

$ rg 'group-hover:opacity-100' app/src/modules/services/ServicesPanel.tsx
					className="opacity-0 transition-opacity group-hover:opacity-100 group-focus-within:opacity-100"

$ rg 'Move up' app/src/modules/collections --glob '!*.test.*'
app/src/modules/collections/useTreeDnd.ts:					label: "Move up",
(plus five comment lines in useTreeDnd.ts, CollectionItem.tsx and CollectionTreeContext.tsx)
```

## Testing

```
$ cd app && pnpm test disabled-hint ServicesPanel CollectionTree.move row-action-reveal
 Test Files  6 passed (6)
      Tests  60 passed (60)

$ cd app && pnpm lint && pnpm type-check && pnpm format:check
(all clean)

$ cd app && pnpm test
 Test Files  775 passed (775)
      Tests  8740 passed | 2 skipped (8742)
```

Mutation checks, each reverted afterwards:

- Drop `pointer-events-auto` from `DisabledHint`'s wrapper → `disabled-hint.test.tsx` "keeps its own pointer events" fails. jsdom has no hit testing, so the class is the assertion; it is the whole mechanism.
- `tabIndex={0}` → `{-1}` → "is a tab stop" fails.
- Drop the reveal `className` from `ServiceRow`'s `RowActionsMenu` → "hides its row actions until the row is hovered or focused" fails.
- The two tree cases name their own checks in comments: pointing `Move down` at `"up"` inverts the asserted orders, and the disabled-entry case fails if a gated item writes.

author: goddivor
body:
Refs goddivor/mlbb-togo#45

## What / why
New `src/league-stats` module serving the league statistics page (issue #45). It aggregates the completed `EsportMatch` rows and their `EsportMatchPlayer` scoresheets in memory (seasons are small, queries are bounded to one season) behind a 60 s per-key cache. No schema change, no touched module outside `src/league-stats` + the `app.module.ts` registration (siblings #43 / #44 own `src/standings` and `src/esport`).

## Endpoints (public)
`seasonId` accepts a season id, `current` (the site's current season) or `all` (default).

- `GET /league-stats/teams?seasonId=` — per team: games, W/L/D, win rate, score for/against, avg kills/deaths/assists per game, MVP count, most played heroes (with images), `avgDurationMin` (always `null`: duration is not recorded on league matches yet).
- `GET /league-stats/players?seasonId&role&sort=kills|kda|mvp|games|assists|winRate|deaths&limit` — individual rankings with user card, team, main lane, games, K/D/A totals + averages, KDA, MVP count, win rate. Only players with ≥ 1 completed game; `role` keeps only the games played on that lane.
- `GET /league-stats/meta?seasonId&minGames&limit` — per hero: picks, pick rate, win rate (null below `minGames`, default 3), KDA, MVP, bans. **Ban source is labelled honestly**: `banSource` is `unavailable` today because league matches carry no ban data, and pick & ban simulator boards are practice data that is deliberately not counted. `bansOf()` already reads an optional `EsportMatch.games` JSON breakdown, so the day bans are recorded the endpoint switches to `banSource: "match-games"` with real ban rates.
- `GET /league-stats/records?seasonId&period=week|season` — top single-game kills, assists, damage, gold, KDA, biggest score margin; `longestGame` is `null` (duration not recorded).

Invalid input is rejected: unknown `sort` / `period` / malformed `seasonId` → 400, unknown season → 404.

## Tests
- `src/league-stats/league-stats.util.spec.ts` — 16 specs on the pure aggregations: team records/averages, player rankings + every sort key + lane filter + "team of the most recent game", meta pick/win/ban rates and the min-games threshold, ban parsing, season vs rolling-week records window.
- `src/league-stats/league-stats.service.spec.ts` — 8 specs on season-scope resolution, query validation, the TTL cache and the decorated payloads.

## How it was tested
Local MongoDB (`mlbb_togo_review`), seeded with a season + 25 completed matches + 96 scoresheets, backend on port 4406:

```
GET /league-stats/teams?seasonId=current  → 200, 21 matches, 5 teams ranked (EPSILON 7-1, 87.5%)
GET /league-stats/players?role=jungle&sort=kda → 200, ranked with team/lane/KDA
GET /league-stats/meta?seasonId=current   → 200, banSource "unavailable", pick/win rates
GET /league-stats/records?period=week     → 200, rolling 7-day window
?sort=foo / ?seasonId=zzz / ?period=day   → 400
```

Quality gate (run in the worktree right before pushing, all exit 0):

```
npx prisma generate → ok
npm run build       → nest build, BUILD=0
npm run lint        → 1 problem (0 errors, 1 pre-existing warning in search.service.spec.ts)
npm test            → Test Suites: 23 passed, 23 total / Tests: 285 passed, 285 total
```

author: wangchangxin0809
body:
## Summary

Fix the first-use AgentRoom race exposed by the Python 3.13 CI lane: multiple processes could concurrently execute `PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL` before the room schema existed, and one process could fail with `sqlite3.OperationalError: database is locked`.

The fix serializes only the one-time WAL/schema initialization with the existing cross-process file lock. Normal room transactions still use SQLite locking as before.

Also bumps the plugin patch version to **1.11.1**, because this changes shipped runtime code.

## Evidence

The existing `test_first_use_from_independent_processes` is the regression test: it launches eight fresh processes against a new room. It passed on Python 3.9 but exposed this race on Python 3.13 in PR #96.

Links previously had `rel="noreferrer"` only or no `rel` attribute at all — all now have `rel="noopener noreferrer"`.

**Cleanup**: Made `BuyCard.onBuy` optional; removed two no-op `onBuy={() => {}}` handlers from `DashboardItemsContent.tsx` (comics and items sections).

body:
Mobilde tur sayfasının başlığı logo + "Giriş Yap / Üye Ol" gösteriyordu: hangi sayfada olduğunuzu söylemiyor, yerin çoğunu harcıyordu. Artık bildirimler ekranıyla aynı düzen — solda yuvarlak geri oku, ortada iki satırlık başlık, sağda tek ikon eylem.

```
  ‹   Kapadokya Turu — 3 Gece 4 Gün        (paylaş)
      Konaklamalı Tur · Göreme, Nevşehir
```

## Üçüncü kopya yerine ortak tanım

Bu başlık zaten iki yerde vardı: `.notif-panel-header` ve `.auth-modal-hero`. İkincisinin başında şu not duruyordu:

> *"Ölçüler bildirimler ekranının başlığıyla birebir aynı tutulur. Biri değişirse diğeri de güncellenmeli."*

Yani elle senkron tutulan bir kopya. Üçüncüsünü eklemek yerine tanım tek yere alındı. Kapsayıcı, geri oku, başlık yığını, alt başlık ve sağdaki eylem zemini artık üç seçici için ortak yazılıyor; `display` ve `flex-shrink` paylaşılmıyor, çünkü her ekranın kendi görünürlük kuralı var. `.auth-modal-hero` geriye yalnızca `display: none` tutuyor. Bir ölçü değişince üç ekran birlikte değişiyor, senkron notuna gerek kalmadı.

Başlık ve alt başlık artık taşarsa kısalıyor (uzun tur adı sarmıyor).

## İki ayrı düzen, tek düzen zorlanmıyor

Masaüstünde her zamanki site başlığı (`.header-inner`) aynen duruyor; mobilde o gizlenip `.tour-mobile-header` açılıyor. Böylece ikisi birbirinin kurallarını ezmiyor.

## Paylaş: ikon

Metin hapı yerine geri okuyla aynı çapta (34px) yuvarlak ikon düğme. Zemin ve hover ortak tanımdan geliyor, yalnızca biçim ayrışıyor — bildirimler ekranı metin hapını ("Tümünü oku") korudu.

Yan fayda: ikon hapa göre dar olduğu için başlığa kalan genişlik 215'ten 268 piksele çıktı ve "Kapadokya Turu — 3 Gece 4 Gün" artık kısalmadan tam sığıyor.

Metin kalkınca düğmenin erişilebilir adı da kalkıyordu; `aria-label` eklendi ve teste bağlandı.

## Oval alt kenar

Başlık zaten 22px yuvarlak alt köşe taşıyordu ama **görünmüyordu**: onu saran `.site-header` de lacivert ve köşesizdi, içteki yuvarlak köşeleri dolduruyordu. Ölçüm bunu gösterdi — başlığın alt köşe pikseli `.site-header`'a, orta pikseli `.tour-mobile-header`'a aitti.

Mobilde sarmalayıcının zemini ve gölgesi kaldırıldı; zemini tamamen içteki başlık çiziyor. Masaüstünde sarmalayıcı kendi zeminini koruyor.

## Kırılma noktaları

Mobilde tamamen gizlendi. Başlık zaten geri okunu ve kategoriyi taşıyor; aynı bilgiyi ikinci kez göstermeye gerek yoktu. **Gizlemek silmek değil:** işaretleme de `BreadcrumbList` yapısal verisi de yerinde duruyor, yalnızca görünürlük değişti.

Masaüstünde kırılma noktaları aynen kalıyor — orada başlık normal site başlığı olduğu için sayfanın yerini gösteren tek şey o.

## Paylaş tek fonksiyonda

Paylaş artık iki yerde: başlık kartındaki yuvarlak düğme (masaüstü) ve mobil başlıktaki ikon. İkisi de aynı fonksiyona bağlı, davranış kopyalanmadı. Favori düğmesi başlığa taşınmadı — iki yerde duran işaretli/işaretsiz durumu senkron tutmak gerekirdi, paylaş ise durumsuz.

## Doğrulama

**211 test geçiyor** (öncesi 199). Yeni testler:

- Her sayfanın mobil başlık metni tur kaydıyla aynı mı
- Başlıkta geri oku ve **tek** eylem var mı
- Paylaş düğmesi ikon mu, erişilebilir adı var mı, görünür metin kalmış mı
- Ortak stil tanımı gerçekten ortak mı, `.auth-modal-hero` kendi kopyasını geri getirmiş mi
- Sarmalayıcı mobilde saydam mı, kırılma noktaları gizli ama işaretleme duruyor mu
- Mobil/masaüstü görünürlük kuralları yerinde mi

Paylaşılan CSS değiştiği için **diğer iki ekran da tarayıcıda ölçüldü**: bildirimler ve giriş/üye ol başlıkları üçü de aynı zemin, yarıçap, gölge, iç boşluk ve 60 piksel yükseklik veriyor. Anasayfanın kendi başlığı ve bildirimler ekranı etkilenmedi (değişiklik `.tour-body` ile sınırlı).

İki tur sayfası 390 ve 1440 pikselde kontrol edildi: JS hatası yok, yatay taşma yok, masaüstü başlığı değişmedi. Paylaş tıklaması pano yedeğiyle "Bağlantı kopyalandı" veriyor.

body:
## What changed

- **Leaderboard** (`lib/screens/player_stats_screen.dart`, replaces the `ExpansionTile` list): game-type chips ("All games" plus each type with finished games, most played first), a teal hero for the best win rate (leader's avatar in a gold ring), one card per player with place, two-letter `PlayerAvatar` in the `player_colors.dart` colour, games, wins · win rate, and a win-rate bar. Players with fewer than 5 finished games of the filter come last, unranked.
- **Player card** (new `lib/screens/player_card_screen.dart`), opened by tapping a player, on the same filter: avatar strip to switch player; games, wins, average place; the place over the last 12 games (a `CustomPainter`, no new dependency) with wins in gold and a trend; current win streak; best final total following `isLowestScoreWins`; average final total; the opponent most often finished ahead of. On "All games" the best total is hidden when the games mix both win rules.
- **Data**: `PlayerStatsRepository.getFinishedGameResults` (Drift impl, exposed by `GameProvider`) reads live finished games with at least one score on a live round, keyed by the global `players.uuid`. All figures are computed in `lib/models/player_stats.dart`. No schema change, no migration.
- **i18n**: 21 new `stats*` keys in all 10 ARB files (ICU plurals for counts; `statsRankOrdinal` is a `select` on a String for the irregular ordinals).
- **Docs**: `.llmwiki/MobileApp.md` (the screens, a decision entry), `I18n.md`/`INDEX.md` key count, `README.md` feature list.
- **wip**: closes `2026-09-19-player-statistics-screen-is-a-plain-list` (moved to `wip/done/`); opens `wip/todo_nr/2026-09-19-players-screen-counts-open-games-and-shows-blue-avatars.md` (the Players screen still counts open games and draws blue avatars).

## Why

The old screen showed "N games" per player, with avatars in `Colors.blue`/stored colours that disagreed with the board, and nothing to compare players by. The user picked the leaderboard and the player card from four drawn directions (target images under `wip/assets/2026-09-19-player-statistics-screen-is-a-plain-list/`).

## Tests

- `test/screens/player_stats_screen_test.dart`: no `ExpansionTile`, avatar colours equal to the board's; a game-type chip changes ranks and wins; tapping a player opens the card scoped to the type, with average place, streak and best total checked on a lowest-wins (ZapZap) and a highest-wins (Tarot) fixture, and switching player from the strip.
- `test/models/player_stats_test.dart`: tied places, unranked threshold, type ordering, colours, 12-game window, trend, best total with mixed rules.
- `test/drift/drift_repositories_test.dart`: the query leaves out open and unscored games and deleted rounds.

Checked visually at 412 dp, light and dark, in French.

author: 0z5a
body:
Related to #2416. This RFC adds a communicator-configured allocator for one audited class: local persistent CUDA Graph work descriptors that do not fit in kernel arguments. It is a scoped prototype, not an implementation of the full external allocator RFE.

The allocator descriptor is copied by value. Paired alloc/free callbacks receive the original byte count and device; allocation receives NCCL's upload stream. Failure propagates without fallback. Plan provenance routes external pointers back to the matching callback. Split communicators inherit the descriptor when no overriding config is supplied. Callback code/context must outlive all graphs, graph executables and communicator destruction, be thread-safe, and must not reenter NCCL.

Transport/exported buffers, registration arenas, NVLS, ordinary enqueue and offload-manager allocations retain their existing paths. Storage remains live throughout graph lifetime. No PyTorch integration or large-model capacity benefit is claimed. The public API and eligibility scope need maintainer agreement.

Validation on upstream 12df1a11afad322be5a204a2db890161cbf8131d, CUDA 12.8, two L20s:
- Clean shared/static build; standalone regression builds with -Wall -Wextra -Werror.
- Six graph captures, three replays each, 64 AllReduce operations per graph with exact outputs.
- Default allocator, legacy config size, missing callback rejection and intentional allocation failure/abort pass.
- External pool and inherited split allocator pass on both enqueue paths, with pointer/size/device validation; 12 allocations and 12 frees, 36,864 bytes per rank.
- The test sets NCCL_WORK_ARGS_BYTES=256 to exercise the persistent path. It does not claim every CUDA failure path has been injected.

Two fresh-process APPA/PAAP quartets, idle L20 GPUs 4/5, CPU affinity 40–47. For each job take the maximum rank mean, then the geometric mean across four jobs per arm. The first graph timing is discarded; each job contributes five capture means and fifteen replays.

| Metric | Baseline default pool µs | External pool µs | Speed change |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Capture + instantiate | 151.720 | 138.192 | +9.79% |
| Replay + synchronize (64 AllReduce calls) | 228.083 | 218.724 | +4.28% |

Speed change = baseline/patch − 1. These are descriptive measurements, not a stable speedup claim. Capture job means span 120.841–206.188 µs for baseline and 101.112–173.159 µs for patch on this shared host with unlocked clocks. All patched runs have balanced allocation/free counts. This measures the collective graph lifecycle, not a full training workload.

Reproduction and the standalone regression are in contrib/graph_work_allocator/.

author: bookasloth
body:
### What / Why

Fixes #71426.

When `assetPrefix` contains a `!` (e.g. `assetPrefix: "https://mycdn.com/!mark"`), `next build` fails with:

```
Module not found: Error: Can't resolve 'mark&nextConfigOutput=export&...&middlewareConfig=e30%3D'
```

**Root cause:** `getAppEntry` serializes the app loader options into the webpack request with `querystring.stringify`, which escapes values via `encodeURIComponent`. `encodeURIComponent` does **not** escape `!`. webpack parses `!` as its inline-loader separator (`loader!module`), so the `!` inside `assetPrefix` truncates the `next-app-loader` request — everything after it is treated as the module to resolve, hence the error. (`middlewareConfig` avoids this because it is base64-encoded; `assetPrefix` is not.)

### Fix

Escape `!` → `%21` when serializing the app loader options. The loader reads them back via `this.getOptions()`, which decodes the query, so `assetPrefix` round-trips unchanged.

Added a unit test (`entries.test.ts`) asserting the serialized request contains no raw `!` before the loader terminator and that the value is escaped.

author: dditsupport
body:
Pure addition (+113, no deletions) to dashboard/index.php: the card, its styling in the page's own <style> block, and the render function. No API change — readings.php already returns kwh_start / kwh_end per bucket, and loadRange() already turns them into each bar's s / e carrying the old-meter offset. The table just tabulates what the chart is already drawn from, so end - start is exactly the bar's kWh rather than a second estimate.

Until now that arithmetic was only visible as the one-line "Meter reading: A -> B" under the chart, and in per-bar labels that the existing code drops once bars get narrow (30 days, or any phone). The table is the fallback that does not vanish.

Two things done deliberately rather than copied:

- Labels come from the ISO string's own fields, not new Date(). The server emits each bucket in APP_TIMEZONE, so parsing it into the viewer's zone shifts a midnight bucket back a day for anyone outside IST and mislabels every row. Verified by rendering with the browser forced to UTC: dates are still correct. (The solar dashboard this was modelled on does use new Date() + toLocaleDateString and has that bug.)
- Multi-meter mode gets a leading Meter column instead of being hidden. Each channel is its own cumulative counter, so two meters cannot share a row. Header and footer column counts are built from the same MULTI flag so they stay aligned.

Verified by rendering the real function against this repo's point shape: the single-meter case reproduces the reference screenshot row for row including Total 140.042, the two-meter case groups by bucket then meter with 5 = 5 columns, and neither throws.

body:
This PR proves the `TauCetiRoadmap/ModularForms/README.md` Layer 7 target “The completed L-function and Hecke's functional equation”: define the level-`N` Mellin completion on bundled cusp forms, identify it with `N^(s/2) · ModularForm.Λ`, prove it entire, establish the two-form equation `Λ_N(k-s,f) = i^k Λ_N(s,g)` under the positive-weight, strict-width-one, and Petersson-normalized Fricke-companion hypotheses, and specialize it to `Γ₁(N)` using `normalizedFrickeOperatorCusp`.

This is the most direct unmet step on the milestone path because Mathlib already supplies the analytic continuation of `ModularForm.Λ` and Tau Ceti already supplies the normalized Fricke operator, so the remaining work is the rescaled-axis identity and Mellin change of variables. After this PR, Layer 7 still needs the sharp noncuspidal abscissa bound, the newform Euler product, and the one-form sign corollary after Layer 6 supplies the relevant Fricke eigenvalue/sign theorem.

The proof adapts `LeanModularForms/Modularforms/LFunctionFEqN.lean` from AINTLIB (Apache-2.0, commit `112d12d95`) and reuses Mathlib's `ModularForm.Λ`, `CuspForm.Λ_eq_mellin`, `mellin_comp_mul_right`, `mellin_cpow_smul`, and `mellin_comp_inv`; no Mathlib infrastructure is vendored.

The prefix-directory rule moves `TauCeti.NumberTheory.ModularForms.LFunction` to `TauCeti.NumberTheory.ModularForms.LFunction.Basic`, updates its in-repository importer, and adds `TauCeti.NumberTheory.ModularForms.LFunction.FunctionalEquation`; no compatibility forwarding module remains.

author: javiercamarapp
body:
## Qué medía realmente el gateway (antes de este cambio)

`packages/agent-core/src/gateway` YA medía, por llamada: tokens in/out, costo
estimado en USD (float), modelo y proveedor que respondió — y YA aplicaba
reserva-antes-de-gastar (`budget.ts`) con tres topes (run/tenant-diario/carril).
Pero:

- El `BudgetLedgerStore` real de producción es **en memoria de proceso**
  (`InMemoryBudgetLedgerStore`, ver `apps/api/src/production/llm-gateway.ts`) —
  un tope diario que reinicia con cada instancia de Vercel Fluid Compute y no
  se comparte entre instancias concurrentes. Sirve como defensa en profundidad,
  nunca como fuente de verdad de un tope de negocio real.
- **Ninguna llamada se persistía en ningún lado** — cero observabilidad de
  gasto real. El superadmin (`apps/web/src/superadmin/`) no mostraba nada de
  gasto.
- No existía ningún tope **mensual** (solo diario) ni ningún tope **de
  organización configurable** ni **global de plataforma**.

Un único punto de intercepción real: `LlmGateway.complete()`
(`packages/agent-core/src/gateway/gateway.ts`), instanciado una sola vez en
producción (`apps/api/src/production/llm-gateway.ts::buildProductionLlmGateway`)
y compartido por las 10 escaleras de las 6 verticales. Ninguna llamada a LLM en
producción salta este punto — no hizo falta reportar call sites fuera de alcance.

## Qué se construyó

**1. Puertos nuevos en agent-core (sin acoplar a Postgres)**
- `usage.ts`: `UsageRecorder` (registro de uso post-llamada, best-effort) +
  `NoopUsageRecorder` por defecto.
- `org-monthly-budget.ts`: `OrgMonthlyBudgetStore`, misma semántica
  reserva-antes-de-gastar, pensado para persistir entre instancias (tope
  mensual por organización + tope global de plataforma), con
  `InMemoryOrgMonthlyBudgetStore` de referencia.
- `gateway.ts` los consume: el tope mensual se verifica ANTES de llamar al
  proveedor (`MonthlyBudgetExceededError`, tipado, `retryable: false`) y el
  registro de uso corre DESPUÉS de un éxito real, en su propio try/catch — un
  fallo de cualquiera de los dos nunca rompe una llamada al LLM que ya tuvo éxito.

**2. Persistencia en Postgres (migración `20240101000124`)**
- `core.llm_usage_daily`: agregado diario por (organización, vertical, rol,
  proveedor, modelo, carril) — un agregado, no una fila por llamada, dado el
  volumen esperado de agentes de WhatsApp conversacionales.
- `core.llm_org_budget` / `core.llm_platform_budget`: tope mensual por
  organización + tope global, con umbral de alerta.
- `core.llm_monthly_reservation`: ledger autoritativo de reserva-antes-de-gastar
  mensual, con `pg_advisory_xact_lock` para el chequeo atómico de ambos topes.
- Funciones `security definer`, `GRANT` a `authenticated` (nunca solo a
  `service_role`, que este monorepo no aprovisiona). Las internas
  (`record_llm_usage`/`reserve_llm_monthly_budget`/`settle_llm_monthly_budget`)
  sin caller check (solo el backend las invoca). Las del back office validan
  `is_platform_superadmin(p_caller_id)` DENTRO de la función.
- Verificada aplicándose sin error contra un Postgres real (las 124 migraciones
  en orden) y probada a mano (reserve/settle, ambos topes, escritura de topes,
  no-superadmin ve 0 filas).
- Espejo byte-idéntico en `supabase/migrations/` — `verify:migration-versions` OK.

**3. API de superadmin** (`apps/api/src/routes/superadmin-llm-usage.ts`)
- `GET /superadmin/gasto-api/resumen?from&to`
- `GET /superadmin/gasto-api/organizaciones?from&to` (incluye % de tope usado
  — ordenado por gasto descendente, así que la propia lista ES el "top
  consumidores")
- `GET /superadmin/gasto-api/desglose?from&to&organizationId?`
- `PUT /superadmin/gasto-api/organizaciones/:id/tope`
- `PUT /superadmin/gasto-api/plataforma/tope`

**4. Pantalla `/superadmin/gasto-api`** — nav item en `SuperAdminShell.tsx`,
ruta en `App.tsx`, totales del periodo, tope global de plataforma con barra de
% usado, tabla por organización con barra CSS de % de tope usado y edición
inline, desglose por proveedor/modelo. Sin librerías de gráficas nuevas (el
repo no tenía ninguna). Estados de carga/error/vacío reales.

**5. Sin credenciales de LLM configuradas**: `llmGateway` queda `undefined`
(comportamiento preexistente, fail-closed) — nunca se registra uso, pero
`llmUsageRepo` es independiente y la pantalla sigue funcionando, mostrando
ceros reales.

## Dónde vive la fuente de verdad del tope

`core.llm_monthly_reservation` (Postgres) — autoritativa, persistente entre
instancias, con los dos topes verificados atómicamente ANTES de llamar al
proveedor. `core.llm_usage_daily` es observacional (best-effort, para
reporting), nunca la autoridad de bloqueo.

## Límite honesto

`MonthlyBudgetExceededError` es un error tipado (mismo criterio que el ya
existente `GatewayBudgetExceededError`), pero ningún turn-handler de las 6
verticales lo traduce hoy a una respuesta específica al usuario final — se
propaga al catch genérico de cada webhook, exactamente el mismo tratamiento
que ya recibe `GatewayBudgetExceededError` hoy (no es una regresión; wirear
una respuesta amigable por vertical es una extensión futura, no pedida en el
alcance de esta pieza).

## Verificaciones que pasaron
- `npm run typecheck` (raíz, todos los workspaces) ✅
- `npm run lint` ✅
- `npm run build --workspace apps/web` ✅
- `npm run test:unit` — 415 archivos, 4425 tests ✅ (incluye
  `packages/db/tests/migration-versions-guard.spec.ts`)
- `npm run verify:migration-versions` ✅
- Migración aplicada a mano contra Postgres real (además de la suite anterior)

## Test plan
- [ ] Revisar la migración SQL y las funciones `security definer`
- [ ] Correr `npm run test:unit` en CI (gate `postgres-real-gate.yml`)
- [ ] Probar la pantalla `/superadmin/gasto-api` en preview con datos reales

author: hyxklee
body:
## 배경

V3 → V4 마이그레이션(WTH-508)에서 **파일만은 SQL로 처리할 수 없습니다.**

| | 이유 |
|---|---|
| `file.file_size` | V4에서 `NOT NULL`인데 V3 DB에 값이 없음 → S3 `HeadObject` 필요 |
| `file.content_type` | 동일 |
| `storage_key` | 키 형식이 달라 **모든 객체를 새 키로 복사**해야 함 |

```
V3  b2835a47-8728-4570-b584-6c0a39d5dbad.pdf          (버킷 루트 평면)
V4  POST/2025-03/b2835a47-...-dbad_영수증.pdf          ({OWNER_TYPE}/{yyyy-MM}/{uuid}_{fileName})
```

`StorageKey` VO가 정규식으로 형식을 강제하므로 예외가 없습니다.

## 변경 내용

### 1. 파일 마이그레이터 (`src/migration/kotlin`)

- **별도 소스셋** — 일회성 도구가 운영 아티팩트(`bootJar`)에 섞이지 않습니다.
- Spring 컨텍스트 없이 JDBC + AWS SDK v2만 사용합니다.
- **기본이 dry-run**입니다. 실제 반영은 `--apply`를 명시해야 합니다.
- **원본 버킷은 읽기만** 합니다. 삭제하지 않으므로 롤백은 V4 쪽 정리로 충분합니다.
- `CopyObject`는 서버사이드라 객체 바이트가 실행 머신을 거치지 않습니다.
- `uuid`를 V3 키에서 재사용하므로 같은 입력이면 같은 키가 나옵니다(멱등).
- `--offline` 모드 — 자격증명 없이 키 생성·소유 매핑만 검토합니다.

### 2. 첨부 허용 형식에 pptx / docx 추가

V3에 세션 자료(pptx 27건)와 문서(docx 2건)가 있어 현행 목록으로는 이전할 수 없습니다.

```kotlin
PPTX("application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.presentationml.presentation", setOf("pptx")),
DOCX("application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document", setOf("docx")),
```

**svg는 추가하지 않았습니다.** XML이라 `<script>`를 품을 수 있어 인라인 서빙 시 XSS 벡터가 됩니다.
**mp4도 제외**했습니다(용량·전송비·Range 요청). 두 건은 `UNSUPPORTED_TYPE`으로 남습니다.

Swagger `@Schema` 설명과 `FileTypeTest`도 함께 갱신했습니다.

## 실행

```bash
# 자격증명 없이 키 생성·소유 매핑만 검토
MIG_DB_PASSWORD=... ./gradlew migrateFiles --args="--offline"

# HeadObject로 생존·크기 확인 (복사 없음)
MIG_DB_PASSWORD=... ./gradlew migrateFiles --args="--source-bucket=... --target-bucket=..."

# 실제 반영
MIG_DB_PASSWORD=... ./gradlew migrateFiles --args="--source-bucket=... --target-bucket=... --apply"
```

## 검증

로컬 V3 복제본(406건)에 `--offline` 전수 실행:

| | 변경 전 | 변경 후 |
|---|---:|---:|
| 이전 가능 | 370 | **399** |
| UNSUPPORTED_TYPE | 31 | **2** (mp4 1 / svg 1) |
| FAILED (비표준 키) | 5 | 5 |

**98.3%가 이전 가능**해졌습니다. 생성 키 최대 길이 216자(한도 500), 키 생성 실패 0건.

`./gradlew ktlintCheck compileMigrationKotlin test --tests "*File*Test"` 통과.

## 남은 확인 사항

- **S3 객체 생존율** — 개발 머신에 AWS 자격증명이 없어 실측하지 못했습니다. 자격증명이 있는 환경에서 dry-run을 돌리면 확정됩니다.
- **비표준 키 5건** — 한글 원본 파일명이 URL 인코딩된 채 키에 들어 있어 수동 확인이 필요합니다.

## 관련

- `docs/plan/v3-to-v4-migration-plan.md` §5
- `docs/migration/v3-to-v4/10_file_prepare.sql` (선행 SQL)
- PR #106 (일정·세션 content TEXT)

body:
## Scope
Continue the hotspot library only; keep the shared AppShell, other libraries and deferred video sizing unchanged. No production deployment, collection run or paid API call.

## Backend and data-boundary fixes
- Growth compares the latest observation with a strictly earlier timestamp; equal-time ingestions do not fabricate growth.
- Future-dated snapshots are excluded from current values and trends.
- Trend data keeps the newest 240 distinct observation times, then returns chronological order.
- Missing heat is not treated as measured zero by threshold filters.
- Backend detail selection stays inside the current filtered page; stale/malformed ids cannot escape it.
- Related videos are deduplicated before the display limit.
- All sort modes have a stable id tiebreaker.
- Backend-only changes now trigger real PostgreSQL integration tests, not just Python compilation.

## Frontend boundary fixes
- Trend x-coordinates now use each snapshot's real `captured_at` interval instead of equal index spacing.
- Invalid timestamps and missing heat values are excluded without converting `null` or an empty string to measured zero.
- A real measured zero remains a valid trend point; numeric strings are normalized defensively.
- Only the newest hotspot-library request may update data, selection, error or loading state.
- In-flight responses are invalidated when the component unmounts.
- After filtering, sorting or pagination, the selected detail id follows the backend's visible-page fallback instead of retaining a stale id.

## Verified validation — 2026-09-19
Current head: `62eb5169db3b89e5e4afc79c513653c81fd10cfd`.

Earlier backend-focused head `f67e31528db3af1b1a61002e70e3e2d243552388` passed 51 PostgreSQL integration/unit tests, including 21 new hotspot boundary cases.

The current frontend head passed both required workflows:
- `web-dashboard` run 35433060588: frontend dependency install, React bundle, and Windmill Python backend compilation succeeded.
- `provider-tests` run 35433060610: disposable PostgreSQL bootstrap, compile, unit tests, and PostgreSQL integration tests succeeded.

## Final acceptance and merge
In addition to the repository/CI checks above, an isolated local DOM harness using the PR's real frontend code and synthetic data verified:
- stale slow responses cannot overwrite the newest platform selection;
- pagination synchronizes the detail pane to the current visible page;
- non-uniform timestamps produce proportional SVG x-coordinates;
- measured zero remains a plotted value while invalid timestamps and missing heat are excluded.

The harness contained no secrets or production data and was not committed. A live Windmill deployment was not performed.

Merged by squash into `main` on 2026-09-19 as `0c93eb672005fd497b4198be17a7eca1d248e954`. No production deployment, live database mutation, collection run, or paid API call was performed.

## Bug
Repeated refreshes created a fresh quota snapshot with `RestUntil == nil`; the rest policy then restarted `now + 16h` for every exhausted Antigravity credential.

## Fix
- Carry an active cached `RestUntil` forward by `AuthIndex` before applying the rest policy.
- Never overwrite an active deadline during repeated probes.
- Allow an expired deadline to be cleared and a genuinely exhausted account to start a new window.

## TDD
- Added `TestAntigravityRestDeadlineSurvivesRepeatedProbes`, covering two probes seven minutes apart and asserting the original deadline remains unchanged.
- Baseline failed because `inheritAntigravityRest` was undefined; implementation then passed.
