## Summary

Evidence for the authorized Stage 2 B4-only session (policy A, strict stop rules) run 2026-09-19 UTC 04:39–07:33 against merge commit `e6c30b7` (PR #131), per `outputs/e1-stage2-b4-execution-plan-2026-09-18.md`: **18/18 cycles — 18/18 flights (LOWER_TO_REST, PLACE_ROUTE, LIFT_TO_PRESENT × 6), 12/12 recorded setups, 18/18 scheduled resets, 18 parked recordings all `stiff-zero`, Stage 0 armon accepted; every gate passed on all 49 recordings; zero contacts and zero disturbance (max displacement 8.5e-9 m). No STOP.**

`docs/reviews/probes-2026-09-19-e1-stage2-b4/` (~3 MB): `REPORT.md`, `ledger.csv` (49 rows), `README.md`, `REPRODUCTION.md`, `summaries/` (planned-vs-realised clearance by route × role × hand × link across repetitions with and without the sleep-affected cycle, per-recording recorder reports, cycle wall times), `control/` (every gate output incl. the force-added `*.log` recorder/notebook outputs, markers, reset/settle/start-variant evidence, checkpoint record, the exact tools and session wrappers run), notebooks as generated and as executed, plans, board sha, server manifest, `SHA256SUMS` over the **full** evidence tree, and `ARCHIVE_SHA256`.

**Not in Git** (raw; originals preserved at `~/e1-stage2-B4-s1-2026-09-18/`, 2.4 GB): `states.jsonl` (1.8 GB) / `commands.jsonl`, the 49 recorder logs + sidecars, `native_server.log`, the per-recording clearance JSON. Local archives (verified by extraction + `shasum -c`): `~/e1-evidence-archive/e1-stage2-B4-s1-2026-09-18-final.tar.zst` (402 MB), sha256 `9565a207c2d4805526e230abde6cd36c49f39057c12ff4597e6e26f6bb0f525d`; the session-close archive `…-2026-09-18.tar.zst`, sha256 `ae0cda95c2183a4d3558e1b68fe2d30556ce2b3465ebf88bc1611761891db19f`. No Release/Drive upload (not authorized).

## Findings (observations, not margins)

- Realised moving-segment clearance to `pool_box_1` on the closest shells link (forearm): RAISE_TO_SIDE setup +5.45..+5.69 cm (planned +6.26), PLACE_ROUTE flight +5.36..+6.05 / setup +5.50..+5.73 (planned +6.26), LOWER_TO_REST +6.39..+6.45 and LIFT_TO_PRESENT +6.20..+6.43 (planned +6.46). Long corridor routes run ~0.65 cm inside plan, short legs ~0.05–0.10 cm — the same split as Stage 1. Tube model −3.7..−4.0 at REST with zero physics contact (known conservative tube).
- **Sleep-affected cycle `S2-B4-c-r1`**: the host idle-slept after that setup's recording and before its flight; verified from the server record (pose Δ 0.0°, stiff, `cmd_seq` unchanged, no commands, no reset). Excluding it changes every group mean by ≤ 0.03 cm and no min/max/ordering — flagged in `REPORT.md` §3.1/§4.

Stage 2's B4 core sample set under the validated procedure (policy A stiff-zero starts, repetition-unique identities, per-cycle start-variant + fresh-compliance gates, experiment gate with `reset_in_window`/board coverage). **Not** proof of a production margin, **not** evidence about B1/B2 or general collision avoidance. author: smaraputra
body:
## Summary

Branch 2 of the forward-only LLM factor: the three admin routes a local panel skill posts against. Branch 1 (PR #26) added the `LlmCall` model and `SignalOutcome.source`.

- `LLM_PANEL_SECRET` bearer auth, separate from `CRON_SECRET`, through a shared constant-time `verifyBearerSecret`; `authorizeLlmPanel` accepts the bearer or an admin session (`src/lib/cron-auth.ts`, `src/app/api/admin/llm-calls/auth.ts`).
- `GET /api/admin/llm-calls/inputs?symbol=&interval=`: a point-in-time packet (last closed bar, 60 closes, the interval style's latest global signal at or before the bar, latest snapshot at or before the close, news published at or before the close) with a sha256 `inputsHash` over the body.
- `POST /api/admin/llm-calls`: validates the vote, rejects unaligned, open, or stale bars, creates the call idempotently on (symbol, interval, candleTimestamp, promptVersion), and creates one pending outcome with `source: 'llm'` so the existing resolver measures it. `GET /api/admin/llm-calls` lists newest first.

No scorer, weight, template, or `GlobalSignal` change. The factor is never backtested; its record is read with `scripts/ops/live-outcomes.ts --source llm`.

## Rollout

After merge and deploy, add `LLM_PANEL_SECRET=<random 48 chars>` to `/opt/sites/crypto/.env` on the VPS and recreate the app container (`docker compose -f docker-compose.server.yml up -d app`). The panel skill lives in `~/.claude/skills/llm-panel/` and reads `~/.claude/llm-panel.env`.

## Verification

- Unit suite: 337 files, 3600 tests green; lint, typecheck, and build clean on every commit.
- Three task reviews (Sonnet) and a whole-branch review (Opus). One Important finding fixed in `9648461`: the packet's global signal query now filters by the interval's trading style, since swing and position styles both write 1d rows on the same bar.
- E2E not run on this branch (no UI change).
- Whole-branch review fix wave in `1d043f2` (Opus findings): unset secret now logs; the packet nulls a signal or snapshot older than two intervals; news is fetched deeper and filtered to the bar close with dateless items dropped; llm outcomes carry the prompt version number in `configVersion`; house 500 handling; test hygiene; changelog corrections.

## Follow-ups (not in this PR)

- Server-side check that `candleTimestamp` exists in the candle store (the skill already posts only the packet bar).
- Paging on `GET /api/admin/llm-calls` (a `before` cursor); the 200-row cap covers about one day at the planned cadence.
- Store snapshot age and news count on the call so a later reader knows what the voter saw without the packet.

author: suwa-sh
body:
## 概要

v0.2.0 で「既知の問題」としていた 2 件の修正。マージ後に `v0.2.1` としてリリースする (バージョン表記の更新もこの PR に含む)。

## 1. CSV エクスポートが画面の絞り込みと一致しない

**原因**: バックエンドが GitLab から取り直して CSV を作っており、受け付ける条件が 4 つ (`state` / `milestone` / `service` / `quarter`) だけだった。Dashboard の期間スコープや除外ルールも反映されず、構造的に画面と一致しなかった。

**対応**: 画面に表示している issue (絞り込み・並べ替え済み) から、フロント側で CSV を作る。表示しているデータそのものを書き出すので、内容も並び順も必ず一致する。

- 列構成は従来の CSV と同じ
- テーブルのソートを共通関数 (`issueSort.ts`) に切り出し、テーブルと CSV の両方から使う
- 数式として解釈される先頭文字 (`=` `+` `-` `@`) を持つセルを無害化 (CSV インジェクション対策。issue のタイトルは GitLab の利用者が自由に書けるため)
- Point の 0 が空欄になる不具合を修正
- バックエンドの `/api/issues/export/csv` は API として残す (画面からは使わなくなった。0 が空欄になる不具合だけ同様に修正)

## 2. テストデータが今四半期で 0 件になる

**原因**: `generate_gitlab_test_data.py` のデータは README のスコープ判定例 (Issue A〜J) で、2024-01-01〜03-31 に固定。README の手順どおりに実行しても、今四半期の Dashboard には何も出なかった。

**対応**: 固定の仕様例は README と対応しているのでそのまま残し、実行日の四半期に合わせたサンプル issue 16 件を追加で生成する。

- 完了日は「四半期の開始日〜実行日」に均等に割り振り、未来の日付は作らない
- 実行日の四半期のラベル (`@FYxxQx`) は自動で作成する

## 検証

- [x] `make check` が exit 0 (frontend 31 件 / backend 45 件。CSV・ソートで 11 件、テストデータで 15 件追加)
- [x] ローカル GitLab (gitlab-ce 17.9.2) + `docker-compose.local.yml` の一式で確認
  - README の手順どおりにスクリプトを実行 → 28 件作成 (失敗なし)、今四半期の Dashboard に 16 件表示
  - 画面のテーブルと、ダウンロードした CSV のタイトル列を突き合わせて一致を確認

| パターン | 画面 | CSV |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Dashboard / 今四半期 / フィルタなし | 16 件 | 16 件 |
| Dashboard / service=backend / Point 昇順 | 5 件 | 5 件 (backend のみ、3→13 の昇順) |
| PBL / フィルタなし | 26 件 | 26 件 |
| PBL / quarter=FY23Q4 (従来は CSV に反映されなかった条件) | 9 件 | 9 件 (FY23Q4 のみ) |

## 挙動が変わる点

- CSV のダウンロードが GitLab への問い合わせなしで即座に終わる
- `=` `+` `-` `@` で始まるセルは、先頭に `'` が付く
- 文字コードと BOM は従来どおり (UTF-8、BOM なし)

body:
Closes #4294

`reject-bad-closing-references` is correct and this PR does not loosen it. What was missing is
that authors keep writing the shape and nothing warns them before CI does — and the advice that
was available named the wrong property.

## The issue's framing does not reproduce

The issue is filed as a **tense** problem and proposes a vocabulary remedy (*settled*, *subsumed*,
*superseded*). Its own first row does not fire:

| clause from the issue | measured verdict |
|---|---|
| `#3153 closed via #4153` (PR 4283's row) | **exit 0 — clean**, through both the shell gate and `tools/pr-body.py`'s port |
| the issue's second row, `#4253 closed` followed immediately by a second number (PR 4291's row) | exit 1 — fires on that second number |

So I re-measured the class instead of implementing the stated remedy. **The discriminator is not
the tense. It is whether a WORD separates the keyword from the number**, because `SEP` matches at
most one punctuation mark and cannot span a word:

| clause | verdict |
|---|---|
| `closed #<N>` | fires |
| `closed: #<N>` | fires (colon — pinned since the incident that shut 2942 for real) |
| a number, a dash, `closed`, a comma, then a SECOND number | **fires on the second number**, not the first |
| `closed via #<N>` | clean |
| `closed by #<N>` | clean |
| `fixed in #<N>` | clean |
| a number, then `(closed)` in parentheses, then another number | clean |

That is a better instruction than a vocabulary list: the author keeps the verb they wanted and
adds a preposition. It is what the gate's message now prints.

## The sub-shape nobody had named: the comma reaches forward

A row of the form *number, dash, `closed`, comma, second number* acts on the **second** number.
The author is tabulating states, the word belongs to the first, and the comma hands the keyword
forward. Every instrument reports this
correctly; none of them said the reported number was not the one the sentence was about. The old
message named a number with no hint of that.

Note which separator it is: colon and semicolon were both pinned after the earlier incident; the
**comma**, in the same `[,;:]` class, had **no case at all**. A table row is what produces it.

## A second hole, in the other direction, found by the same sweep — filed, not fixed here

A line whose **entire** content is a keyword plus a number matches `CANONICAL_LINE_RE` wherever it
sits, **including inside a fenced block**, so it is read as a *declaration*: the gate prints
`declared target(s): ...` and exits **0**. The issue acts on merge with no error for anyone to
read. `tools/pr-body.py`'s port behaves identically, so this is not a parity break.

It is narrow — a bullet, a blockquote marker, a table pipe or any other text on the line breaks the
canonical match and the stray check sees it again. **Not fixed here**: a fence-aware parser has its
own false-positive surface and is a different question from this issue's. Both edges are pinned,
and the hole itself is pinned at what the script does **today**, so a follow-up has a starting point
and any change to it is deliberate. **Filed as #4393** and put on the ready queue; the test block and
the incidents section both cite it.

## What changed

- **`check_closing_reference.sh`** — the stray message. It said *"written inline in a sentence"*,
  which a table-row author scans past, and offered only `see #<N>`, which loses the meaning when the
  sentence is about what *happened* to an issue. It now names the preposition rewrite, says markdown
  is not protection, says a past-tense mention fires identically, and tells the author to read the
  reported number because a comma reaches forward. One line changed.
- **`.claude/rules/branch-and-pr.md`** — the shape beside the existing negation traps, claim +
  citation + trap per `CLAUDE.md` § "How a rule is written", plus the pre-publish recipe, which is
  the only thing that catches this locally. Measured while writing it: a body whose only content is a
  canonical trailer naming some *other* issue, on branch `agent/x/issue-4294`, exits 0 with
  `PR_HEAD_REF` unset and 1 with it set — so the recipe passes the variable.
- **`docs/incidents/branch-and-pr.md`** — the derivation, the measurement table and the second hole.
- **`test_check_closing_reference.sh`** — 14 table-driven arms over the whole separator class, from
  both sides.

## Scope, and why this one

Three candidates were on offer. I took the message **and** the rule prose, because they fail
differently: the rule is what an author reads *before* writing, the message is the only thing they
read *at the moment of failure*, and neither substitutes for the other. I did not touch detection —
the gate is right, and every escape it could offer would have to model tense.

## Mutations

Table-driven arms need a per-property mutation, not one red. Four, each a **value** edit applied
with `tools/apply-mutation.py` (`apply rc=0` every time), judged with `tools/mutation-verdict.py
--exit`. Baseline after the tests and before the message fix: `95 passed, 1 failed`. After:
`96 passed, 0 failed`.

| # | target | edit | result | what it establishes |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| M1 | `SEP` | `[[:space:]]*[,;:]?[[:space:]]*` → `[[:space:]]+` (the pre-fix form: stuck **shut**) | `84 passed, 12 failed` | the fires-side arms are load-bearing; **every clean-side arm stayed green** |
| M2 | `SEP` | widened to span one word (stuck **open**) | `93 passed, 3 failed` | red set is **exactly the three clean-side arms** — disjoint from M1 |
| M3 | the message | `'closed via #$stray_number'` → `'see #$stray_number'` | `95 passed, 1 failed` | the message arm is pinned to the recommendation, not to the message existing |
| M4 | `KEYWORDS` | dropped `closed` only | `90 passed, 6 failed` | reds **exactly** the five past-tense arms plus the message arm, leaving the present-tense comma arm green — each arm is pinned to its own keyword |

M1 and M2 are the two opposite mutations the brief asks for and their red sets are **disjoint**,
which rules out stuck-open and stuck-shut together. M2 is the **green control**: without those three
arms, a widening that ate the very rewrite the new message recommends would ship green. The
pre-existing arm `a keyword separated from the reference by prose still passes` does **not** cover
this — it puts three words between keyword and number, so it only detects a three-word widening,
while the realistic mistake is one word.

All four re-applied cleanly after the review repairs below (`apply rc=0`, same red counts), so no
anchor went stale.

## Fix the shape, not just the reported line

1. **Same wrong pattern at another call site?** Yes — `tools/pr-body.py` carries a port of this
   logic. I measured every case above through both and they agree everywhere, including on the
   fenced hole, so parity holds and no second edit is needed. `tools/test_pr_body.py` (which
   includes the shell/python parity suite) passes.
2. **Sibling function with the same assumption?** `part_of_references.sh` shares the `SEP` shape.
   It is unaffected: `Part of` carries no closing keyword, so a separator question there cannot act
   on an issue. Its tests pass.
3. **Two paths writing the same state with different invariants?** Yes, and this is the finding
   above — `CANONICAL_LINE_RE` (declaration) and `STRAY_MATCH_RE` (stray) both decide what a line
   means, and a bare clause on a fenced line satisfies the first. Filed rather than folded.

## Queue scan

By file (`batch-sibling-issues-by-file.md`): nothing else open lands in
`check_closing_reference.sh`. **4293 is adjacent and deliberately not folded** — the coordinator
recorded why on 4294, and I agree: it is the gate *failing to fire* on a scope mismatch, the
opposite direction, with a remedy in a different script. Its PR 4391 touches
`.claude/rules/branch-and-pr.md` and `docs/incidents/branch-and-pr.md`, so I placed my rule bullet
in the "Three traps" section, which 4391 does not touch, and appended my incid

author: teknium1
body:
`hermes usage [--provider NAME] [--json]` prints the account-limits block of the `/usage` slash command — Codex 5h/weekly windows, plan, banked resets (and Anthropic / OpenRouter limits) — from any shell without starting a session, so cron jobs and scripts can read quota state.

- New `hermes_cli/subcommands/usage.py` (`cmd_usage`, `build_usage_parser`), registered in `hermes_cli/main.py` next to `insights` (+ `_BUILTIN_SUBCOMMANDS` / session-name coalescing set).
- Same data, same renderer as the REPL and gateway `/usage`: `agent.account_usage.fetch_account_usage` → `render_account_usage_lines`. No duplicated formatting.
- Credential resolution is exactly what `/usage` does in a session with no live agent (auth store, then credential pool); the command never adds, adopts or refreshes a credential it would not use for chat.
- `--json`: one document on stdout with a stable, documented schema — `provider`, `source`, `title`, `plan`, `fetched_at`, `windows[{label, used_percent, resets_at, detail}]`, `details[]`, `unavailable_reason`. Derived from the snapshot fields (does not depend on `AccountUsageSnapshot.raw`, which is not on main).
- Exit `0` on success; `1` with a single stderr line (stdout empty) when no credential is configured, the provider has no usage endpoint, or the fetch fails.
- Docs: `website/docs/reference/cli-commands.md` — command table row + `## hermes usage` section with the JSON schema example.
- 2 invariant tests (`tests/hermes_cli/test_usage_command.py`) drive the real `hermes_cli.main.main()` entrypoint: JSON schema keys/values; missing-credential exit code + one stderr line. Both red on `origin/main` (`'usage'` is not a command), green on this branch; `test_startup_plugin_gating.py` and `tests/cron/test_estop.py` (subcommand-set invariants) still pass — 31 passed.

**Live repro** (real CLI entrypoint, temp `HERMES_HOME` with a fixture Codex credential, `HERMES_CODEX_BASE_URL` pointed at a local fake server replaying a `/usage`-shaped payload; no real credential touched):

| | `hermes usage --json` |
|---|---|
| before (`origin/main` 8df0a03) | exit 2 — `hermes: 'usage' is not a hermes command. Did you mean: pause?` |
| after | exit 0 — JSON document: `provider: openai-codex`, `plan: Plus`, `windows: [Session 37.0% → 2026-09-19T21:00:00+00:00, Weekly 12.5% → 2026-09-25T09:00:00+00:00]`, `details: ["You have 1 reset banked …"]`; fake server saw exactly one `GET /api/codex/usage` with the fixture bearer + `ChatGPT-Account-Id` |
| after, human | `📈 Account limits / Provider: openai-codex (Plus) / Session: 63% remaining (37% used) • resets in 13h 1m … / Weekly: 88% remaining (12% used) • …` — byte-identical to the `/usage` block |
| control: empty `HERMES_HOME` | exit 1, one stderr line, stdout empty, zero requests to the server (no adoption/refresh attempted) |

Root cause: the Codex quota fetch only had interactive callers (`cli_info_mixin._show_usage`, `gateway/slash_commands_status._handle_usage_command`); there was no top-level `usage` subparser.

Fixes #33094
Related: #57476 (its `hermes status --all` / gateway `/status` usage rows are a separate atom; the gateway `/usage` command already covers its `/codex-usage` ask)
Salvages #81819 (@himanusia) — slim redo with `Co-authored-by`; `Supersedes #33998` (@Padanerd) — see below.

## Dropped hunks
- #81819 `--all` / `--account LABEL`: per-entry rendering passed the pool token as an explicit `api_key`, which the anthropic fetcher ignores (every banner showed the same account) and which bypassed the runtime resolver for the codex default path (showed the pool head, not the credential chat uses). Dropped; the default path here goes through the resolver.
- #81819 `--reset` / `--force`: banked-reset redemption from a script spends a credit non-interactively — left to `/usage reset` (interactive) pending a maintainer call.
- #81819 `hermes auth usage <provider>` placement: this lands as top-level `hermes usage` per the issue's "script-friendly command" ask; the 1,566-line diff (20 tests) was rebuilt at 185 lines.
- #33998 `/codex-usage` slash command (`cli.py`, `gateway/run.py`, `gateway/slash_commands.py`): superseded — the interactive `/usage` command already renders the Codex windows on CLI, TUI/Desktop and gateway (and #115766 fixes its remaining gaps). Nothing to port.

author: xurunxin
body:
## Problem

Fixes GEN-550.

`apply_project_import` hashed the caller's plan verbatim, while `prepare_project_import` hashed a fully **normalized** plan. The two hashes therefore diverged whenever the replayed plan was any schema-valid spelling other than byte-identical to prepare's output — array order, field casing, surrounding whitespace, duplicate labels.

Because the documented replay path ("pass its contentHash and plan together without modification") is always byte-identical, every existing test, dry run and manual check stayed green. The defect only surfaced for callers that re-serialized an equivalent plan, which is why it presented as "the same plan and the same hash keep failing".

## Root cause

`apps/mcp/src/coordination-product.ts`:

- `prepareProjectImport` trims every field, upper-cases `teamRef`, sorts milestones/workItems/relations by `sourceId`, de-duplicates and sorts labels, then `planHash(normalizedPlan)`.
- `applyProjectImport` called `planHash(input.plan)` directly — **no normalization**.

Two corrections to the original report, both verified:

1. `expectedContentHash` is **not** per-request. Repeated calls with the same plan return a stable value; the four differing hashes in the report came from four different plan spellings.
2. The prepare side is **not** untrustworthy. It is deterministic; only the apply side was wrong.

## Change

- Extract a single `normalizeProjectImportPlan()`; prepare and apply now both funnel through it, so the hash always fingerprints the normalized plan. Normalization is idempotent, so replaying a verbatim prepare response is unaffected.
- Apply now persists values from the normalized plan rather than the caller's spelling.
- Replace `localeCompare` with code-unit comparison in every ordering that feeds the hash. `localeCompare` is ICU/locale dependent, so hashes could differ across processes, regions or images.

## Verification

Reproduced live before the fix (bogus `teamRef` keeps the call side-effect free):

| call | supplied | expected |
|---|---|---|
| `prepare(teamRef: "  wm  ")` | — | `sha256:21386f…` |
| `apply(plan.teamRef: "wm")` | `sha256:21386f…` | `sha256:60cb2bc5…` ❌ |

- **The regression test was verified to fail before the fix** and pass after. The first draft passed on unfixed code because it exercised the verbatim-replay path, which was never broken — it was rewritten to send a schema-valid but unnormalized plan.
- `pnpm lint` 17/17 · `pnpm typecheck` 17/17 · `pnpm test` 28 tasks green (MCP 38 tests) · `pnpm ci:validate` · `pnpm check:route-policy` · `pnpm check:workmesh-skill` · `@workmesh/contracts test` 152 tests · MCP build.

## Known limitations

- `pnpm build` fails locally at `@workmesh/web` with a module-resolution error pointing at `G:/Projects/MetronX/.wm-virtual-store/...`. That path comes from an **untracked** local `.npmrc` (excluded via `.git/info/exclude`) used to work around pnpm-on-ReFS failures; it cannot reach CI, which uses the default `node_modules/.pnpm`. This PR touches neither `apps/web` nor any tracked config. All other 16 build tasks pass.
- `test:integration` / `test:e2e` were not run locally (no Postgres / integration env). CI covers both.

## Spec divergence

None. No API, event or schema change: the hash algorithm for canonical input is unchanged, so existing idempotency keys and replay behaviour are preserved.

author: alenizy361
body:
## Overview
- I ran an experiment to run a 27B model (from the hybrid Qwen3.5 series) on a laptop that has no GPU and uses single-channel RAM.
- While running concurrent sequences, perf showed that about 27% of the step time is wasted in get_rows and cpy operations for the GDN layer states, even though the state is already in place.
- I added an in-place state update inside the cache, applied only when all sequences read their own cells; otherwise the previous path is used, with an environment variable to go back to the old behavior for comparison. I also made the zeroing of the state memory lazy via mmap instead of memset, so inactive cells do not consume RAM.
- Results on my machine (using the AVX2 kernels from the PrismML fork): for 16 sequences the speed went from 9.5 to 13.5 tokens/s, for 8 sequences from 10.1 to 13.3 tokens/s, and RAM usage for 16 slots with speculative decoding dropped from 12.8 to 8.4 GB.

## Additional information
- This change resolves #28841 (the single-sequence case) and handles any number of sequences.
- Verification: a byte-for-byte unit test passes for 48 cases; perplexity is exactly identical with or without the change (even at ub=32); and the md5 of greedy generation matches exactly.
- Fork version: PrismML-Eng/llama.cpp#207. The new path is for CPU only; the old path is kept when n_rs_seq > 0.
- Note: I wrote this description in Arabic and translated it to English.

## Requirements
- I have read and agree with the [contributing guidelines](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- AI usage disclosure: YES — the code was written by Claude Code under my supervision; I defined the problem and the goal, ran the tests and measurements on my computer, and reviewed the results.

author: slim3joker
body:
## Was

Bindet den Scarlett-MCP-Server (`https://api.scarlett.ai/mcp`) in Claude Code ein – als Projekt-Konfiguration im Repo, ohne dass der API-Key im Repo landet.

## Änderungen

- **`.mcp.json`** (neu): HTTP-MCP-Server `scarlett` im Projekt-Scope. Der Bearer-Token kommt aus `${SCARLETT_API_TOKEN}` und wird von Claude Code beim Start aus der Umgebung eingesetzt.
- **README**: Neuer Abschnitt „Scarlett-MCP-Anbindung (Claude Code)“ – Key als Umgebungsvariable hinterlegen, Variante A (Projekt-Scope über `.mcp.json`) und Variante B (User-Scope via `claude mcp add-json --scope user …`), Prüfung per `/mcp` bzw. `claude mcp get scarlett`, Fehlersuche-Tabelle.
- **`CLAUDE.md`** (neu): Kurze Hinweise für Claude-Code-Sitzungen (Server ist vorhanden, Key nie ins Repo, nicht doppelt anlegen).
- **`.gitignore`** (neu): `.env*` und `.claude/settings.local.json` ausgeschlossen, damit ein lokal abgelegter Key nicht versehentlich committet wird.

Dashboard (`index.html`) und Datenschema sind unverändert – die Scarlett-Anbindung ist unabhängig von der Amazon-MCP-Roadmap im README.

## Geprüft

- `.mcp.json` mit `claude mcp get scarlett` (Claude Code 2.1.278) eingelesen: Server wird als Projekt-Config erkannt (Typ http, URL, Header mit Platzhalter), Status „Pending approval“ bis zur einmaligen Freigabe.
- Eine Live-Verbindung zu api.scarlett.ai konnte in der Sandbox nicht getestet werden (Domain vom Egress-Proxy blockiert, kein Key vorhanden) – bitte lokal mit gesetztem `SCARLETT_API_TOKEN` per `/mcp` prüfen.

## Einrichtung nach dem Merge

```bash
export SCARLETT_API_TOKEN='YOUR_SCARLETT_API_KEY'   # dauerhaft in ~/.zshrc bzw. ~/.bashrc
claude                                              # Freigabe für .mcp.json bestätigen, dann /mcp
```

author: kooshapari
body:
## **User description** ## Problem The `Security Scan` check (ci.yml, job `security`) has been red on every recent PR and on `main`. It fails before gitleaks ever scans anything: ``` gitleaks cmd: gitleaks detect --redact -v --exit-code=2 ... --log-opts=--no-merges --first-parent ^.. ERR [git] fatal: ambiguous argument '^..': unknown revision or path not in the working tree. ERR failed to scan Git repository error="stderr is not empty" [ERROR] ERROR: Unexpected exit code [1] ``` ## Root cause `gitleaks-action` derives its scan range as `^..`, which requires the **parent commit object** to be present in the clone. The `security` job's `actions/checkout@v4` had no `fetch-depth`, so it defaulted to `1` — only the tip commit exists, `HEAD^` cannot be resolved, and git aborts. ## Reproduction (not inferred — run locally) | Clone | Command | Result | |---|---|---| | `--depth 1` | `git log -p -U0 --no-merges --first-parent HEAD^..HEAD` | `rc=128`, `fatal: ambiguous argument 'HEAD^..HEAD': unknown revision or path not in the working tree.` | | full | `git log --no-merges --first-parent de144fe^..de144fe` | `rc=0`, scans normally | The shallow-clone stderr is character-for-character the CI error. ## Fix ```diff security: name: Security Scan runs-on: ubuntu-latest continue-on-error: true steps: - uses: actions/checkout@v4 + with: + # gitleaks-action derives its range as '^..'; with the + # default fetch-depth of 1 the parent object is absent and git + # aborts with "ambiguous argument ... unknown revision". + fetch-depth: 0 - name: gitleaks uses: gitleaks/gitleaks-action@v3 ``` The sibling `gitleaks.yml` workflow already pins `fetch-depth: 0`; this simply brings the `security` job in `ci.yml` in line with it. 1 file, +5 lines, no behavioural change other than gitleaks now being able to resolve its range. ## Out of scope (worth a follow-up) The `lint` aggregate job reads `needs.dependency-review.result`, but the actual job id is `dep-review` (its display name is "Dependency Review"). The expression resolves to empty, so the loop falls through to the `?` branch and a failing Dependency Review can never fail the gate. Left untouched here to keep this diff to a single concern. ## Verification - Reproduction above proves the mechanism and that full history resolves it. - `x`/`y` in the diff is the only change; `git diff --stat` = `1 file changed, 5 insertions(+)`. - CI on this PR should show `Security Scan` green (previously red on `main` and on PRs #257/#258/#259). ## Related - PR #259 (`fix/testing-library-react-19`) — the Node 20 → 22 + LF + testing-library work; its PR body documents this `Security Scan` failure as pre-existing. This PR is the fix for it. Signed-off-by: KooshaPari ___ ## **CodeAnt-AI Description** Restore security scanning for pull requests and main-branch changes ### What Changed - The security scan now checks out the full Git history so it can resolve the commit range required by the scan - Gitleaks can run instead of stopping with an unknown revision error ### Impact `✅ Fewer skipped security scans` `✅ Reliable secret detection in CI`
💡 Usage Guide ### Checking Your Pull Request Every time you make a pull request, our system automatically looks through it. We check for security issues, mistakes in how you're setting up your infrastructure, and common code problems. We do this to make sure your changes are solid and won't cause any trouble later. ### Talking to CodeAnt AI Got a question or need a hand with something in your pull request? You can easily get in touch with CodeAnt AI right here. Just type the following in a comment on your pull request, and replace "Your question here" with whatever you want to ask: 
@codeant-ai ask: Your question here
This lets you have a chat with CodeAnt AI about your pull request, making it easier to understand and improve your code. #### Example 
@codeant-ai ask: Can you suggest a safer alternative to storing this secret?
### Preserve Org Learnings with CodeAnt You can record team preferences so CodeAnt AI applies them in future reviews. Reply directly to the specific CodeAnt AI suggestion (in the same thread) and replace "Your feedback here" with your input: 
@codeant-ai: Your feedback here
This helps CodeAnt AI learn and adapt to your team's coding style and standards. #### Example 
@codeant-ai: Do not flag unused imports.
### Retrigger review Ask CodeAnt AI to review the PR again, by typing: 
@codeant-ai: review

This tool helps you identify potential issues and areas for improvement in your codebase, ensuring your repository maintains high standards of code health.

author: fmsmith91
body:
A full-repo security review, fanned out across seven attack surfaces. **Seven findings are fixed here**; the rest are reported separately with file:line locations.

Every fix is pinned by a gate that was **verified to fail when the fix is reverted**.

## The headline

`install_root_tools` copied three files out of the working tree and installed them root-owned — the helper the sudoers rule names, `db_maintenance.py`, and `install.sh` itself. The integrity argument was that `fetch_code` had just run `git reset --hard`.

That is not a guarantee. Both bypasses confirmed by execution against a scratch repo on git 2.55:

| bypass | effect |
|---|---|
| `git update-index --skip-worktree <path>` | exempt from `reset --hard`; attacker content survives, **and so does a deletion** |
| smudge filter in `.git/info/attributes` | the file is rewritten *during* checkout |

Both live in `.git/` — untracked, panel-owned — and `_gitc` runs git **as the checkout owner**. `check_origin_trusted` compares the remote URL and sees neither.

The deletion variant is sharper: a missing `tools/panel-helper` zeroed `HELPER_OK`, and `write_sudoers_grant` replaced the narrow rule with `NOPASSWD:ALL`. **The panel user could remove its own sudo restriction by deleting a file it owned.**

Fixed by staging with `git cat-file blob HEAD:<path>` — committed bytes, consulting neither working tree, index, nor filters — into the root-owned `HELPER_DIR`. The grant now asks whether the helper actually exists root-owned, so a failed refresh cannot widen a narrow grant.

## Also fixed

- **Root `rm -rf` of the panel's own home.** `useradd --system` gives the panel's account a uid below 1000 but not 0, so the uid-0 test let it through. A game server named `lgsmpanel` ran `userdel -r` and `rm -rf -- /home/lgsmpanel` as root — over `panel.db`, both encryption keys, the config and every backup. Unrecoverable: the backups live inside the tree being removed. `MANAGE_SERVERS` sufficed.
- **`run_command` deadlock.** It called `recv_exit_status()` *before* reading — `status_event.wait()`, no timeout — and a command cannot exit while blocked on a full 2 MiB window. Any command printing more hung the greenthread permanently (the 14-day `journalctl`, fail2ban's log grep, a long update's `cat`). Both streams drained while the command runs, 8 MiB cap that discards rather than stops. Reproduced against a fake channel: old ordering hangs, new does not, console reads unchanged.
- **`_rewrite_crontab` built `sudo bash -c` by interpolation with `sudo=False`** — the shape `SECURITY.md` says is gone, invisible to all three ratchets — with the account name **unquoted** into a root pipeline.
- **`ssh_test_connection` accepted any host key**, while three of its four callers pass an existing remote's stored credential (including `_wait_for_reboot`, retrying ten minutes while the host is expected down). A password remote with an undecryptable credential also fell through to key auth with the panel user's own `~/.ssh/id_rsa`.
- **`read_file` reported a failed read as an empty file**; Save then wrote that over the real config.
- **API tokens answered to no revocation the panel offers** — not a password change, not "sign out everywhere".

## `SECURITY.md` corrections

Three falsified claims corrected: that root executes nothing out of the checkout; that the `_sudo_sh` route "cannot come back by accident"; and that the remaining `sudo=True` sites are reads with values validated upstream (the metrics probe no longer escalates — the real fourth site is `install_game_dependencies`, an `apt-get install` as root whose package list is parsed unvalidated from a panel-writable cache file).

## One agent finding I disproved

An agent reported that deactivating an account leaves its sessions working. **It does not.** `UserMixin.is_authenticated` returns `self.is_active`, which the model overrides with a DB column, so `@login_required` already refuses — verified by running it. The `load_user` check here is defence-in-depth for a load-bearing coincidence between a mixin property and a column name, and the comment says so rather than claiming a fix.

## Verification

Nine suites green: unit 1915/1915, smoke 786/786, rbac 92/92, input-validation 143/143, url-map, template-actions 102/102, setup-wizard 41/41, manage 21/21, perf-budget 5/5.

Mutation-verified: each fix reverted in turn, confirming its gate fails **by name**. One gate that crashed rather than failed was rewritten to fail cleanly; one that passed with the fix removed was rewritten to cover the branch it had been missing.

> **This changes the installer's root path.** Worth a read before merge.

body:
Resolves #16 — the prototype ticket — as an integration ADR (no new spike, as ADR-0011 was): every contract it pins is owned by an accepted ADR, every number cited or labelled a model.

**`docs/decisions/0015-dashboard.md`** — annotated page-shell wireframe (§1.0), per-panel wireframes + JSON data contracts (§1.1–§1.3, §2, §3.3), component tree (§5.4), theme tokens (§5.6), rules R112–R117, seven reopen triggers, nine steelmanned-and-rejected alternatives.

The ticket's five questions, answered:

1. **Panel inventory** — six panels: P1 money (margin earned vs cost = the ADR-0002 reward, decomposed, one money axis; latency as a hover-locked strip with the deadline reference line — the answer to "three y-axes or normalised overlay?" is *neither*, on three independent grounds), P2 policy regret vs oracle (**sim-only by construction**; cumulative line primary, per-arm missed-opportunity stack exact via `all_arms` recording; live runs get a stated-unavailable card, never a winner-biased proxy), P3 counterfactual, P4 processor health (traffic light pinned to ADR-0007's Tier-1/Tier-2), P5 rollout (ADR-0013's payload, verbatim — it names #16), P6 engine/store health (ADR-0012's named metrics).
2. **Processor health** — one tile per acquirer: light + tier + `since`, trailing auth rate + n, p99 vs deadline, volume share, auth-rate sparkline. Data contract in §2.
3. **Data contract** — the engine's `/v1` stays routing + outcomes (zero new surface on the hot binary). The dashboard talks to a FastAPI sidecar in `analysis/` owning exactly the two read classes R94 permits: long reads over sealed Parquet, short bounded tail reads of today. Cadence: batch (seal-time aggregates + seal-time π₀ grid) + 60-s polling with server `next_poll_after` + on-demand async jobs; **no WebSocket** (the data has no stream; the header shows the tail lag instead of a fake "live" badge). The tail read is sized (~0.5% duty, model on measured rates) and made falsifiable (Reopen trigger 2).
4. **Counterfactual UX** — two-tier: slider scrubbing reads the seal-time π₀ grid (ADR-0014 already builds it: "a pane refresh is a sum") → full answer contract in <1 s; off-grid ρ / custom windows → async job (202 + polls; measured cost class 43–408 s) with progress, ETA, serial queue, non-blocking page. Targets: grid ≤ 300 ms p95 (labelled requirement), exact ≤ 60 s p50 (measured class 43–49 s), ≤ 10 min worst (measured ~408 s). Uninformative states: REFUSED renders the pinned refusal copy with N and no number; CI width > |Δ| renders the low-informativeness badge with `head_rows`/ESS/Ē[w̃] promoted to the number's type size; FAIL renders admissibility reasons. Standing law (R114): no point without its verdict; the ADR-0014 answer contract renders whole.
5. **Tech** — React 18 + Vite static SPA served by the sidecar; Recharts (chosen on contract surface — `syncId` hover-lock, `ComposedChart` bands; ≤ 1,440 points per chart makes the performance argument moot); TanStack Query for server state, plain React state otherwise; no Next.js (the API is Python by law), no Zustand in v1 (named reopen trigger), no hand-rolled D3.

Also: README "Decided so far" + ADR index updated; the missing ADR-0014 README entry was added in passing.

## Summary
- Adds `src/app.py`, the Task 11 CLI entry point wiring together all of Tasks 1-10 (data/feature/train/caption/narrative/eval/tts/report services + meerax LLM providers) behind `--mode {train,caption}`.
- Adds `tests/unit/test_app.py` per the task-11 brief (verbatim, Step 1).

## Deviations from the brief (both flagged as risks by the controller, both verified before merging in)

1. **meerax LLM import paths** — verified against the installed `meerax==1.10.3` package:
   - `from meerax.llm.claude import ClaudeProvider` — correct as written.
   - `from meerax.llm.ollama import OllamaProvider` — correct as written.
   - `from meerax.llm.openai_provider import OpenAIProvider` — correct as written.
   No corrections needed; used verbatim.

2. **`main([])` vs `SystemExit` conflict between the brief's own tests** — `test_missing_mode_errors_cleanly` calls `main([])` directly (no `pytest.raises`) and expects an int != 0, but the brief's argparse setup (`required=True` on `--mode`) makes `parser.parse_args()` itself call `parser.error()` → `sys.exit(2)` on a missing `--mode`, which raises `SystemExit` straight out of `main()`. Meanwhile `test_caption_mode_requires_image_path` explicitly expects `SystemExit` to propagate from the brief's own later manual `parser.error("--image is required when --mode caption")` call.
   Resolution: wrapped only the `parser.parse_args(argv)` call in `try/except SystemExit as exc: return exc.code if isinstance(exc.code, int) else 2`, converting a missing-required-arg failure into a plain int return. The later, explicit `parser.error(...)` call for a missing `--image` in caption mode is left unwrapped, so it still raises `SystemExit` uncaught. Verified both tests pass under this split, along with the third given test.

author: jgyy
body:
## Summary Player report (Discord, "Dash (druid spell) gives wrong amount of speed"): Dash and Loping Stride SET the movement speed instead of increasing it. In Cat Form (a 15% passive) Dash produced a flat 150% run speed, not the 172.5% its "+50%" tooltip promises, and the Loping Stride shift sprint produced a flat 160% instead of 184%. Root cause: `moveSpeedMult` (`src/sim/player_motion.ts`) folded the Cat Form passive (`CAT_FORM_MOVE_MULT`) into the same `Math.max` as the temporary speed buffs, so any sprint replaced the form bonus instead of riding on top of it. The mobility design doc had recorded that as intended, but it contradicts every Cat-only sprint tooltip and the classic-era rule (a form's passive speed stacks with the one strongest temporary sprint). The fix keeps the form passive as its own layer that multiplies the strongest temporary buff. Temporary buffs (Dash, Loping Stride, Fleet Form, Enrage) still follow the classic rule among themselves: the strongest applies, they never stack with each other. | Situation | Before | After | |---|---|---| | Cat Form alone | 115% | 115% (unchanged) | | Cat Form + Dash | 150% | 172.5% | | Cat Form + Loping Stride (shift sprint) | 160% | 184% | | Cat Form + Loping Stride + Dash | 160% | 184% for the stride, then 172.5% | | Fleet Form, Bruin Form + Loping Stride | 140%, 160% | unchanged (no Cat passive) | | Any slow on top | multiplicative | multiplicative (unchanged) | The report's third expectation (Dash and Loping Stride multiplying each other for 192%) is deliberately not adopted: temporary sprints never stack with each other in the classic model, and the fix is scoped to the form passive that the tooltips describe as separate. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[auras] --> B{temporary speed buffs
buff_speed, form_travel,
form_fireball, enrage} B -->|Math.max, never stack| S[strongest sprint] A --> C{form_cat} C -->|CAT_FORM_MOVE_MULT| P[form passive 1.15] S --> M[speed = strongest x passive] P --> M M --> N[+ mount pct, + Fiesta pct] N --> O[x slow / stealth] O --> R[moveSpeedMult] style M fill:#2b5,color:#000 ``` Because `moveSpeedMult` is the one pure function shared by the offline `Sim`, the server, and the online client extrapolator, all three hosts change in lockstep with this single edit. ## Type of change - [x] Bug fix - [x] Documentation (`docs/design/druid-cat-mobility.md` corrected to the layered rule) - [x] Tests ## How was this tested? - Commands: - `npx vitest run tests/druid_form_speed_stack.test.ts` (new; the four stacking cases fail on the base branch for exactly the reported values and pass with the fix) - `npx vitest run tests/druid_spell_pack.test.ts tests/druid_wildfang_kit.test.ts tests/druid_engines.test.ts tests/architecture.test.ts tests/localization_fixes.test.ts tests/parity` - `npx tsc --noEmit`, scoped biome on the changed files - `node scripts/gate_select.mjs` - Manual steps: `scripts/dash_speed_shot.mjs` (new capture rig) boots the offline client as a level 20 druid, shifts to Cat Form, lets Loping Stride expire, casts Dash, then holds the real forward key for 60 sim ticks on a lane the sim's own `resolveMove` confirmed clear. It stamps the measured yards on the frame. Base branch: 32.0 yd in 3 s (150%). Fix: 36.2 yd in 3 s (172%). Same reading on the mobile landscape viewport. ## Screenshots / recordings Desktop, before (150% of run speed) and after (172%): ![before desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jgyy/world-of-claudecraft/fix/dash-speed-stacks/docs/screenshots/dash-speed-stack/before-desktop.png) ![after desktop](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jgyy/world-of-claudecraft/fix/dash-speed-stacks/docs/screenshots/dash-speed-stack/after-desktop.png) Mobile landscape, before and after: ![before mobile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jgyy/world-of-claudecraft/fix/dash-speed-stacks/docs/screenshots/dash-speed-stack/before-mobile.png) ![after mobile](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jgyy/world-of-claudecraft/fix/dash-speed-stacks/docs/screenshots/dash-speed-stack/after-mobile.png) --- ## Checklist ### Quality - [x] **The gate passes.** `node scripts/gate_select.mjs` is green. Decisive tests added for the changed behavior. ### Cross-platform - [x] **Tested on desktop and mobile.** The rig captures both viewports; no UI layout is touched. - [x] ~Accessible~ N/A, no UI change. ### Localization (i18n) - [x] N/A. This PR adds no player-visible strings (the existing Dash, Cat Form and Loping Stride tooltips already describe the stacked values). ### Hygiene - [x] No secrets, credentials, or `.env` committed, and `ALLOW_DEV_COMMANDS` is not enabled in any production path. - [x] I didn't hand-edit generated files. 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

author: eddeee888
body:
## Description

`dev-test/graphql-config`'s `generate:cjs:multi` and `generate:esm:multi` scripts intentionally run the CLI against `multi/.graphqlrc.yml`'s `default` project, which has no `extensions.codegen` block — the CLI is expected to exit `1`. The scripts swallowed that expected failure with `|| [ $? -eq 1 ]`.

That's POSIX shell syntax. `pnpm run` invokes `package.json` scripts through its own script-shell resolution — `cmd.exe` on Windows, regardless of what shell the *outer* CI step uses (`shell: bash`, added in #10957, only governs that step's own `run:` block, not pnpm's internal script invocation). `cmd.exe` never expands `$?`, so the check broke there: `[: invalid integer '$?'`, always failing the script.

This is "finding 3" from #10957: an unrelated, pre-existing gap that blocks the new `windows-latest` `dev-tests` CI leg from ever going green, independent of any `codegen.ts` fix (confirmed live on #10956/#10957's CI — see linked comments below).

This PR replaces the shell idiom with a small Node helper (`assert-exit-code.mjs`) that spawns the command directly via `child_process.spawnSync` and inspects its exit code in JS, sidestepping shell portability entirely — matching the repo's existing convention of small standalone Node scripts for CI-portability concerns (`scripts/fix-bin.js`, `scripts/match-graphql.js`).

Related # (issue): none filed — this is the follow-up called out in #10957's "Further comments" section ("Landing this CI improvement for real needs ... a cross-platform replacement for `dev-test/graphql-config`'s `|| [ $? -eq 1 ]` checks").

## Type of change

- [x] Bug fix (non-breaking change which fixes an issue)

## What

- `dev-test/graphql-config/assert-exit-code.mjs` (new): runs a command via `spawnSync`, exits `0` if its exit code matches the expected code given as the first argument, otherwise prints the mismatch and exits non-zero.
- `dev-test/graphql-config/package.json`: `generate:cjs:multi`/`generate:esm:multi` now run `node assert-exit-code.mjs 1 node ../../packages/graphql-codegen-cli/dist/{cjs,esm}/bin.js --config multi/.graphqlrc.yml` instead of the old `... || [ $? -eq 1 ]`.

## How Has This Been Tested?

- [x] `pnpm run dev-test:generate:cjs` and `pnpm run dev-test:generate:esm` locally, both exit `0` as before, and `git diff --exit-code -- dev-test/` is clean (no generated-output drift — only the two intended files changed).
- [x] Unit-checked `assert-exit-code.mjs` directly against all three outcomes: expected exit code (`1`) → helper exits `0`; unexpected success (`0`) → helper exits `1` (a bug caught and fixed during review — the first version reused the inner command's own `0` status, silently passing); an unrelated non-zero code (`2`) → helper propagates it.
- [x] `npx prettier --check` on both changed files: clean.
- [x] Experimentally cherry-picked #10957's `windows-latest` matrix commit on top of this branch and pushed it to real CI: confirms this fix works (zero `invalid integer '$?'` occurrences on either `windows-latest` leg) and doesn't regress the ESM path fix from #10956 (zero `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_ESM_URL_SCHEME` occurrences either). That experimental commit was reverted afterward — see Further comments for what it surfaced instead.

**Test Environment**:

- OS: local (ubuntu) — the actual regression only reproduces on `windows-latest`, tracked via #10957/#10956's CI runs and the experimental run noted above
- `@graphql-codegen/cli`: unaffected (fixture-only change)
- NodeJS: 24

## Checklist:

- [x] I have performed a self-review of my own code
- [ ] Everything else: N/A for this one-file fixture fix

## Further comments

This closes finding 3 from #10957, which is what's currently keeping `windows-latest` red on #10956's CI despite that PR's fix being verified correct (see [this comment](https://github.com/dotansimha/graphql-code-generator/pull/10956#issuecomment-5740296737)).

**However, merging this alone won't make `windows-latest` fully green yet.** Stacking #10957's matrix commit on this branch surfaced a fourth, previously-undiscovered Windows bug: `dev-test/general`'s `hooks: { afterAllFileWrite: ['prettier --write'] }` fails on Windows with `No files matching the pattern were found: "'D:\...\modules\types.ts'"` (literal quote characters baked into the path). Root cause is in `packages/graphql-codegen-cli/src/hooks.ts`: `executeHooks()` quotes file-path arguments with the `shell-quote` package, which only produces POSIX-style quoting, then hands the command to `child_process.exec()` with no explicit `shell` option — which defaults to `cmd.exe` on Windows, and `cmd.exe` doesn't strip single quotes. This is unrelated to this PR's fix and not yet tracked anywhere; happy to size/file it separately if useful.

author: ibanner56
body:
## Summary

Stacked on #1315 (adds the `classify_changes.py` extraction this PR builds on).

`builds_changed` was a bare alias for `app_tests_changed`
(`.github/workflows/ci.yml:209`, pre-#1315), which requires a path under `app/`
or `packages/compendium_core/`. `packaging/linux/*` (AppRun, the `.desktop`
file, the icon — consumed only by `release.yml:496-498`'s AppImage assembly)
and `packaging/windows/CallersCompendium.iss` (consumed only by
`release.yml:1312`'s Inno Setup compile) match neither, so a PR touching only
`packaging/` set `validation_changed=true` (checks still ran) but
`builds_changed` stayed `false` — the 5-platform build matrix never ran.

Widens `builds_changed` to also trigger on any `packaging/` path,
independently of `app_tests_changed`.

## Scope (discussed and agreed with Isaac this session)

This is the **minimal** fix: it reuses the existing 5-platform `flutter build`
smoke-test matrix. It does **not** add new per-package jobs that actually
assemble the Linux AppImage or compile the Windows Inno Setup script —
`release.yml` remains the only place those are built. The build matrix's
`flutter build` steps don't read anything under `packaging/` today, so this
doesn't yet catch a broken `.desktop` file or a broken `.iss` script; it only
guarantees the build matrix (which validates the app itself still builds)
runs when packaging inputs change. That narrower gap is a stated, accepted
scope exclusion — the alternative (extracting `release.yml`'s packaging steps
into standalone PR-runnable jobs) was considered and explicitly deferred as
out of scope for this fix.

## Blast radius

| Consumer | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `packaging/`-only diff | `builds_changed=false`, build matrix skipped | `builds_changed=true`, build matrix runs |
| `app/`+`packaging/` diff | `builds_changed=true` via `app_tests_changed` | Unchanged (redundant `or`) |
| `release.yml` | Only consumer of `packaging/**` | Untouched |

## Red-run evidence

Against this branch's pre-fix `classify_changes.py` (i.e. `builds_changed = app_tests_changed`, unchanged from what #1315 shipped):

```
packaging-only diffs still build:
  FAIL linux packaging asset alone: ... want {'builds_changed': True} got False
  FAIL windows packaging script alone: ... want {'builds_changed': True} got False
  FAIL packaging alone does not imply app_tests_changed: ... want {'builds_changed': True} got False
  ok   packaging plus an app change still builds (no interaction bug)
3 failure(s)
```

After the fix: `python3 tools/ci/test_classify_changes.py` → `All classify_changes tests passed.`

## Verification

- `python3 tools/ci/test_classify_changes.py` — pass
- `python3 tools/preflight.py --only classify-gate` — pass
- No `ci.yml` change in this PR (only the classify script), so no new actionlint/YAML surface.

## Scope exclusions

- No new packaging-specific build/validation job (see Scope above).
- No change to `release.yml`.

#20, #21 remain open — tracked in PR3, stacked on top of this one.

Execution, buffered writes, cancellation, retry, durable recovery, and shutdown now share explicit ownership and commit boundaries. Browser persistence and session restoration preserve concurrent changes. Early-development contracts use their current schema only, with affected development data recreation documented instead of adding compatibility migrations.

Align all 19 framework manifests and README release links to 0.0.37, publish the changelog, and repair two live E2E selectors for the current world cards and advanced plugin controls.

author: honeybbq
body:
## Author

- [ ] Human
- [x] Agent

## Type

- [ ] bug
- [x] feat
- [ ] test

## Summary

叠在 #1333 之上。前两层让日志能关联到一次请求，这一层补上产生关联的那一端：本仓此前**没有任何东西会产生 span**，`internal/logger` 读的 `trace_id` / `span_id` 永远是空的。

日志回答「发生了什么」，trace 回答「时间花在哪、哪一步失败」——后者在这里更要紧，因为一次 agent turn 串起模型调用、容器内工具执行、数据库访问和 compaction，而「回复很慢」不说明是其中哪一段。

### 默认关闭，而且关闭就是真的不装

没配置 collector 时**不装 TracerProvider**，不会构造一个指向默认地址的 exporter。这点必须显式做：OTLP SDK 会把未设置的 endpoint 默认成 `localhost:4317`，永远构造 exporter 的实现会让每一个没有 collector 的部署都在后台重试一个不可能成功的连接。

无条件装的只有**上下文传播**。这不是疏忽而是刻意：propagator 背后没有 provider 时无 span 可写，代价是查一个通常不存在的 header；而把它做成可选，代价是一个几乎不可见的故障——只在部分服务开启 tracing 的部署会得到「每一跳一条互不相连的 trace」，每个服务看起来都正常、都在产生 span，唯一症状是同一个请求的两半永远接不上，而且没有任何错误日志。

### 埋了哪些

| 位置 | 内容 |
|---|---|
| HTTP server | 每请求一个 server span，按**匹配到的路由**命名（`GET /bots/:id`），两个壳都装 |
| gRPC 内部 RPC | client + server span（channel 进程 ↔ server 进程） |
| gRPC workspace bridge | client span（宿主 → 容器） |
| gRPC 远端 runtime | client span（server → WebSocket 隧道） |
| PostgreSQL | 每查询一个 span，三个连接池全覆盖 |

三处拨号与内部 RPC server **在同一个提交里一起埋**是有意的：只埋一端的 gRPC 连接正是那个「没有症状」的故障形态，留一处以后再说等于主动发布这个状态。

### 两个刻意的缺口

**`internal/agent/application` 的手工 span 不在这一刀里。** 那一层的 trace 价值最高，但它也正在被重构（9 月还在做签名级改动）。span 名字和属性是看板与告警写死依赖的接口，在底下的代码定型前固化它，等于给自己安排一次破坏性变更。这是下一刀，不是遗漏。

**`cmd/bridge` 永久不埋**，理由和它的日志不被采集完全相同：它跑在每个 bot 的工作区容器里，那里没有 collector 可导。每次 bridge 调用的宿主一侧都有 client span，所以调用本身可见，容器内部不可见。

### 依赖成本比想象小

OTel 的 API 面**今天就已经链进这些二进制**（Docker client 等依赖自带插桩），`go.mod` 里 otel 相关本来就在模块图中。这一刀新增的是 SDK 与 OTLP exporter：实测在已有 gRPC 的基线上约 **1.9 MiB**，二进制约 148 MiB，占 1.3%。`google.golang.org/grpc` 与 protobuf 版本未动（otelgrpc 特意钉在与现有 otel 同代的 v0.65.0，而非会连锁升级 grpc 的 v0.71.0）。

### 几个实现选择

- **Echo 中间件自己写**，因为 contrib 的 `otelecho` 已标记废弃、官方指定的替代仓没有任何 release tag。顺带也确定了两件通用库会做错的事：span 按匹配路由命名（否则每个 bot 各成一个 operation），URL 属性走和访问日志同一个脱敏函数。
- **pgx 用它自己的 `QueryTracer` 钩子**，不引第三方桥。除了少一个依赖，更重要的是由我们决定：**查询参数一律不记录**——那是被读写的行内容；SQL 文本记录，它是代码不是数据。
- **otelgrpc 用 stats handler**，interceptor 构造函数已废弃，且只有 handler 能看到流式消息事件。
- **传输安全由 endpoint 的 scheme 决定**（按 OTLP 规范），压过配置里的 `insecure`。

最后一条是实跑时发现的真问题：把明文 collector 写成无 scheme 的 `host:4317`（最常见写法）会走 TLS，15 秒后报一个 `tls: first record does not look like a TLS handshake`,既不指出是哪个配置导致、也不指出改哪个能修。现在 scheme 说了算，且启动日志打出 `tls=true/false`——无 scheme 的写法没有携带这个信息，只能靠日志让人看见。

### 审查发现并已修的三条

**Baggage 被无条件转发。** 本仓从不写 baggage，装这个 propagator 只会让进程变成转发器：调用方传来的 `baggage:` 会经内部 RPC 一路送进**每个 bot 的工作区容器**。转发一个我们既不产生也不读取的值，是一条没人能交代的通道。现在只传 `traceparent`，与文档一致。

**数据库错误带出了行内容。** 参数是刻意不记的，然后 `RecordError` 把驱动消息原样记了进去——PostgreSQL 会把违规的值写在消息里，唯一约束冲突读作 `Key (email)=(a@b.com) already exists`。现在按 SQLSTATE 分类（没有 SQLSTATE 的错误记类型名，一个 Go 类型名装不下一行数据）。

**启动日志原样打出 endpoint。** `http://user:pass@collector:4317` 是个合理的配置，却不是个合理的日志内容。现在打之前剥掉 userinfo 与 query，导出失败的错误处理里同样。第一版修复漏了无 scheme 的形式——而 `user:pass@collector:4317` 恰恰是唯一带凭据、又会走进那个回退分支的输入。

另外：scheme 比较改为大小写不敏感（`HTTP://` 此前两个分支都不匹配，会对明文 collector 发起 TLS 并报一个跟根因无关的握手错误）。

## Related Issues

依赖 #1333（及其下层 #1332），需先合入。

## Validation

- `go build ./...` 通过；`go test ./...` 全绿（0 个非 ok 包）；`mise exec -- golangci-lint run ./...` 无输出。
- **接真 OTLP 后端实跑**：dev 栈旁起一个 `otel/opentelemetry-collector-contrib`（debug exporter，把收到的 span 全打出来），用 `OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT` 打开 server 的导出。
  - 启动日志：`tracing enabled endpoint=http://... protocol=grpc tls=false sample_ratio=1 service_name=memoh-server`，即环境变量覆盖这条路通。
  - 一次登录请求产生的 trace：`POST /auth/login`（Server span），`request_id=lDXuejLSFxhqDVMsKpDukhtTFHabTdeb` 与 curl 响应头里的值**逐字符相同**；`url.path=/auth/login`、`status=200`；同一条 trace 下挂着 **2 个 `postgresql.query` 子 span，父节点正是该 server span**——HTTP → DB 的因果链成立。
  - Resource 属性正确：`service.name=memoh-server`、`service.version`、`telemetry.sdk.*`。
  - 敏感信息：collector 收到的全部 span 里，登录密码出现 **0 次**；带 `?token=synthetic-leak-check` 的请求，该值出现 **0 次**、`url.path` 为 `/bots`；`db.query.text` 只有语句文本、参数保持 `$1` 占位符。
  - 关闭后（不设 endpoint 重启）：启动日志无 tracing 行，再发请求新增 span 为 **0**。期间观察到的 1 个 span 经时间戳核对属于旧进程优雅关停时的最后一次 flush（span 产生于 `07:54:06.565`，新进程 `07:54:07.628` 才启动），正是 fx OnStop 调 `provider.Shutdown` 应有的行为。
- **跨进程连续性做了变异测试**：`internal/rpc/trace_test.go` 用真实 gRPC 连接断言两端 trace id 相同、server span 的父节点是 client span；分别摘掉 client 与 server 的 stats handler，两次都变红。这个故障没有别的症状，只能靠端到端断言守住。
- `internal/telemetry` 的测试用 `-shuffle=on` 复跑通过——otel 的全局 tracer 一旦设过就永久委托，断言若依赖执行顺序会时好时坏，所以「未配置时不装 provider」是直接断言全局 provider 未被替换，而不是断言某个 span 不记录。

## Screenshots / Recordings

本 PR 没有可见界面：改的是进程产生什么遥测数据。替代验证见上一节，核心是接真 OTLP collector 后逐字段核对收到的 span——包括因果链、`request_id` 与客户端所见一致、以及敏感信息的零出现计数。

## Human QA

- [ ] Human QA passed

## Summary
- Adds a Manifest V3 Chrome extension (`chrome-extension/`) called "מציאון" that shows the same AliExpress deals feed already used by the Telegram bot and website, in a browser toolbar popup.
- Adds an opt-in daily notification with the top deal, category filters, and a lightweight local-only badge on matching AliExpress product pages (no network calls from the content script, no personal data collection).
- `site/build.mjs` now also writes a public, secret-free `dist/feed.json` (top 60 deals) that GitHub Pages serves with open CORS, so the extension can fetch it directly with no backend and no API keys embedded client-side.

author: nxank4
body:
Asked "who are you?", a worker answered like a generic assistant: it received instructions and a skill sheet, but was never told its own name, role, team or job for the turn.

Every run now opens with an identity line built from what the workspace already knows:

- the worker's name, and the role it was hired for (its short description)
- the skill sheet it follows
- its team and its part in it: writing the team's final answer, or answering its own part
- the colleagues answering alongside it, with their roles, so it can leave their part to them
- what this turn is for: planning, a member brief, synthesis, or a group chat where it should add what is missing instead of repeating others
- in a one-to-one chat, that other workers and teams exist but are not visible to it, so it can say so plainly

The identity block is recorded in the run's context manifest like every other layer, so Details still shows exactly what was sent.

## How it was checked

- New tests: solo worker, worker with no description, one-to-one chat, team member, synthesizer and group chat
- Typecheck clean; 265 tests pass, 1 skipped
- Live Claude Code run in the dev app: "Tên tôi là Researcher… Tôi được giao việc gì: đọc các tài liệu bạn đưa vào và viết ra một bản nhận xét ngắn gọn"

author: manjesh-raj
body:
## Summary

Full review #3's two performance findings (§3) and three security findings (§4), batched into one PR per the captain's request, one commit per finding.

| | Finding | What changed |
|---|---|---|
| **S1** | HIGH | Every `claude -p` run is fail-closed on the built-in tool set via `--tools`; `SRELeadRunner` loses `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` |
| **S2** | MED/HIGH | The unlocked vault reconciles with a file a git pull changed underneath it; reveal/copy no longer rewrite-and-commit the whole file |
| **S3** | LOW | Session-restore state moves from `UserDefaults` into a 0600 file |
| **PF1** | MEDIUM | Hidden destinations leave the window's constraint graph (nothing is unmounted) |
| **PF2** | LOW | Module cards size to their content, uniform per row |

Plus one commit recording the durable rules in `AGENTS.md` and the branch's account in `docs/history/30-full-review-3.md`.

## Reason

### S1 - the exploit was run, not reasoned about

`--allowedTools` is *additive to* `~/.claude/settings.json`'s `permissions.allow`, and `--strict-mcp-config` scopes only MCP servers. Against the captain's real settings file (42 allow rules, including `Bash(python3 -)`), a real `claude -p` given only `--allowedTools mcp__luffy-stores__shift_read` — today's Straw Hat shape — ran `echo '...' | python3 -` and **wrote the marker file**, with `permission_denials: []`. The prompt asking for it was ordinary conversation text, which is exactly what a runbook body, task title or sticky note is.

Three further measurements chose the fix:

- `--tools ""` denies it — the model reports having no Bash tool.
- `--tools "Task,TodoWrite"` denies it **even with `--permission-mode bypassPermissions` also passed**, so `--tools` gates below permission checking and cannot be widened by a settings file or a permission mode. That is why the bypass flag is gone rather than kept.
- `--tools ""` does **not** strip MCP tools, which is what makes it usable here.

A positive allowlist rather than `--disallowedTools`: a denylist goes stale the moment the CLI gains a built-in nobody here has heard of. `ClaudeOneShot` emits the flag on every run from a parameter defaulting to none, so a new runner is fail-closed by construction, and `ClaudeOneShotToolPolicySelfTest` guards the argv, the call sites and the two personas' lists.

> **For the captain, outside this repo:** the report separately suggests pruning `Bash(python3 -)` (and `Bash(.venv311/bin/python -c ' *)`) from the **global** `~/.claude/settings.json` allowlist. This PR makes that unnecessary for this app's personas, but those rules still widen every other `claude` session on the machine. Relaying, not implementing.

### S2 - a real data-loss path

`CredentialVaultSync` never pulls, but `ShiftGitSync.pullNow` runs a whole-tree `merge --ff-only` every five minutes, which updates `vault.enc.json` on disk while the in-memory copy stays stale. Every `persist()` then rewrote the whole file from that stale memory. Mac A has the vault unlocked, Mac B adds a credential and pushes, A's pull fast-forwards, A's five-minute **auto-lock** fires — and `lock()`'s audit write overwrites B's credential, with the debounced commit pushing the loss onward.

`persist()` now three-way merges against a decrypted `baseline` (the set as of the last time memory and disk agreed): adopt what was added or changed elsewhere, honour a local delete, keep the local side on a genuine conflict. A re-key that landed from another Mac is **refused** rather than merged — this machine's key opens nothing in that file.

Reveal and copy were the worst of both problems at once: the two most frequent actions in the feature, each a full-file overwrite *and* a git commit, so the git host's commit timestamps recorded when the captain looked at which secret. They batch now, and no audit-only write marks the sync dirty.

### S3 - the 0600 story

Host IDs are UUIDs, so nothing here is a secret — but the console and Tools **tab names** are captain-authored strings that in practice name what a tab is connected to. That is the same argument `SnippetStore` already makes for its own 0600 file. This deliberately reaches a different answer from end-to-end review #1's L4 (which declined a sidecar for the vault's throttle counters); the reasoning for the difference is on `SessionRestoreStore` itself so nobody re-litigates it from L4 alone.

### PF1 - the profiling, including the two suspects that were wrong

Every number below is a 5s `sample` at 1ms, counting main-thread samples inside CoreAutoLayout.

**The captain's own running instance (pid 43464, unmodified HEAD build): 1095 of 4072 main-thread samples — 26.9%**, all under `_doUpdateTilingConstraintsImmediately → minFullScreenContentSize → NSISEngine`. The review's finding reproduces.

**What it is not.** A standalone stock-AppKit probe (one full-screen-capable window, N destination containers pinned into one body view, real rows of content) measured **0%** for a settled graph — at 1 destination and at 27. This is not stock idle work that merely scales. Both of the review's named candidates are also exonerated:

- Forcing a real layout pass 20×/second: **0%**. The per-navigation `layout()` forces in `ChromeFusionRootView`/`HelmSegmentedTabs`/`TrailingActionsStack` are not the cause.
- Marking views `needsLayout` 20×/second: **0%**.
- `reassertBodyContainerWidthTie`'s constraint reactivation is not firing at all — its `AppLog.ui.error` on that path has **zero** entries in six hours of the captain's instance.

**What it is.** Anything that invalidates the window's constraint-derived minimum size makes AppKit re-solve the whole graph, and a single label's text changing is enough. Cost is near-linear in how much of the graph is in the window:

```
 1 mounted     16 samples    0.4% of the main thread
 3 mounted    134            3.1%
 7 mounted    357            8.3%
14 mounted    973           22.7%
27 mounted   1877           43.4%
```

The captain's 26.9% sits squarely on that curve. An explicit `contentMinSize`/`minSize` does **not** short-circuit it (97% of busy time either way).

**What the fix buys.** Deactivating a hidden page's four pins leaves its subtree with no required path to the window. Same probe, 27 mounted, same invalidation: **1823 samples → 55** (42.5% → 1.3%). In the real app, measured through `Scripts/build-probe-app.sh`'s separately-identified probe bundle with identical temporary instrumentation on both sides:

```
without the fix   637 samples   17.3% of the main thread
with the fix      360            9.5%
```

A 43% cut. Smaller than the isolated model's 97% because the real app has genuine layout work the model does not — the showing page, the top bar, the session strip — which this fix correctly does not touch. The instrumentation was reverted before committing, per AGENTS.md's "Verifying native UI bugs" convention.

**GL-37's other half — unmounting cold destinations — is deliberately not attempted, and the measurement is the argument for not needing it.** The scaling curve says the cost is about what is in the *constraint graph*, not about what is mounted; detaching gets essentially all of the saving for none of the risk of reasoning about ~27 controllers' live ssh sessions, in-flight fetches and per-page state. Recommended as separate future work only if a reason other than this one appears.

### PF2 - measured, then rendered

Every body kind at its realistic width (from `DaylightModuleSelfTest`'s table, which now prints card heights):

```
note        176 → 124pt     briefing (empty)  176 → 124pt
ring        176 → 141pt     metric            176 → 151pt
peekRows    176 → 161pt     paragraph         176 → 162pt
progress    176 → 169pt
```

Even the tallest body kind was 7pt short of the fixed height, and the most common one now was wasting 52pt — 30% of the card. A realistic two-row canvas rendered 368pt of grid before and 311pt after. Judged as rendered off-screen, not just as numbers: uniform rows, n

body:
## DAT-007 item #1 — the fence-bound run-JWT currency resolver, slice 2

Builds on slice 1 (the pure `classifyRunCurrency` decision, merged #492): the DB reader + the `/mcp` mount, **inert behind `AOA_DISTRIBUTED_EXECUTION_ENABLED`** (default off → byte-identical legacy).

### What lands
- **`distributed-run-currency-resolver.ts` (new)** — the bounded, fully-indexed reader keyed on the **signed** run id: the `guardActiveFence` join (`job-control.ts:1920-1967`) with a `heartbeat_runs` hop, computing lease freshness against `clock_timestamp()` **in SQL**. Every hop is a unique-index probe (PK / `leases_active_per_attempt_idx` / `execution_targets_authority_id_uq`) — no scan, no new migration. Kept in its **own module** so the pure classifier stays drizzle-free (the `lease-truth.ts` isolation pattern). **Fail-CLOSED**: DB errors propagate, never swallowed to admit.
- **`server.ts`** — inject `resolveDistributedRunCurrency` (defaulted from the reader), read the flag **once** at construction (it throws on a garbage value → a per-request read would 500 every call), and mount the gate right after `ensureProtocolAccess` (`server.ts:446`) so it dominates **both** tool-dispatch paths + `tools/list` + `resources/*`. A deny throws the **same coarse** `forbidden` as wrong-tenant (extracted to `MCP_CROSS_COMPANY_FORBIDDEN_MSG`) — no oracle. Keyed on `req.actor.signedRunId`, never the header-overridable `runId`.
- **`auth.ts` + `express.d.ts`** — surface `signedRunId` (= the signed `claims.run_id`) on the `agent_jwt` actor (edge-16 fix).

### Tests (Tier 2 — route mount)
`mcp-run-currency-gate.test.ts`: deny→403 on `initialize`/`tools/list`/`tools/call`; admit→200; **board / no-`signedRunId` / flag-off** → resolver never consulted; **resolver throws → non-2xx** (fail-closed, Correction A). The deny-vs-admit differential (identical setup, only the stub's verdict differs) proves the 403 comes from the mount — the anti-vacuity control. The real DB query is proven in **slice 3** (Tier-3, real PG) alongside the RLS precondition.

Register: DE-16/DE-19 `server.ts` citations re-pointed for the mount's line shift (`policy` green locally).

body:
新機能ではなく、ここまでに育った `tick` を **固める** PR です。全体プラン 9.4、9.12 ／ Phase 1 プラン PR 12。

固めにきて 2 つ出ました。**遷移表の 1 行が実態から浮いていた**ことと、**席が永久に塞がる筋書きが 1 つ残っていた**ことです。

## 1. 遷移表 61 行のうち、60 行に「実際に通る証拠」を置いた

証拠は 1 行につき 1 つ（`reachability.test.ts`）。それぞれが 2 つのことを同時に示します。

1. **その事象を起こす道がある** — `apply` か `tick` を 1 手動かして、対象が `from` から `to` へ動く
2. **その行が採られる** — 同じ（状態、事象）に複数の行があっても、`ticketTransitionRow` / `tableTransitionRow` がまさにその行を返す

**証拠の無い行は落ちます。** 遷移を足したら、ここに証拠を足さないと通りません。

### 残る 1 行は、この版では通らない

> `FREE --CHECK_IN_EARLY--> OCCUPIED`（7.8 の 4 行目、空席への前倒し着席）

**割当がコマンドのたびに必ず走るので、「収まる空席があるのに待っている人が残る」という状態が作れません**（不変条件 `no_starvation`）。空席の QR を読んだ待ち人は、その瞬間にはもう呼ばれていて、通常の着席（7.8 の 1 行目）になります。

行は**消さずに残しました**。7.8 が書いている画面は実在しますし、`CHECK_IN_EARLY` 自体は「確認要」の席で通っています（7.11 の 3 層目）。代わりに「通らない理由」を書いて数え上げ、`tick.property.test.ts` に「空席に前倒しで座れる人は残らない」という性質を置いて主張のほうを検証しています。

## 2. 席が永久に塞がる筋書きを 1 つ塞いだ

PR 10 の性質「どんな筋書きのあとでも、時間を十分に進めれば席が空く」が、**PR 11 で生成器にコマンドが増えたあと 10 回に 3 回ほど落ちる**ようになりました。道筋はこうです。

```
運用終了で待っている人が全員取り消される
  → limit_only_when_waiting が立っているので上限が効かない
  → 一度「まだ利用中」と答えた人には問いかけが二度と出ない（7.11 の「1 回」）
  → OCCUPIED から出る道が 1 本も残らない
  → 次の OPEN でも戻らない（運用開始が戻すのは DISABLED の席だけ）
```

**日をまたいで 1 卓失われます。**

7.11 の「1 回」と、同じ 7.11 の「最悪でも席が永久に塞がらない」が食い違っていたので、**保証のほうを残しました**。問いかけを **「答えたら、そこから測り直してもう一度」** に変更しています（全体プラン 7.11 の 2 層目を改訂）。答える手間は 1 タップで、答えているかぎり席はその人のものなので、繰り返し聞くほうが利用者の利益にもかないます。

実装は期限の式 2 つだけです。「答えたか」ではなく **「最後の問いかけより後に答えたか」** で見るようにし、答えの時刻は消さずに残します（上限の超過を抑えるのに要る。PR 10 の直しを壊さない）。

## 3. 時計の単調性を実装した

状態が「最後に進んだ時刻」（`clockAt`）を持ち、`apply` と `tick` が入口で確かめます。戻っていれば `CLOCK_WENT_BACKWARD` で拒否し、**`isDefect` が真を返す側**に置きました（利用者の操作の誤りではなく、実装の誤りなので）。

期限の判定はすべて絶対時刻の比較なので、**時計が戻ると、いったん過ぎた期限がまた「これから」に戻ります。** ホールドが切れて保留に戻った人に、もう一度ホールドの期限が生える。壊れ方が静かなので入口で落とします。同じ時刻は通します（冪等性を保つため）。

## 4. 時間の飛びの保証を 2 本に分けた

プランは「1 時間を 361 回に分けても 1 回でも同じ状態になる」と書いていましたが、**これは条件つきでしか成り立ちません**（PR 6 のファズが見つけていた）。

| 保証 | 条件 |
|---|---|
| 刻み方によらず同じ状態に落ち着く | 空席が無いとき |
| **一度の `tick` で、来ている期限がすべて片づく** | **条件なし** |

2 つ目が「再起動しても取りこぼさない」の本体で、無条件に成り立ちます。`tick` のあと、どのチケット・どの席にも「もう来ているのに処理されていない期限」が残らないことを性質にしました。

**呼び出しだけは遡りません。** 1 時間止まっていた施設が再開したとき、席が空いた時点に遡って呼び出すと、届いていない呼び出しのホールドがすでに切れていることになります。再開した時点で呼び直すほうが利用者に不利でない（CLAUDE.md 2.5）。両方の筋書きを並べたテストで、違いが出ることそのものを固定しました。

## 5. そのほか

- **`tick` の評価順をテストで固定した** — チケットの期限 → 施設の期限 → 席の期限 → 割当 → 不変条件。1 回の `tick` で 4 段すべてが起きる筋書きを作り、イベントの並びで押さえています
- **ガードの宣言・参照・実装が一致することを固定した**（チケット 10 個、席 5 個）
- **選び方の規則を 1 か所にまとめた** — 遷移表から「いま採られる行」を返す `taken()` を切り出し、`transit()` もそれを使います。網羅性の検査と実際の遷移が同じ関数を見るので、答えが割れません
- **冪等性は 100 回で確かめる** — 2 回で足りるように見えますが、「経過した回数」で進む実装はここで必ず落ちます

## 実証実験中の挙動がどう変わるか

- **「まだご利用中ですか」が、答えたあと p90（既定 50 分）でもう一度出ます。** 長く座る人には繰り返し届きます。答えているかぎり席はその人のままで、答えが無ければ 5 分で確認要（これまでどおり）
- ほかの利用者向けの挙動は変わりません。時計の単調性は、サーバ側の呼び出し方が正しければ表に出ません

スキーマ変更はありません（Phase 1 は純粋な TypeScript のみ）。

## 全体プランを直した箇所

- **7.11 の 2 層目**: 問いかけを「1 回」から「答えたら測り直してもう一度」へ
- **7.8**: 4 行目（前倒しの着席）が実装では「確認要の席」でだけ起きる理由
- **9.4**: `tick` の評価順、時計の単調性、呼び出しを遡らないこと

```

author: memtomem
body:
## What this does

Two things, in two commits.

**A bare `mm index` says which directory it is about to walk.** `PATH` defaults
to `.`, so someone following a setup guide inside a code repository indexes the
repository rather than their memory directory. The walk pulls in fixtures and
tooling, the redaction gate blocks the ones carrying secret-class patterns, and
the command exits 1 — a refusal that reads as a broken install rather than a
mis-aimed command. The notice goes to stderr, so `--json` and every other
stdout contract is untouched, and the default is **not** changed: scripts
legitimately pass no path.

**And then it fixes the code that notice was written with.** Detecting whether
`PATH` came from the default reads `ParameterSource`, which was spelled
`click.ParameterSource`. That alias does not exist on the floor this package
declares.

## The measurement

`packages/memtomem/pyproject.toml` requires `click>=8.1`. In a clean venv:

| click | `click.ParameterSource` |
|---|---|
| 8.1.8, 8.2.1, 8.3.0, 8.3.1, 8.3.2 | **absent** |
| 8.3.3, 8.4.0, 8.4.1, 8.5.0 | present |

The lockfile installs 8.5.0, so the whole suite was green over a command that
could not start on a supported version. The lookup sits inside the comparison,
ahead of the DEFAULT branch, so it is not confined to the bare form: on the
floor **every direct `mm index` raised `AttributeError`**, including one given
an explicit path. Verified end to end by downgrading a venv to `click==8.1.8`
and running both forms.

## Three regression tests, because call time and import time fail differently

Deleting the attribute and invoking the command covers the call site, for the
bare and the explicit form. That cannot reach a *module-level* alias, which is
evaluated once at import. Executing the module's source under a throwaway name
covers that — by property rather than by spelling, so
`ParameterSource = click.ParameterSource`, `getattr(click, "ParameterSource")`
and an aliased package import are all caught. Each was confirmed by making the
change and watching the test go red.

Not `importlib.reload`: reloading the real module rebinds the classes defined
in it, and four unrelated tests in `test_indexing_cli.py` then failed their
`pytest.raises` — only in a full-suite run, because running the file alone
never reaches them.

## Verified

Full CI-filtered suite green; `ruff` clean. Reviewed; both minors from that
review are in the second commit, including a correction to the version
boundary, which an earlier draft put at 8.4 by sampling 8.3.0 and 8.4.0 and
interpolating.

author: natanielmarmucki
body:
Fixes the reported bug: moving between songs animated in the wrong direction, and the animation did not fit a songbook.

### What was wrong
- Every song change replaced the whole screen with `pushReplacement` and the platform's default *forward* transition, so the **previous song also came in from the right**. The next one was right by accident; the bars moved with the text.
- The swipe fired only when a *single touch event* moved more than 10 px, so a slow, deliberate drag did nothing.
- The reported "text comes in from the left" is most likely the **iOS back gesture**: a swipe that starts at the left edge goes back to the list, which slides in from the left. Confirmed on the iPhone simulator; that gesture stays as it is.

### What changed
- `SongDetailView` is a `PageView` over the songbook. Only the text moves, the bars stay; the next song comes in from the right, the previous one from the left; the swipe follows the finger. `PageView.builder` keeps 1 page alive at rest and 2 while dragging (measured with 2000 pages).
- Arrows: 200 ms, `Easing.emphasizedDecelerate`; instant with reduced motion. Go to number: instant (opening the book at a page). After a swipe the page settles on a stiffer, critically damped spring: ~0.45 s instead of ~0.9 s.
- While turning, a hairline marks the seam between the two songs, like a page edge; not drawn at rest.
- Gaps in the numbering are skipped instead of stopping the swipe (the real data has no gaps). Recorded in `docs/PARITY.md`.
- `ScreenWakeLock` is a plain on/off pair again: only one song screen exists at a time. A comment explains why it was a counter (#16) and when it must be again. The #16 regression tests keep their promise: *the screen does not turn off when switching songs* (by number, by swiping, with the arrows).
- `docs/DESIGN-SYSTEM.md` section 5 describes the page turn; `CLAUDE.md` describes the song screen.

### Verification
- `flutter test`: 460 passed, 25 skipped (451 before; new tests for direction, bars staying put, reduced motion, 200 ms arrows, settle time, drag past half the width, the hairline, and the iOS edge gesture). `flutter analyze --no-fatal-infos`: 1 info, as on `main`. `tools/golden.sh`: 25 passed, no image changed.
- iPhone simulator, touches injected into the running app: swipe from the middle right → song 9 from the left, bars still, hairline at the seam; left → song 11 from the right; from the left edge (held or quick) → back to the list.
- Checked by hand on the simulator: speed and look accepted.
