author: neo-opus-grace
body:
Resolves #18944

A focus move the App Worker handles late no longer leaves the old path marked as focused. `manager.Focus` paired a focusout with its focusin by the worker's clock. When the worker spent more than `maxFocusInOutGap` (50 ms) between handling the two — a heavy render is enough — the focusin became a bare `focusEnter`, and the focusout's timer then saw a newer focusin and delivered no leave. Every component on the old path kept `containsFocus: true`.

The pair is now decided by the pending focusout itself. `onFocusout` records its `opts` as `pendingFocusOut` and schedules the leave, as before. `onFocusin` completes a move when it finds one pending, and an enter otherwise. The timer delivers the leave only for the focusout still pending — the identity guard the `Date` comparison stood in for — and still not for a removed floating component shown again. `lastFocusInDate` and `lastFocusOutDate` retire; nothing outside the spec's reset read them.

`component.Base#containsFocus_` now states its contract. It answers whether focus is inside the subtree, never which descendant holds it — a grid View holds DOM focus for all its cells. It is App-Worker state that settles one gap after a focusout, so a same-tick read sees the state before the gesture. Three #18762 leaves misread it within a day.

Evidence: L1 (unit, the manager driven directly with the worker's interleaving reproduced by a synchronous busy period) → L1 required (a classification rule inside one singleton). Residual: none — idle behaviour is unchanged, and every pre-existing arm pins it.

agent-preflight: not hosted here; baseline `pr-body` and `substrate-size` run in CI.

## AC Evidence

| AC | |
|---|---|
| AC-1 | `unit/manager/Focus.spec.mjs` › *a focusin the App Worker handles after the gap still makes a move with the focusout waiting for it*: focus on A, focusout, the thread busy for 2 × the gap, focusin on B, timer run out → A `false`, B `true`, log `[enter A, leave A, enter B]`. RED on `dev`'s `Focus.mjs` (the only failing arm, 8 pass) |
| AC-2 | the other 8 arms pass unchanged at both heads: superseded focusout, removed floating menu shown again, the three dismissals, the closest-common-component moves |
| AC-3 | reverting the classification to the clock comparison is exactly `dev`'s `Focus.mjs`: the AC-1 arm fails |
| AC-4 | `containsFocus_`'s JSDoc: whether, never where; App-Worker state; when it is set and cleared |
| AC-5 | unit 4280, component 380, e2e `grid` + `form` 66 — all green at this head |

## Deltas from ticket

- None in mechanism. The superseded-focusout arm's comment described the old clock pair as the thing the first timer consults; it now describes the pending focusout.

## Test Evidence

- At this head: unit 4280 (2 skipped), component 380, e2e `grid` + `form` 66; `Focus.spec` + `form/field/Picker.spec` + `tab/HeaderActions.spec` 31/31 — the three specs that drive `FocusManager`.
- Red-first, one variable: `dev`'s `src/manager/Focus.mjs` swapped in place → only the new arm fails.
- The probe that found it (scratch spec, deleted): on `dev`, idle → A `false` / B `true`; 80 ms busy → A `true` / B `true`.

## Post-Merge Validation

- None: the arm runs in the unit tier on this PR.

author: mikeypetrillo
body:
Two commits. Neither changes runtime behaviour.

**A guard on what a seller can buy by renaming.** Twice we have answered a seller by quoting the router's weights, and both times they rewrote the operationId rather than the product. It worked honestly, because the keywords were true of their endpoint, but the weighting is an incentive we publish and nothing measured what it is worth.

Measured against the live scorer: the placement premium is about 2.4x (the same words score 13 in the description and 31 in the slug), it is bounded by query length so a 40-keyword slug scores 8 to 12 on ordinary two and three word queries against live winners of 14 to 28, and a length penalty would hit the wrong people because 94% of 429 sampled external slugs are five tokens or fewer and the long tail is almost entirely FastAPI auto-generated ids. That measurement is why the ranker is left alone; the guard exists so those three facts stay true.

The first draft of it asserted the premium as a ratio, and the single most important mutation survived, because raising the slug weight lifts both rows. The numbers are absolute now. It also asserted a name match is worth the documented 2 when the scorer gives 7, since a row's name is an implicit slug alias and `hay` is built from the name. Both mistakes are kept in the file as comments. Five mutations killed.

**The Wellknown uptime badge on the README.** An independent index has connected to our MCP server on a schedule since 2026-09-05 and publishes what it observes: 43 probes over 30 days, 100% answered, 164 ms p50. Unlike the CI badges beside it, this one is somebody else's observation and goes stale or red on its own. The record is verified-owner as of today, proved with a well-known file served through the operator store.

Also in this batch's window, requiring no code: `SOLANA_RPC_URL` is now an Actions secret, so the three corpus holder cases that were skipping will run for real on tonight's nightly.

author: ugurkocde
body: ## Summary A first sign-in fires several requests at once (layout, page, prefetch). Each of them found no membership and created its own workspace, so new users ended up with an empty twin next to their real workspace. On the hosted database 10 owners have such a twin, each created within two seconds of its sibling and with no Microsoft connection and no findings. - `createOwnedWorkspace` takes a transaction-scoped advisory lock per user and looks for a membership again inside the lock. The first request creates the workspace, the others adopt it. - The accessible-workspaces read in `resolveWorkos` is ordered oldest first. Without a workspace cookie the active workspace was `rows[0]` of an unordered read, so it could differ between requests. Found while testing a sandbox purchase: the plan was written to one twin and the billing page showed the other. ## Not in this change - Cleaning up the existing empty twins on the hosted database. That is a data change and should be reviewed separately. ## Test plan - [x] New integration test: three concurrent `provisionForSignIn` calls for one user create one workspace and one membership. Verified that it fails without the fix. - [x] A second person still gets their own workspace - [x] `npx tsc --noEmit`, `npx eslint`, `npm run format:check`, full `npx vitest run` > [!NOTE] > ### Fix first sign-in creating duplicate workspaces via advisory lock in `createOwnedWorkspace` > - Adds a PostgreSQL transaction-scoped advisory lock keyed by WorkOS user ID in `createOwnedWorkspace` so concurrent provisioning requests for the same user serialize and reuse the first request's membership instead of each inserting a tenant. > - Adds deterministic ordering (tenant creation time ascending, tenant ID ascending as tiebreaker) to `resolveWorkos` so workspace selection is stable when no workspace cookie is present. > - Adds integration tests in [domainJoin.integration.test.ts](https://github.com/ugurkocde/licensemeter-website/pull/54/files#diff-c30e9a154ae177e0b1c06d16ee5dc7556c7b258cd29af571d651e48a0f32cc12) covering concurrent first-sign-in provisioning for the same identity and sequential provisioning for two distinct users. > - Risk: advisory lock uses the WorkOS user ID as the key; if a lock key collision occurs with another advisory lock using the same integer key space, provisioning could block unexpectedly. > > > > Macroscope summarized 4b63616. > > ## Summary by CodeRabbit * **Bug Fixes** * Improved reliability during simultaneous first-time sign-ins, ensuring a user receives exactly one workspace and membership. * Made default workspace selection consistent when multiple workspaces are available. * Preserved separate workspace creation for different users. * **Tests** * Added coverage for concurrent sign-ins and independent workspace provisioning.

author: ikac22
body:
Fixes #9.

## Summary

Update the Vercel Git deployment rules so that only `main` can trigger a deployment.

The repository now enforces branch naming so every non-`main` branch uses a slash-separated prefix such as `feature/...`, `fix/...`, `chore/...`, etc. Because of that, a single `**/*` rule is sufficient to match all allowed development branches.

## Change

```json
"git": {
  "deploymentEnabled": {
    "**/*": false,
    "main": true
  }
}
```

This replaces the previous `"*": false` pattern, which did not reliably match slash-separated branch names and allowed Vercel Preview Deployments to run on PR branches.

## Expected behavior

- `main` → Vercel deployment enabled
- any valid development branch matching `**/*` → Vercel deployment disabled
- GitHub CI continues to validate pull requests without consuming Vercel preview-build resources

author: ledo9315
body:
Zwei Ausfälle meldet Sentry bisher nicht, weil beide kein Fehler sind, sondern Schweigen: ein Erinnerungs-Cron, der nicht mehr läuft, und eine Seite, die nicht erreichbar ist. Wenn die App weg ist, kommen auch keine Fehler mehr an.

## Cron-Monitor

`/api/cron/daily-reminder` legt seine Arbeit in `Sentry.withMonitor`. Sentry bekommt damit einen Check-in beim Start und einen beim Ende, und merkt vor allem, wenn ein fälliger Lauf gar nicht erst kommt.

- Slug und Konfiguration in `lib/server/cron-monitor.ts`, nicht in der Sentry-Oberfläche — dort erinnert sich nichts daran, warum die Zahlen so sind.
- **75 Minuten Toleranz**, weil der Hobby-Plan stundengenau plant statt minutengenau: Vercel nennt ±59 Minuten, ein Job um 17:00 feuert also irgendwann bis 17:59. Eine engere Toleranz meldete an den meisten Tagen einen verpassten Lauf, und die Meldung wäre nach einer Woche nichts mehr wert.
- **`maxRuntime` über `maxDuration`**, damit nur ein Lauf als Timeout zählt, den die Plattform schon abgebrochen hat — darunter träfe es den langen, aber gesunden Versand.
- Beide Check-ins liegen hinter dem Secret. Ein abgelehnter Aufruf ist kein Lauf und darf nicht in die Historie.
- Vor der Antwort wird geflusht: die Instanz kann einfrieren, sobald die Antwort raus ist, und ein Check-in im Puffer ist ein gesunder Lauf, den Sentry als Timeout meldet.

Ein Test vergleicht den Crontab der Konfiguration mit dem `crons`-Eintrag in `vercel.json`, ein zweiter die Timeout-Grenze mit `maxDuration` der Route.

## Uptime-Monitor

Angelegt in Sentry, nicht im Repo: alle fünf Minuten ein GET auf `https://daily-coding.dev/`. Die Startseite ist `force-dynamic` und liest den Ring, ein grüner Check heißt also App **und** Datenbank. Als „unten" gilt sie nach zwei aufeinanderfolgenden Fehlschlägen, damit ein einzelner Kaltstart keinen Alarm auslöst.

## Prüfung

1606 Tests grün, `tsc --noEmit` sauber, `pnpm lint` sauber, `next build` läuft durch.

body:
## 1. Bouton « Envoyer cette réponse »

Un seul geste pour envoyer la proposition telle quelle, à côté du lien d'inspection.

L'envoi est **rattaché à la génération** (`linkOtaAiGenerationAudit`), ce qui la classe « envoyée sans retouche ». C'est ce chiffre qui décidera du pilote automatique au seuil des 90 %. Sans ce rattachement, on saurait qu'une réponse est partie, pas si elle venait du modèle.

Un rattachement raté **ne fait jamais croire à un échec d'envoi** : c'est une mesure, pas une garantie.

## 2. Nom du modèle réservé à l'admin

« claude-sonnet-4-6 » n'apparaît plus qu'en admin. C'est une information d'ingénierie, utile pour comparer deux versions, sans objet pour un owner à qui elle ne dit rien sur la qualité de la réponse.

## Ce qui ne change pas

La **génération** continue de ne rien envoyer. Seul ce nouveau bouton envoie, sur un clic explicite.

## Honnêteté sur le test

Type-check : 0 erreur. Mais **je n'ai pas réussi à vérifier le bouton à l'écran** : mes clics automatisés ratent la cible sur ce composant, un piège déjà rencontré ici. Tawfiq teste lui-même sur un vrai fil.

Premier test à faire sur un fil sans enjeu : ce bouton envoie réellement au client.

body:
… destination

Closes #4000.

An empty client-paginated table with URL state (the Devices table on a site with no devices) looped forever: clientTotalPages was 0, so the page-clamp effect saw page 1 as out of range and reset it to 1, and updateUrlState called router.replace even though the URL was unchanged. Each replace produced a new searchParams object, which recreated the page handlers and re-ran the effect. Chrome then throttled replaceState and the in-app Back button, a bare router.back(), stopped working.

- ReusableTable: only call router.replace when the query string actually changes, matching useServerSideTableState; treat an empty table as one page so the clamp effect has nothing to correct
- site details pages: Back now pushes the page the site was opened from (path + query, recorded by both sites tables) instead of relying on history, falling back to /admin/sites or /sites/overview; the recorded path must be a same-origin path in the same admin/user area
- tests: regression test for the empty table (fails on staging), a clamp test for an out-of-range page, and return-path helper tests

New companion binary exposing a skret project to MCP clients (Claude Code, OMP, any stdio harness) — read-only by default.

### Server (`internal/mcp` + `cmd/skret-mcp`)
- MCP stdio transport: newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0, protocol version negotiation (2024-11-05 / 2025-03-26 / 2025-06-18), `initialize`/`ping`/`tools/list`/`tools/call`, spec-correct split between protocol errors (`-32601`/`-32602`) and `isError` tool results; stdout carries protocol only, diagnostics on stderr

- Write tools `skret_set`/`skret_delete`/`skret_rotate` **gated behind `mcp.allow_write: true`** (default off); gated calls return an error result naming the exact config field + remediation. Rotate records as a rotation in the audit trail (`WithAuditOp`)
- Optional `mcp.allowed_envs` filter (validated against declared environments at load); a startup `--env` outside the allowlist fails closed at launch; per-call `env` arguments enforced per request; clients cached per environment

A tick happened where it could not be seen: the row was marked done and
moved into the completed section — closed by default — inside the same
render as the press, so the box that was pressed was gone before it could
show anything. The row is now held where it is for the length of its own
animation: the box fills and pops, the words strike through, and the row
slides away into the heading that already popped to receive it.

Beside it, how far along a list is:

- a bar on the list's own page, inside ListItems so the same optimistic
  state that moves the rows moves it — counted on the server it would sit
  one press behind every time — with "3 of 7 ticked off" beside it;
- the same bar on the cards on /lists and the dashboard, from stored
  counts, where there is no press to be behind;
- drawn in --chart-lists, not the home's accent (that dresses controls,
  and a bar is read rather than pressed) and not green at the end (green
  is "added" everywhere else in the app). aria-hidden throughout: every
  place it appears says the same proportion in words right beside it.

And clearing the last item is celebrated once: confetti over the page,
which takes itself off again, and a longer buzz than an ordinary tick.
It fires from the press that empties the list, counted before the change
is applied, so a list emptied by deleting its rows is not celebrated —
nothing was finished.

tests/unit/gamification.test.ts holds the colours and keyframes to the
stylesheet the way theme.test.ts and storage.test.ts hold theirs, and

author: renesenses
body:
Ferme #4494 — closes #4494.

Bertrand, 19/09/2026 : *« La recherche se fait en deux temps : local puis streaming. Il ne faut pas faire patienter l'utilisateur »*.

Le premier temps allait déjà : `SearchV2` lance local et fédérée en parallèle, et son voyant ne suit que le local. C'est le second qui coûtait.

## Mesuré sur le .18 (0.9.155), requête « coltrane », à chaud

| | temps |
|---|---|
| `/library/search` — le local, celui que l'écran affiche | **0,24 s** |
| `/search` — la fédérée | **2,03 s** (5,2 s à froid) |
| ↳ le bloc `local`, refait à l'intérieur puis **jeté** par l'écran | 0,95 s |
| ↳ les 4 services, **à la file** | 1,20 s |
| qobuz / tidal / youtube / bandcamp, seuls | 0,13 / 0,03 / 0,42 / 0,30 s |

## 1. Les services partent ensemble, et le registre est relâché

La boucle portait son `await` **à l'intérieur**, sous le verrou du registre. Les poignées (`Arc<RwLock<…>>`, clonées par `registry.get`) sont maintenant ramassées d'abord, le verrou tombe, puis les recherches partent sous `join_all`.

🔴 **La seconde moitié n'est pas cosmétique.** Le `Mutex` du registre était tenu pendant des appels **réseau** : toute autre route qui le demandait — statut des services, favoris, catalogue — faisait la queue derrière une recherche Qobuz. Ce n'est pas la recherche qu'on accélère là, c'est le serveur qu'on arrête de bloquer.

## 2. Un jeton `sources=streaming`

« Tous les services authentifiés, **sans** le local ». L'écran tient son local de `/library/search` et jetait celui de la fédérée — il ne lit que `r.services`. Il manquait le mot pour le dire au serveur, qui « ne calcule rien plutôt que jeter ».

Nommer les services un par un (`sources=qobuz,tidal,…`) l'aurait fait aussi. J'ai écrit cette version d'abord, **et je l'ai retirée** : elle oblige le client à *connaître* la liste avant de chercher, donc à appeler `/streaming/services` — dont l'échec, avalé par `statutsStreaming`, rend **zéro résultat de streaming sans un mot**. Vingt tests existants l'ont montré en rougissant, et ils avaient raison. Le serveur sait déjà qui est authentifié.

⚠️ `streaming` **ne remplace pas** `all` : `all` rend le local en plus. Les deux jetons disent deux choses différentes.

## La garde est un CHRONOMÈTRE

Une boucle qui `await` en son sein rend exactement les mêmes octets qu'un `join_all`, simplement plus tard. Aucune assertion sur le contenu ne peut voir ce défaut. La concurrence est donc extraite dans `recherches_concurrentes()`, une fonction qui prend des futures nues et se mesure.

## Preuves — Shrek, worktree `rech4a9`, `CARGO_BUILD_JOBS=6`

```
cargo fmt --all -- --check                      → FMT=0
cargo test -p tune-server --lib                 → 1389 passed, 0 failed
cargo test -p tune-server --lib routes::search  → 7 passed
cargo test -p tune-server --lib routes::filtre_sources → 5 passed
cargo test -p tune-server --test recherche_sources_i3226 → 7 passed
```

Le dernier est le témoin de non-régression du contrat de #3226 : les autres lignes du tableau de `filtre_sources.rs` ne bougent pas.

### Contre-épreuve — deux sabotages, tous deux compilants

```
1. join_all → boucle à la file
   les_quatre_partent_en_meme_temps ... FAILED
   panicked at search.rs:591:
     les services sont interrogés À LA FILE : 604.883305ms pour
     4 services à 150ms (à la file : 600ms)
   → 6 passed, 1 failed

2. `streaming` ramène AUSSI le local
   streaming_ne_rend_pas_le_local ... FAILED
   assertion failed: !FiltreSources::depuis(Some(JETON_SERVICES)).local_demande()
   → 4 passed, 1 failed
```

body:
## Ringkasan

Branch ini membawa aplikasi SPR dari laptop (Laragon) ke produksi di UGREEN NAS DXP2800, diakses lewat HTTPS Tailscale, plus sejumlah fitur dan perbaikan UI. Semua isi branch sudah **berjalan di NAS** (deploy nyata 16 September 2026).

Catatan: branch ini berangkat dari `feat/proposal-word-pdf-and-rework` (PR #1), jadi riwayatnya ikut menyertakan commit dari branch tersebut.

## Deploy & infrastruktur

- **`Dockerfile`** — base image di-pin ke `php:8.3-fpm-bookworm`. Tag generik `php:8.3-fpm` sempat berpindah ke Debian baru dengan LibreOffice 25.2, dan itu membuat PDF proposal ter-generate tanpa isi. Bookworm memakai LibreOffice 7.4.7.2 yang terbukti jalan.
- **`Dockerfile`** — tambah `chmod -R a+rX /var/www/html`. File yang disalin dari Windows lewat SMB mendarat sebagai `770 root:root`, sehingga nginx/php-fpm (`www-data`) tidak bisa membaca `public/index.php` dan server membalas 403/404.
- **`docker/nginx.conf`** — teruskan `HTTP_HOST` berikut portnya. Tanpa ini Laravel mengira aplikasi berjalan di port 80, sehingga redirect dan URL asset kehilangan `:8080`; browser lalu mendarat di panel UGOS (port 80 dialihkan ke 9443) dan halaman tampil tanpa CSS.
- **`bootstrap/app.php`** — `trustProxies`, supaya URL asset dan redirect ikut `https://` saat diakses lewat Tailscale Serve. Akses langsung lewat IP LAN tetap normal.
- **`docker-compose.yml`** — service `tailscale` opsional (profile `tailscale`, `network_mode: host`), plus variabel `TS_HOSTNAME`/`TS_AUTHKEY` di `docker/env.nas.example`.

## Fitur

- **Penilai lapangan 1–3 orang setara** — tabel `project_appraisers`. Semua penilai dianggap pemilik proyek di Beranda, filter Proyek Saya, Timeline, export Excel, dan notifikasi WhatsApp.
- **Foto profil** — unggah dengan editor crop (geser, zoom, cubit di HP), hasil dipotong 512×512 dan dikompres ulang di server, foto lama otomatis dihapus. Ikon edit/hapus menempel di lingkaran foto.
- **Favicon** — logo SPR persegi di semua halaman, plus `favicon.ico` untuk halaman error bawaan.
- **Nomor WhatsApp** dipindah ke bawah Password pada form Tambah/Edit User.

## Perbaikan

- Cegah klik ganda pada form POST, plus penolakan invoice duplikat dalam 30 detik di server.
- Penilai lapangan & Surat Tugas terkunci sampai pekerjaan benar-benar dimulai, untuk kedua skema pembayaran.
- Tombol aksi di List Project diringkas jadi **Excel** (outline) + **Proposal Baru** (solid), ukuran kecil, tinggi seragam.

## Dokumentasi & tooling

- `docs/tutorial-deploy-nas-tailscale.md` — tutorial lengkap deploy NAS via Tailscale, termasuk semua jebakan yang ditemukan saat deploy nyata.
- `.claude/skills/` — skill Caveman dipasang di tingkat proyek.
- `.gitignore` — dump `.sql` dan folder `backups/` diabaikan agar data klien tidak pernah masuk repo.

## Catatan untuk reviewer

- Ada dua migrasi baru: `2024_01_23_000010_create_project_appraisers_table` (dengan backfill dari `assigned_appraiser_id`) dan `2024_01_23_000011_add_avatar_path_to_users`.
- Pengujian dilakukan lewat skrip yang selalu di-rollback, ditambah pemeriksaan render halaman di browser pada lebar desktop dan 375px.
- Belum ada automated test untuk perubahan ini.

body:
## 변경

매 실패마다 오류 알림이 나가 일시적 실패(예: `Page.goto: Timeout 30000ms exceeded`, 다음 실행에서 자동 복구)가 그대로 노출되던 것을 정리한다.

- `fail_count == ALERT_FAIL_THRESHOLD`(기본 3)째에 `/error` 1회. 그 이후(4회)는 조용
- `fail_count >= MAX_FAIL_COUNT`(기본 5): 비활성화 + `disabled=true`로 알림 (기존엔 조용히 꺼졌음). 임계치와 같은 횟수면 한 번만 발송
- 알림이 나간 뒤(직전 `fail_count >= 임계치`) 성공하면 `/recovered` 발송. 이를 위해 `db.update_success`가 리셋 직전 `fail_count`를 반환 (`UPDATE ... FROM (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE)`, 로컬 Postgres 16으로 동작 확인)
- 알림 발송 실패는 크롤러 실패로 집계하지 않음 (복구 알림은 try 밖에서 발송)

`run_batch` 경로는 범위 밖 → #3

## 배포 순서

sender가 `/recovered`를 아직 모르면 404(무시됨), 추가된 `disabled` 필드는 구버전 sender가 무시하므로 순서 강제는 없다. 다만 실제 알림이 운영 채널로 가려면 watch-sender / watch-infra PR과 서버 `.env`의 `ALERT_DESTINATION_ID` 설정이 필요하다.

## 검증

- `pytest` 45개 통과 (신규 16개)
- Slack 실발송 end-to-end는 미확인

body:
Refs #26. **Fallback, not a fix.** The gate suite stays off on macOS 15, as on `main`, but the skip now prints its reason instead of a bare "skipped".

## What changed (net against the merge base 39e550c)
Only `Tests/MarsDawnKitTests/MarkdownParsingTests.swift`: `WorkerGateTests` goes from `@Suite(.enabled(if: runtimeAnswersExecutorQuestions))` to the same condition with a comment string, plus an updated source comment. The CI experiment commits on this branch are reverted: `git diff 39e550c HEAD --stat` shows that one file.

## Why the earlier version (enable 5 of 6 gate tests) was withdrawn
The refutation (issuecomment-5741782885) saw a macos-15 debug run die with signal 5 in `ScopedFileReaderTests.refusesAFIFOWithoutHanging`. CI experiments on macos-15 (runs 35444353074, 35445250665, 35445595580, 35446184467) found:
- It is **not** order poisoning by the gate tests. On that branch the FIFO test traps **run alone** (`swift test --no-parallel --filter refusesAFIFOWithoutHanging`).
- The crash is `closure #1 in refusesAFIFOWithoutHanging` → `swift_task_isCurrentExecutorWithFlagsImpl` → `dispatch_assert_queue` → `_dispatch_assert_queue_fail`. Disassembly on the runner shows the `Thread { }` closure compiled as `@Sendable @MainActor` (mangled `yyYbScMYcc`). Its prologue checks `MainActor.shared.unownedExecutor` with `swift_task_isCurrentExecutor`. The same happens for `Thread { }` written in a file-scope function.
- `SWIFT_IS_CURRENT_EXECUTOR_LEGACY_MODE_OVERRIDE=legacy` makes the lone run **pass**. `=swift6` makes it trap. So the trap is the runtime's swift6 (crashing) check mode.
- **The same lone run on `main`'s tree (39e550c) passes**, as do the whole `ScopedFileReaderTests` suite and `headingsAreCollectedOnAParsingWorker`. Something in the enable-the-gate branch makes the process pick the crashing mode. I have not found what. That is what's left for #26.

## Verify (GitHub only)
1. The PR's CI: `test (macos-15)` and `test (macos-26)` both green, each running `swift test --no-parallel` and `swift test -c release --no-parallel`.
2. In the macos-15 job log, the skip line for `WorkerGateTests` carries the text "macOS 15's Concurrency runtime kills the test process…(mars-dawn-kit#26)". On macos-26 the suite runs, and its tests appear as passed.
3. `git diff 39e550c HEAD --stat` touches only `MarkdownParsingTests.swift`.

No GUI steps: the change is test-only.

author: alexislaporte
body:
## Résumé

Trois signaux `feedback` (agents, via `oto_admin_signal`) groupés sur `data_write`, traités indépendamment.

## Bug 1 (#1015) — colonne non déclarée stockée malgré `strict:true`/`unknown_fields:"reject"` : **non reproduit, documenté**

Le signaleur avait déjà testé et confirmé le refus sur `row=`, `rows=`, et `id=`+`_run_id=` — les trois formes d'écriture qu'il pouvait tester. J'ai vérifié le code : `_check_row`/`off_schema_refusal` sont câblés aux **cinq** sites d'appel qui existent dans `oto_mcp/datastore/` (`ecriture.py` ×3, `ecriture_par_id.py`, `lots.py`) — un seam unique documenté comme voyant « TOUS les chemins d'écriture ». Aucun chemin d'écriture actuel du datastore ne contourne cette garde.

La ligne incriminée (une colonne `error` avec un monologue d'agent, sans couche `origine`) est très probablement une donnée **antérieure** à la pose de `unknown_fields: "reject"` sur ce tableau — cohérent avec la mesure du signaleur lui-même sur le même tableau (189 clés hors schéma, 34 avec valeur réelle, aux noms d'une ancienne génération de procédure). Pas de correctif forcé : rien à corriger dans le code actuel sans preuve d'un chemin qui contourne la garde.

## Bug 2 (#923) — update partiel refusé par des cellules HÉRITÉES non touchées : **corrigé**

`types_trahis` (armée le 08/09) jugeait tout le row **mergé**, pas seulement les colonnes écrites par le geste — contrairement à ses fonctions sœurs `etats_trahis`/`couches_manquantes`, bornées à `written` depuis le 07/09 pour la même raison (documentée dans le docstring de `validate_row`, qui déclarait déjà l'intention sans que le code la tienne). Un patch partiel se heurtait donc à une valeur héritée invalide qu'il ne touchait pas, avec un message trompeur (« `ca` … reçoit … » comme si l'appel l'avait envoyée).

Fix : `types_trahis(schema, merged, written=, gelees=)`, même patron que `etats_trahis` — une colonne hors type NON écrite par le geste va dans `gelees` (signalée, jamais bloquante) au lieu de `errors`.

## Bug 3 (#994) — clé métier `@empty` en conflit → 500 interne : **corrigé**

Une clé posée à `@empty`/`@clear` (« vide assumé ») n'est pas indexée comme la donnée réelle — la cellule stockée porte le marqueur de vide assumé, pas le mot réservé littéral. Deux lignes vidées sur la même colonne violent donc l'index UNIQUE de clé métier sans que la recherche exacte de convergence (course perdue) ne les retrouve jamais l'une l'autre : le code relançait alors l'exception driver brute (`UniqueViolation`), jamais convertie en refus nommé.

Fix (`ecriture.py` + `lots.py`, écriture unitaire et lot) : quand une clé DÉCLARÉE existe mais que la recherche de convergence échoue, refus `ValueError` nommé expliquant la cause probable. Le cas « aucune clé déclarée » (violation vraiment inexpliquée) garde son `raise` nu inchangé — tests de régression existants préservés.

## Schéma / environnement

Ni l'un ni l'autre — changements Python purs, aucun DDL, aucune nouvelle variable.

## Tests

- `tests/datastore/test_types_declares_written_scope_923.py` (nouveau, 3 tests) : héritée invalide → gelée pas bloquante ; écrite → toujours refusée ; insert sans `written` → comportement inchangé.
- `tests/datastore/test_datastore_business_key.py` (+2 tests) : conflit `@empty` en lot et en écriture unitaire → `ValueError` nommé, jamais `UniqueViolation` brute. Rouge avant/vert après vérifié explicitement (`git stash` du correctif).
- Suite complète `tests/datastore/` : 1928/1928 verts, aucune régression (les tests existants sur violations "vraiment inexpliquées" sans clé déclarée continuent de passer).

author: jmevatt
body:
Closes #111. Second of three in the **"Manifest fields that do nothing"**
milestone.

## What it was

`Root.Hooks` — a path to a JavaScript file the JavaScript CLI would have
loaded. That CLI was removed in #154; the field outlived it as a struct member
with no reader. AGENTS.md's own test, grep the name outside its definition:

```
$ grep -rn '\.Hooks\b' --include='*.go' . | grep -v _test.go | grep -v types.go
(nothing)
```

No real manifest declares it. The only place it appeared was the blueprint
fixture, advertising a mechanism that did not exist — the same thing #199
found for `plugins:`.

## Removed, not implemented

#111 offered both. The plugin runtime an implementation would sit on has since
landed (#202, #205), so "wait for plugin work" is no longer the reason. The
reason is that lifecycle hooks need lifecycle points, and the Go codebase has
none — no `configure`/`seed`/`open` moment exists for a hook to attach to.
Inventing those so a dead field has something to do is backwards. If hooks
return, they return as plugin provisions at points that exist because
something needed them.

## Now

```
$ kraai plan dev
kraai.yaml:2: (root): unknown field "hooks"
```

With the file and line, since strict decoding catches it — which is what a key
that does nothing should have done from the start.

Three lines changed: the field, one test assertion, one fixture line.

author: eldad-caura
body:
Closes enterprise finding `ent-060`. It has to be fixed **here** rather than in caura-enterprise: `common/events/pubsub.py` is vendored there, so patching the copy would be drift.

## What was actually wrong

`publish()` fires into the client's batch queue and returns without blocking on the returned Future. The comment there explains why at length, and it is right: `.result(timeout=30)` would tie up a `publish_concurrency` thread on a slow Pub/Sub, and admin-API request handlers await this call, so a sustained outage would wedge them.

**That stays. What was wrong is that the Future was then discarded.** A publisher-side failure — a 403 on the topic, an exhausted quota — produced log lines from a `google.cloud` logger and nothing this platform watches, while `is_healthy` stayed true because every condition it checks is about the pull side.

## The fix

A done-callback, which closes the gap without reintroducing the blocking the comment exists to prevent: it runs on the SDK's own commit thread when the batch settles, so `publish()` still returns as soon as the message is queued. There is a test for exactly that.

It logs at ERROR with **`dropped=True`** — the field five other places in `common/events` already use to mark an event lost, so existing log-based alerting covers this path with **no new rule**. A publish that failed *is* a dropped event: there is no queue to return it to, because it never reached one.

**Deliberately not flipped into `is_healthy`.** That drives readiness, and draining a pod from the load balancer on one transient publish failure trades a lost event for an outage, and would flap.

## A docstring that was wrong

`is_healthy` opened:

> True when the bus is in a state where it can still deliver events **end-to-end**.

It is not end-to-end. A publisher-only bus whose every publish is 403ing reports healthy, because nothing in that function looks at publishing. Now says so, and says where publish failures surface instead.

## On the finding's wording

`ent-060` called publisher-side failures "permanently invisible". That overstated it — the SDK's own logger did record them, and the audit's own residual note already said as much. The real gap was an **app-level** signal, which is what this adds. Worth stating plainly rather than quietly fixing something narrower than the ticket claimed.

## Evidence

5 tests. Only `test_a_failed_publish_is_logged_as_a_dropped_event` distinguishes before from after — verified failing with the Future discarded again:

```
E  AssertionError: a publish that failed produced no app-level signal;
   the SDK's own logger is the only thing that saw it
1 failed, 4 passed
```

The other four pass either way **by design**, and the module docstring says so: they guard the properties the fix had to preserve (publish stays non-blocking, readiness does not flip) and the ways it could have been wrong without failing a test (logging unconditionally, raising on the SDK's thread where an exception is swallowed and would make the failure *more* invisible).

They use a real `concurrent.futures.Future`, not the shared fixture's `MagicMock` — whose `add_done_callback` records the call and never invokes it, so the callback would never have run.

## Gates

`ruff check` clean across the full CI scope; `ruff format --check` clean on the same minus `common/`, plus `--isolated` on the three `common/` files CI checks. mypy: core-storage-api and core-operations clean; core-api and core-worker each report the 2 standing errors in `common/llm/providers/openai.py` (the httpx/openai conflict) — verified identical on a clean `origin/main` checkout. `gen_events_manifest.py --check`: up to date. Legacy-name ratchet: no new lines. Suites: events **165 → 170**, core-worker **100**, root **31 failed / 7187 passed** — 31 is the standing baseline.

## ⚠️ Enterprise follow-up this creates

`common/events/pubsub.py` is a **`manual`** entry in caura-enterprise's `vendored_files_manifest.json`. Merging this moves the OSS baseline, so that repo's drift gate will fail on every PR until someone reconciles it:

```
FAIL  common/events/pubsub.py: OSS SOURCE MOVED since this copy was last reconciled
```

The 6-hourly re-vendor bot will **not** do it — it skips manual entries by design. That is the same loop that went stale this morning and turned every enterprise PR red. It needs a deliberate re-vendor, and enterprise's copy carries its own divergence (the `DeliveryMetadata` / `DiscardHandler` discard API) that has to be preserved through it.

body:
Closes out the final open slivers of tasks 55 and 58 with their resolved scope:

- **55 archive repair**: Ruby's `archive_repair` is RAR recovery-record repair only — every other format prints "not supported". Porting it means RAR5 RR/RS record parsing + recovery inside `omnizip-rar`, which is **blocked on fixtures**: the local `rar` binary is Gatekeeper-killed, so recovery-record archives cannot be created locally. Unblock via CI (apt `rar` on an ubuntu runner) or the libarchive corpus. The parity commands shipped earlier are the general recovery story.
- **58 archive-level parallelism**: a design pass is required before any code — extract needs readers whose `read_entry` works concurrently (Sync-ification: shared immutable buffer + per-entry offsets snapshot); create needs writer-level compress-concurrent/emit-serialized support, with output pinned to entry-list order. The workspace invariants (determinism, bounded work) outrank the speedup; the doc records the refactor plan so it is not parallelized around.

author: aedefruscio
body:
## What
Phase 1 ledger **L-3**: `model_general` (deepseek-v4-pro:cloud) landed **exactly on its `num_predict` in 13 % of calls** over 14 days — at every caller's budget (1024 / 2048 / 2500 / 3000 / 8192) — with nothing usable back: `done_reason='length'`, empty or truncated content. Each such draw is 10–25 s for nothing; 116 on 2026-09-18 alone. The existing §17.1053 (tool_call) and §17.876 (generate/chat) rescues switch to `think=False` only **after** the wasted draw, on that one call, so every call pays again.

## Fix
`app/utils/think_policy.py` — a per-model, windowed memory:
- `note_starved_draw(model)` records a starved draw (length stop + empty content, or truncated content with a non-empty `thinking` field, §17.877).
- `think_default(model)` answers `False` once a model has starved `think_off_after_starved_draws` (2) times within `think_off_window_minutes` (60), `None` (model default) otherwise. **Explicit `think=` is never overridden.** The window decays, so a model that stops starving gets its chain-of-thought back (`think_policy_restored`).
- Wired into `model_router.generate`, `chat`, and `tool_call`: when the caller left `think` unset, the policy fills it in from the first draw; every draw is inspected for starvation. Logs `think_policy_flipped` once per flip.

## Tests
`tests/test_think_policy.py` (+9). Model-router / retry / tool-call suites: 198 passed. `make ci-tier-0` green.

## Proof plan
After deploy: the durable metric is the share of `llm_call_logs` rows landing exactly on a budget (before: 13.4 % for deepseek over 14 days). A live hit needs a real starved draw; reported in the merge note either way.

author: lemybetheone
body:
Run before making the repository public, because **checking the current tree is
not the same as checking history**: a file committed and later removed stays
reachable by SHA. That distinction is why a previous project's repository had to
be deleted and recreated rather than force-pushed.

All **82 commits** searched, by path and by content.

## No credential has ever been committed

| Checked | Result |
|---|---|
| `PROFILE.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `*.private.md`, `.env` | never in any commit |
| `WAREHOUSE_PASSWORD`, `REPORTING_PASSWORD` | never in any commit |
| `AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID`, `AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`, `WAREHOUSE_USER` | never in any commit |
| `AKIA…`, `ghp_…`, `sk-…`, `xox…`, PEM private keys | none, anywhere |
| `.env.example` | blank placeholders in **every** version it has ever had |
| `dbt/profiles.yml` | `env_var()` only, in every version |

The secret values were searched **by their live content**, not by variable name —
searching for the string `WAREHOUSE_PASSWORD` would prove nothing, since the
point is whether the *value* ever landed in a blob.

**That method is why the sweep was worth running.** A check of the current tree
would have returned "clean" and been useless: the one finding below was already
absent from `HEAD`.

## The one exception

The **S3 bucket name** appears in 8 historical blobs of
`context/SECURITY_AND_GOVERNANCE.md`. The no-identifiers rule was introduced by
`e219fea — docs: keep concrete resource identifiers out of the repository`, which
removed it from the working tree. Commits before that still carry it.

**Accepted rather than purged**, and the reasoning is recorded rather than
assumed:

- **It is an identifier, not a credential.** The bucket blocks public access and
  is reached only by a scoped IAM user with no `DeleteObject`. Nothing in history
  grants access to anything.
- **Purging costs more than it buys.** Rewriting all 82 commits changes every
  SHA; deleting and recreating the repository destroys **25 pull requests** whose
  descriptions record the reasoning behind most of the decisions in this project.
  That history is a more valuable asset than a private bucket's name is a
  liability.

### What it constrains

SECURITY §3 already named the residual risk: **a deleted bucket name can be
claimed by someone else.** So this bucket must be renamed or replaced rather than
simply deleted. Renaming it at any convenient point makes the historical mention
inert — the cheap fix, whenever it suits.

The rule itself is unchanged for everything written from here on.

## A note on how it is recorded

Both the SECURITY amendment and decision 42 **deliberately avoid restating the
bucket name**, which would have been a self-defeating way to document the
exception. Verified after committing: the name does not appear in `HEAD`.

A security document that says "we found nothing" is unfalsifiable. One that says
"we found this, here is why it was accepted, and here is the constraint that
creates" can actually be audited — the same instinct as a decision log recording
what was rejected.

## Decisions added

42 (accept the historical mention; rename rather than delete the bucket).

author: rrahimi-uci
body:
## Summary

`docs/workspace-plan.md` section 16's `P2-E` row flagged the residual part of item 7 ("route Aria capabilities and durable plan execution through the central authorization contract"): the already-delivered part wired `require_project_access_if_scoped`/`resource.execute` onto `routes/aria_plans.py::execute_plan`/`poll_plan`, and `assistant/agent_tools.py::_dispatch_capability` now consults `scopes_for_user` per call — but every one of these checks was re-derived live on each call, with nothing persisted onto the `CaliberAriaPlan`/`CaliberAriaPlanStep` rows themselves for after-the-fact auditability ("under what authorization did this plan/step actually run").

This PR closes that gap, mirroring the exact precedent the task pointed at: `db/models.py::CaliberWorkspaceReleaseDecision`, which snapshots `actor_role_snapshot`/`effective_scope_snapshot` at decision time in `workspace_release_governance.py::record_workspace_release_decision`, alongside — not instead of — its own fresh CAS checks.

**What's persisted, and where:**

- **Plan-level** (`CaliberAriaPlan.actor_role_snapshot` / `.effective_scope_snapshot` / `.authorization_recorded_at`): recorded **once**, the first time a shared `_authorize_plan_execution` helper (now used by both `execute_plan` and `poll_plan`) clears the plan's `resource.execute` check. `actor_role_snapshot` is `None` for a personal (`project_id is None`) plan, which has no project role to snapshot; `effective_scope_snapshot` (the caller's scopes + `POLICY_VERSION`) is always recorded. A later `execute`/`poll` call that re-passes the still-live check does **not** overwrite the snapshot — it records what *first* authorized the plan, not a rolling cache.
- **Step-level** (`CaliberAriaPlanStep.capability_scope_decision`): recorded by `PlanExecutor` at **both** places it already checks a capability's declared `required_scopes` against the plan owner — `_plan_next_action`'s early-admission check (fails the step before it's ever selected to run) and `_run_step`'s own re-check immediately before dispatch (a defense-in-depth re-derivation against the scope landscape changing in between). Both call sites now share one `_capability_scope_decision` helper so the exact same decision shape (`required_scopes`, `checked_scopes`, `checked_against`, `missing_scopes`, `satisfied`, `policy_version`) is persisted regardless of which check catches a denial.

**What's deliberately unchanged:** the live per-call checks. `execute_plan`/`poll_plan` and `PlanExecutor` keep re-deriving authorization on every call — a still-active plan's authorization can genuinely change between calls (a role edit, a membership change), so re-deriving live stays the safer default. The snapshot exists purely for auditability, not as a cached replacement, the same judgment `CaliberWorkspaceReleaseDecision` applies alongside its own fresh CAS checks.

**A deliberate scope boundary, not a gap:** `assistant/agent_tools.py::_dispatch_capability` (the synchronous per-turn tool-call path) gets **no** snapshot. Reading it in full showed `AgentToolset` carries a `session_id` and an acting identity, not a `plan_id` — this dispatch path can run with no `CaliberAriaPlan`/`CaliberAriaPlanStep` row in existence at all (it's the live chat tool-calling loop, not bound to any Aria plan). There is no durable row to attach a snapshot to without inventing a new mechanism outside this task's actual scope ("mirror `CaliberWorkspaceReleaseDecision` onto `CaliberAriaPlan`/`Step`"). This check stays live-only/re-derived, and both the code (a new comment at the check site) and `docs/workspace-plan.md`'s `P2-E` row say so explicitly rather than glossing over it.

author: mrmps
body:
`/admin` could not be opened in Chrome. Driving a real headless Chrome against production shows why:

    POST https://classifier.dev/admin
      wire headers: { cookie: '__Secure-cd_csrf=8a2d…', origin: 'null' }
      <- 403   "Bad request origin."

A page that sends `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer` — which the login page does — has the origin of its form posts serialized to the literal string `null`. So the header that already stripped Referer takes `Origin` with it. The site did this to itself, and the door has been shut in a real browser since those headers went in; only `curl`, which states a real `Origin`, could get through.

`new URL("null")` throws, so #32 classified it as a *mismatched* origin and refused outright — the token fallback it had just added never got to run, even though the cookie and the field were both right there in the request.

## What changed

`Origin: null` is now read as what it is: the browser declining to say, not a wrong answer. That routes it to the form token, which is the case the token was built for.

It is never a pass on its own — a sandboxed frame sends `Origin: null` too, so it only buys the right to be asked for the token, and a cross-site post cannot produce one: it cannot read the field, and `SameSite=Strict` keeps the cookie at home.

## Checks

`tsc` clean, 153 tests pass, including `Origin: null` with a valid token (302) and `Origin: null` without one (403).

Verified against production after deploy with the same headless Chrome that reproduced the failure.

author: keeganhall33
body:
## Why
The canonical V1 release certificate currently accepts a gate as mechanically passing when its evidence says `state: PASS` even if the same record says `actionRequirement: KEEGAN` or `UNKNOWN`. That is an internal truth conflict: a release gate cannot be complete while an unresolved or unknown required action still exists. In the worst case, otherwise valid evidence plus final acceptance could allow the certificate to reach `RELEASED` despite that unresolved gate action.

## What
- add `GATE_UNRESOLVED_ACTION_REQUIREMENT` to the release-certificate blocker contract
- fail closed whenever a gate claims `PASS` while `actionRequirement` is anything other than `NONE`
- preserve the action owner in blocker output, so `KEEGAN` remains an explicit Keegan action and `UNKNOWN` remains unknown rather than being silently cleared
- ensure the corresponding certified gate claim remains false and final acceptance cannot override a mechanically blocked gate
- add focused regression coverage for both `KEEGAN` and `UNKNOWN` action states

## Guardrails
- no deployment, production, mailbox, CRM, approval, or external mutation authority is added
- no live evidence is fabricated or upgraded
- existing state, freshness, exact-SHA, timestamp, provenance, privacy, and final-acceptance checks remain unchanged
- correctly complete gates with `actionRequirement: NONE` are unaffected

## Coordination
Inspected current `main`, open PRs/issues, exact-main CI/status, recent release failures, and active V1 file ownership first. #1990, #1997, #2003, #2010, #2016, and #2023 own separate paths. This PR changes only:
- `src/lib/release/v1-release-certificate-v1.ts`
- `test/release/v1-release-gate-action-requirement-v1.test.tsx`

Current external release blockers remain separate: Vercel production propagation is rate-limited for current `main`, and the live IONOS three-mailbox proof still requires the authorized Mac/1Password runtime.

## Validation
Exact-head CI required: TypeScript, focused/unit suite, production build, diff hygiene, zero unresolved review threads, and independent exact-head review before merge.

Advances #1458.

KEEGAN_ACTION_REQUIRED=NO.

author: wlrnjs
body:
## 무엇을 구현했나

폴더 화면·채팅·추천에서 요청마다 GitHub 레포 트리와 파일 본문을 다시 받던 걸 캐시로 바꿨어요.

- **트리**: 요청마다 `branches/{branch}` 로 HEAD 커밋 sha 만 받고, 트리는 `설치 id + owner + repo + 커밋 sha` 키로 `unstable_cache` 에 넣어요. 커밋이 바뀌면 키가 바뀌어서 새로 받아요.
- **캐시 크기**: 소스·테스트·tsconfig 의 `[경로, 크기, blob sha]` 만 저장하고, 나머지 파일은 `totalBytes` 합계에만 넣어요. 2MB 를 넘으면 캐시하지 않고 받은 값을 그대로 써요(`lib/github/content-cache.ts`).
- **파일 본문**(`blob.ts`): 트리에 blob sha 가 있으면 blob sha 키로 캐시하고 `git/blobs` 로 받아요. 트리에 없는 파일은 전처럼 contents API 를 캐시 없이 써요. 내용이 바뀌지 않는 키라서 push 직후 옛 내용이 보일 일은 없어요.
- **요청 안 중복 제거**: 라우트 핸들러(채팅)에서는 React `cache` 가 기억하지 않아서, 한 턴에 브랜치 조회가 4번 나갔어요. repo 객체 키 WeakMap 을 더해 1번으로 줄였어요.

샘플 레포 dev 서버 로그 기준이에요.

| 요청 | 전 | 후 |
|---|---|---|
| 폴더 파일 열기 (요청당) | `git/trees` 1 + contents 1~2 | `branches` 1 (다시 여는 파일은 blob 0) |
| 폴더 응답 시간 | 약 740~770ms | 약 440~600ms |
| 채팅 한 턴 | `git/trees` 2 + contents 2 | `branches` 1 |

## 참고사항

- `meta.sizes` 에는 이제 소스·테스트·tsconfig 만 있어요. 호출처가 찾는 파일이 이것뿐이라 동작은 같아요. `meta.shas` 를 새로 추가했어요.
- 권한 경계: 두 캐시 키 모두 설치 id 를 넣었어요. 캐시를 쓰기 전에 그 프로젝트 설치 토큰으로 브랜치 조회가 먼저 성공해야 하고, 캐시에는 토큰을 넣지 않아요.
- 새 커밋 sha 가 처음 쓰일 때 동시 요청이 모두 miss 되는 건 그대로 뒀어요. push 직후 한 번만 생겨요.
- 확인 못 한 것: 폴더 화면에서 실제 클릭으로 파일 이동(`?file=` 전체 로드로 대신 확인), 헤더 파일 검색 UI(API 는 200 확인), 트리가 truncated 되거나 2MB 를 넘는 큰 레포.


## 체크리스트

- [x] 로컬에서 `pnpm lint && pnpm typecheck && pnpm build` 통과 (또는 CI 초록불)
- [x] 새 npm 패키지 추가 안 함 (했으면 참고사항에 이유)
- [x] 1 PR = 1 목적 — 관련 없는 변경 안 섞음

author: alter-yash
body:
#### What type of PR is this?

/kind bug

#### What this PR does / why we need it:

When `--label` flags are provided on the `buildah build` or `podman build` CLI, Buildah synthesizes a `LABEL` instruction line and appends it to the list of build instructions for `imagebuilder`.

Because `imagebuilder` performs shell-style word expansion, literal `$` characters in label values (e.g., `--label foo='$5 off'`) were being evaluated as variable references and dropped when unresolved.

This PR escapes literal `$` characters as `\$` in the generated instruction line, ensuring `imagebuilder` preserves `$` as literal text without affecting other characters or existing escaping behavior.

#### How to verify it

1. Build a container image using a label containing a `$` character:

   ```bash
   echo "FROM busybox" > Dockerfile
   ./bin/buildah build -t test-label . --label 'test=$something'
   ```

2. Inspect the image annotations/labels to verify `$` was preserved:

   ```bash
   ./bin/buildah inspect --format '{{ index .ImageAnnotations "test" }}' test-label
   ```

   **Expected output:**

   ```text
   $something
   ```

#### Which issue(s) this PR fixes:

Fixes [https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29095](https://github.com/podman-container-tools/podman/issues/29095)

#### Special notes for your reviewer:

This bug was reported in the Podman repository (`podman-container-tools/podman`), but the issue resides in Buildah's synthesized instruction parsing before handing them off to `imagebuilder`.

#### Does this PR introduce a user-facing change?

Yes.

Fixed an issue where literal `$` characters in CLI `--label` values were stripped during build instruction expansion.

author: sorsama
body:
Fixes #25.

Answering a question card or an approval never worked against any harness 0.1.2 or later. Tapping Submit failed instantly with the red footer "Could not reach the harness.", the tool call on the host stayed blocked, and the only way past it was to stop the turn and send the choice as an ordinary message. Chat and every other unary call in the same session were fine, which is what made this look like a connection fault rather than a protocol one.

## Cause

`$events/result` is an ordinary Remote, so its three fields ride inside the same `args` object every other call uses. `answerEvent` posted them bare:

```kotlin
): RpcResult<JsonElement> = unary(
    REMOTE_EVENT_RESULT_ENDPOINT,
    encodeToJsonElement(                       // {clientId, eventId, outcome}, no wrapper
        RemoteEventResult.serializer(),
        RemoteEventResult(clientId = clientId, eventId = eventId, outcome = outcome),
    ),
    JsonElement.serializer(),
)
```

It was the only call in `DshApiClient` that did not go through `call()`, which is where the wrapping happens. The gateway answers a bare payload with `ok:false` / `gateway/internal` and the message *Remote event result requires exactly one plain-object args field*, inside an HTTP 200 — so nothing logs a refusal at the relay or transport layer either.

Unchanged since the 0.1.2 baseline move in `286f26e8`, so every release from 0.8.0 on has it.

## Fix

`answerEvent` goes through `call()` like the rest, and its doc comment says why that path is load-bearing rather than tidy.

`SessionStore.answerOutcome` also stopped reporting host refusals as network failures. It matched the literal code `not-pending` and folded everything else into `QuestionOutcome.Unsent`, which is what put "Could not reach the harness." under a request that reached the harness and came back refused. The split is now whether the host answered at all: an error carrying a `TransportFailure` marker is a carrier failure and stays `Unsent`, anything else is `Refused` with the host's own code, which the card already renders. A malformed envelope now reads "The harness would not accept that answer (gateway/internal)" instead of sending the reporter off to debug their Wi-Fi.

## Why the tests never caught it

The mock harness was written from this client rather than from the host, so it documented and enforced the app's shape: `judgeEventResult` read `clientId`, `eventId` and `outcome` straight off the payload with no `args` step. Both halves of the repo agreed with each other on a payload no harness would take. The existing conformance tests pin the answer *value* encoding, which was correct all along — the defect sat one envelope level out.

The mock now requires the wrapper and refuses a bare payload with the gateway's own code and wording. Three new tests pin it from both directions: the client's envelope in `QuestionResponseEncodingTest`, the mock's refusal in `MockHarnessTest`, and the pre-fix wire shape posted raw over a socket in `ProtocolEndToEndTest`, since the typed client can no longer express it.

## Also

- `docs/PROTOCOL.md` showed the bare payload in its worked example, which is where the wrong shape was ratified; it now shows `args` and names the refusal.
- `docs/COMPATIBILITY.md` gains the same clause, and its support table marks 0.11.1 and 0.11.2 as unable to answer questions or approvals against a harness 0.1.2 or later.
- Version bumped to 0.11.3 with a changelog entry.

## Testing

380 unit tests pass across `:core`, `:mock-harness` and `:app`, three of them new. `:app:lintDebug` and `:app:assembleDebug` are clean.

Not yet driven on a device against a live harness. Worth doing before tagging, since the mock agreeing with the app is the exact failure this PR is about and a fresh mock test cannot rule it out a second time.

Reported by @djurcola, who traced it to `answerEvent`, reproduced the rejection with curl against a real harness both through the relay and directly, and confirmed that the same call parses with the wrapper.

body:
## HOLD — do not merge this draft

Operation `uiowa-059-oriel27-20260919`; ZZ-ORIEL-27 / GPT-6 Astra Pro. Tracks #16112.

The eight-file implementation is retained at `85e86e534442916313a544d12ce5f71619e12ff0`, package subtree `1d05e8a46e45e32576e035307221bd3132d320cd` (60,802 bytes). It includes the offline engine/CLI, synthetic fixtures, schema, metadata template, interpretation guide, interview worksheet and 25 retained tests. Exact provider blob readback matched cloud execution: 25 normal and 25 optimized tests passed. **Those tests missed the chronology defect subsequently found in source review; this head is not approved.**

### Unresolved source findings
1. Non-ASCII year digits can pass calendar parsing but violate the lexicographic timestamp assumptions used to select the latest observation. The runtime and structural schema need one canonical ASCII-digit timestamp contract, with retained regression coverage.
2. The uncorroborated-disposal diagnostic overstates absence when older supporting records exist but later observations leave the current state unresolved. The diagnostic must preserve that distinction and retained history.

A local repair passed 27 normal and 27 optimized tests, but publication of the corrected source was blocked twice, including one unchanged retry, by the tool-layer response:

> This tool call was blocked by OpenAI because we couldn't determine the safety status of the request.

This was not a GitHub authentication or repository-permission error. The corrected bytes have **not** reached this branch, no new head exists, and no merge or hosted-CI success is claimed. The draft preserves the published original and the source-review findings; it must not be integrated as the repaired generation. The separately usable, non-executable interview worksheet can be delivered independently without treating this engine as complete.

### Scope retained
The intended engine uses metadata only; it does not read or delete data, access live systems, schedule anything, contact anyone, prescribe vendors, or determine compliance. Each copy has separate identity and disposition evidence. Written procedures, observations, contradictions and unknown evidence remain distinct. All ESS/RIS/IAM examples are fictional, not University findings.

Coordination: https://tokenjunkielabs.slack.com/archives/C0C2M1K2V4P/p1789824736853349 .
Source review: https://github.com/woahwhattheheck/commons/pull/16231#issuecomment-5742459026 .

author: andtii
body:
Closes #285.

## What was broken
`ask_user` held its question open inside one blocking tool call. Three things cut that call short:
- the engine's MCP tool timeout ("The operation timed out.");
- the daemon's 10-minute tool cap;
- the router closing the session at turn end.

After that, `Session.respond` returned `closed`, and the answer went nowhere.

## What changes
- **Async `ask_user` (runtimes + platform).**
  - In a chat, the tool waits `ASK_QUICK_WAIT_MS` (25 s) for a quick answer. After that it calls `Session.detachInput` and returns `{ status: 'pending', questionId, note }`.
  - The tool description tells the agent to end its turn.
  - `detachInput` is atomic with `respond`: an answer that beats the detach is returned as the result, never lost.
  - The daemon path gets the same behaviour: `createToolCallPort` now looks up the session's chat for `ask_user`.
- **Questions outlive the turn (Session).**
  - A detached request stays open. The close doesn't cancel it and `finishInterrupted` skips it.
  - `respond` accepts its answer even when the session is closed.
  - The answer is parked in `answeredDetached`. The `deliverAnswers` actor task hands it to the new `SessionPorts.answered` once the session is closed, outside any turn, and it is restarted after an eviction.
- **Restart with the answer (`routing/answers.ts`).** `createAnswerFollowUp`:
  1. posts the answer in the chat as the person who answered, mentioning the asker (`@Ada — re: “…” → …`);
  2. creates the asker's task with `answerContract`, whose origin is that message, whose context is the question, the answer and the chat, and which sets `resumeFrom` (merged in #297);
  3. runs it through `Routing.run`.

  The task id is deterministic, so a replayed answer starts nobody twice. A failure is posted in the chat (`answer-not-delivered:`).
- **Router.**
  - `resumeFrom` resumes the earlier engine conversation (`OpenSpec.resume` = the old session's `ref`) only when a daemon ran it for the same agent, runtime, environment and machine.
  - An API session opens fresh from the contract's context, because its transcript lives in its own Session record.
  - A task still `waiting {input}` on its own session at turn end is released, so it completes. Before, `waiting → completed` wasn't allowed and the task stayed stuck.
- **Chatless asks keep blocking** (a delegated child has no chat to be restarted in).
- **UI.**
  - `QuestionPrompt` takes a new `stale` prop, which shows "Ada has stopped waiting. Answering starts Ada again with your answer."
  - `DescribeRequestFn` can return `stale`.
  - The Inbox card and title name the agent instead of its id.
  - The live chat shows a card for each open question whose session has ended (`detachedQuestions`, with the session taken from the Inbox row), and names the asker on in-flight question cards.
- **Docs.** `docs/architecture.md` §5a, a `docs/decisions.md` entry, and the platform and runtimes READMEs.

## Acceptance
- [x] An `ask_user` answered long after the turn ended still reaches the asker, which continues with the answer (`ask-user.test.ts`, local and daemon paths).
- [x] No answer is silently dropped: each one is posted in the chat, and a restart failure is said there too.
- [x] Three agents asking at once each get their own answer (`three agents asking at once…`), and the cards and Inbox name who asked.
- [x] A question whose call has ended is shown as such (`detached` → `stale` note).
- [x] Tests:
  - platform: late answer restarts the asker; cancel starts nobody; replay starts nobody twice; detach/respond race; chatless still blocks; answer before close delivered at close; daemon resume ref;
  - runtimes: `pending` passes through;
  - UI: stale note and asker labels in `question.test.tsx`;
  - web: `detachedQuestions`.

## Verification
- `pnpm typecheck`, `pnpm lint`, `pnpm size` and `pnpm --filter @agentic/web test:workers` are green.
- `pnpm test` is green (221 files) after merging main, which now has the chat-list order fix (#247).
- Behaviour change: Inbox titles now use the agent's name (`Ada needs input`) instead of its id. Tests were updated to match.

author: iwandejong

author: antosubash
body:
Closes the "I want to host a demo instance" gap: turn `demo_mode` on and the sign-in card grows a button per demo account. One click signs a visitor straight in — no email, no password, no signup.

```
users.demo_mode        = true
users.demo_admin_email = demo-admin@example.com
users.demo_user_email  = demo-user@example.com
users.demo_read_only   = true       # default — keep it on
```

Set under **/admin/settings/ → Users**. Changes apply live: the existing `SettingsReloaded` handler re-seeds the accounts and refreshes the cached ids, so there is no restart.

## Two accounts, not one

An **administrator** and an ordinary **standard user**, because the two halves of the app look nothing alike. The admin surface — users, roles, settings, modules, audit history — is what the framework is *for*, and a visitor who only ever sees the end-user app never meets it. One who only ever sees `/admin/*` never meets the app you actually build for people. Offering both, and letting someone switch between them **without signing out**, is what makes a showcase instance answer "what is this?" in one visit.

Each is independently switchable: blank an email and that button disappears *and* its route starts answering 404. The offer and the endpoint come from the same resolution, so hiding a button can never leave a live way in behind it.

## Why it's three pieces, not one

A demo account is a **published credential** — the sign-in page hands it to whoever asks, and the admin one carries the whole admin surface. The account alone would mean publishing write access to the settings editor, the user table and maintenance mode, so the guard and the banner are part of the feature rather than follow-ups.

**`users/demo.py`** — resolves the configured accounts and reconciles their rows on every boot and every settings reload. It *reconciles*, not just creates: the admin row carries `is_superuser` and the `admin` role, the user row carries neither, and repointing an address from one to the other demotes it rather than leaving the old grant behind. One account failing to seed does not withdraw the other. A blank password is hashed from a random secret on create only, so that account is reachable solely through its button — no password reaches the browser. That is the difference from the existing dev quick-fill buttons, which paste real credentials into the form and are development-only for exactly this reason.

**`users/demo_guard.py`** — `DemoReadOnlyMiddleware` refuses every unsafe HTTP method from either demo session while `demo_read_only` is on (the default), except signing out, signing *in*, and the demo sign-in routes themselves.

- It reads the **session**, not `request.state.user`. `users` depends on `Auth`, so its middleware wraps outermost and runs *before* `AuthMiddleware` — reading the session cookie (already decoded by `SessionMiddleware`) means the guard needs nothing Auth provides, and refuses the write before any handler, middleware side-effect or DB session runs.
- It matches on the **user ids as well as** the stamp the demo endpoints write, which catches a visitor who signed in with a published demo password through the ordinary form.
- Inertia requests get the protocol's `409` + `X-Inertia-Location` instead of a raw `403` body — Inertia renders a non-Inertia response as a modal with the body in it, which on a showcase instance reads as a crash. `fetch` callers (how most of this app writes) get `403 {"detail": "DEMO_READ_ONLY"}`.

**`DemoBanner`** — a standing bar in every app shell, driven by a new `demo` shared prop. **Per session, not per install**: an operator signed in to their own account on the same instance is doing real work, sees no banner, and is untouched by the guard. Without it, a refused save on a demo instance is indistinguishable from a bug.

## Third commit: three ways the guard failed on its own state

A review pass over the first two commits found these. All three reproduce against a booted app; `c91b6e3` fixes them and adds a regression test each.

| | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| stale demo stamp → `POST /auth/login` | `403` — locked out | `204` |
| demo session after `demo_mode=off` → write | `200` — promoted to writable superuser | `403` |
| admin disables demo row → next reconcile | silently re-enabled | stays disabled |

1. **A lapsed demo session locked the visitor out of signing in.** Nothing ever cleared the `is_demo` stamp — `UsersAuthProvider._forget` drops user id, context, version and the remember window, but left the marker. Once a demo session lapsed (expiry, "sign out everywhere" on the demo account, or a nightly reset recreating the rows with new ids) the browser was anonymous *and* still stamped, so its login POST was refused as a demo write. No way back short of clearing cookies. The stamp moved to `users.constants` so `manager`/`provider` can clear it without importing the seeding module; `on_after_login` pops it (the demo endpoint re-stamps *after* the hook, so every other sign-in path clears it) and `_forget` pops it too. `/api/users/auth/login` joins the allowlist — it is how you stop being the demo, it costs a real password, and the rate limiter still applies. `/auth/token` deliberately stays blocked.

2. **Turning `demo_mode` off promoted every live demo session to a writable superuser.** The guard short-circuited on that flag, so the operator action meaning "end the showcase" did the opposite for everyone already inside it. **Behaviour change worth a reviewer's attention:** the guard (and the banner prop, which must agree with it) now key on `demo_read_only` plus the session's own stamp. `demo_mode` governs whether the instance still *offers* the demo, not what an already-minted session is — so ending the sessions themselves means disabling the rows, which the docs now say. Revert this one if you'd rather the toggle be the off-switch and accept the promotion window.

3. **Reconcile re-enabled a demo account an admin had disabled.** `reconcile_demo_user` wrote `is_active=True; disabled_at=None` unconditionally, reverting the kill switch on the next boot or the next unrelated Users settings save. Both fields are now set on create only, matching how the generated password already worked.

## The dangerous combination, and why it isn't blocked

`demo_read_only = false` with an admin demo configured hands anyone who reaches the sign-in page a writable superuser — settings editor (SMTP password, OAuth client secrets), user table, maintenance mode. It is allowed, because an instance whose database is rebuilt on a timer has a legitimate reason to want it, and refusing would make the settings edit fail with no way to opt in. It logs `users.demo.writable_admin` at WARNING and is called out in the docs. Blanking `demo_admin_email` is the way to have a writable demo without that exposure.

## Limits, all documented

- The accounts are **shared** — two visitors on the same one see each other's state, and with writes on can overwrite each other. Periodic database resets are the only real answer.
- Bearer tokens aren't matched directly, but minting one is itself a `POST`, so a read-only demo can't obtain one.
- The demo admin satisfies the first-run setup gate, so seed your own admin first — a read-only demo session cannot complete the wizard.

## Changes

| Area | |
|---|---|
| New | `users/demo.py`, `users/demo_guard.py`, `users/auth_local/demo_api.py`, `users/auth_local/components/DemoSignIn.tsx`, `packages/ui/src/components/DemoBanner.tsx` |
| Settings | `demo_mode`, `demo_admin_email`/`demo_user_email`, `demo_admin_password`/`demo_user_password`, `demo_read_only`, grouped as "Demo account"; the password fields mask in the settings UI by the existing named-secret rule |
| Endpoint | `POST /api/users/auth/demo/{role}` — role as a path segment so each account gets its own `auth_rate_limit_*` budget (the limiter keys on path + IP) and an unknown role 404s in routing. 404 for every failure, matching `/users/register`, so prob

author: mhdyaseensidhik
body:
## What this is

The CI pipeline for `claire-test` (S-6): a GitHub Actions workflow that runs, on **every pull request** and on pushes to `main`, the same gates a reviewer would otherwise run by hand — and **fails the build on any of them**:

| Gate       | Command             |
|------------|---------------------|
| Install    | `npm ci` (from committed `package-lock.json`) |
| Type-check | `npm run typecheck` (`tsc --noEmit`) |
| Lint       | `npm run lint` (`eslint … --max-warnings 0`) |
| Test       | `npm test` (`vitest run`) |
| Build      | `npm run build`     |

All four scripts exist in `package.json` on `main`, and the lockfile is committed — so `npm ci` runs reproducibly on a clean shared runner. This replaces "it passed on one machine" with real CI evidence on every PR.

## Why the workflow `.yml` is not in the diff

The connected token (`MhdYaseenSidhik`) **lacks the `workflow` OAuth scope**. Bisected live on this branch:

- `PUT .github/workflows/ci.yml` → **HTTP 404** (masked-403 for a missing-scope write)
- `PUT .github/CI_WORKFLOW.md` — same branch, same `.github/` directory → **succeeded** (`d59d9cf`)

Same directory, same branch; only the `workflows/` sub-path is refused → the cause is the token scope, not permissions or content. This PR will show "no checks configured" because CI is not yet installed — the **absence** of CI, not a red build.

## Files in this PR
- **`.github/CI_WORKFLOW.md`** — the full, ready-to-commit `ci.yml` contents + the scope diagnosis.
- **`.github/CI_STATUS.md`** — current status and the one action to install it.

## To install CI (commander action — one of)

1. **Grant the token the `workflow` scope**, then re-run this ticket; the YAML in `.github/CI_WORKFLOW.md` will push to `.github/workflows/ci.yml` and start gating PRs — **or**
2. **A maintainer commits `.github/workflows/ci.yml` directly** using the exact contents in `.github/CI_WORKFLOW.md`.

author: phamthang1997
body:
## Summary

The `rust-clippy analyze` workflow has been failing before it lints anything: it runs `cargo clippy` from the checkout root, but this repo's Cargo manifest lives in `src-tauri/`, so every run ends at `error: could not find Cargo.toml`. This fixes that job and, while in these files, moves every action off the node20 runtime GitHub is deprecating.

## Type of change

* [ ] Feature
* [x] Bugfix
* [ ] Refactor / cleanup
* [ ] Performance
* [x] Build / CI / dependency
* [ ] Docs
* [ ] Security
* [ ] i18n / localization

## Linked issue

None.

## Key changes

* **clippy job now finds the crate** — `working-directory: src-tauri` on the clippy step, and the `upload-sarif` step follows the SARIF file to `src-tauri/rust-clippy-results.sarif`.
* **clippy job can now compile the crate** — added the same `libgtk-3-dev` / `libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev` / `libayatana-appindicator3-dev` / `librsvg2-dev` / `patchelf` install that `rust.yml` already does. Without it the job would still have died in `webkit2gtk-sys`'s build script after the path was fixed.
* **`--all-features` → `--all-targets`** so CI lints what `npm run lint:rust` lints.
* **Every action off node20**, verified by reading `runs.using` in each action's `action.yml` rather than by picking the newest tag: `actions/checkout` v4→v7 (4 workflows), `actions/setup-node` v4→v7, `actions/labeler` v5→v7, `actions/dependency-review-action` v4→v5, `github/codeql-action/upload-sarif` v3→v4.
* **`actions-rs/toolchain` → `dtolnay/rust-toolchain@stable`** — the old one is archived and runs **node12**, worse than the deprecation this PR is chasing. The replacement is a composite action, so it has no node runtime to be deprecated next time.

## Technical decisions

* **`working-directory`, not `--manifest-path`.** Cargo discovers `.cargo/config.toml` upward from the *current* directory, so running from the root with `--manifest-path` would silently ignore `src-tauri/.cargo/config.toml` — the same trap CLAUDE.md documents for the `npm run *:rust` scripts, which `cd` for this reason.
* **Latest major rather than the first node24 major.** Every call site here passes either no inputs or one trivial one, so the extra majors carry no surface for us. The two breaking changes in range were checked and neither applies: `setup-node` v5's automatic `packageManager` caching is moot because `release.yml` already sets `cache: 'npm'` and the repo has a `package-lock.json`; `checkout` v7's block on checking out fork PRs under `pull_request_target`/`workflow_run` is moot because the only `pull_request_target` workflow (`labeler.yml`) never calls checkout.
* **`profile: minimal` and `override: true` are gone** with `actions-rs/toolchain` — `dtolnay/rust-toolchain` has no such inputs; it installs via rustup and sets the toolchain as default itself. `components: clippy` carries over unchanged.
* **`continue-on-error: true` is left as-is** on the clippy step. That is what keeps this a SARIF-upload job rather than a gate; `rust.yml` remains the actual gate.
* Known limitation: `swatinem/rust-cache@v2` and `tauri-apps/tauri-action@v0` are left alone — both already declare node24.

## Out of scope / follow-ups

* Does not make clippy a blocking gate, and does not touch the three `allow` lints at the top of `lib.rs`.
* The first green run of this workflow may surface warnings that have never been reported through SARIF, since the job has been failing. Triaging those is a separate PR.

## Testing

**Verified:**

* [ ] Happy path
* [ ] Empty or invalid input
* [ ] Error path
* [ ] Regression on the surrounding features

Nothing is ticked on purpose. A workflow file can only be verified by running on a GitHub runner, and this PR is that run: `rust-clippy analyze`, `Rust` and `Dependency review` all trigger on it, which exercises `checkout@v7`, `dependency-review-action@v5`, `dtolnay/rust-toolchain`, the new apt step, the working directory and the SARIF path. **Please check those three jobs before merging** — the clippy one in particular should now get past `could not find Cargo.toml` and upload a report.

What was verified locally: each action's declared runtime, read from `runs.using` in its `action.yml` at the pinned ref, and the release notes of every major crossed.

**Ran against:**

* [ ] SQLite
* [ ] PostgreSQL
* [ ] MySQL
* [ ] Redis
* [x] N/A — no database code touched

**How to re-verify:**

1. Open the checks on this PR; `rust-clippy analyze` should reach the "Run rust-clippy" step and produce `src-tauri/rust-clippy-results.sarif`.
2. Confirm the "Upload analysis results to GitHub" step succeeds and the findings appear under Security → Code scanning.
3. Confirm no job annotation mentions a deprecated Node version.

## Cross-cutting checks

No Rust ↔ TypeScript boundary is crossed: this PR touches `.github/workflows/` only, no `src/`, no `src-tauri/src/`, no `vite.config.mts`.

## Impact & risk

* **Breaking change:** no
* **Migration, schema, config or env change:** no — CI configuration only, nothing in the app or its build output changes.
* **Needs a native rebuild or an app version bump:** no
* **Rollback plan:** revert the commit; the workflow returns to its current (failing) state and nothing else is affected.

## Checklist

* [ ] Rust CI green (build, test, clippy) — pending this PR's own run, see Testing
* [x] Frontend checks — not run, and not applicable: no file under `src/` is touched
* [x] Read the whole diff myself
* [ ] Added or updated tests — a workflow file has no unit test; its test is the run
* [x] Updated docs / doc comments where behaviour changed — each non-obvious line carries a comment in the workflow explaining why
* [x] Every user-facing string goes through i18n — N/A, no app strings
* [x] No leftover debug code, `console.log`, throwaway `unwrap()` or stray TODO
* [x] No secrets, tokens or connection credentials

## Notes for the reviewer

* The one line worth a second opinion is the jump from `checkout@v4` straight to `@v7`. If you would rather cross one major at a time, `@v5` is the first node24 release and fixes the deprecation just as well.
* The apt-get step is copied verbatim from `rust.yml` rather than factored out — two copies of five package names seemed better than a composite action for this.
