author: rootfreedata
body:
## What

Two complementary, opt-in changes that cut the most expensive LLM usage in the pipeline — the multi-round `gpt-4.1` `reasoningEffort: "high"` merge in `src/ai/deduplicate.ts`.

### 1. Quality gate (`src/ai/qualityGate.ts`, 0 token)

Pure-local pre-filter run **before** any LLM call. Drops too-short posts (`QUALITY_GATE_MIN_CHARS`, default 80 net chars) and exact-hash duplicates (sha256 over normalized text). Every item removed here also saves the downstream `Summarize` call. Default **ON** — it only removes junk/exact duplicates, never merges semantically.

### 2. Embedding dedup (`src/ai/embeddingDedup.ts`)

Replaces the costly multi-round LLM merge with cheap embedding cosine clustering: embed each post once, cluster, keep the longest post per cluster as representative, union all source URLs → same `SimplifiedNewsItem[]` shape the Summarize stage expects. Default **OFF** (`EMBEDDING_DEDUP=1` to enable).

### Runs on your own stack, not only OpenAI

`embedding.ts` works with any OpenAI-compatible `/embeddings` endpoint:

| env | Qwen / Bailian | Zhipu GLM |
|---|---|---|
| `EMBEDDING_API_URL` | `https://dashscope.aliyuncs.com/compatible-mode/v1` | `https://open.bigmodel.cn/api/paas/v4` |
| `EMBEDDING_MODEL` | `text-embedding-v4` (1024-dim) | `embedding-3` (2048-dim) |
| `EMBEDDING_API_KEY` | your key | your key |

Unset → previous OpenAI behaviour unchanged. Vector length differs per model; clustering only needs cosine, but re-check the threshold (below).

## Three real bugs found by testing against the live endpoints

1. **`encoding_format` silently produces garbage vectors.** Since `openai-node` v5 the SDK defaults the flag to `base64` and then base64-decodes the response *unconditionally*. Zhipu ignores the flag and returns float arrays → verified: **dim=512, all zeros, cosine = NaN, no error raised**. The dedup would have silently done nothing. Pinned `encoding_format: "float"`.

2. **Batch size limit.** `text-embedding-v4` rejects >10 inputs (`batch size is invalid, it should not be larger than 10`). Sending all posts in one request would 400 on any real batch and silently fall back to the expensive LLM path — the feature would have been dead on arrival. Now chunked via `EMBEDDING_BATCH` (default 10).

3. **Stale client cache.** The OpenAI client was memoised once per process, so after reconfiguring the endpoint a request for another provider's model was still sent to the first host — surfacing as a misleading `404 model does not exist`. Now keyed on `(baseURL, key)`.

Plus a **degenerate-vector guard** (all-zero / non-finite / dimension mismatch → throw) so a broken provider falls back to the LLM path *visibly* instead of producing NaN cosines.

## Threshold calibration (measured, live endpoints)

| pair type | Qwen `text-embedding-v4` | Zhipu `embedding-3` |
|---|---|---|
| same event, reworded | 0.967 | 0.903 |
| **same event, differing detail** | **0.826** | **0.851** |
| **same topic, different event** | **0.678** | **0.639** |
| same domain, unrelated | 0.580 | 0.564 |
| unrelated | 0.282 | 0.311 |

Default threshold is **0.78** (was 0.85) — it sits in the gap between the two bold rows for *both* providers. At 0.85 a genuine same-event pair (0.826) fell just below the line and was missed.

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit --strict` on all four files: **0 errors**.
- **Live end-to-end** with 14 Arabic items (crossing the 10-item batch limit), calling the real `embeddingDeduplicate()`:
  - Qwen / `text-embedding-v4` → **exactly 4 clusters**, matching the 4 hand-labelled same-event groups.
  - Zhipu / `embedding-3` → 5 clusters (splits one marginal follow-up story; legitimate provider sensitivity at the margin — see header table).
- Degenerate-vector guard: a stub returning all-zero vectors is correctly intercepted.

## Safety

- Both features are behind env flags; existing behaviour is unchanged until enabled.
- Any embedding failure falls back to the original `deduplicateLLM` path, and the reason is logged.
- `embedding.ts` gained a batched `getEmbeddings()`; `getEmbedding()` kept as a thin wrapper.

## Env flags

| flag | default |
|---|---|
| `QUALITY_GATE` | `1` |
| `QUALITY_GATE_MIN_CHARS` | `80` |
| `EMBEDDING_DEDUP` | `0` |
| `EMBEDDING_DEDUP_THRESHOLD` | `0.78` |
| `EMBEDDING_BATCH` | `10` |
| `EMBEDDING_API_URL` / `EMBEDDING_API_KEY` / `EMBEDDING_MODEL` | unset (OpenAI defaults) |

## Files

- new: `src/ai/qualityGate.ts`, `src/ai/embeddingDedup.ts`
- modified: `src/ai/deduplicate.ts` (orchestrator; original renamed to `deduplicateLLM`), `src/ai/embedding.ts`

## Not yet verified

- Real Qwen/Zhipu keys **are** exercised above (that is how the three bugs were found).
- Not yet run inside the actual Lambda environment (env-var plumbing, cold start, IAM).

author: christopherthompson81
body:
The dictionary gained **17,825 rows** (117,483 → 135,308) since #1341 retrained the OOV models — almost all of it the Moby imports of #1344 and #1353 — and the tagger had seen none of it.

## The held-out headline is flat, and only splitting it shows why

The raw number reads 70.7% stress-independent against a 71.5% baseline, which looks like a small regression and isn't one: the held-out is 10% of a dictionary that *gained* the hard Moby tail. The md5 split is deterministic, so the old population survives inside the new one exactly:

| held-out population | stress-indep | incl. stress |
|---|---|---|
| words the old dictionary also had (n=11,748) | **71.4%** — baseline 71.5% | 66.4% |
| words added since, the Moby tail (n=1,780) | **65.7%** | 53.7% |

The shipped model *before* this run scored **56.3%** on those same added words (they postdate it, so all 17,825 were unseen). So the extra data taught the model nothing about vocabulary it already handled, cost it nothing either, and bought about **+9 points on the obscure/foreign/proper-noun tail** the OOV tier exists for. A narrow gain, not a general one — worth stating plainly since "more data" invites the other reading.

## The referees agree, including the independent one

    wikipron primary (independent)   62.7% → 64.0%   (2531 → 2584)   symbol 90.8% → 91.3%
    Moby — the OOV tier              38.1% → 44.2%   (15,056 → 17,454)  symbol 85.6% → 87.4%
    Moby — words the dict carries    75.7%, unchanged — correct, the model is not consulted for them

This matters because the new training rows are **Moby-derived**, so a jump against the Moby OOV referee could be the model learning that corpus's conventions rather than learning English. wikipron has no such relationship to them, and +1.3pp is the largest single move it has recorded in this audit.

Worth knowing for calibration: a quarter of the OOV corpus is exactly **one symbol** off (0 off 37.9%, ≤1 off 63.0%, ≤2 off 81.4%), and reading those misses the symbol is almost always an unstressed vowel — `aerometry ɛɹɑmətɹi` vs `ɛɹɑmɪtɹi`, `acmatic əkmætɪk` vs `ækmætɪk`. That's the weak-vowel axis already declared intentional on the other two referees, so a good part of the OOV gap is a referee floor rather than a model ceiling.

## 55 golden languages moved

232 rows, and none of it is English-only: the English neural tagger renders **embedded English** inside every other language's text, so Cherokee (`Sundance`), Tibetan (`vasanta`) and Belarusian (`caro`) move when it's retrained. Sampled before accepting rather than regenerated on faith — the changes are majority repairs:

    medicines   mˈɛd̬ɪsˌaᶦnz → mˈɛd̬ɪsˌɪnz     (was reading as "medi-signs")
    Aldwych     ˈɔːɫdwɪk    → ˈɔːɫdwɪt͡ʃ
    panthera    pʰˈænθɚə    → pʰˌænθˈɛɹə      + a dropped /ɡ/ in a compound

    goldens 0 stale after regeneration · C# parity 189 byte-identical · 6,076 tests

## One correction and one open flake

**I reported a false measurement before the run** and it's recorded in the investigation doc: "the BiLSTM scores 37.8% on the Moby OOV referee against the sync path's 38.0% — no advantage over its own fallback". `PHON["en"]` resolves to `engine-text-neural`, so both columns were the neural path and the tie was tautological. The conclusion I drew — that the retrain might not be worth it — was unfounded.

**`test/check-goldens-jobs.test.ts` fails intermittently** in a full suite run and passes in isolation. I misdiagnosed it twice (contention, then maxBuffer); both are wrong. Run cleanly the serial and pooled reports are byte-identical (159,335 bytes each), the tool already refuses an incomplete pool, and the captured failure is a *truncated capture* — 349 lines against 644 — with no error line. It predates this change (first seen during #1357). Not fixed, not explained, not dismissed.

Run 40 in `docs/investigations/en/en_moby_source_audit_investigation.md`.

author: totally-tim
body:
## Summary

Adds size share locks: a hotkey freezes the focused window's share of the tiled area, and the remaining windows divide the rest.

```diff
 sugarglider.default.toml                   + Ctrl+Shift+1/2/3/4 → set_size_share (1.0 / 0.5 / ⅓ / ¼)
 src/config.rs                              + size_share.overflow = reject | squeeze
 src/model/size.rs                          + per-window locks + mass redistribution
 src/model/layout_tree.rs                   + estate lock queries (groups share one rectangle)
 src/actor/layout.rs                        + SetSizeShare command; resize releases locks
 src/actor/reactor.rs                       + badge feedback after layout update
 src/ui/swift_bridge.rs, preferences_json.rs + FFI bridge + hotkey descriptions
 SugargliderUI/SizeShareBadge.swift          + transient overlay badge
```

Pressing the same binding again releases the lock; resizing the window (mouse or keyboard) releases it too. A lock that would leave unlocked windows less than min(10%, 1/n) of the tiled area is rejected unless `settings.size_share.overflow = "squeeze"` scales locks down to fit.

## Evidence

- **Verification:** `cargo test` — 275 unit tests + 7 doctests pass, including new model, layout-manager, and end-to-end reactor tests (`it_locks_and_releases_size_shares_end_to_end`, `a_keyboard_resize_releases_a_size_share_lock`). `swift build` and `cargo build --all-features` compile with zero warnings.
- **Config:** default bindings parse and `size_share.overflow` defaults to `reject` (covered by `size_share_bindings_parse` and `size_share_overflow_defaults_to_reject`).
- **Not verified:** live badge rendering and hotkey handling — running the window manager is out of scope for agent sessions, so this needs a manual run.

## Merge Danger

**Door:** two-way — additive feature behind new keybindings, revertable in one revert.
**Blast radius:** default keybindings gain four Ctrl+Shift slots (users with `default_keys = true` get them automatically). Layout math changes only when a lock exists; `masses()` returns early when no locks are set, so unlocked layouts are unchanged.

author: tryinget
body:
Fixes #9777.

Related: #9340 is deliberately **not** fixed here; stopping the surrounding prompt is separate from cancelling a compaction attempt.

## Symptom

Automatic compaction can wait on authentication with no compaction indicator and no active cancellation controller. Calling `abortCompaction()` during that wait does nothing. A synchronous cancellation listener on `compaction_start` also runs before the controller exists.

## Cause

`AgentSession._runAutoCompaction()` resolves summarization auth before creating the controller, and then emits the start event before assigning that controller. Reproduced on main `36b60d2e8` with offline AgentSession tests and no loaded extensions.

## Change

- Prepare the eligible compaction span first, then install the controller before publishing `compaction_start` or awaiting auth.
- Forward the optional signal through the existing auth helpers and use the existing abort-race helper. Check cancellation before and after the auth await.
- Emit an aborted terminal without an error message when the attempt signal was cancelled; preserve genuine auth failures as non-abort failures.

No prompt-run, queue, retry-policy, extension-dispatch, summary-content or retention changes. Manual/tree callers keep their existing behavior. Only `agent-session.ts` and the issue regression test change.

## Tests

Five Given/When/Then regressions failed before the production change and pass afterward: pending auth cancellation, synchronous start cancellation, successful auth, auth failure with later recovery, and no eligible preparation. The pending-auth test also releases the abandoned auth result and verifies it cannot resurrect the attempt.

- Targeted suites: **226 passed, 15 skipped**.
- `npm run check`: passed.
- `npm run build:offline`: passed.
- Full built `./test.sh`: **not green**. A separate pristine worktree at the same base has the same six failing cases; this branch adds five passing tests and no failing cases. Coding-agent totals: pristine 2,290 passed / 5 failed / 50 skipped; branch 2,295 passed / 5 failed / 50 skipped. Both also have the same server failure.

Pre-existing failures on this Linux/Node 26.9.0 test setup:

1. `experimental-internal-process`: starts the coordinator through the current runtime.
2. `package-command-paths`: initializes fresh project settings.
3. `package-manager`: resolves symlinked user/project resources once.
4. `package-manager`: autoload-disabled positive-only package filtering.
5. `trust-manager`: detects trust-requiring project resources.
6. `server`: concurrent-start Unix listener (`listen EINVAL` with the long isolated temporary socket path).

These failures are disclosed, not fixed or counted as passing in this PR.

## Verification

Offline tests exercise the real AgentSession lifecycle with the existing faux provider and controlled auth promises. Independent source review found no blockers within the attempt-only scope. No real OAuth/provider latency or live terminal rendering verification is claimed. A noncooperative auth implementation may still finish internally; its late result cannot advance the cancelled compaction attempt.

AI-assisted implementation and report. Contributor approval/auto-close handling remains with maintainers.

author: lord-ehis
body:
## Summary
- **Approve and publish are separate, per-class actions.** Previously one click published every class using a template. Batches now move `SUBMITTED → APPROVED → PUBLISHED` (or `REJECTED` from either of the first two). Approval re-validates every score and locks the batch.
- **Immutable snapshots.** Publishing freezes each student's result into a self-contained, SHA-256-checksummed payload with a verification code. Parent dashboard, public lookup and the new print page read only the snapshot, so editing a template afterwards can't relabel published history. A database trigger rejects changes to the frozen columns.
- **Append-only audit log.** `result_events` records every submit / send-back / approve / publish with actor, role, reason and template version; a trigger blocks updates.
- **Preview as parent** on the review page, built by the same code that creates the snapshot.
- **Printable result page** (`/result/<id>/print`) — linked parent, the school's admin, or a short-lived signed token issued by the lookup; browser Save-as-PDF.
- **Public `/verify`** — confirms a code and shows only school, term, class, date and the student's initials.
- **Retry-safe notifications.** De-dupe key per snapshot + channel; repeating Publish never messages anyone twice and only retries failed sends.
- **Backfill** (`prisma/scripts/backfill-phase3.ts`, idempotent) gives existing results batches, snapshots and `backfilled` events.

## Verified (dev DB, browser as Teacher / School Admin / Parent)
Two classes on one template moved independently · approve locks scores (inputs disabled) · double-click Publish raced two requests → exactly 3 snapshots, 1 PUBLISHED event, 1 notification · template relabelled after publishing → parent view, lookup and print page unchanged · SQL `UPDATE` of snapshot payload/checksum/code and of an audit event rejected by triggers · send back from `APPROVED` → correct → resubmit → approve → publish, full history recorded · print page refused without a valid token, with a forged token, and unauthenticated · `/verify` accepts a real code (initials only), rejects a wrong one · backfill idempotent. `tsc`, lint, `next build` clean; 23 pure-logic checks passed.

## Deployment notes
- Migration `add_snapshots_and_events` is additive (2 tables, 1 enum, 1 nullable unique column, 2 trigger functions) and must be applied to production **before** this deploys.
- Run `backfill-phase3.ts` on production before deploy **and again right after** (catches anything the old code published in between).
- The review route moved from `/admin/results/[templateId]` to `/admin/results/[batchId]`.

## Deferred
Amendments (Phase 5; snapshots carry `version`/`supersededAt`), real PDF file/storage, a separate approver role, verification-endpoint rate limiting, annual summary (Phase 4).

author: wjrnj9zy72-design
body:
Une app web de comptage de points pour les jeux à manches : on saisit chaque manche, elle tient les totaux, le classement et détecte la fin de partie. Aucune dépendance, aucun build — `npm start` et c'est tout.

## Le principe

Le moteur de score est générique, **les jeux sont des données**. Un jeu = une entrée dans `src/games.js`, décrite par sept réglages : sens du classement (plus petit ou plus grand total gagne), condition de fin (score limite / nombre de manches / à la demande), total attendu par manche, scores négatifs autorisés ou non, joueurs ou équipes, bornes de participants, et un champ facultatif par manche. Ajouter un jeu ne touche pas à l'interface.

Dix jeux sont fournis — Papayoo, Hearts, Belote/Coinche, Tarot, Skyjo, 6 qui prend !, Uno, Rami, Yams, Mille Bornes — plus un jeu entièrement personnalisable. Tous les réglages restent modifiables à la création de la partie : les variantes de table sont la règle, pas l'exception.

## Papayoo

La règle est connue de l'appli : une manche distribue exactement 250 points de pénalité (210 de Payoos + 40 pour le Papayoo, le 7 de la couleur tirée). Le total saisi est vérifié en direct, le bouton *Compléter* remplit le dernier score manquant, et la couleur du Papayoo est enregistrée manche par manche. Un total qui ne tombe pas juste déclenche un **avertissement, jamais un blocage**.

## Le reste

- Correction d'une manche en cliquant sa ligne, suppression, annulation de la dernière manche
- Classement avec ex æquo et écart au leader
- Interface français / anglais, thème clair / sombre, mobile d'abord
- Sauvegarde dans le navigateur (`localStorage`, tolérante aux erreurs) et export / import JSON

## Vérifications

- `npm test` : 28 tests (`node --test`, sans dépendance) — totaux, classement et ex æquo, les trois conditions de fin, validation d'une manche, complétion automatique, cohérence des presets, parité des deux dictionnaires de traduction.
- Parcours complet piloté dans Chromium : création de partie, saisie, complétion, refus d'un score négatif, édition d'une manche, partie par équipes, partie à manches fixes, bascule langue/thème, persistance après rechargement. Zéro erreur console.

Deux bugs CSS trouvés à l'écran pendant cette vérification et corrigés : `[hidden]` écrasé par `display: grid` (barre d'erreur vide visible) et `.button:hover` qui l'emportait sur `.button--primary` (texte blanc illisible au survol). Le re-rendu du formulaire de création a aussi été restreint aux seuls champs qui changent sa structure, sinon un clic dans un champ nom juste après avoir tapé une règle perdait la frappe.

## Note sur les branches

Le dépôt était vide : le premier push a donc fait de `claude/game-points-counter-eicwb2` la branche par défaut, sans base à comparer. `main` a été créée à partir d'un commit racine vide pour servir de base, puis fusionnée dans cette branche pour leur donner une histoire commune (plutôt que de réécrire ce qui était déjà poussé) — d'où le commit de merge. Après fusion de cette PR, il reste à passer la branche par défaut du dépôt sur `main` dans les réglages GitHub.

author: joelb-401
body:
Requested by Joel on 2026-09-19 — "close out and create prs for any open work"

One of six independent branches opened together. None depends on another and all merge clean against `main`.

## What changed

Ledger item 3, settled 2026-09-18 by #115 and recorded in `DECISIONS.md`.

- `TABS` loses `feed` and the labelled empty slot it rendered.
- `.tab-empty` goes from `globals.css` — that slot was its only user.
- `board` keeps its id and changes only its label, to **Pit Wall**.

## Why

The Feed was deleted rather than parked: it was named in the settled tab order and nowhere else, and nothing in the repo said what it carried.

**`board` keeps its id on purpose.** The id is in the query string, so `/?tab=board` is a link that may be bookmarked, and renaming an id to fix a label breaks a URL for a cosmetic reason. What was actually wrong is that "Board" named this tab *and* the thing the hub is — so the tab takes the real name and the id keeps the old one.

## Blast radius

**One app, no shared files.** `apps/home` only — `app/Landing.tsx` and `app/globals.css`. No `lib/`, no schema, no environment variable, no auth plumbing.

## Verification

- [x] `npm run test --if-present` passes in every touched app
- [x] `npm run build` passes in `apps/home`
- [x] CI is green — measured live on this head
- [x] No personal information anywhere in the diff. No `.docx` involved
- [x] `HANDOFF.md` updated, 79 of 80 lines
- [x] Second-order questions answered before the work
- [x] No schema change, so no migration

**Checked against a running dev server, not by reading the diff:** `/?tab=board` still resolves, reads "Pit Wall" and renders the board; a stale `/?tab=feed` falls back to Paper rather than rendering an empty frame — which is `tabFrom`'s existing behaviour for an unknown id, and why no redirect is needed.

## Deployment

**Nothing — it deploys itself on merge.**

- **On merge, by itself:** `tp-home` rebuilds and deploys. About a minute.
- **What a human does:** nothing, in any order.
- **How to verify it is live:** techpaddock.io shows two tabs, Paper and Pit Wall. `/?tab=feed` lands on Paper.
- **If the steps are skipped:** nothing breaks. The Feed tab keeps rendering a slot that says it is undefined.

## Brief impact

None contradicted — this executes a decision already recorded rather than making one.

One observation rather than an objection: the sidebar's first item is also called **Pit Wall**, so the word now appears twice on the same screen pointing at two different things — the landing route, and a tab within it. The decision named this tab explicitly, so it stands, but it is worth knowing it traded one collision for a smaller one.

The five rustup-based release candidate jobs selected the moving `stable` channel, so a new upstream release could change their compiler without a reviewed project update. They now select the already-tested Rust 1.98.0 release. A separate manifest and Dependabot proposal stream allow reviewed compiler updates, including patch fixes, without changing the MSRV or rolling-stable CI.

The lint gate rejects a differing, floating, missing, duplicate, expression-based, or additional Rust action selection and rejects a pin below Cargo's compiler floor. Existing action-commit enforcement remains in place. This is a compiler-version pin; Rust distribution/bootstrap digests, Arch and Flatpak compilers, native package repositories, and the remaining H2.2 input controls stay open. No signing or provenance work is added.

Validation: 5 new drift tests, 8 existing Rust/MSRV policy tests, and 8 builder-image tests pass; all consistency checks, YAML/Actions lint, Markdown, TOML formatting, and whitespace checks pass. The official Rust 1.98.0 distribution manifest lists all required host targets as available. Full candidate package acceptance remains a release check; this PR does not publish a release.

Depends on #134, whose locked YAML environment runs the new checker. Its documentation overlap has been resolved here; merge #134 first. This PR targets main so the full CI matrix runs.

body:
Closes #3.

## What
- `scripts/validate.py FILE [--base OLDER]`: every rejection and degrade rule of the game rules file spec, one stable reason code per rule. A rejection prints `REJECT <code> <where>: <message>` and exits 1; exit 2 means the script could not run. `--base` also rejects a file in which a rule set from the older copy changed or vanished. Standard library only.
- Shared samples: `tests/valid/` (8 files), `tests/invalid/` (41 samples, one or more per rule, plus base/changed pairs for the held-rule-set rule), `tests/expected.json` and `tests/invalid/README.md`.
- `tests/test_validate.py` runs every sample through the command line and requires exactly the expected reason code.
- README, CHANGELOG and Journal updated.

## Decisions where the spec is silent
Written up in `tests/invalid/README.md`:
- **Tier that cannot match:** more main numbers than drawn, more of an extra set than it draws, a Bonus Ball the game lacks, or a Bonus Ball together with all the main numbers.
- **Rising `effectiveFrom`:** rule sets are ordered by (date, revision), so same-date corrections are allowed.
- An unsupported-currency Game is still fully checked.
- Removing a held rule set counts as changing it.

## Review
A two-axis review found that a `null` required member and duplicate JSON keys were accepted; both are fixed, with samples added first.

## Follow-up (not in this PR)
The tier-match wording should also go into the spec's "Prize tier" section in the app repo, so the app's validator agrees.

## Testing
`python3 -m unittest discover -s tests -v`: 62 tests pass locally.

Sample files are shared with the app's tests, and `scripts/` runs in CI on a PR's own copy, so both are worth reading before merging.

author: teetangh
body:
## Problem

Clicks across explore listings + details, programs, checkout, dashboards, landing and all their buttons feel slow on prod, dev and deploy previews. Full-surface audit (4 explorer passes + live probes + Netlify/Next.js docs) found three layers:

1. **Platform (dodge, don't fix):** Netlify `___netlify-server-handler` stalls ~28s on instances created under concurrent load (vendor-confirmed, ticket #1112198). Every function invocation plays this lottery. Captured live again during this PR: preview `/explore/experts` first hit **32.4s TTFB**, `/explore/programs` first hit **40.0s** on the idle preview pool.
2. **App routes that needlessly invoke the function** per click (`force-dynamic` where ISR works, uncached list APIs, per-visit waterfalls).
3. **Dead-feel navigation:** `div[role=button]+router.push`, `preventDefault+push`, `<a>` footers, skeleton-forever gates, double-render role defaults.

## What changed (40 files)

**Explore experts — one availability query instead of three (P1-1)**
- New `app/explore/experts/[consultantId]/hooks/useAvailabilityWindow.ts`: shared React Query reader (`staleTime 30s` = endpoint's `private, max-age=30`, `retry: 1`, in-flight dedupe by key, `bypassRef` preserves the #1591 `?conflict=1`/bfcache no-store flow).
- `ExpertProfileClient`: pricing-day fetch deleted; derives the week window containing the selected day with the same computation as the overview → same key → shared request. Day clicks inside a loaded week cost zero requests. `onRefreshSlots`/pageshow now invalidate the shared key.
- `ConsultantAvailability`: same hook; keeps stale week visible (dimmed) while next loads instead of full loading card per arrow click.
- Overview gated one effect tick on timezone resolution — kills the wrong-zone `"UTC"` first fetch (was: 1-day + 7-day-UTC + 7-day-real = 3 computes/visit).
- **Verified live on preview:** exactly **1** `availability-with-allocation` call per detail visit (was 2–3).

**Checkout — one round trip instead of two (P1-2)**
- `/api/checkout/context` now embeds `referralCreditsPaise` (null = failed, distinct from zero) resolved via `Promise.all` with the tax profile.
- `useReferralCreditsBalance(loaded, paise)` consumes it; standalone credits endpoint kept as fallback (context failure/older server). Wired in all 4 plan pages.

**Dashboards — parallel reads, no skeleton traps (P1-3, P3-8/9)**
- `lib/data/consultant-dashboard.ts`: `soonestSlots` + `orgSessionRows` head reads parallelized (were serial).
- Consultee home: `HomePageClient` paints events first; `HomeTab.userDetails` nullable with inline greeting shimmer (was: full skeleton until layout fetch landed).
- Org home: neutral stat skeleton while `useOrgRole` loads (was: LEARNER-default consumer card → flip for operators). Hook's fail-closed posture untouched.
- `SettingsTab`, admin payouts: `router.replace(?tab=)` → local state + `history.replaceState`. DocumentsPage/AppointmentsPage/ScopeToggle deliberately kept (server or `useSearchParams` derivations depend on router state — noted in code review).

**Links everywhere (P2)**
- `ProgramCard` (grid/list/carousel) + `FeaturedCarousel`: `div[role=button]+router.push` → plain `<Link>` via shared `planHref()`; inner button → styled span (no nested interactive); carousel arrows/dots moved outside the link, `stopPropagation` removed.
- Dashboard rows/cards → `Link`/`Button asChild`: consultant HomeTab session row, FinanceLeadViewCard stats, CatalogClient new-offering buttons, appointments adapter primary action, consultee Find Experts + payment widgets, dispute eye/back actions, Allocate Slots.
- `Navbar` sign-in → `Link` (menu still closes); checkout success/failure footers `<a>` → `Link`; `CategoriesSection ?category=` → `?domain=` (old key silently ignored by the filter reader); dead `Learn More` → `#how-it-works` anchor.
- **Verified live on preview:** 17 plan-card links are real anchors, 0 leftover div-buttons; viewport `?_rsc=` prefetches fire per card; card click commits in ~105ms.
- Skipped with reason: consultee meeting join (URL computed async at click), adapter overflow items + dispute row-click (need shared-component href support), `/dashboard` callers (audit: all legitimately generic — role unresolved at call site).

**Cache hardening (P4)**
- `/api/plans/consultations` + `/subscriptions` GET: `limit` capped 50 (no caller exceeds 10), `page` floored, + `public, s-maxage=60, SWR=300` like siblings. GETs verified session-free (trial floor is a global singleton).
- Shared `parsePlanFilters`: same cap (only callers: classes/webinars lists, ITEMS_PER_PAGE=12).
- Trending rank scans (`webinars`, `classes`) wrapped in `unstable_cache` 60s keyed by the JSON where clause (pure data by construction).
- Recordings detail: `force-dynamic` → `revalidate=120` + `dynamicParams`; triple read (metadata + body + liveness) → single `React.cache`d read; purchase route re-checks eligibility live (404/409) so a ≤120s shell can't sell a withdrawn replay. Publish AND unpublish routes already purge list+slug (verified) — no change needed. Same for experts/orgs (`public-cache.ts`).
- Plan-detail `generateMetadata` double-read already deduped via `React.cache` getters — verified, no change.
- `explore/programs` listing + 4 plan details stay `force-dynamic` (session badge/gate; ISR needs a viewer-orgs endpoint first — follow-up).

## Measurements (sequential curls + DevTools, no prod bursts)

| Probe | Prod | Preview (this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| `/explore/experts` cold-ish → warm | 0.9s → edge-hit 0.37–1.0s | **32.4s** (cold pool stall, platform) → 0.8s |
| `/explore/programs` (force-dynamic) | 1.0–1.4s | **40.0s** (cold) → 1.2s |
| `/explore/recordings` | 6.9s regen → 1.0s | 0.6–0.9s, durable-hit |
| `/`, `/pricing`, `/organisations` | 0.4–1.6s, edge/durable hits | same shape |
| Click landing → experts (prod) | 124ms commit | — |
| Click experts → detail (prod) | 106ms commit | 6.1s to content on cold preview pool |
| Click programs card (preview) | — | **105ms commit**, prefetches observed |
| Availability calls/detail visit (preview) | 2–3 overlapping | **1** |
| Preview console | — | clean (only expected logged-out 401) |

Cache headers confirm the primitives work (`Next.js hit` + `Netlify Durable stored` + `Edge hit` progression); the wins come from invoking the function less, not from platform tuning. No memory/timeout/keep-warm changes (settled).

## Verification

- `tsc --noEmit`: 39 errors, all pre-existing (`react-email` not installed in this env + 1 stream script) — identical count before changes; zero in touched files.
- `eslint`: 0 errors on all touched files (4 pre-existing warnings elsewhere).
- `prettier --check`: clean.
- Full `jest`: 4583 passed. Failing suites reproduced **identically on clean `origin/dev`** (missing `react-email` package + missing `.env` in worktrees; 4 parallel-run flakes that pass grouped/isolated in both trees). Targeted: `__tests__/explore` + `__tests__/plans` 119 pass, shell-overflow contract 19 pass, `isr-routes-never-fail-open` guard green (new ISR route is fail-closed compliant).
- Worktree env notes: tests run with symlinked `node_modules` + `.env`; jest needs `--testPathIgnorePatterns`/`--modulePathIgnorePatterns` overrides because the repo config ignores `.claude/worktrees/`.

## Reviewer checklist (preview)

- [ ] Program cards/carousel hover-prefetch (Network `?_rsc=`), click commits instantly
- [ ] Expert detail: one availability request, week arrows keep stale rows (dimmed), no UTC-flash
- [ ] Checkout totals identical with credits applying (embedded path) vs hard-refresh fallback
- [ ] Consultee home paints events before greeting; org home shows skeleton (not consumer card) on hard load
- [ ] Recording detail route serves ISR; fake slug 404s correctly (note: adapter returns 200 status with not-found UI on both hosts — pre-existing, possible soft-404 follow-up)

body:
Closes #818.

`@glion/lint-profile-events-segments-order` and `@glion/lint-profile-required-fields` call `visit(tree, "segment", …)` and read only the segment name (and, for required-fields, `node.children`), but never returned `SKIP`, so `visit` walked every field, repetition, component, and subcomponent under each segment. Both now return `SKIP` once a segment is handled. The `EXIT` on the first order error stays.

Segments never contain segments. Group nodes are still descended, because the callback only runs on segments. New tests in each package pin that: segments nested in `g(...)` groups are still checked.

## Local benchmark (`benchmarks/suites/lint-profile.bench.ts`, ops/s)

| bench | before | after | change |
| --- | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| validate 3 segments | 6,221 | 8,166 | +31% |
| validate 13 segments | 2,040 | 2,449 | +20% |
| validate 53 segments | 558 | 662 | +19% |
| validate 103 segments | 281 | 327 | +16% |
| violations (3 segments) | 6,030 | 7,214 | +20% |
| validate 3 segments (cold cache) | 4,448 | 5,511 | +24% |
| validate 53 segments (cold cache) | 489 | 632 | +29% |

These numbers come from one wall-clock run on a laptop, so treat them as noisy. CodSpeed on this PR is the reference.

## Verification

- `pnpm --filter @glion/lint-profile-events-segments-order test`: 46 passed
- `pnpm --filter @glion/lint-profile-required-fields test`: 8 passed
- `check-types` and `ultracite check` clean for both packages
- Mutation testing: neither package has a `stryker.config.mjs`, so nothing ran.

body:
Backend da Fase 1 do indicador de janela WhatsApp (mockup: <https://claude.ai/code/artifact/88dc1e43-2093-40e4-ba1f-eb36318eee3f>).

A partir de **01/10/2026** a Meta cobra R\$ 0,035 por mensagem de serviço entregue fora das janelas grátis, com franquia de 1000/mês por número. Precisamos deixar a atendente ver, em cada conversa, qual janela está aberta e quanto tempo resta.

## O que muda
- `Conversation#messaging_window` retorna a janela aberta em conversas de WhatsApp Cloud (`{ kind:, opened_at:, expires_at: }`), com três estados:
  - `ctwa_72h` — última mensagem CTWA há menos de 72h (grátis)
  - `standard_24h` — última resposta do paciente há menos de 24h
  - `closed` — nenhuma janela ativa; só template inicia contato
- `nil` em Baileys / legado — não seguem o modelo pago da Meta.
- Exposto em `Conversations::EventDataPresenter#push_data` — o front recebe via Cable no mesmo broadcast de update de conversation. Também flui pro webhook (`webhook_data` herda).
- Novo card `whatsapp_pricing` em Super Admin → Settings com a chave `WHATSAPP_MESSAGING_WINDOW_INDICATOR_ENABLED`. O backend calcula sempre; o toggle só decide se o chip aparece no front. Ligar globalmente em 01/10.

## Como testar
1. `bundle exec rspec spec/models/conversation_spec.rb -e "messaging_window"` — 7 casos cobrindo cloud/baileys/CTWA/24h/closed.
2. Super Admin → Settings → **WhatsApp Pricing Indicator** (o card aparece com toggle vazio; salvar `true` grava `WHATSAPP_MESSAGING_WINDOW_INDICATOR_ENABLED=true` em InstallationConfig).
3. Rails console:
   \`\`\`ruby
   conv = Conversation.where(inbox_id: <inbox_cloud_id>).where.not(additional_attributes: {}).first
   conv.messaging_window
   \`\`\`

## Fora do escopo (próxima PR)
- Componente `<WindowChip>` no front (Fase 2 do plano).
- Worker de sync com Meta Conversation Analytics API pra mostrar "faltam X das 1000 grátis" no Super Admin.

author: davidharrishmc
body:
The PMP covergroups guard their NA4 coverpoints with `UDB_PMP_GRANULARITY_2`, and the `NA4` bin of `rs1_val_for_pmpcfg_A` in PMPSm is not guarded at all. NA4 is a property of the configuration in its own right (`PMP_NA4_SUPPORTED` in the UDB yaml, which becomes `UDB_PMP_NA4_SUPPORTED` in `rvtest_config.svh`), and it is what the test generator consults when it decides whether to build the NA4 tests. A configuration that does not support NA4 therefore never runs those tests, and any NA4 bin that is still compiled in can never be covered.

Guard every NA4 coverpoint, cross and bin on `UDB_PMP_NA4_SUPPORTED` instead. The Sail configurations all declare NA4 support at grain 2, so nothing changes for them. On CORE-V-Wally rv64gc (grain 6, NA4 unsupported) this retires the last unreachable bin in `PMPSm_cg`, `cp_cfg_A_all_even <*,NA4,*,pmpcfg2>`, on top of #2426.

author: jtomaszewski
body:
## Problem

The Factory's coding run was a `docker run` the orchestrator never saw: nothing on Backend → Agents, Traces or the process activity trail, no log of what the agent did, and a failed run left only a one-line reason on the task (see the 2026-09-19 rehearsal).

## Solution

The Developer agent runs **inside** the orchestrator's OpenCode sidecar as a file agent (`factory.developer`, `files: true`, `filesBash: true`). The workflow becomes:

```
settle → factory.prepare_checkout (clone into the run sandbox, task In progress)
       → INVOKE_AGENT factory.developer (edit + npm ci/lint/typecheck/build, submit outcome)
       → factory.deliver_product_pr (diff → commit → PR → task In review)
```

Every run now has a row on Agents/Traces with its tool calls (request/response), timeline and outcome. `runner.ts` and `docker/developer-runner` are removed. This reverses D-009 ("keep coding execution outside the orchestrator") — the spec decision record is a follow-up.

First real run (task DEMO-5, ZWM-1500): 94 s, 20 tool calls, all checks green, PR jtomaszewski/hackaton-stal-zbiorniki-landing#10, task In review.

## Details

- `docker/opencode/Dockerfile`: node 22 + git on the pinned OpenCode base; `entrypoint.sh`: `OM_OPENCODE_BASH_ENABLED` exposes `bash` (agents still gate it per frontmatter); compose builds the local image.
- The run principal is additionally granted `agent_orchestrator.agents.run` — the agent's OpenCode session submits its outcome through MCP as that principal.
- `lib/checkout.ts`: checkout at `$OM_OPENCODE_WORKSPACE_ROOT/factory/<taskId>`, git dir outside the sandbox, same protected-path/symlink/generated-file rules as before.
- Two 0.8.0 workarounds (documented in the module README): the enterprise file-agent loader imports the package's own manifest before the app's, so `ai-agents.ts` registers the agent from the app manifest; the CLI renders every agent `.md` with `write/edit/bash: deny` and `yarn dev` regenerates that dir, so `scripts/fix-file-agents-manifest.mjs` renders the file-plane frontmatter into `docker/opencode/agents-local/`, mounted over the generated file.
- Setup is in `.env.example` (factory section).

## Verification

- `yarn jest src/modules/factory src/modules/task_delegation`: 109 pass (new `checkout.test.ts`, rewritten `deliver`/`developer` tests).
- `yarn typecheck`, `yarn eslint src/modules/factory scripts/…`, `yarn ds:check` clean.
- Real run end to end as above; run visible on `/backend/agents` and `/backend/traces/<id>`.

## Follow-ups

- Spec: decision record reversing D-009 (SPEC-001, execution spec EX-P0 note).
- Cost/tokens are `null` on OpenCode-runtime runs (framework gap); drawer link to the run; report the two 0.8.0 gaps upstream.

author: mustaphabenseguenimed
body:
Step 4 was offering a Rotation/Année of its own to bare questions that belong inside a clinical case.

A real step 3 output had **24 top-level objects — 18 cases and 6 standalone questions** — for a document holding 18 complete cases and nothing else. The six strays were q5, q11, q50, q51, q62 and q76: in every instance the **last question of its case**. Nothing was missing; the questions were simply detached, so `toJsonObjects` emitted each as its own object.

## Root cause

The document is read correctly. `buildQuestionUnits` gives all 92 units the `case_stem` its "Cas clinique n°N" marker puts them under — 1–5, 6–11, 12–16 … 87–92.

What fails is delivering it. `applyChunkContexts` matches the model's questions back to the source with `alignByStems`, and at the chunk size step 3 runs (4), **22 of the 92 matched nothing at all** and so kept the model's own values instead of the document's. Six of those had no case from the model either, and came out as standalone objects.

`tokenSimilarity` divided the shared tokens by the **larger** of the two sets, but the two sides are never the same length by construction: `PreparedChunk.stems` is the first 140 characters of a unit — heading, stem, and the start of the options — while the model returns the stem alone, in full. For q50, "Résultats des examens : TDM thoracique : multiples adénopathies hilaires…", that is 95 model tokens against a 15-token source prefix, capping the score at **15/95 = 0.158** against a 0.35 threshold. No such stem could ever match, however perfect the match was — and every long "results of the examinations" stem in the paper is in that position.

## The change

Score by **containment** — the shared tokens over the *shorter* set, floored at `MIN_ALIGN_TOKENS` so a two-word stem cannot reach 1.0 on nothing — and raise `ALIGN_MIN_SIMILARITY` to 0.5, since containment is a much easier score to earn. Everything else in `alignByStems` is unchanged: the cursor still only moves forward, and a question that matches nothing still returns `null` rather than a guess.

`fillCaseGaps` and `resolvePageCases` are untouched. They were behaving correctly — they were being fed questions the document context never reached.

## Verification

Replaying `buildQuestionUnits` → `chunkUnits` → `alignByStems` over the real `.docx` and the real step 3 JSON, exactly as production runs it:

| | before | after |
| --- | --- | --- |
| unmatched, chunk size 4 | **22 / 92** | **0** |
| unmatched, chunk size 8 / 15 | 22 / 22 | 0 / 0 |
| mis-aligned (wrong context applied) | 0 | 0 |
| model drops one question per chunk (276 matches) | 66 unmatched | **0 unmatched, 0 mis-aligned** |
| step 3 grouping | 18 cases + 6 standalone | **18 cases + 0 standalone**, 92 questions |

That fourth row is the scenario `alignByStems` exists for, and the new metric is strictly better at it.

`questionChunks.ts` had no tests; `alignByStems` now has its own file covering the long truncated-source match, a dropped question, a stem too short to match on, and the forward-only order.

Gates: 270 tests green (261 + 9 new), `tsc --noEmit` clean, `prettier --check` clean, `eslint` clean on both files, `vite build` OK.

author: nicholasrbowers
body:
## Problem / Motivation

The Browser panel says the CLI is installed, but every browser call fails. The failure is `.../bin/node_real: No such file or directory`, for a path under `~/.kiro/crew/playwright-cli/` that does not exist.

The installer copies one file into the managed leaf as the gateway's Node (`gateway-node`). On a host whose Node distribution ships `bin/node` as a shell script that starts the real binary, that copy is the script. The script looks for the binary next to itself; in the leaf there is nothing next to it.

## Why it matters

The install reports success and the status probe keeps saying "installed", because both check that the staged file exists, not that it runs. The user sees a working panel and a dead browser, with an error naming a file they never heard of. Any distribution that wraps `node` in a script hits this; the wrapper is common on older enterprise Linux images where Node needs an `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` for a bundled `libstdc++`, and on those hosts even the real binary cannot run outside its wrapper.

## What changed (motivation → approach → change)

| | |
|---|---|
| The installer asks **the kernel** which Node binary is running | `_node_runtime_executable` runs `realpathSync('/proc/self/exe')` and falls back to `process.execPath` where there is no procfs (macOS, Windows) |
| The installer **runs the staged copy before it becomes `gateway-node`** | `_staged_node_runs` executes the copy from the leaf, under the gateway's own environment, with `--version`; if it exits non-zero or reports no version, `_stage_managed_node` raises `OSError` naming the source file and the reason, and the copy is removed |

The installer asked Node itself which file it is: `process.execPath`. That value is argv[0] made absolute. A launcher script that starts the binary with `exec -a <script> <binary>` sets argv[0] to the script, so Node answers with the script's path, and the existing regular-file and executable checks both pass for a script. `/proc/self/exe` is the kernel's own link to the running image; no argv trick reaches it, so a host with a plain wrapper now stages the native binary.

Naming the right file is not enough on its own. A binary from a wrapped distribution may link only under the wrapper's `LD_LIBRARY_PATH`; it copies cleanly, passes every static check, and dies on the first call. The one invariant that matters is "the copy runs from the leaf", so the installer tests exactly that, once, at `stage-node`. One probe covers a script with missing relative targets, a binary that needs its wrapper's environment, and a build for another architecture. On Windows the staged file is `node.exe`; it gets the same run.

## Backwards compatibility

Compatible: a Node that runs standalone (nodejs.org tarballs, nvm, fnm, volta, Homebrew, apt/dnf, Windows) answers `--version` and stages as before; the probe resolves the same file it did. The only inputs that behave differently are copies that could not have run, which used to produce a broken install.

## Tests

`test/test_browser_cli_install.py`:

- `test_install_refuses_a_launcher_script_that_cannot_run_from_the_leaf`: a real shell wrapper that works in place is copied, run from the leaf as a real process, dies looking for `node_real` inside the leaf, and the install refuses naming the source and that leaf path; no `gateway-node` and no `.incoming` copy is left behind.
- `test_install_refuses_a_binary_that_only_runs_under_its_wrapper_environment`: a plain executable whose run fails with a shared-library error is refused with that error in the message.
- `test_install_refuses_a_copy_that_runs_but_is_not_node`: exit 0 without a version banner is refused.
- The two existing staging tests (POSIX and Windows) now pin the smoke run and the Windows one asserts the probe ran the staged copy inside the leaf, not the source.
- `TestNodeRuntimeExecutableProbe`: the probe expression asks `/proc/self/exe` before `process.execPath`; its output goes through the same absolute-path, single-line, executable-file validation; a relative or multi-line answer is rejected.

The three refusal tests and the probe tests fail on the base `install.py` and pass on this one.

## Manual verification

On a Linux host whose `bin/node` is an `exec -a` wrapper: with the base code, `_node_runtime_executable` returns the wrapper and the staged `gateway-node` is a bash script; with this change it returns `.../bin/node_real`, an ELF binary that answers `--version` standalone, and `_stage_managed_node` stages it. The fallback branch was exercised by pointing the probe at a non-existent procfs path, which returned `process.execPath`.

## Related Issues

no linked issue: found while operating the Browser panel on a host with a wrapped Node; the fix is self-contained.

## Pattern harvest

Rule candidate: review-prompt
Pattern: an executable is copied out of its tree after "regular file + executable bit" checks only; whether the copy actually runs from its new location is never tested until the first real call.

## Checklist

- [x] At most two commits (one is the norm), with a Conventional Commits title (`feat|fix|docs|refactor|perf|test|chore|ci|build|revert: ...`)
- [x] Existing tests pass and new tests added for new functionality
- [x] Self-review completed; code follows project style guidelines
- [x] Documentation updated (if applicable)
- [x] No secrets, credentials, or internal references in the diff

author: josemerca
body:
Closes #458. Follow-up of the amendment in #456 / #457.

## Why it goes, rather than moves

`SliceSession.tsx:56` rendered a label, a textarea and a button under each slice panel and `POST`ed them to `/slices/:issue/message`. That is a person writing straight into a slice's conversation.

**D-20 already said the change does not travel that way** — *"you tell the boss and the boss makes it happen: it asks the backend to resume that slice's conversation with the change"*. The box went round the boss, so it was never the channel the spec described. This is a return to D-20, not a departure from it.

Three positions this morning (#453, #455 and the one that closed #455) argued *when* to show this box. All three took for granted that it exists. It does not any more.

## What stays

The panel: its title and its `ImplementProgress`, pull request link included. You read there, and you write to the coordinating session, whose own place to talk D-21 guarantees in every phase — a test pins that the drawer is still standing beside the panel.

**`POST /slices/:issue/message` stays in the backend.** It stops being the user's and becomes the coordinating session's, which is what makes D-20's sentence true for the first time.

## What goes with it

- `client.ts` and `SliceSession.types.ts` — the second held the message outcome alone.
- The `agent` prop. With nothing to address, `SliceSession` needs only the issue, the root and the repository its progress is read with; `Home.tsx` stops passing it at both call sites.
- The box's three CSS classes.
- Nine tests that pinned the box, gone or rewritten to pin its absence.

Net: **67 lines added, 321 removed.**

## The guard that replaces them

The fake backend of both Home suites no longer answers the message endpoint at all — a call to it now throws `unexpected fetch`. So the page reaching it again is a red test rather than a silent regression. Three tests also assert positively that no call whose url contains `/message` was made.

## Evidence

- `npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.json` → exit 0, after removing an import the deletion left unused.
- `npm test` in `frontend/` → **76 files, 1535 tests, all passing**.
- `npm run build` → built.
- The issue's own predicate: `test -z "$(grep -rl '/slices/' frontend/src)"` → exit 0.
- `__tests__/yardstick.test.ts` compares the walked census against `git ls-files`, so the two deletions had to be staged before it agreed — worth knowing for whoever deletes a frontend file next.

## Out of scope, and untouched

`ImplementProgress` and its contract, which this only stops wrapping. The backend's route and the queue merged in #452. The coordinating session's own input. `#460` and `#461`, which build the escalation this panel will eventually show.

author: ellyess
body:
Implements the #28 decision. Three commits; the third revises the first two before they were pushed.

## The rule

- **Accepted years:** the training years whose offset was fitted and accepted. A year with a NaN or zero observation is not a fit and is not in the set.
- Each factor's **scalar and offset are both averaged over that set** and nothing else. Before, the scalar averaged every year and the offset only the accepted ones.
- **Refused factor:** fits were attempted, but the accepted years are not a strict majority of the training years (2 of 3, 3 of 4, 3 of 5; `MIN_ACCEPTED_YEAR_SHARE = 0.5`). Scalar and offset are NaN, and `fit_quality` counts it as a failed offset.
- **Unfitted cluster:** no usable observation in any training year, so no fit was attempted. It keeps the identity, with `n_years` 0, as before, and is not counted as a failure.
- **Output and manifest:** every factor carries `n_years` in `factors_<slice>_<k>.csv`. The train manifest gains `accepted_years` per factors file: training years, the minimum, `n_partial`, `n_refused`, `n_unfitted`, and the count for every factor.
- **Transfer:** the collapse sums over fitted clusters only. It used to keep a NaN cluster's capacity in the weights, pulling the collapsed pair toward zero.

`CONTEXT.md` gains "accepted years", "refused factor" and "unfitted cluster", and `output-structure.md` states both cases.

## What moves

| Configuration | Moved | Newly refused | Other |
|---|---|---|---|
| DK k100 fixed (pin) | none | none | all 100 clusters rest on 5 of 5 years |
| CL k10 fixed (pin) | none | none | clusters 6 and 8, already refused, now report a NaN scalar (were 80.2345 and 29.4921) |
| US k250 fixed (no pin; checked in a scratch run) | cluster 223: scalar 2.338 → 2.154, now over 2 years; offset unchanged | cluster 15 (1 of 3 years) | clusters 38, 102, 156 and 183, already refused, now report a NaN scalar; the 74 unfitted clusters keep the identity |

Both pins are re-recorded in `1e93c23`, which adds the `n_years` column. The golden regression test is unmoved, because both of its paths go through `format_bc_factors`.

**Consequence for the scorecard:** `fit_quality`'s maximum scalar no longer sees refused clusters. On rerun, CL's 80.23 and the US's 46.39 leave the max-scalar column, and the failed-offset counts carry the dagger. The US row is re-run after this merges, as agreed.

honeygarg389
body:
…nfm_reply sibling key

WhatsappDriver::persistInboundMessage() extracted flow_token from $nfmReply['flow_token'], a key Meta's real webhook payload never populates — flow_token only ever appears nested inside response_json, alongside the flow's answer fields. The guard silently evaluated to false whenever a real Flow completion arrived, so
WhatsappFlowSubmitted was never dispatched: no exception, no log line, nothing. The inbound message still displayed correctly in the Inbox, which is exactly why this went unnoticed since the feature shipped — every visible signal looked fine.

The test suite couldn't catch it because
WhatsappFlowSubmissionTest.php built its nfm_reply fixture with the same wrong assumption (flow_token as a sibling key), so it exercised a shape Meta never actually sends. Confirmed live via message id=93 in the Flows worktree — a real "Honey" Flow submission captured by the webhook — whose stored payload has flow_token only inside response_json.

Fix: decode response_json first, then read flow_token from the decoded array. Rebuilt the test fixture to match the real captured shape. Mutation-verified: reverting the driver fix against the corrected fixture makes the test fail with
"No query results for model [FormSubmission]" — proving the test now discriminates on real behavior rather than the old shared wrong assumption. Replayed the fixed extraction logic directly against message id=93's actual stored payload (not a synthetic fixture): it now produces a real FormSubmission row with the correct answers ({"field":"Honey","flow_token":"flow_test_o1iT4FtXpu"}), correct flow_token and contact_id, and correctly-null
whatsapp_flow_id/automation_run_id (a Send-Test token has no underlying Flow/AutomationRun to correlate against).

Audited every other flow_token reference in the Flows test suite; none carry this same assumption (FlowDataExchangeEndpointTest covers a different, genuinely token-as-sibling-field Meta API, and WhatsappFlowTestSendTest asserts only the outbound payload shape).

Full suite: 2102 PHP tests / 44937 assertions / 0 failures / 1 skip (baseline-matching); 29 vitest files / 370 tests. PHPStan scoped diff on both changed files: 6 errors, identical to origin/master's own copies — 0 net new.

author: chenchaoyi
body:
日志体系第一期的前半部分：日志库本身、文件默认私有、目录整理。按 openspec 变更 `diagnostics` 实现。serve 和隧道开始写日志、`gtmux logs`、doctor 的「日志」一节在下一个 PR。

## 日志库（`internal/diag`）

- 所有 gtmux 进程都往同一个地方写：`~/.local/share/gtmux/logs/`，每天一个文件，格式统一。诊断记录和操作记录都在里面，操作记录会写明谁发起、作用在什么上、结果如何。
- 每条记录只用一次写入，最多 4KB。这样 hook、serve、命令同时写也不会串行。写日志失败不会影响正在做的事。
- 凭证在写入时统一替换：登记过的密钥、名字像凭证的字段、链接里的 `#c=`/`#g=`、`Authorization` 的值。
- 自己控制增长：保留 30 天或 100MB，都可以改。每天第一个写日志的进程负责清一次，serve 的磁盘清理也会清。单日超过 20MB 就在当天切出新文件，并记下是哪个组件、哪类记录写满的；超过 50MB，当天剩下的 debug 记录直接丢弃。删掉的每个文件都会留一条操作记录。
- 状态文件 `status/<组件>.json` 记录「现在是什么情况」，带过期时间：写的一方挂了，读的一方会当作「不知道」。
- 调试开关合成一个 `GTMUX_DEBUG`，旧的三个变量继续兼容。

## 文件默认私有

- CLI 入口和菜单栏启动时都把 umask 设成 077。代码里有 155 处写死了 0644，这样不用逐处改，新建出来就是 0600；以后新写的代码也自动私有。
- gtmux 会改但不归它所有的文件（各 agent 的设置和指令文件、`~/.tmux.conf`、Warp 配置），统一走 `state.WriteForeign`，保持惯例权限。
- 两个根目录在 serve 启动和每次磁盘清理时都会重新收紧。规则是去掉组和其他人的权限、保留所有者原有的，所以 HQ 自己写的脚本仍然能执行。

## 目录整理

- 新增 `state.ConfigDir()`。两个根目录下的所有路径，Go 里只经 `state` 生成，菜单栏只经 `Paths.swift` 生成；`check-design.sh` 加了规则拦截手工拼路径（已确认它能拦住违规写法）。
- `tunnel-url` 从配置目录挪到数据目录，读取时兼容旧位置一个版本。
- 图标缓存挪进 `cache/`，旧的会删掉，之后自动重新生成。
- 删掉已下线机制留下的 4 个文件。`hq-feed/` 目录保留，因为里面还有两个 doctor 在用的时间标记。这一点是写代码时查出来的，设计文档原先写的是「整个目录删掉」，已经改正。

## 验证

- 新增测试：多个进程同时写仍是完整的行、凭证在各个位置都不会落盘、单条不超过 4KB、新的一天会触发清理、超过上限先删最旧的并保留当天、刷屏的组件会被点名且只记一次、超过每日上限丢 debug、调试开关、状态文件的起始时间和过期判断、收紧权限（包括可执行脚本和符号链接）、外部文件保持权限、umask 让 0644 变成 0600、入口一开始就设 umask、清理流程端到端。
- `make check`、`check-design.sh`、`swift build -c release`、209 个 Swift 测试都通过。

author: franklinmdev
body:
Closes #83.

Unpaired lines become findings. The matcher reports an unpaired invoice line as an **extra line** (hold, placed on the invoice line) and an unpaired PO line as a **missing line** (note, placed on the PO line). Each finding carries its closest candidate, the candidate's code and description scores, and the reason it was not taken. The generator injects both types, and `docmatch match` prints both rows. Extends #82's matcher, generator and report; nothing was rebuilt.

## Real report

At `99f9e49`, run locally with `uv run docmatch match --data-dir <DocILE>`. Counts only.

```
Seed pool
  pool   documents  lines  without lines
  train       5180  36147            313
  val          500   2531             42

Pairing floors
  code         0.5
  description  0.4

Per-type table, over cases from train and val
  type            precision  recall    n  documents
  price variance      1.000   0.990  500       5076
  extra line          0.984   0.994  500       4750
  missing line        0.990   1.000  500       5325
  clean-case false-positive rate  0.000 of 1000 cases

Labels control, over cases from the fixed subset
  manifest                        engine/src/docmatch/evals/subset.json
  documents                       93 of 100 with lines
  precision                       1.000
  recall                          1.000
  clean-case false-positive rate  0.000 of 1000 cases

  type            precision  recall    n  documents
  price variance      1.000   1.000  500         85
  extra line          1.000   1.000  500         91
  missing line        1.000   1.000  500         93
```

What the gap to 1.0 is made of (counted locally, no document text):

- **The #82 edge, surfaced as intended.** Five price-variance cases lower the only price on a nameless line. Those lines no longer pair, so each case shows a missing line plus an extra line: 5 missing-line false alarms and 5 extra-line false alarms. One of the extra lines lost its candidate to another line.
- **3 extra-line misses.** In each, the removed line is close to another line on its pairing cells without being equal to it. The other line takes the PO line on the value tiebreak. This is the matcher's own cost, left in the table.

## Decisions not in the ticket

1. **A line with nothing to pair on is not compared** (owner's call). DocILE has 1,271 labeled lines (3.3%, in 81 of 5,325 seeds) that carry no code, description, quantity, unit price or amount. 999 carry only `line_item_date` and 264 only `line_item_position`. Such a line cannot pair even with an identical copy of itself, so before this rule it showed up as an extra line plus a missing line on clean cases:
   - clean-case false-positive rate 0.014 before, 0.000 after
   - extra-line precision 0.63 before, 0.984 after
   - missing-line precision 0.63 before, 0.990 after

   Pairing now leaves such a line out. The line is nobody's candidate and is listed in `not_compared` with a new reason, `nothing to pair on`, with `cell` set to `None`. This extends #76's rule that nothing comparable means no finding, and it **amends #76 point 4**, which listed three reasons and a cell on every entry. CONTEXT.md's "Unpaired line" entry now states the rule.
2. **The generator never injects a line the matcher could not tell apart.** A line whose normalized pairing cells (code, description, quantity, unit price, amount) equal those of another line in the records it would leave or join is never removed or added. Neither is a line with no pairing cell. Without this rule, 51 of 500 extra-line truths could not be scored: the removed line had an equal twin. The rule only excludes exact equals. A donor line that is merely close to a seed line (same description, different amount) can still be added, so the missing-line row includes some near-duplicates alongside the cross-document lines the floor was set on (#77).
3. **The missing line goes in at a random position** in the PO, not appended. It also gets a receipt line, since the receipt copies every PO line. #86's short-ship and over-ship will read receipts, so this is stated here.
4. **`MatchResult.unpaired_invoice` and `unpaired_po` are now derived from the findings,** so the candidate is stored once. `findings` is `Finding | UnpairedFinding`, and `explain()` quotes the candidate for an unpaired line.
5. **Extra line and missing line have no band.** `Injected.band` is `None` for both.

## Acceptance criteria

- [x] Extra line: an unpaired invoice line, a hold, on the invoice line.
- [x] Missing line: an unpaired PO line, a note, on the PO line. A case whose only finding is a missing line is `approvable`.
- [x] The added PO line is a labeled line from another seed in the same pool, with its code and description.
- [x] Each unpaired line carries its best candidate, the candidate's scores per cell, and the reason. There is no full score matrix.
- [x] An extra line beside a price variance leaves the price variance on its own PO line. This is pinned at Seam 1 on hand-built records. Generated mixed cases belong to #87.
- [x] Both rows appear in the per-type table with n, and CI's `Match` step prints them. The fixture's expected output is updated.

## Notes

- The real report takes about 58 s locally. Profiling puts almost all of it in the existing Levenshtein pairing, which now runs over three times the cases #82 did (#82 was not timed). Not optimized here.
- Checks: ruff, mypy strict, and pytest (521 passed).

author: nickcjordan
body:
## What this is

Pass 15 attacks the log's top open item: crowd worlds further, if it can be afforded. 56 percent of contested worlds are still one creature against one, and pass 9 established that the cause is arithmetic (sends per world), not scoring. Pass 9 raised the budget as far as it could. The other half of the ratio is the frame, and the frame turned out not to be testable.

**`worldsPerFrame` has been a key in `DEFAULT_RULES` since pass 9, and nothing read it.** `drawFrames` dealt from the module constant, and the clinch was a hard 5 in five separate places. Four passes cited a narrower frame as the untried alternative to a budget change; it was never testable. This pass makes it real and then measures it.

## The wiring

`clinchFor(worldsPerFrame, framesPerMatch)` derives the bar as a majority of the worlds on offer, which yields the shipped 5 of 9 unchanged and makes any other width a coherent game rather than a half-applied setting.

- `drawFrames` deals from the rules, so a narrower frame draws fewer worlds and still never repeats one within a match.
- The Ruling and the bot read the derived bar. The bot reads it off the rules already travelling in `publicState`.
- The status pips and the reachability line read it off the live frame, so the UI prints the bar it is actually playing to.
- `matchShapeOf` and `lockedRoundOf` take it as a parameter, defaulting to the shipped 5 so no existing caller changes.

Eight new tests in `frameWidth.test.ts` pin one place each, including that the bar is always takeable and never reachable by both sides at once.

## The measurement (600 matches, seeds 7/13/21)

| frame | worlds | clinch | 1v1 | downs | flips | worst naive (bar 8) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 3 x 3, s11 (shipped) | 9 | 5 | 55.1-56.1% | 4.64-4.85 | 28.1-30.5% | 12.3-18.0 |
| 2 x 3, s11 | 6 | 4 | 18.3-19.3% | 5.21-5.64 | 27.9-29.7% | - |
| **2 x 3, s9** | 6 | 4 | **30.1-31.1%** | 4.27-4.52 | 29.0-30.5% | **7.5-9.5** |
| 2 x 3, s8 | 6 | 4 | 42.4-44.2% | 3.63-3.77 | 26.4-30.1% | 4.5-12.5 |
| 4 x 3, s14 | 12 | 7 | 68.7-69.4% | 5.60-5.63 | 29.5-30.3% | - |

A 2 x 3 frame at sendable 9 nearly halves the 1v1 share, 56 percent to 30, while holding downs and flips in band on all three seeds. **It is the best crowding result any pass has measured, and it is not shipped.**

## Why it is not shipped

**1. It fails the naive-policy bar,** which is the one gauge that says the game asks a question. Pass-early (deploy an even share, then stop thinking) sits 12.3 to 18.0 points under the proctor mirror at the shipped width and only 7.5 to 9.5 points under it at 2 x 3 / sendable 9, through the bar of eight on seed 13. With two worlds a round there is no allocation question left: spreading evenly *is* the right answer. Pass 9 recorded that a generous budget makes deploy decorative; a narrow frame does the same thing from the other direction, and harder.

**2. A two-world round can only be level or swept.** Measured: 51 percent of rounds end 1-1 and 48 percent end 2-0, with nothing in between, against 10 percent level at the shipped width. Half of all rounds would say nothing about the score. The stake does not rescue it, either: the bot stakes 0.10 times a match at width 2 against 0.33 at width 3, because a stake among two worlds is transparent and easily answered, and level rounds stay at 51 percent with it off (51.8) or on (50.6).

Both readings, and the full sweep, are written into the comment above `WORLDS_PER_FRAME` so this is not rebuilt.

## What is worth keeping from a negative result

- **A wider frame is unambiguously worse on every axis** (1v1 to 69 percent, downs over band, comeback under band). It spreads the same roster thinner. Nobody had checked.
- **The narrow frame does make the last round matter more**: 91.8 to 92.7 percent of matches are still live entering round 3, against 82.5 to 84.7 shipped. That is the one reason to come back here, if a later pass finds a per-world decision deeper than "how many do I send".
- 1v1 at 56 percent is now recorded as the accepted cost of a game whose deploy decisions matter, in a new "closed by measurement" section of the log, rather than sitting at the top of the open items where it would be retried.

**The lesson:** a lever nothing reads is not a lever. When a lever is recorded, the same pass should make something read it, or record that it does not.

## Verification

- 1940 tests green (eight new), typecheck clean on `packages/rules`
- `npm run build -w apps/web` inside budgets
- `node apps/web/scripts/reclamation-proving.mjs` green in all four configurations (simple/advanced at 1440/390, 11 sends each)
- The derived clinch checked by paint against the live page: five pips a side, "First to 5 sites takes the Charter", three worlds on the table

author: copilot
body:
Die Website wirkte in mehreren Bereichen noch zu knapp oder unfertig, besonders bei leeren Zuständen ohne konfigurierte Inhalte. Dieser PR verdichtet die inhaltliche Führung über die gesamte App, ohne erfundene Sendungen, Termine, Metadaten oder externe Profile einzuführen.

- **Hero & Einstieg**
  - Hero-Text auf neue Besucher ausgerichtet: Was die Seite ist, was hier möglich ist und was beim Start des Streams technisch passiert
  - vier klare Eigenschaftskarten ergänzt (`Direkter Browserzugang`, `Manueller Start`, `Ohne Tracker`, `Installierbar`)
  - kompakter Abschnitt **„So funktioniert es“** mit nachvollziehbarem Ablauf

- **Player, Diagnose & Werkzeuge**
  - Status- und Diagnosebereich sprachlich erweitert: verständliche Erklärung für Bereit, Verbinden, Live, Puffern, Blockiert, Fehler und Offline
  - zusätzliche Hilfeblöcke zu Autoplay, Lautstärke, Retry, Direktstream und laut.fm-Fallback
  - bestehende Tools (Sleep-Timer, Teilen, Tastaturkürzel, Favoriten, PWA/Theme) um konkrete Nutzungshinweise und Grenzen ergänzt

- **Now Playing & Historie**
  - Bereiche erklären jetzt klar den Unterschied zwischen aktuellem Titel und Historie
  - Fallbacks ausgebaut: warum Daten fehlen können, wie same-origin-Quellen gepflegt werden und dass der Stream davon unabhängig funktioniert
  - Quellenlabel präzisiert, inkl. Host/Pfad/Query und Polling-Hinweis bei konfigurierter Quelle

- **Leere Inhaltsbereiche als echte UI-Zustände**
  - Sendeplan, Events, News, Archiv und Plattform-Links zeigen nun informative Empty States statt bloßer Leerflächen
  - jeder Zustand beschreibt Zweck, Pflegeort, Voraussetzungen und sinnvolle nächste Schritte
  - Archivbereich zusätzlich mit einklappbarer „Archiv vorbereiten“-Hilfe

- **Nutzung, FAQ, Sicherheit & Kontakt**
  - Abschnitt **Hören / Nutzung** um konkrete Desktop-/Mobil-/Fallback-Abläufe erweitert
  - FAQ deutlich ausgebaut um reale Fragen zu Streamstart, Direktstream vs. Website, Now Playing, Historie, localStorage, PWA, Datenschutz, Datenverbrauch, Theme und Shortcuts
  - Sicherheits-/Datenschutzbereich trennt lokale Browserdaten sauber von externen Verbindungen
  - Kontakt-/Feedback-Bereich erklärt klar, was lokal passiert, wann E-Mail verfügbar ist und wie GitHub Issues als Fallback genutzt werden

- **Footer & Orientierung**
  - Footer um schnelle Abschnittslinks und kompakten technischen Status der Seite ergänzt
  - zusätzliche responsive Abstufung für die Hero-Karten (`4 → 3 → 2` Spalten), damit die erweiterten Inhalte auf mittleren Viewports lesbar bleiben

- **Pflege & Dokumentation**
  - `README.md` erweitert um Überblick über die neuen Informationsbereiche und deren Pflegeorte
  - bestehende Tests an die präziseren Empty-State- und Quellen-Texte angepasst

Beispiel für die neue, präzisere Quellenkennzeichnung im Metadatenbereich:

```js
return 'Datenquelle: ' + url.host + url.pathname + url.search
  + ' · Aktualisierung ' + formatNowPlayingIntervalLabel() + '.';
```

author: arena-ai-coding-agent[bot]
body:
## Problem

Every repost failed with:

```
❌ Upload failed: Failed to post to all 2 platforms
Instagram: failed: API returned 404: {"error":"No such API endpoint: POST /api/v1/upload","type":"not_found","code":"endpoint_not_found", ...}
TikTok:    failed: API returned 404: {"error":"No such API endpoint: POST /api/v1/upload", ...}
```

`uploader.py` was written against an assumed API (`POST /v1/upload`, multipart `video`/`caption`/`platform` fields, host `api.zernio.com`) and still carried a `TODO: verify against Zernio docs`. The real [Zernio API](https://docs.zernio.com) lives at `https://zernio.com/api/v1`, has no upload endpoint, targets accounts by id, and requires TikTok consent/privacy settings on every post.

## Fix

**`uploader.py`** now implements the documented flow:

1. `GET /v1/accounts` → `accountId` per platform (override with `zernio_account_ids` in config)

- Thumbnail is only uploaded where Zernio uses it (Facebook/YouTube, or as TikTok cover when enabled) — Instagram Reels/TikTok take no custom thumbnail via the API

author: rcownie
body:
Follow-up to #1916 and #1912, now that the PRs they were waiting on have landed.

## 1. The entity lifecycle page describes tenant suspension

#1916 landed with its tenant section deliberately narrow — it pointed at the playbook rather than describing suspension, because #1915 was still open and a reference page must not describe unmerged behaviour as current.

#1915 has merged, so the section can say what the mechanism is: the two states, the `cleatctl` verbs, and — the part worth a reader's attention rather than a footnote — the two things suspension deliberately does **not** do:

- **A run mid-flight is not frozen.** Suspension stops new claims; it does not interrupt what is already executing. That is why it needs no special handling anywhere else in the engine: nothing is left half-run for the reclaim loop to find, and `cleat_workflows_stuck` never sees a population that is not actually stuck.
- **Reads stay open.** A tenant suspended for non-payment can still see its own runs.

Plus the "absent is not suspended" rule, which is the kind of thing an operator hits once and remembers badly.

## 2. Managed PostgreSQL multi-tenancy is complete

#1912 added a capability table with one row reading **"a non-default tenant's cron — does not fire"**. #1913 made that false: due schedules are now read per tenant, under each tenant's own RLS context, with no grant.

Flipped here rather than in #1913 because the two were on different branches — and a row claiming a capability the tree does not yet have is the same defect in the other direction.

The table now says multi-tenancy on a managed instance is **complete**, and that the **default** configuration is the one that works there. It also records what the row used to say, because a deployment sized against the old table may have been planned around a limitation that no longer exists.

## Testing

- `bash scripts/check-doc-consistency.sh` — OK
- `python3 scripts/check-entity-contract.py` — OK
- No other doc still claims a non-default tenant's cron cannot fire there (checked)

author: copilot
body:
This updates `cerdman/ECC`’s Claude hook configuration to match the current upstream-compatible format: `hooks/hooks.json` now contains only loader-supported keys, while stable matcher metadata lives in a sidecar file. The change preserves the target repo’s ECC-specific hooks, ordering, and runtime behavior.

- **Hook config format**
  - Removed `$schema`, matcher `id`, and matcher `description` from `hooks/hooks.json`
  - Added `hooks/hooks.metadata.json` as the canonical sidecar for stable IDs, descriptions, and 12-char SHA-256 fingerprints
  - Preserved all existing target-specific hook matchers, commands, and lifecycle behavior

- **Metadata merge + fingerprinting**
  - Added `scripts/lib/hooks-config.js` to:
    - merge metadata back onto parsed hook configs
    - compute stable fingerprints from matcher + hook payloads
    - detect missing, duplicate, reordered, or drifted metadata
    - refresh fingerprints immutably
  - Hardened refresh behavior to reject ambiguous duplicate fingerprints rather than rebinding stable IDs

- **Validation + CI wiring**
  - Extended `scripts/ci/validate-hooks.js` to validate:
    - `hooks/hooks.json` schema
    - optional `hooks/hooks.metadata.json` schema/alignment
    - Claude loader compatibility
    - safe `--update-fingerprints` behavior
  - Added `schemas/hooks-metadata.schema.json`
  - Added `scripts/ci/check-hooks-schema-keys.js` to enforce documented loader key sets, scoped to files that exist
  - Wired the new checker into `package.json` and validation workflows

- **Install/runtime compatibility**
  - Updated install-time hook handling to read the sidecar-aware config, resolve plugin-root placeholders, and write refreshed metadata alongside installed Claude hooks
  - Kept merged metadata available to runtime/test codepaths that rely on matcher IDs/descriptions

- **Docs + tests**
  - Updated `hooks/README.md` to document the sidecar format and fingerprint refresh flow
  - Added focused tests for:
    - metadata alignment and uniqueness
    - fingerprint drift/reordering detection
    - immutable merge behavior
    - loader-key rejection
    - install-time sidecar invariants
  - Updated hook/integration tests to read merged hook configs where IDs/descriptions are expected

Example of the new split:

```json
// hooks/hooks.json
{
  "hooks": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "matcher": "Bash",
        "hooks": [
          { "type": "command", "command": "node ... pre-bash-dispatcher.js" }
        ]
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

```json
// hooks/hooks.metadata.json
{
  "entries": {
    "PreToolUse": [
      {
        "id": "pre:bash:dispatcher",
        "description": "Consolidated Bash preflight dispatcher for quality, tmux, push, and GateGuard checks",
        "fingerprint": "c3cf36d57167"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```
