body:
A fold of two branches that refactored this role independently, hours apart, and
conflicted in four places. Each axis was adjudicated rather than merged.

Loops take the shape that removes `loop_var` from eleven non-nesting loops, because
LOOP-01 sets it only where a nested loop would shadow `item` and the checker enforces only
the dunder-naming half of that rule. Ansible attaches each iteration's item to its result
under the `loop_var`'s name, so the loops reading a previous looped task's `.results` move
to `item.item`; producer and consumers are rewritten in one pass, because a half-renamed
reference is a silent undefined that no checker sees. Everything else — the wrapper names,
the four expanded register nouns, the 2.21 floor with its README explanation, and the
formatting — comes from the other branch.

The two source branches, `chore/polish-05-linux-disk-manager-patterns` and
`chore/polish-12-linux-disk-manager`, are superseded by this and should be closed rather
than merged. This branch is an ancestor of neither; their content was folded.

author: mobileoverlord
body:
Adds the Variscite DART-MX95 SOM on the Sonata-Board as `avocado-imx95-var-dart`,
and fixes four pre-existing bugs in shared i.MX code that the bring-up exposed.
Three of those also affect the existing `avocado-imx8mp-var-dart`.

## The machine

The vendored `meta-variscite-bsp-imx` pin (`wrynose_6.18.20_2.0.0_var01`) already
carries `imx95-var-dart.conf`, so no vendor repin is needed. It is release-matched
to meta-imx `wrynose-6.18.20-2.0.0`: u-boot-variscite is `lf_v2026.04` and the
layer appends imx-atf 2.14 / imx-system-manager 2026q2 / imx-oei, so the
SPL-to-System-Manager pairing that forced `PREFERRED_VERSION_u-boot-imx = 2026.04`
on `avocado-imx95-frdm` needs no pin here — this board does not build u-boot-imx.

MMC numbering is the reverse of the i.MX8MP DART, and the boot env, the stone
`uuu-emmc` profile and `fw_env.config` all key off it: eMMC is mmc 0 /
`/dev/mmcblk0` (42850000.mmc), SD is mmc 1 / `/dev/mmcblk1` (42860000.mmc).

What both Variscite machines share moves into a new
`conf/machine/include/avocado-variscite.inc`, and `UBOOT_DEFCONFIG` is derived
from the vendor machine's `UBOOT_CONFIG[sd]` instead of being hardcoded to the
i.MX8MP value, so a second Variscite board cannot silently inherit the first
board's defconfig.

## Shared fixes

- **`avocado-img-bootfiles`: anchor the /var skip.** The skip list is unanchored
  substring matches against deploy filenames and `-var-` stood in for the /var
  image. Every Variscite machine is named `*-var-dart` / `*-var-som`, so it also
  matched the kernel, every device tree and the bootloader — dropping all three
  while keeping the bare `Image` and `imx-boot` symlinks. The package looked
  fine and `stone bundle` failed much later with "File 'Image' not found in any
  input directory". `avocado-image-var-` names the same image with a prefix no
  MACHINE can contain.
- **Ship the IW612 wlan driver, not just its firmware.** There is no in-tree
  `nxpwifi`/`mwifiex` for this part on 6.18, and `meta-variscite-bsp-imx` carries
  a `kernel-module-nxp-wlan` bbappend specifically to control how `moal` loads.
  Removing `packagegroup-avocado-imx-extra` dropped the only thing pulling that
  recipe, so the firmware shipped with no driver and WiFi was silently dead.
- **Fix the redundant-environment Kconfig symbol.** `CONFIG_SYS_REDUNDAND_ENVIRONMENT`
  no longer exists in U-Boot 2026.04 (`ENV_REDUNDANT` now), and Kconfig ignores an
  unknown symbol in a defconfig without warning — which also dropped
  `CONFIG_ENV_OFFSET_REDUND`, whose dependency is `... && ENV_REDUNDANT`. With
  `MKENVIMAGE_EXTRA_ARGS = "-r"` writing the redundant layout (CRC + flag byte +
  data) and a non-redundant U-Boot CRCing from byte 4, the environment was intact
  on disk and still failed its checksum. U-Boot reported only "bad CRC, using
  default environment" and ran the vendor's `bsp_bootcmd`.
- **A/B the bootloader on i.MX9.** `avocado-imx-bootpart` was mx8m-only because
  its boot-image guard knew only the HABv4 IVT; i.MX9x boots an AHAB container
  (tag `0x87` at byte 3). The guard now accepts both and `COMPATIBLE_MACHINE`
  widens to `imx-generic-bsp` — the script already no-ops on media without eMMC
  hardware boot partitions, and a board only exercises it if its stone manifest
  wires the hooks.

`imx95-var-dart` also restores the dm-verity placeholder before `stone bundle`.
`runtimes/<name>` is both the dnf installroot and the build output dir, and the
CLI's rootfs image step removes `${ROOTFS_OUTPUT%.*}.verity` in its verity-off
branch — which is exactly the placeholder `avocado-img-bootfiles` installs. The
restore is guarded on the file being absent, so enabling verity later leaves a
real hash tree untouched. The general fix belongs in avocado-cli.

## Verification

`bitbake -p` and `bitbake -g avocado-complete` clean on both
`avocado-imx95-var-dart` and `avocado-imx8mp-var-dart`.

On hardware (DART-MX95 on Sonata, eMMC-provisioned via `uuu-emmc`): boots
unattended to a login, `/` on `/dev/mmcblk0p5` (erofs ro), `/var` on
`/dev/mmcblk0p9`, kernel 6.18.20-var-lts-next. `moal`/`mlan` load and `mlan0`
appears. `/dev/neutron0` and `neutron-rproc` are present.

A/B verified over `avocado runtime deploy`, slot a -> b: rootfs `mmcblk0p5` ->
`p6`, `avocado_boot_slot` a -> b, eMMC boot1 `00 00 00 00` -> `02 23 20 87`,
`avocado-imx-bootpart status` a -> b, and the board came back up booting from
boot1. `avocado-imx-bootpart`'s host test is extended for AHAB and passes 12/12.

Not verified: the shared fixes on `avocado-imx8mp-var-dart` hardware.

author: alan-schramm
gmhelmold
body:
## WP-02/E4.1 integrado — limite de envelope e recusa de transferência incompleta

Merge concluído em `503eae8a8e7e927c571ae5721ba1792eaefcb3af`, com expected_head_sha=`3cd74301b4a2956b15895d663ea7c115c0a8eeb3`. Base `6a66222fbc70e5384516e1a6df025da438943b56`; checkout efetivo do CI `efb04ef9c11846df8ac79a651398b3d42b3af7a9`. Objetos Git do head, checkout CI e merge consultados: árvore idêntica `08a062bea39ac9b38123d99d67dcb21068b429f0`. Gate final: https://github.com/gmhelmold/context-continuity/pull/43#issuecomment-5745628186. Ref #5, que permanece aberta.

### Defeitos corrigidos

O loader anterior fazia SELECT de meta.value e só depois aplicava Buffer.byteLength <=16384. Uma página limitada em quantidade ainda podia carregar envelope excessivo antes de recusá-lo. A correção consulta apenas tipo e octet_length antes do valor, exige TEXT/UTF-8 e limite inclusivo de 16384 bytes. Preserva checagem posterior, parser, digest, binding, reserva e owner, no mesmo snapshot/lock dos chamadores existentes.

A revisão da fixture NUL revelou também uma fronteira de integridade: conversão textual do driver nos runtimes fixados pode entregar somente um prefixo JSON válido, ignorando NUL e sufixo, mesmo quando o registro cabe no teto. O loader agora exige que o tamanho UTF-8 recebido seja igual ao tamanho escalar armazenado, antes do parser. Prefixo truncado não é aceito como registro completo. Essa igualdade não autentica conversões de mesmo comprimento ou um banco inteiramente reescrito.

O loader é compartilhado por ID, página/lookahead, leitura de bytes, replay, release e recovery. Não transfere propriedade, não altera reservas por diagnóstico, não lê fontes durante descoberta e não faz recuperação automática. Encoding incompatível é recusado, não migrado. Sem promessa de teto global de RSS ou I/O SQL constante; duas consultas escalares adicionais por envelope válido, sem benchmark de latência alegado.

### Provas e revisão concluídas

21 comportamentos novos passaram nas duas versões: sete entradas de API/lookahead, multibyte/astral/NUL, prefixo válido+NUL curto/no limite, BLOB indevido, 16383/16384 bytes válidos com Unicode, janela além do lookahead, escrita concorrente entre medida/valor, falha escalar, UTF-16le/be e histórico released. Observação do resultado real do driver e testemunha Python; nenhum contador do produto aceito como prova. Nenhum dos 334 testes históricos foi editado.

Cinco pares controle/mutante passaram: limite prévio, contagem de caracteres, limite exclusivo, encoding e tamanho recebido. Cada controle passou e cada mutante falhou no teste selecionado com ERR_ASSERTION e marcador previsto. Timeout/import/setup não contam. Pares contados uma vez; as campanhas históricas também passaram.

Diff final relido. Dois commits, seis arquivos; somente source-pins.ts em produção. SPEC-21/22 e docs/implementation/WP-02-E-PIN-ENVELOPE-BUDGET.md registram blast radius, limitações e cinco axiomas. Revisão do autor, não auditoria independente. Fixtures JSON preenchidas são diagnósticas e restauradas antes de cleanup; não alteram a semântica CAS de envelopes não canônicos.

### Primeira rodada preservada

Head `0fdb0a9`, coordenação run35471425949/jobs105972965430 e105972965503: 356/357 nos dois Nodes. Única falha era a testemunha de preservação NUL usando SELECT TEXT truncado; contagem SQL, recusa e não materialização passaram. Corrigida a testemunha para comparar bytes via CAST AS BLOB somente no teste. Nenhuma entrada/teste removido nem erro relaxado. Depois a revisão acrescentou a guarda de integridade e dois cenários+mutante. Histórico no comentário5745568726 e no relatório. Esse resultado inicial não foi usado para aprovar o novo head.

### Gate final — exclusivamente Actions, antes do merge

Sete workflows/dez logs completos conferidos no head3cd7430: coordenação/build360 =334+21+5, core/typecheck198 e storage/typecheck155 nos pins Node22.17.1/24.0.0; cinco verificadores documentais, componentes12, testemunha4, gateway13; OpenCode oficial1.18.31/provider sintético16; controle do host e oito corrupções rejeitadas por E_ORACLE_WITNESS_PAYLOAD. Suítes sem fail/cancelled/skipped/todo. Componentes repetidos nos workflows de host não são somados novamente.

Runs: coordenação35471888841; core35471888846; storage35471888844; spec35471888831; gateway35471888861; stock35471888879; host-mutations35471888895. Os dez job IDs constam no comentário de gate5745628186. Artefatos do stock10593033111 (SHA256 ZIP `67a4244acd47f193c34eca5fad1bcb8ffd20062aba0570dbbd43baa68fb1a2be`) e mutações10593155257 (`785b2b6f6bf881879bfe6f8b43849bddb578ec32e5c9343694793808b4f3adc6`).

As execuções usadas no aceite são PR-triggered, anteriores ao merge, não novas execuções pós-merge; a equivalência posterior foi verificada pelos objetos Git. Avisos herdados de runtime/Actions seguem visíveis sem supressão.

Sem build/teste/typecheck/produto no Mac ou contêiner. Código, docs, PR e merge publicados pelo conector GitHub. Sem mudança de DDL, core, ponte C, dependências, quotas ou workflows; sem release ou inferência paga. Evidência com SQLite/FS/locks/processos reais e dados sintéticos, não homologação completa do plugin. E4.1 concluído; WP-02/#5 continua aberto para staging/blobs/GC, publicação e demais serviços.

body:
起因：worker-done-verdict-call-site-untested（#1343）

## 目标

#1289 的病是「判据对了、调用方漏传」，#1341 把漏传的那一处（`mirasimWorkerDone`）接上了，
但**正控只锁了 `dao.mjs`**——`reviewer-mirasim.mjs` 那 25 行再被删掉，现有测试全绿。

更细一层（#1343 自己指出的）：现有 `fakeGh` 遇到 `--json …reviews` 只回 `{ reviews }`、不带 `headRefOid`，
于是新加的快照解析在单测里**永远走 `null`**（没查成 → 维持复用），**新代码一行都没被行使**。

## 两类正控（缺一即红）

- **源码锁**（`tests/reuse-needs-verdict.test.js`）：`mirasimWorkerDone` 函数体里同时有
  `'headRefOid,reviews,comments'`、`verdictOnHead: verdict`、`handoffTimesOf(parsed.comments)`。
  切段用「到下一个顶层 `export` 为止」——按 `\n}` 切会被函数体里第一个列 0 的右花括号提前截断
  （本笔第一版就是这么栽的，当场改掉）。
- **行为锁**（`tests/mirasim-reviewer.test.js`）：注入「一次快照里 head=新、票打在旧 oid、会话
  `phase=done`、有未答问题」→ `reworked-new`、`startSession` 调 **1** 次、`interact` 调 **0** 次；
  对照（快照读不到，等价于修前漏传）→ `reworked-interact`、`startSession` **0** 次。
  `fakeGh` 加 `snapshot` 注入口（不给时行为不变，老用例不受影响）。
  > 踩到的坑记一笔：`phase` 必须在 **view 顶层**——`sessionStateOf` 读 `state/phase/observedState/runState`，

`mirasimWorkerDone` 这条调用面原来也**只在比 oid**——返工只改正文时同样会假阳「本轮已判定」。

author: thesevenpens
body:
Fixes #718.

Every piece of text in OTA has been rendering in the OS default font, on any machine without Inter installed system-wide — which is most of them, including this one. Not a few headings: **the whole app**.

## Why

`App.axaml` declared the display family as a bare name:

```xml
<FontFamily x:Key="DisplayFontFamily">Inter</FontFamily>
```

A bare name goes to the **system** font manager. The bundled Inter is registered by `.WithInterFont()` (`Program.cs:88`) as an *embedded collection* — `fonts:Inter` → `avares://Avalonia.Fonts.Inter/Assets`, confirmed by reading the strings out of `Avalonia.Fonts.Inter` 12.1.2 itself. A bare name never reaches it.

It failed invisibly because a fallback font looks fine. There is no error, no warning, and no visual tell unless you already know what Inter looks like.

## Confirmed independently

#718 diagnosed it by pixel-comparing against a family that cannot exist. I confirmed it by a different method — asking the font manager what each form actually resolves to:

```
Inter              ->  family = BareMinimum
fonts:Inter#Inter  ->  family = Inter
ZZNoSuchFont       ->  family = BareMinimum
```

The bare name resolves to the same thing a nonsense name does.

**Note what that also shows.** `TryGetGlyphTypeface` returns `true` for all three — it succeeds *by falling back*. A test asserting the boolean would pass in every possible world. The discriminator is `FamilyName`, and that is what these tests assert.

## Seven places, not three

The issue found `App.axaml` and two in `TabletDetailView.axaml`. There were four more in `Styles.axaml`, and one of them is why this was app-wide rather than cosmetic:

```xml
<Style Selector=":is(TopLevel)">
    <Setter Property="FontFamily" Value="Inter" />   <!-- every piece of text inherits this -->
</Style>
```

All seven point at the single `DisplayFontFamily` resource now rather than repeating the URI, so there is one place to be wrong.

## Tests

Three, and the reasoning behind each is the point:

1. **The app's own resource resolves to Inter.** Read from `Application.Current`, not a copy of the string — a test that hardcoded the expected value would pass while the app was misconfigured, which is exactly how this survived.
2. **A bare name does *not* resolve to Inter.** Pinned because the fix is one "tidy-up" away from reversion by anyone who finds `fonts:Inter#Inter` odd. Asserted against what a nonsense family resolves to.
3. **No XAML names a font family literally.** Repeating a font URI is how six places would stay wrong after the seventh was fixed.

### The third test's first version was itself a probe that could not fail

It matched only `FontFamily="..."` and missed `<Setter Property="FontFamily" Value="..." />` — **four of the seven offenders**. I found it by mutating a setter back to a literal and watching the test pass.

Both forms are covered now, and both mutations fail it. Reverting `App.axaml` fails test 1.

## Not touched

`MonoFontFamily` is `Consolas, Cascadia Mono, monospace` — a list of *system* fonts with nothing bundled, so it has no equivalent defect. Bundling a cross-platform monospace is #627.

## Verification

- 0 warnings, 0 errors. Format gate clean.
- `1048 + 94` passing, 2 skipped by platform.
- Three mutations confirmed caught: the original bug restored, and a literal family name reintroduced in each of the two XAML forms.
- The app launched from this build and logged no font errors.

**The visual confirmation is worth doing by eye** — the typography should now differ across the entire app, which is the claim this makes and the one a test can only approximate.

author: ferraroroberto
body:
## Summary

Slice 5 of 5 for #1070, and a different surface from the other four. Life OS skills get the Coding tab's favorites treatment (#250): a star on each row, starred skills sorted to the top, persisted server-side.

Built deliberately to the *same* contract rather than as a parallel invention — `life_os_favorites` is a plain string list beside `coding_favorites` in the same config (no new file, no new store), `POST /api/life-os/favorites` mirrors `/api/claude-code/favorites` body-for-body, `is_favorite` joins the skills payload, and `renderSkills()` does the same stable partition `renderCodingList()` does so both groups stay in the scanner's alphabetical order rather than reshuffling around a star. The star reuses the Coding row's classes and its filled-gold `.is-fav` treatment, so the two tabs read identically.

**No header favorites-*filter* toggle.** The issue lists it as optional and names the star plus the ordering as the ask, so that is what this does.

## One deliberate non-validation

The starred id is **not** checked against the scanner. A skill can be renamed or removed on disk between a star and the next scan; a stale entry simply matches nothing when the list renders, and refusing it would mean a disk read on every tap for no gain. There is a test asserting a stale favourite neither 500s nor invents a row.

## A test-isolation bug worth reading

The backend tests point `life_os_dir` at a temp checkout **through the config file**, not by assigning `app.state.webapp_config`. My first version did the latter, and it was wrong in a way that looked green: `update_webapp_config()` reloads from disk and replaces that object wholesale, so the in-memory override silently reverted mid-test and the scanner walked the **real life-os checkout on the dev box** — 15 private skills. Two of the three tests passed against private on-disk content instead of the fixture, and only the third failed loudly enough to expose it.

That is the same species as the stale pins in the #1025/#1040 episode: a test describing what the code happened to do rather than the requirement. Worth flagging because the failure mode here was privacy, not just correctness.

## The gate caught a security gap — worth reading

The first gate run went **red**, and correctly. `POST /api/life-os/favorites` sits under the terminal-grade `/api/life-os` prefix, and `test_terminal_guard_coverage` (#999) refuses any route there that matches no row in `_TERMINAL_GUARD_RULES` — because that default *fails open*: a new route beside gated siblings silently inherits **less** protection than they have. Exactly the #985/#997 failure mode that test exists to prevent. Mine would have shipped on the bearer token alone with nothing saying so.

Classified deliberately as `DELIBERATELY_TOKEN_ONLY`, with the reasoning recorded in the file:

- It writes skill **ids** to config and echoes them back. No private subtree is read, nothing is spawned, no PTY is touched.
- It is strictly less sensitive than the `/api/life-os/skills` list it reorders — which is itself already deliberately token-only.
- Every passkey-gated `life-os` row is a *private-content* read (`/file`, `/files`, `/conversations`, `/conversations/search`). This is not one.
- Its Coding twin `POST /api/claude-code/favorites` sits outside every terminal prefix and is token-only for the same reason.
- Worst case for a bearer-token holder is reordering a list they can already read in full.

Removing that entry makes the test fail again, so the classification is load-bearing rather than decorative. **If you disagree with the reading, this is the one line to change** — and re-gating it would also be a client change (the tab would have to send `X-Terminal-Token`, cf. #997), which is the same open question the file already records for the two Life OS launch routes.

## Test plan

- [x] Four tests, **all proven to fail against pre-fix code** (3 backend failures; the e2e failing on the absent `.star-btn`).
- [x] Backend: round-trip + persistence to disk, idempotence under repeated taps, 400 on a missing id, and a stale favourite being harmless.
- [x] e2e: the star posts the right body, the row sorts to the top from the re-fetched payload, and the star paints as pressed.
- [x] The e2e mock keys its response on the POST having happened, not on a call count — the tab fetches the skills list more than once, so a "second call" switch flipped before the star was tapped and made the pre-tap ordering assertion read the post-tap payload. Caught and fixed.
- [x] `pwsh -File scripts/verify-before-ship.ps1` — red first (the guard gap above), green after classifying the route. `scripts/classify_e2e.py` routed this to `tier=surface` (`lifeos`), its designed narrowing when every changed path sits in one declared surface.

## What to look at on the phone

Life OS tab. Each skill row should carry a star to the right of 🚀; tap one and the skill jumps to the top of the list and the star fills gold. Close and reopen the app to confirm it survived — that is the half that needed a server round trip rather than localStorage.

Closes #1070

author: rodacato
body:
ADR-0003 says a prompt injection could write to `src/`. It cannot, and the ADR is public,
so it currently argues a risk it overstates.

[ADR-0002](docs/adr/0002-cli-internal-tools-off.md) was accepted the same day and gives every
request:

```
--tools ''  --permission-mode dontAsk  --settings '{"disableAllHooks":true}'
```

The model has no file, shell or web tool, and no hooks run. **There is no known path today
from a request to a write.** I wrote the threat model without checking the ADR sitting next
to it in the same directory.

## What this does not change

Part 1 was still worth shipping, for a reason the ADR now states instead:

- It narrows what a compromise of the service *process* can reach — the Node process does own
  the checkout, and `Restart=on-failure` does reload whatever is on disk.
- It removes a step that a future agentic endpoint would restore. ADR-0002 says such a feature
  supersedes it rather than flipping the flag back, and the day it lands, an unconfined
  checkout is a real hole rather than a theoretical one.

Doing it before that feature exists is cheap. Doing it after would be a scramble.

## Related, and not fixed here

Verifying the deploy on the host turned up that the CLI entrypoints live under
`/home/shellmer/.local/bin` and `.npm-global/bin`, which the unit grants as writable — so the
sandbox closes the checkout and leaves the binaries open. That observation is correct, but it
inherits the same unverified premise: it needs a process already able to write as `shellmer`,
and the vector we both assumed is the one `--tools ''` closes. Worth a decision on its own
terms rather than an urgent patch.

author: liinoorf
body:
Iba a hacer la pantalla de empresas y, verificando el camino primero —como debí haber hecho desde el principio—, me encontré con que **el módulo entero está en la ruta equivocada**.

`empresas.controller.ts` es el **único** de los 28 que declara el prefijo a mano:

```ts
@Controller('v1/empresas')   // y main.ts ya hace setGlobalPrefix('v1')
```

Comprobado contra la API corriendo:

```
antes:  /v1/empresas → 404   ·  /v1/v1/empresas → 200
ahora:  /v1/empresas → 200   ·  /v1/v1/empresas → 404
```

## Y no fallaba nada, que es lo peor

El controller se registra igual. Las rutas existen igual. El OpenAPI las publica —en la ruta equivocada— y el SDK se genera desde ahí. **Y los tests que lo probaban usaban la ruta equivocada también**, así que estaban verdes probando algo que ningún cliente podía alcanzar.

Su segundo controller tenía lo mismo: declaraba `v1/contacts` y convivía sin ruido con el de contactos de verdad — uno respondiendo en `/v1/contacts` y este en `/v1/v1/contacts`.

## La guarda

Cruza los `@Controller` contra el prefijo global. Probé que atrapa el caso real revirtiendo el arreglo:

```
× ningún @Controller empieza con 'v1/'
  → empresas.controller.ts: @Controller('v1/empresas')
    Sus rutas quedan en /v1/v1/… y la dirección documentada devuelve 404.
```

Hay un tercer test que comprueba que el prefijo global **sigue siendo** `v1`: si alguien lo cambia, esta guarda deja de tener sentido y hay que mirarla de nuevo, no dejarla comprobando algo que ya no aplica.

## Verificado andando

```
crear empresa            → Peluquería Ñuñoa SpA · RUT 76086428-5
RUT con DV malo          → COMPANY_INVALID: dígito verificador no coincide
colgar un contacto       → 200
ficha de la empresa      → 1 contacto
```

**156/156** en `api`, `pnpm lint` limpio. La pantalla va aparte, ahora que la ruta existe donde dice.

body:
## Description

Fixes #33

This PR addresses the race condition in `ToolResultGuard` where concurrent `ascan()` calls on the same guard instance could trigger a `KeyError` during `_cache.move_to_end()` or `_cache.popitem(last=False)`.

### Key Changes
- **Thread-safe cache operations (`src/prompt_shield/tool_guard/guard.py`)**:
  - Added a per-instance `threading.Lock()` initialized in `ToolResultGuard.__init__`.
  - Encapsulated cache access into `_cache_lookup(cache_key)`: acquires lock, checks membership, moves key to end on hit, and returns the cached report atomically.
  - Encapsulated cache insertion and LRU eviction into `_cache_set(cache_key, report)`: acquires lock, inserts report, and evicts oldest items if exceeding `cache_size` atomically.
  - Policy enforcement (`_enforce`) remains outside the lock to minimize lock contention.
- **Regression Test (`tests/tool_guard/test_guard.py`)**:
  - Added `TestConcurrentAscan.test_concurrent_ascan_cache_thread_safety` which fires 32 concurrent `ascan()` calls with overlapping keys against a guard with a small LRU cache (`cache_size=4`), verifying that no exceptions or race conditions occur.

### Verification
- Tested locally:
  - `pytest tests/tool_guard/test_guard.py -k TestConcurrentAscan`: Passed.
  - `pytest tests/tool_guard/test_guard.py -k TestCache`: Passed.

💡 The vulnerability class is unbounded memory growth (a form of resource exhaustion/DoS) in the content script, where `discoveredMedia` and `pendingNetworkFilter` grew without limit for every unique media URL found on the page.
🎯 The impact if exploited is that a hostile page can allocate 1 million URLs which consumes ~318MB of DOM memory in its own process, driving up the extension's memory consumption by ~165MB (for the Map) and ~123MB (for the Set), leading to high memory footprint.
🔧 The fix places a constant cap (`MAX_TRACKED_MEDIA = 10000`) on both sets. This limits memory consumption to under 2MB, which is safe and far exceeds reasonable infinite-scroll gallery needs.
✅ Verified by running `npm test` and `bash build.sh` without any breakages.

author: rowan-claude
body:
Twelve simultaneous launches tripped sshd's `MaxStartups`, and 119 cards started within one minute
against a single provider key. Glenn: *"Staggering is always important."*

**(1) `--stagger <duration>`, default `3s`**, between launches to the SAME bench on `nova-pulse
launch` and `nova-pulse fill`, and a **jittered 0–2 s start** on `nova-swarm native`. A wave no
longer opens N ssh sessions or N provider streams in the same second.
**(2) `--max-inflight` per route** — #1784's flag, which landed as a squash in `integration-16t`
(`2d99edbf`) and is parsed at `cmd/nova-swarm/main.go:512` — is now passed by `fill`, keyed on the
already-exported `swarm.RouteKey` (`internal/swarm/inflight.go:56`). **Reused, not reinvented.**
**(3) `harvest --bench` and the batch's bench reads** stagger the same way.

**THE TEST DOES NOT SLEEP AND HOPE.** A timing test is the easiest kind to write so that it cannot

author: realsdx
body:
Runtime-rs uses the unmaintained Jaeger exporter ([RUSTSEC-2025-0123](https://rustsec.org/advisories/RUSTSEC-2025-0123.html)), and
service exit can race the final trace flush.

The changes are split into two commits:

1. Migrate the exporter: replace the deprecated Jaeger exporter with
  OTLP/gRPC, retain the existing configuration keys and Basic auth support,
  and route exporter warnings and errors to the shim journal.
2. Fix shutdown ordering: move provider shutdown from the shutdown
  request handler to the service-exit path, where it is awaited while
  Tokio can still drive the exporter. Take the provider only once and
  release locks before flushing on a dedicated thread. Bound the tracing
  phase to five seconds and log failures without preventing shim exit.

The second commit is needed because changing the exporter alone does not
prevent service exit from interrupting the final flush of buffered spans.

### Configuration Change

The existing `jaeger_endpoint`, `jaeger_user`, and `jaeger_password` keys
remain. The default endpoint changes from `http://localhost:14268/api/traces`
to `http://localhost:4317`.

Enable the collector's OTLP/gRPC receiver and update explicit Thrift URLs.
Go tracing is unchanged; Jaeger can accept both protocols. Basic auth is
retained where the receiver/proxy supports it; use HTTPS for credentials
sent over a network.

author: imaustink
body:
## The short version

**33 environment variables the code reads appeared in no document at all.** Everything is now written down, and a test keeps it that way.

## Why it drifted

They aren't read in one place. Most by `ferry` and `install.sh` in shell, `SERVICE_CIDR` and the etcd ports by `control-plane/up.sh`, and three — `FERRY_ALLOW_OFF_SLICE`, `FERRY_NODE_VERBOSE`, `FERRY_NODE_NO_CONFIG` — by the **Swift binaries** through `ProcessInfo.environment`.

Those last three are how it went unnoticed. `FERRY_ALLOW_OFF_SLICE` is in `ferry --help`, yet no sweep written against the shell can find it — I only caught it because my first coverage check flagged it as "documented but not read by the code", which was backwards and made me look.

`docs/INSTALL.md` now carries a parameter reference with **defaults extracted from the source rather than remembered**, grouped by purpose: installing, cluster identity, pods, networking, machines, GPU, versions/building, upgrades/joining, plus an explicitly-internal set.

A test sweeps **both halves** and fails on anything new that isn't documented or exempted. I verified it fails when a variable is deleted from the doc rather than passing vacuously:

```
✗ read by the code, documented nowhere: FERRY_MACHINE_SUBNET
```

## Install paths

Eight, written as paths rather than as a pile of variables to assemble yourself: install and run, install without starting, a particular version, from a mirror or air-gapped or a local build, joining another Mac, building from source, upgrading, uninstalling.

## Adding nodes

This was the worst of it, because it means **three different things** with different isolation and different commands:

| | what it adds | isolation |
|---|---|---|
| `ferry node add` | another kubelet on **this** Mac | a VM per pod |
| `ferry join` | **another Mac** | a VM per pod |
| a `Machine` | a Linux node VM on this Mac | pods share its kernel |

Each gets a section, including the things that actually bite: pod network slices and what happens on a cluster predating the node-index label; that a token is reusable for 24 hours; that joining over SSH gives you a node that dies ~20s after the session closes; and that a Mac which joined **does not come back after a reboot**.

## The pitch now leads with performance and not sizing anything

The README sold the *mechanism* — "the pod is the virtual machine" — rather than the reason to want it. It now leads with the two things true whichever mode you use: **nothing to size up front, and nothing to wait for.**

Both measured, not asserted:

- 128 pod VMs configured with 512 MiB each — **64 GiB asked for — consumed 1.6 GiB**, because guests are lazily backed and pay for pages they touch
- a real Alpine pod is up in **0.33s**, answers ping in 0.34ms, and the **128th VM starts as fast as the first**

The comparison table changed axis with it: it compared *isolation*, which is the implementation, and now compares **what you size up front** and **what it costs idle** — the part that shows up in someone's day.

Choosing isolation is now a footnote, as it should be: one paragraph noting a `Machine` is denser and faster per container (~45ms vs ~300ms), that a pod picks with `nodeSelector`, and that neither mode asks you to size anything in advance.

**One number was wrong on the way through**, worth flagging since the pitch rests on these: `0.06–0.09s` is the hypervisor *starting a VM*, not the guest reaching userspace, which is `~0.12s`. Experiment 03 measures both and I'd conflated them. Every figure in the opening is now checked against the experiment that produced it.

## The README had a false claim

> there is no Linux host anywhere in the system

True of mode 1. Mode 2's node *is* a Linux host — `docs/MACHINES.md` already said the README would have to stop claiming this. The comparison table also listed ferry as vm-per-pod only, which undersells what mode 2 buys: one cluster holding both, with a pod choosing by `nodeSelector`.

Also added Status bullets for mode 2 and the installer, and Layout entries for `ferry-machined/`, `manifests/machines/`, `node-image/` and experiments 17–20 — none of which it knew existed.

I kept mode 1 as the headline rather than re-pitching the project around "choose your isolation", since that's your call. `MACHINES.md` argues for the broader framing if you want to go further.

211 tests pass. All README links and all INSTALL.md anchors resolve.

author: kobzevvv
body:
## Problem

After `/restart`, the maintenance drain flag (`maintenance.json.drain`) is created on disk. The old process waits 85s for active tasks to drain, then calls `process.exit(0)`. systemd restarts the process — but the new instance sees the drain flag and stays in paused mode **indefinitely**. No tasks run, users see \"Ожидание: N с.\" growing forever.

Root cause: `resumePendingTasks()` had a comment saying "coordinator --ready will clear it", but the coordinator was removed. Nobody ever clears the drain flag after restart.

## Fix

Call `maintenance.resume()` in `resumePendingTasks()` so the drain flag is unconditionally removed on every process startup. This is safe — a fresh process should always start clean.

## To unblock now (before deploy)

```bash
ssh vova@136.65.7.197 'rm -f ~/agent-data/maintenance.json.drain && sudo systemctl restart assist-agent'
```

author: tato123
body:
The Linux regression check commissioned with `macos-platform-floor` (#2364) has reported. **Decision 4 stands** — the camera carries the device's capture instant — and **the gate on the timestamp work in #2359 is lifted.** Two findings amend §Media I/O rather than reopening the block.

## 1. A bag carries two stamps, and the consumers split across them

| | where | who reads it |
|---|---|---|
| **payload** `VideoFrame.timestamp_ns` | `camera_source.rs:1152` | the encoder (`:234`, `:249`, `:280`) |
| **envelope** `FrameHeader.timestamp_ns` | set inside `OutputWriter::write` (`output.rs:575`) | `Mp4Sink` (`mp4_sink.rs:105-111`), the mesh |

The camera calls plain `write()`, so both are publication time and **agree by accident**. `MicrophoneSource` calls `write_with_timestamp` — with a comment naming this exact hazard — so audio's envelope already carries capture time.

Moving only `:1152`, as the ticket was scoped, would give **two different answers for one frame in one graph**: encoder on capture time, `Mp4Sink`-direct and the mesh still on publish time. The camera moves to `write_with_timestamp` instead.

*Verified here against the tree, not taken on report.*

## 2. The monotonic flag is necessary and not sufficient

`vivid` sets `V4L2_BUF_FLAG_TIMESTAMP_MONOTONIC` **honestly** — the stamp really is on `CLOCK_MONOTONIC` — and still reports every stamp roughly **nine tenths of a frame period in the future**:

```
1280x720@30   p50 = -29787 µs   (0.894 frame periods)
 640x480@60   p50 = -14903 µs   (0.894)
1920x1080@15  p50 = -59560 µs   (0.893)
```

Same ratio at three rates, ~130 µs spread end to end — a deterministic synthetic cadence, not jitter. A rule of *"trust it iff monotonic"* would accept a stamp that puts video a frame period **ahead** of audio on the rig and in CI, since the E2E fixture drives `vivid`.

So: take the stamp when the device reports it monotonic and non-zero; otherwise fall back to the engine's clock at dequeue and warn once per device. **A stamp ahead of the engine's clock at dequeue is clamped to that instant and counted.**

Owner's call, 2026-09-19 — a stable fixture over a visible skew, on the reasoning that no real capture happens in the future and trusting one silently is how A/V skew ships.

## What did not change

No consumer breaks outright. No test asserts on a camera timestamp today — timestamp assertions exist only on audio, and the loss-visibility metrics are sequence-based and immune.

## Residual, carried rather than closed

**No real camera was available to the check** — all four nodes on that box are `vivid` — so what a UVC device reports is unmeasured. The clamp is what makes that gap safe to carry, and it is stated in the change rather than left implicit.

Follows #2364. Ticket #2359 updated with both findings inline.

author: coreentryadmin-web
body:
## Root cause

#5257 (merged earlier this cycle) fixed the "Current" tile's desktop truncation by widening the primary grid column's *relative share* (`1fr` → `1.5fr`) and dropping the swing-largo font-size override back to 22px. Both changes are unconditional (not media-gated), so they apply at every viewport — but the PR's own verification (local Playwright screenshots "at the real ~500px hero width", plus the live desktop repro) never checked the *absolute* pixel result once the whole hero shrinks to phone width. Its own write-up flagged this explicitly as unverified: "spot-check the same tile at phone width (430px, mobile UA) — this fix only touched the swing-largo desktop-scale override and the shared grid rule, so confirm mobile wasn't already fine and isn't now regressed."

This cycle's retry of exactly that check found it was NOT fine: 1.5fr of a ~400px-wide phone hero still isn't enough absolute room at 22px, even though it comfortably fixed the desktop case where the hero is 2-3x wider.

## Evidence

- **Live repro** (`proxy-browser.cjs`, minted premium Clerk session, phone viewport 430x932, `/nighthawk?view=SWING`, clicked into a real HOLD swing position): "Current" tile visibly rendered `"+$..."` (CSS ellipsis — confirmed no such literal placeholder string exists anywhere in `TerminalPremiumPanels.tsx`, which only ever renders `${dollarSign}${usd(dollar)}` or an em dash).
- **Mechanical confirmation** (headless DOM measurement, same viewport, same live production page, 8s initial + 8s post-click wait to rule out a transient pre-hydration frame — an earlier, shorter-waited sample on a different play happened to catch a frame where the value fit, which is what forced this more deliberate re-measurement): `{"text":"+$0.00","scrollWidth":112,"clientWidth":74,"overflowing":true}` on `.nh-deck-trade-hero__metric.is-primary .v` — the shortest, plainest dollar string this field ever produces (no negative sign, no thousands separator) already overflows, so every realistic value does too.
- CloudWatch (`/ecs/blackout-production`, checked twice this cycle, `TypeError`/`Unhandled`/`"undefined is not"`) both clean — unrelated, logged for completeness per the cycle's standing checklist.

## Blast radius

Same root cause hits every swing play with any dollar-formatted "Current" value viewed on a phone (≤480px) — the majority of real traffic to a quick-glance P&L check. The 0DTE view shares the same base (non-swing-largo) `is-primary` rule so it's exposed too (less severely — 18px base vs swing-largo's font history), and gets the same protection from this fix since the plain selector is also covered.

## Fix rationale

Added a `@media (max-width:480px)` block, placed after both the base and `.nh-deck--swing-largo` `is-primary .v` rules so it wins on source-order for equal selector specificity:

1. `.nh-deck-trade-hero__metrics` grid-template-columns: primary column widened further, `1.5fr` (the desktop #5257 value) → `2.5fr`, only below 480px — desktop untouched, media-gated.
2. Both `.nh-deck-trade-hero__metric.is-primary .v` and its `.nh-deck--swing-largo`-scoped counterpart get font-size dropped to `18px` (from 22px) only below 480px — re-capped both because the swing-largo-scoped rule is the one that actually renders on `/nighthawk?view=SWING`; fixing only the plain selector would look fixed while leaving the real production repro broken.

Deliberately kept the existing `overflow:hidden;text-overflow:ellipsis` clip guard as a backstop for a genuinely extreme value (e.g. a 4-digit P&L), which can still occur even at 18px.

Extended `nh-deck-metric-value-overflow-css.test.ts` with a third test asserting: the mobile media block exists, its primary column fraction is strictly greater than the desktop 1.5fr, and both the plain and swing-largo `is-primary .v` font-sizes inside it are strictly less than the desktop 22px. Verified RED→GREEN (git-stash the CSS-only diff). 436/436 nighthawk command-deck tests pass, `tsc --noEmit` clean.

Staged finding: `docs/audit/findings-staging/2026-09-19-nh-swing-current-tile-mobile-overflow.md`. Market-open validation entry added to `docs/audit/MARKET-OPEN-VALIDATION.md`.

author: marcsaad-hadidi
body:
## Summary

Add a separate local cleaning stage for standardized historical OHLCV. Recoverable invalid rows are removed with one reason per row; structural ambiguity fails. Ingestion remains explicit and separate. No API calls or new dependencies.

## Cleaning Policy

Normalize an input copy, remove invalid/future rows, detect conflicting valid keys, remove exact duplicates, sort by symbol/date, and explicitly validate the final contract. Deterministic and idempotent with an explicit inclusive as_of_date; one valid row is sufficient.

## Schema

Require exactly date,symbol,open,high,low,close,volume, rejecting missing, unexpected, and duplicate columns. Output order is fixed: naive datetime64[ns], string symbol, float64 OHLC, Int64 volume. Multi-symbol support preserves punctuation and exchange qualifiers.

## Missing Values

Drop rows with any missing or blank required cell. No imputation, forward/backward fill, interpolation, or invented financial values.

## Duplicates

Deduplicate identical normalized observations. Different valid OHLCV observations for one (symbol,date) raise DuplicateConflictError. Invalid and future rows are removed first.

## Invalid Values

Drop nonfinite/malformed numerics, nonpositive prices, inconsistent OHLC, and negative/fractional/out-of-range volume. Preserve integral numeric volume exactly, including large binary floats and Int64 strings.

## Date Safety

Accept calendar dates and naive midnight representations within the pandas nanosecond range. Reject ambiguous dates, timezone-aware values, and intraday timestamps without conversion. Drop dates later than as_of_date; the default is the local date. Never infer or add missing sessions.

## Leakage Prevention

Unexpected future/target columns fail. Cleaning is row-local plus structural duplicate handling; no future values repair observations. No outlier statistics, scaling, features, targets, or labels.

## Cleaning Report

Report input/output/removed counts, nine mutually exclusive primary removal categories, retained date range, sorted symbols, and retention ratio. No generated timestamp, source rows, provider URLs, or credentials. Categories sum to input_rows - output_rows.

## Storage

Read local UTF-8 CSV with a 64 MiB limit and no dtype/NA inference. Preserve source files; default outputs are processed/cleaned/<dataset>.csv and <dataset>.report.json, already ignored by Git. Reject path aliases and existing hard links. Both destinations are checked before writes, overwrite defaults to false, and both reuse the existing atomic writer. Each file is atomic; the pair is not a transaction, so a report-write failure can leave a new CSV with an absent/older report. Only a successful return denotes a complete run.

## Tests

- Python 3.12.14 environment from #54; pip install -r requirements.txt succeeded with existing dependencies; pip check passed.

## Summary

The vault watch re-reads the open folder whenever its fingerprint moves, and that rebuild dropped the session back to `loading`. Everything the screen derives from "loaded" went with it.

Measured on the map at 1512×982 with nothing touched, sampling twice a second for 22 seconds:

| | |
|---|---|
| Folder name and document count missing | about 3.5 s out of every 8.6 s |
| Blank samples, before | 14 of 40 |
| Blank samples, after | 0 of 40 |
| What the recent filter said while blank | nothing changed in seven days |
| What had actually changed that day | 20 of 20 documents |

So for roughly two fifths of the time the map did not say which folder it was showing, and told the reader a zero that was false. Reproduced on the dev server and on the static export, with no interaction.

A rebuild of the same handle now keeps the frame already on screen and swaps in the new manifest when it arrives. A different folder, or one not loaded yet, still shows `loading`, because there is nothing to keep there.

## Summary
- Choosing colours with the native picker on a phone is slow and imprecise, and the colour drives the whole engine; the photo already has the answer. Picking a photo in the add form now offers one to three colours as editable chips, each with the engine's own Sanzo name (`anchorFor`, from #120). Nothing is sent to a server and there is no new dependency.
- `extractColours` (`src/lib/colors/extract.ts`) is pure and takes RGBA pixels: it drops the background (the alpha of a cut-out, else the dominant border colours flood-filled in small steps, so a vignette or a letterbox bar goes but a garment merely touching the edge does not), runs k-means (k=3) in OKLab, orders by area and folds away tiny and near-duplicate clusters. `suggestColours` only decodes the file at 64 px; the uploaded file is untouched.
- Near-black and near-white snap to exact `#000000` / `#ffffff` (`snapNeutralExtremes`) because `SAFE_NEUTRAL_SHOE_HEXES` compares the exact hex. A test runs every colour of the #119 reference set through the snap and requires the anchor to stay acceptable, which is where the thresholds come from (L under 0.26 or over 0.94, chroma under 0.025: a navy or a black-green is left alone).
- A suggestion only fills an empty list or replaces its own previous suggestion, never a colour the person picked. Chips show the names in the edit form too.

## Decisions
- Background removal went through three versions against the real garment photos in the dev wardrobe (40 of them, product shots on grey or white and garments hanging on a wardrobe door): a global reference colour left vignettes and screenshot bars as chips; the final one seeds from each dominant border colour and spreads in small steps. Of the 40 photos, 12 give one chip, 10 two, 18 three.
- One new string, `form.colorsFromPhoto`, in ca, es and en.
- The add form only. Replacing a photo in the edit form does not touch the colours.

## Known limits (accepted in the issue)
Garments on a busy background (the wardrobe-door photos give wood colours until #125), a white garment on a light grey sheet (it merges with it), shadows and patterns. The chips are always editable and never block saving.

## Test plan
- [ ] `/add` at 375 px and on desktop, pick a product photo: one to three chips with Sanzo names and the note under them
- [ ] Pick a second photo: the untouched chips are replaced; edit a chip first and pick another photo: your colour stays

author: justin-stanley
body:
Closes #141.

## What was wrong

`update_subscription` is a `putRecord`, and a putRecord replaces the **whole** record — per its own doc at `src/atproto.rs`. The handler built a fresh record and handed that over:

```rust
let mut sub = Subscription::new(feed_url, now_rfc3339());
sub.title = form.title...;
sub.site_url = form.site_url...;
sub.folder = form.folder...;
```

`templates/manage_row.html` posts `url`, `title` and `folder` — and nothing else. So every field the form does not carry was written back as its default, on **every rename**:

| field | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `siteUrl` | whatever the feed advertised | gone |
| `fetchHint` | as set | gone |
| `private` | as set | gone |
| `createdAt` | original subscribe time | reset to now |

**That is four fields, not the three #141 names.** `private` is the one the issue missed: `Subscription::new` sets it to `None` and the handler never assigns it. The two `private` mentions in that function are the feed-privacy classification check, which is a different thing. I've corrected the issue.

`createdAt` is the worst of the four. It is the reader's subscribe time, the sort key for "when did I subscribe", it lives in **their** repo rather than our cache, and once overwritten it is gone with nothing in the UI to say so.

## The fix

Read-modify-write. There is no single-record read on `Repo` — no `getRecord`, only `list_subscriptions_sorted` — so this lists and filters by rkey. That is one extra round trip on an action already doing a PDS write, and it is bounded; a `get_subscription` on the `dispatch!` macro would be strictly better if it ever measures badly, and drops in behind the same handler logic.

**A repoint at a different feed URL is allowed** — it is what the global-feeds-ceiling check above exists for — so the two kinds of field are treated differently:

- `createdAt` and `private` belong to the **subscription**, and always carry over. A URL correction is not a new subscription.
- `siteUrl` and `fetchHint` describe the **specific feed**, and are dropped on a repoint rather than left hanging off the new one. An explicit form value still wins if the form ever starts carrying one.

**A failed read refuses the rename.** Falling back to rebuilding from scratch would reinstate the data loss on exactly the flaky path, which is the worst place to have it. The write below already takes this stance — *"a failure here means nothing was renamed or moved"* — and the read now gets the same one. An rkey that is not in the repo is refused too: renaming a record that is not there would **create** one, with a fresh `createdAt`.

## Tests

The characterization test was written first and seen to fail, printing the reset it exists to catch:

```
left:  "2026-09-19T21:38:49Z"
right: "2024-03-01T00:00:00.000Z"
```

All three assert on **the bytes the sidecar receives**, not on a `Subscription` built in the test — the record only becomes wrong on the way out, so checking the value passed in would pass just as happily with the fix removed.

The mock reads to `content-length` rather than taking one `read`, and each captured body must mention the collection, so a truncated capture fails loudly instead of satisfying the assertions vacuously (refs #144).

Mutation-checked five ways, each caught by its own test and no other:

| mutation | caught by |
|---|---|
| `createdAt` not preserved | `renaming_preserves_…` (+ `repointing_…`) |
| `private` not preserved | `renaming_preserves_…` (+ `repointing_…`) |
| `siteUrl`/`fetchHint` not preserved | `renaming_preserves_…` |
| repoint carries the old feed's two onto the new one | `repointing_…` |
| failed read rebuilds from scratch | `a_rename_whose_read_fails_writes_nothing` |

That last one is the one worth having. Falling back on a read error looks like graceful degradation and is in fact the original bug, reinstated where it is hardest to notice.

## Known limit, not addressed here

`putRecord` has **no `swapRecord` support** in either backend — verified in both `atproto.rs` and `oauth/xrpc.rs`. `WriteResult` carries a `cid` but nothing consumes it. So a read-modify-write still has a lost-update window against another atproto client writing between our read and our write.

That window is far narrower than unconditionally destroying four fields on every rename, but it is not zero, and it should not be implied away. Closing it means threading `swapRecord` through `putRecord` on both backends — a separate change.

## Verification

733 lib + 16 bin green, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` clean, `cargo fmt --check` clean. No existing test disturbed.

author: wdhaines
body:
Closes the first child of the 2026-09-19 duplicate/slow-render epic: **tunatale-rwkz.1**.

## What happened
One pasted story became two review sessions on prod. Two `POST /api/review-sessions/import` calls ~75 s apart, each minting an id and each starting a render — on a 953 MB box where one render already fills memory. They took 47 and 58 minutes.

Neither POST has a uvicorn access line, because **uvicorn omits the access log when the client has already disconnected**. The first connection died on the phone; the second was cut off by a page reload ~15 s before it would have answered. From the server's side a lost request and an absent request look the same.

## Why the fix is server-side
`ManualStoryPanel` already disables the Import button while a request is in flight — and re-enables it in its `finally` when the fetch fails on the network, which is exactly what happened. 75 s is far too slow for a double tap on a disabled button, and a **browser-level POST retry** on a dropped mobile connection produces the identical trace. The user could not say which it was, so the guarantee has to hold when the second request is not a tap at all.

## The change
- **`app/api/idempotency.py`** — single-flight keyed on `(route scope, language, key)`. Every caller awaits the work through `asyncio.shield`, so a client disconnecting mid-request neither cancels the work nor loses its result; the retry is handed the session the first attempt created.
- **Failures are deliberately not memoised.** A generation that 429s must leave the key free — a wedged button is a worse bug than the duplicate this prevents.
- **A header, not a body field.** `CreateReviewSessionRequest` is `extra="forbid"`, and a browser resending a dropped POST repeats headers verbatim while it would never repeat a freshly-generated body field.
- **CORS** — `Idempotency-Key` added to `allow_headers`. It is not safelisted, so without this a dev browser's preflight refuses it and deduplication is silently off.
- **Client** — the key is minted when an attempt starts, **kept while it keeps failing**, dropped on success. Both the paste panel and the home page's Generate button. Minting a fresh key on the retry would reproduce the duplicate with idempotency "implemented" on both sides.

## Verification
Red-first, measured: **4 of 7** new backend tests failed before the change; **3 passed** (the two describing today's keyless behaviour, plus different-keys). That split is what said the harness was measuring the right thing — an earlier run where *all 7* failed turned out to be a missing `X-TT-Language` header in my test client, not a product fact. The CORS test and both frontend key-lifecycle suites were also red before their changes.

`./test.sh` green on the committed tree:
- backend **100.00%** coverage, 7962 passed
- frontend **100%** on 78 files
- 69 E2E passed, peer-sync 7 passed
- ruff 613 files (611 + the two new backend files)

The TTL sweep is tested as a pure function rather than through the API: reaching it there would need either a 15-minute sleep or a clock patch inside `app.`, which the mock-boundary rule forbids and which would be testing the patch.

## Not in this PR
The other two children of the epic: the render itself (`rwkz.2` — concurrency cap and the full-lesson re-encode) and LLM call prioritisation (`rwkz.3`). This narrows the duplicate window but does not make a render fit on the box.

body:
## Summary

Checkpoint 2 of 9 on the vertical slice (MICH-577): the pre-Verse combat kit per `docs/design/vertical-slice.md` §3.2 (Strike) and §3.3 (Answer), the input-buffering layer `ARCHITECTURE.md` calls for, and the debug-overlay tell-vs-input instrumentation (§11.2/§11.3).

- **Input buffering** (`scripts/common/input_buffer.gd`): generalizes checkpoint 1's jump-buffer pattern into a reusable class that tracks the actual press timestamp (not just a consumed countdown), so it's inspectable — the overlay reads it directly. Checkpoint 1's jump buffer itself is left as-is (already reviewed/merged); Strike and Answer are built on the new shared class.
- **Strike** (`scripts/player/combat.gd`): startup 90ms / active 70ms / recovery 140ms, 22×30px hitbox forward of the collider edge, damage 1, one hit per activation, no combo. Jump is locked during startup/active and unlocked from the first recovery frame for free (nothing else needed for "cancellable into Jump").
- **Answer**: 0ms startup / 180ms active pose / 220ms whiff recovery / 0ms success recovery, resolved against registered `TellEmitter` nodes. The 120ms pre-window buffer collapses to one inequality (a press counts from 120ms before onset through the window's close), so a pre-emptive press and an in-window press share the same check. Overlapping windows resolve to the soonest-closing tell. A tell closing unresolved applies §3.3's failure effects (1 damage, 180px knockback, 400ms hitstun, 600ms invuln) to the player regardless of the Answer move's own state.
- **Dummy tell emitter** (`scripts/combat/tell_emitter.gd`): minimal, throwaway-shaped scripted fixture — checkpoint 3 replaces it with real enemy tells.
- **Player**: facing direction, `take_hit()` with minimal HP tracking (no death/respawn yet — later checkpoint), jump buffer now also checks `combat.is_jump_locked()`.
- **Debug overlay**: extended readout (hp/strike/answer state) plus a new timeline widget plotting the tell window — including the pre-window buffer segment — against the actual Answer press, color-coded by outcome.
- `scenes/test_room.tscn` gets a scripted dummy `TellEmitter` plus a manual "T"-key director for playtesting Answer against it in a running build.

Out of scope, untouched: real enemies, Return's effect, Sustain, rooms beyond the test room, LDtk, FMOD, save/load.

- [ ] CI (`gut-tests`, `export-smoke`) passes on this PR

- [ ] Press `T` to open a tell window, press `K` (Answer) inside it: success, no damage, overlay shows the press landing inside the window
